o: Its first flight in 1979 successfully carried Rohini RS-1.
Its first successful launch occurred on 18 July 1980 with Rohini RS-1.
35.x: The first SLV-3 attempt on 10 August 1979 failed with the Rohini Technology Payload. The successful flight on 18 July 1980 carried Rohini RS-1.
35.tq: Distinguish the first attempt from the first successful mission.

35.s: The first successful payload of the PSLV was:
35.x: The PSLV’s first successful flight was PSLV-D2 on 15 October 1994, carrying IRS-P2.
35.tq: Match the launch vehicle with its first successful payload.

35.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: SSLV — first flight in 2001 with EOS-07
ASLV — first success in 1987 with SROSS
GSLV — first flight in 2001 with GSAT-1
LVM3 — first flight in 1994 with IRS-P2
35.x: GSLV’s first flight was GSLV-D1 on 18 April 2001, carrying GSAT-1. ASLV’s 1987 and 1988 attempts failed, LVM3 began later, and EOS-07 was associated with SSLV-D2 in 2023.
35.tq: Check both the vehicle date and the first payload before accepting a match.

35.s: The first successful ASLV mission in 1992 carried a satellite of the:
35.x: The ASLV achieved its first success in 1992 with a SROSS-series satellite; its 1987 and 1988 attempts had failed.
35.tq: Use the first-success payload association for ASLV.

35.s: CARE, launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014, was a:
35.x: CARE was a suborbital experimental payload launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014.
35.tq: Distinguish an experimental suborbital payload from operational orbital satellites.

35.s: Why are rockets generally launched eastward from a spaceport?
o: To ensure that every launch reaches a polar orbit
To cancel the rotational velocity of the Earth
To avoid entering an orbit around the Earth
To gain the Earth’s rotational speed and save fuel
35.x: An eastward launch receives an additional velocity from Earth’s rotation, thereby reducing the fuel required to attain orbital speed.
35.tq: Apply the physical principle rather than memorising the direction alone.

35.s: Which location provides the greatest advantage from the Earth’s rotational speed for eastward launches?
o: A site farthest from the equator
A site at a high mountain latitude
A site near the North Pole
35.x: The rotational speed of the Earth is greatest near the equator, so equatorial or near-equatorial sites provide the maximum eastward-launch advantage.
35.tq: Use the latitude comparison: rotational speed is highest near the equator.

35.s: Sriharikota’s east-coast location is especially advantageous because it:
o: Allows rockets to fly over the sea away from populated land
Permits launches only towards the west
Places every satellite directly into geostationary orbit
Eliminates the need for a launch azimuth
35.x: Sriharikota’s east-coast position allows launch trajectories to pass over the sea, reducing risk to populated areas.
35.tq: Identify the safety advantage of the launch-site location.

35.s: Polar and Sun-synchronous orbit launches from Sriharikota generally require a dog-leg trajectory around Sri Lanka because they proceed:
35.x: Polar and Sun-synchronous launches generally follow a southward trajectory from Sriharikota; a dog-leg is used to avoid Sri Lanka.
35.tq: Connect the orbit type with the launch direction and geographical constraint.

35.s: Which launch vehicle is associated with approximately 1,750 kg to SSO and approximately 1,425 kg to GTO?
35.x: The PSLV has an approximate capacity of 1,750 kg to SSO and about 1,425 kg to GTO.
35.tq: Match the paired orbit capacities with the correct vehicle.

35.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its approximate payload capacity?
35.x: GSLV Mk-II can carry about 2–2.5 tonnes to GTO. SSLV, ASLV and SLV-3 have much lower capacities than those stated in the other options.
35.tq: Reject the options with swapped capacity ranges between generations of launch vehicles.

35.s: According to the stated capacity figures, LVM3 can carry approximately how much payload to GTO and LEO respectively?
o: 8 tonnes to GTO and 4 tonnes to LEO
4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO
2 tonnes to GTO and 4 tonnes to LEO
500 kg to GTO and 1,750 kg to LEO
35.x: The stated LVM3 capacity is about 4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO, although some descriptions cite approximately 10 tonnes to LEO.
35.tq: Read the orbit–capacity pair in the correct order.

35.s: Which PSLV variant has no strap-on boosters and uses only the core vehicle?
35.x: PSLV-CA is the core-alone configuration with zero strap-on boosters.
35.tq: Decode the variant by the number of strap-ons rather than by the mission code.

35.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (PSLV variant)
a. PSLV-CA
b. PSLV-DL
c. PSLV-QL
d. PSLV-G

List-II (Number of strap-ons)
i. Six
ii. Two
iii. Zero
iv. Four

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
35.x: PSLV-CA has zero strap-ons, PSLV-DL has two, PSLV-QL has four and PSLV-G has six.
35.tq: Start from the core-alone variant and then assign the increasing strap-on counts.

35.s: PSLV-C62 flew in which configuration?
35.x: PSLV-C62 flew as the PSLV-DL variant, which uses two strap-on boosters.
35.tq: Distinguish the mission number from the vehicle configuration designation.

35.s: RLV-LEX refers to:
o: A sounding-rocket series for atmospheric research
Autonomous landing tests of the Reusable Launch Vehicle Technology Demonstrator
A cryogenic engine test for GSLV Mk-II
35.x: RLV-LEX denotes autonomous landing tests of the Reusable Launch Vehicle Technology Demonstrator. The tests began with a landing on 2 April 2023, followed by Pushpak landings in 2024.
35.tq: Expand the programme acronym through its principal test objective.

35.s: The later reusable-launch-vehicle landings in 2024 were associated with the name:
35.x: The later RLV landing demonstrations in 2024 were referred to as Pushpak landings.
35.tq: Separate reusable-vehicle test names from private-rocket mission names.

35.s:
Which of the following statements about the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) is correct?
1. It is about 90 m tall.
2. Its lift-off mass is approximately 1,000 tonnes.
3. It is intended to support the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035.
4. It is intended to support a crewed lunar landing by 2040.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
35.x: All four statements are correct. NGLV is described as about 90 m tall, with an approximately 1,000-tonne lift-off mass, and is linked to the 2035 space-station and 2040 crewed lunar-landing goals.
35.tq: Verify each numerical and mission objective statement before selecting the complete combination.

35.s: The Third Launch Pad is particularly required for the development and operation of:
35.x: The NGLV programme requires the Third Launch Pad, with an estimated construction period of about four years.
35.tq: Match the infrastructure requirement with the future launch vehicle.

35.s: Which launch vehicle is intended to carry Gaganyaan crew to approximately 400 km LEO for three days?
35.x: The human-rated LVM3, designated HLVM3, is intended for the Gaganyaan crew mission to a 400 km LEO orbit for three days.
35.tq: Match the human-rating designation with the mission profile.

35.s: SOLVE, associated with the Gaganyaan programme, is a:
o: Suborbital test vehicle using a solid motor
35.x: SOLVE is a suborbital test vehicle using a solid motor; its motor was ground-tested at SHAR in July 2026.
35.tq: Distinguish the test vehicle from the human-rated orbital launcher.

35.s: The first Integrated Air Drop Test associated with the human spaceflight programme was conducted on:
35.x: The first Integrated Air Drop Test was conducted on 24 August 2025.
35.tq: Match the test milestone with its exact date, avoiding confusion with RLV and SOLVE dates.

35.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Falcon 9 — SpaceX; New Shepard — Blue Origin
Falcon 9 — Blue Origin; New Shepard — SpaceX
Falcon 9 — Skyroot; New Shepard — Agnikul Cosmos
35.x: Falcon 9 is a reusable launch vehicle developed by SpaceX, while New Shepard is Blue Origin’s reusable suborbital vehicle.
35.tq: Start from the company–vehicle pair and distinguish orbital Falcon 9 from suborbital New Shepard.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian cryogenic and semi-cryogenic engines:
1. CE-7.5 and CE-20 use liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.
2. SCE-200 uses refined kerosene and liquid oxygen.
3. SCE-200 is intended for the LVM3 upgrade and NGLV.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct. CE-7.5 and CE-20 are cryogenic engines using LH2 and LOX, whereas the semi-cryogenic SCE-200 uses refined kerosene and LOX and is planned for LVM3 upgrades and NGLV.
35.tq: Check the propellant distinction first, then verify the stated applications.

35.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Russian cryogenic engines were used in the early GSLV launches.
2. India developed its own cryogenic engine after technology-transfer denial in the 1990s.
3. GSLV-D5 marked the first successful use of India's indigenous cryogenic engine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct. Russia supplied cryogenic engines for early GSLVs; following technology-transfer denial in the 1990s, India developed its own engine, whose first success was GSLV-D5 in 2014.
35.tq: Use the chronological cause-and-effect chain to test all three statements.

35.s: The first successful flight of an Indian indigenous cryogenic engine was associated with which launch vehicle and year?
35.x: GSLV-D5 in 2014 marked the first successful use of India's indigenous cryogenic engine.
35.tq: Match the milestone with its precise vehicle and year rather than a nearby launch event.

35.s: Engine tests for Indian cryogenic and semi-cryogenic systems are conducted at:
35.x: The tests are conducted at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC), Mahendragiri, in Tamil Nadu. LPSC Valiamala is associated with design work and is not the testing facility identified here.
35.tq: Discriminate between the design centre and the propulsion-test facility.

35.s: Why are orbital launches generally conducted in an eastward direction?
o: It prevents the launch vehicle from entering a polar orbit
It adds Earth's rotational speed to the launch vehicle's velocity and saves fuel
It places every satellite directly into geostationary orbit
It reduces the effect of Earth's gravity completely
35.x: An eastward launch takes advantage of Earth's west-to-east rotation. The rotational velocity contributes to the launch vehicle's speed and consequently reduces fuel requirements.
35.tq: Apply the physical principle to identify the operational advantage of eastward launch.

35.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)?
o: An orbit whose perigee and apogee are both near 36,000 km
A circular orbit over the equator at a fixed altitude
An elliptical transfer orbit with its apogee near 36,000 km
A near-polar orbit passing places at the same local solar time
35.x: GTO is an elliptical transfer orbit whose apogee is near 36,000 km. It is used as a transfer path toward geosynchronous or geostationary orbit.
35.tq: Distinguish the transfer orbit from the final geostationary and sun-synchronous orbits.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding GSO and GEO:
1. A geosynchronous orbit has a period of one day.
2. A geostationary orbit is a geosynchronous orbit over the equator.
3. A satellite in a geostationary orbit appears fixed in the sky.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct. GSO has a one-day period, while GEO is the equatorial form of such an orbit in which the satellite appears fixed relative to the sky.
35.tq: Separate the broader geosynchronous category from its equatorial geostationary form.

35.s: A sun-synchronous satellite is particularly suitable for imaging because it:
o: always travels in an eastward equatorial orbit
passes over a given place at the same local solar time
35.x: A sun-synchronous orbit is generally near-polar and passes over a given location at approximately the same local solar time, which is useful for consistent imaging conditions.
35.tq: Link the orbital characteristic with its practical imaging advantage.

35.s: What is the principal function of strap-on boosters attached to a launch vehicle?
o: To reduce the apogee of the transfer orbit
To maintain the satellite in geostationary orbit
To provide the satellite's communication payload
To increase lift-off thrust available to the core vehicle
35.x: Strap-on boosters supplement the core stage by providing additional thrust during lift-off.
35.tq: Identify the component by its function during the initial phase of flight.

35.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Perigee — highest point of a geostationary orbit only
35.x: Apogee is the farthest point of an orbit from Earth, while perigee is the nearest point.
35.tq: Discriminate between the commonly confused orbital terms by their distance from Earth.

35.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the launch and payload event of 4 September 2026?
o: PSLV-C61 placed EOS-09 into a sun-synchronous orbit
GSLV-F17 placed EOS-05 into a sub-GTO
PSLV-C62 placed EOS-N1 into a geostationary orbit
LVM3 placed EOS-05 into a polar orbit
35.x: GSLV-F17 successfully placed EOS-05, India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit, into a sub-GTO on 4 September 2026.
35.tq: Match the vehicle, payload, orbit and date without confusing nearby PSLV events.

35.s: EOS-05, placed into a sub-GTO by GSLV-F17, was significant because it was India's first imaging satellite in:
35.x: EOS-05 was India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit; GSLV-F17 placed it into a sub-GTO as part of that mission.
35.tq: Use the payload's stated orbital distinction rather than the launch vehicle alone.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent PSLV missions:
1. PSLV-C61 carrying EOS-09 failed at the third stage on 18 May 2025.
2. PSLV-C62 carrying EOS-N1 failed at the third stage on 12 January 2026.
3. No ISRO launches took place in the first quarter of 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct. The failures of C61 and C62 at the third stage were followed by the absence of ISRO launches in the first quarter of 2026.
35.tq: Verify each date-event relationship before selecting the coded combination.

35.s: According to ISSAR 2025, which of the following figures correctly represents the number of successful launches worldwide?
35.x: ISSAR 2025 recorded 315 successful launches worldwide. It also reported 4,651 objects placed in orbit, while India's figures were 86 satellites in orbit and 27 operational satellites.
35.tq: Separate the global launch count from the objects-placed and India-specific figures.

35.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the ISSAR 2025 figures?
o: 315 successful launches worldwide and 4,651 objects placed in orbit
4,651 successful launches worldwide and 315 objects placed in orbit
86 successful launches worldwide and 27 objects placed in orbit
27 successful launches worldwide and 86 objects placed in orbit
35.x: ISSAR 2025 reported 315 successful launches worldwide and 4,651 objects placed in orbit.
35.tq: Match the two related numerical indicators without reversing their meanings.

35.s:
The proposed Third Launch Pad is primarily intended to support which of the following future objectives?
1. Launches of NGLV and semi-cryogenic LVM3
2. Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035
3. Crewed lunar landing by 2040
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: The Third Launch Pad is planned to support NGLV and semi-cryogenic LVM3 missions and is associated with the objectives of establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and achieving a crewed lunar landing by 2040.
35.tq: Treat the launch-pad proposal as a linked infrastructure-and-objectives question.

35.s: Which launch vehicle and satellite combination marked India's acquisition of its own orbital launch capability in 1980?
35.x: Rohini RS-1 was launched by SLV-3 in 1980, marking India's status as a nation with its own orbital launch capability.
35.tq: Identify the first milestone by pairing the launch vehicle with its payload and year.

35.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. GSLV-D5 achieves the first successful indigenous cryogenic-engine flight
B. Rohini RS-1 is launched by SLV-3
C. PSLV-C61 fails at the third stage
D. PSLV-C62 fails at the third stage
35.x: Rohini RS-1 was launched in 1980, GSLV-D5 succeeded in 2014, PSLV-C61 failed in May 2025, and PSLV-C62 failed in January 2026.
35.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate milestones.

35.s: The current foreign direct investment rules permit what level of automatic FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports?
35.x: The revised rules allow 49% automatic FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports.
35.tq: Recall the precise percentage and distinguish it from nearby investment thresholds.

35.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Indian launch sites is correct?
o: All orbital launches take place from Kulasekarapattinam, while Sriharikota is used only for defence launches.
Private Agnibaan launches take place exclusively from Kerala, and SSLV launches are restricted to Sriharikota.
All orbital launches, including private Agnibaan, take place from Sriharikota; a second SSLV spaceport is being established at Kulasekarapattinam.
Sriharikota is being replaced by a second spaceport at Mahendragiri for all orbital launches.
35.x: Orbital launches, including private Agnibaan missions, are conducted from Sriharikota. A second spaceport for SSLV is being established at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu.
35.tq: Use the location rule and the planned second-spaceport distinction to reject swapped locations.

35.s: The foundation for the second spaceport intended for SSLV launches was laid at Kulasekarapattinam on:
35.x: The foundation for the second SSLV spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam, Tamil Nadu, was laid on 27 August 2025.
35.tq: Match the infrastructure milestone with its exact date rather than a launch date.

35.s: Which of the following was India's first indigenous launch vehicle and its associated satellite milestone?
35.x: The first indigenous launch milestone was achieved in 1980 when SLV-3 placed Rohini in orbit.
35.tq: Use the launch-vehicle and payload pairing rather than the satellite name alone.

35.s: Which of the following correctly compares the payload capacities of SLV-3 and ASLV to LEO?
35.x: SLV-3 carried about 40 kg to LEO, while ASLV was designed for about 150 kg to LEO.
35.tq: Compare the two early vehicles using their LEO capacity figures.

35.s: EOS-05, as listed for September 2026, was placed in a
35.x: EOS-05 was placed in a sub-geostationary transfer orbit, or sub-GTO, in September 2026.
35.tq: Recognise the precise transfer-orbit term instead of substituting GEO or LEO.

35.s:
With reference to BlueBird Block-2, consider the following statements:
1. It weighs 6,100 kg.
2. It was associated with LVM3-M6.
3. It is described as the largest commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: BlueBird Block-2 is associated with LVM3-M6, weighs 6,100 kg and is described as the largest commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit.
35.tq: Verify a three-part description by checking weight, launch vehicle and orbital status.

35.s:
Arrange the following events or developments in chronological order:
A. Launch of GSAT-9 as the South Asia Satellite
B. Launch of CMS-03/GSAT-7R
C. Association of BlueBird Block-2 with LVM3-M6
D. Recognition of BlueBird Block-2 in APPCA 2026
Which of the following is the correct sequence?
35.x: GSAT-9 was launched in May 2017, CMS-03/GSAT-7R relates to November 2025, and BlueBird Block-2 is associated with LVM3-M6 and APPCA 2026 thereafter.
35.tq: Use the first dated event and then place the 2025 and 2026 developments.

35.s: Which one of the following correctly describes BlueBird Block-2?
o: A US satellite of AST SpaceMobile launched by LVM3-M6, with a 223 m² phased array for direct-to-smartphone broadband.
An ESA solar satellite launched by PSLV-C59 for corona studies.
A UK navigation satellite launched by PSLV-C48 with a 64 m² radar antenna.
An Israeli weather satellite launched by GSLV-F14 for disaster warning.
35.x: BlueBird Block-2 belongs to AST SpaceMobile of the United States. It was launched by LVM3-M6 and has a 223 m² phased array for direct-to-smartphone broadband.
35.tq: Combine ownership, vehicle, antenna size and application to avoid mixed attributes.

35.s:
Consider the following statements about SpaDeX:
1. It was launched on 30 December 2024.
2. Its two spacecraft docked on 16 January 2025.
3. It was launched using PSLV-C60.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct: SpaDeX launched on 30 December 2024 aboard PSLV-C60 and docking occurred on 16 January 2025.
35.tq: Verify date, follow-up event and launch vehicle as separate factual components.

35.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. India becomes the fourth nation to dock in space through SpaDeX
B. National Quantum Mission is launched
C. IndiaAI Mission is introduced
D. Semicon 2.0 is approved

Select the correct sequence.
35.x: The National Quantum Mission dates to 2023, the IndiaAI Mission to March 2024, SpaDeX docking to 16 January 2025, and Semicon 2.0 approval to July 2026.
35.tq: Place the dated developments first and use the latest approval as the final item.

36.s: Which of the following correctly describes ISRO's RLV-TD ‘Pushpak’?
o: A reusable winged vehicle intended to support a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system
A single-use solid-propellant launch vehicle for lunar missions
A cryogenic upper stage used in the GSLV Mk II
A reusable capsule designed exclusively for crewed re-entry
36.x: Pushpak is ISRO’s reusable winged vehicle and is intended to contribute to a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system.
36.tq: Use the exact vehicle-purpose association rather than confusing it with a launcher stage.

36.s: The RLV-TD ‘Pushpak’ completed which of the following experiments?
o: Integrated hot test of a semi-cryogenic engine
36.x: Pushpak completed LEX-03, an autonomous landing experiment.
36.tq: Match the named vehicle with its specific test or mission.

36.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated benefit of reusable launch systems?
o: Elimination of the need for thermal protection systems
Reduction in launch cost by up to 80 percent
36.x: Reusable vehicles require a reusable Thermal Protection System; its elimination is not a benefit identified for such systems.
36.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated benefit into an impossibility.

36.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reusable launch systems:
1. Autonomous precision landing is one of the technological challenges.
2. High research and development cost is a challenge.
3. Reusable Thermal Protection Systems are required.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: All three statements identify challenges associated with reusable launch systems.
36.tq: Check each statement against the separate challenge categories before choosing the combined code.

36.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
36.x: New Glenn is associated with Blue Origin. Falcon 9 and Starship belong to SpaceX, while Zhuque-3 belongs to LandSpace.
36.tq: Start with the company–vehicle pair that is directly identifiable and eliminate swapped-company options.

36.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Reusable rocket)
a. Falcon 9
a. Starship
c. New Glenn
d. Zhuque-3

List-II (Company)
i. Blue Origin
ii. LandSpace
iii. SpaceX

The correct matching is:
36.x: Falcon 9 and Starship are SpaceX vehicles, New Glenn is associated with Blue Origin, and Zhuque-3 with LandSpace.
36.tq: Begin with the repeated SpaceX association and then resolve the remaining company pairs.

36.s: Which reusable rocket is associated with first-stage recovery more than 520 times?
36.x: Falcon 9’s first stages had been recovered more than 520 times as stated.
36.tq: Link the distinctive numerical figure with the correct vehicle rather than with another reusable rocket.

36.s: Which one of the following statements about Starship is correct?
o: It uses approximately 1,200 tonnes of liquid methane and LOX and is fully reusable.
Its booster is recovered only by parachute.
It is an orbital-class recovery vehicle developed by LandSpace.
It uses refined kerosene and LOX and has no planned in-orbit refuelling.
36.x: Starship is described as fully reusable and using about 1,200 tonnes of liquid methane and LOX.
36.tq: Separate the vehicle’s propellants and reusability from the characteristics of other rockets.

36.s: How many in-orbit refuellings are needed by Starship for NASA’s Moon-landing mission, as indicated?
36.x: Starship is indicated to require more than 10 in-orbit refuellings for NASA’s Moon-landing mission.
36.tq: Distinguish an approximate threshold from an exact numerical claim.

36.s: Which company developed Zhuque-3, associated with attempted recovery of orbital-class stages?
36.x: Zhuque-3 is associated with LandSpace of China.
36.tq: Use the developer–vehicle association and avoid confusing it with the two SpaceX vehicles.

36.s: Agnilet, developed by Agnikul Cosmos, is described as the world’s first:
36.x: Agnilet is described as the world’s first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.
36.tq: Identify the exact superlative and engine category associated with the named product.

36.s: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from which launch pad?
o: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre’s private pad
Dhanush, India’s first private launch pad at Sriharikota
Satish Dhawan Space Centre’s second launch pad
A private launch pad at Bengaluru
36.x: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from Dhanush at Sriharikota, described as India’s first private launch pad.
36.tq: Test the precise location and identity of the launch facility.

36.s:
Which of the following statements about Agnite is correct?
1. It is a single-piece 3D-printed booster engine.
2. It is made of Inconel.
3. It is intended for the Agnibaan booster stage.
36.x: Agnite is described as a single-piece 3D-printed engine made of Inconel for the Agnibaan booster stage.
36.tq: Verify the material, manufacturing method and intended stage separately.

36.s: EVEREST, unveiled by Astrobase in August 2026, is described as India’s first private:
o: 800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine
solid motor for the Agnibaan booster
36.x: Astrobase’s EVEREST is described as India’s first private 800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine.
36.tq: Combine the distinctive thrust rating with the engine cycle and propellant pair.

36.s: ISRO’s 1,000-hour life test was conducted on which propulsion system?
o: A 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster of the Hall type
36.x: The test involved a 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster, a Hall-type thruster using xenon.
36.tq: Match the test duration and thrust rating to the correct propulsion technology.

36.s: Which propellant is used in the Hall-type Stationary Plasma Thruster tested by ISRO?
36.x: The Hall-type Stationary Plasma Thruster uses xenon as its propellant.
36.tq: Discriminate the electric-propulsion propellant from chemical rocket propellants.

36.s: The specific impulse of the tested Hall-type thruster is approximately how many times that of chemical systems?
36.x: Its specific impulse is approximately six times that of chemical propulsion systems.
36.tq: Recall the distinctive comparative figure rather than the absolute thrust value.

36.s: The Hall-type Stationary Plasma Thruster is intended to replace chemical propulsion on future:
36.x: The thruster is intended for replacing chemical propulsion on future communication satellites.
36.tq: Connect the propulsion technology with its stated operational application.

36.s: Why is LOX-methane considered important for Mars-return missions and in-situ resource utilisation?
o: It can be stored indefinitely without refrigeration.
Methane can be produced from Martian resources, while the combination is cleaner and cheaper.
LOX-methane is a hypergolic combination that ignites on contact.
Methane has the highest density of all cryogenic fuels and needs no oxidiser.
36.x: LOX-methane is considered cleaner and cheaper, and methane can be produced from Martian resources.
36.tq: Use the cause–application link instead of confusing methane with hypergolic or earth-storable propellants.

36.s: POEM is correctly expanded as:
36.x: POEM stands for PSLV Orbital Experimental Module.
36.tq: Test the exact expansion of the acronym and avoid substitutions of similar space terms.

36.s: What is the principal function of the spent PS4 stage in POEM?
o: It is used as a planetary landing engine.
It is converted into a reusable crew capsule.
It is reused as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
It serves as a cryogenic upper stage for GSLV.
36.x: POEM reuses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
36.tq: Follow the transformation of the spent stage into its orbital-platform role.

36.s: In a cryogenic engine, the fuel and oxidiser are respectively:
36.x: Cryogenic propulsion uses liquid hydrogen as fuel and liquid oxygen as oxidiser.
36.tq: Keep the fuel–oxidiser order distinct from the reverse order and from semi-cryogenic combinations.

36.s: Which of the following correctly gives the approximate temperatures of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen?
36.x: Liquid hydrogen is approximately −253°C, while liquid oxygen is approximately −183°C.
36.tq: Watch the reversed-number trap in paired temperature values.

36.s: The exhaust of a liquid hydrogen–liquid oxygen cryogenic engine is predominantly:
36.x: The exhaust is described as only water vapour because hydrogen combines with oxygen.
36.tq: Infer the exhaust from the chemical composition of the propellants.

36.s: Which characteristic of cryogenic propulsion is correctly stated?
o: It uses dense kerosene and is non-toxic.
It has a specific impulse of approximately 260 seconds and cannot be restarted.
It is unsuitable for upper stages because of its low efficiency.
It has a specific impulse of approximately 450 seconds, the highest among the listed categories.
36.x: Cryogenic propulsion has an approximate specific impulse of 450 seconds and is the most efficient category listed.
36.tq: Associate the highest specific impulse with cryogenic propellants, not solid or semi-cryogenic systems.

36.s: Why are liquid hydrogen cryogenic systems unsuitable for military missiles?
o: Liquid hydrogen has an exceptionally high density and requires no insulation.
Liquid hydrogen has very low density, about 0.071 g/ml, requires huge tanks and is difficult to store for long periods.
Liquid hydrogen cannot produce water vapour on combustion.
Liquid hydrogen ignites spontaneously on contact with nitrogen tetroxide.
36.x: The very low density of liquid hydrogen, about 0.071 g/ml, necessitates large tanks and makes long-term storage difficult.
36.tq: Link the numerical density with the storage and tank-size consequence.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Cryogenic Upper Stage Project began in 1994.
2. The project cost was ₹300 crore.
3. India tested a full cryogenic stage in 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: The Cryogenic Upper Stage Project began in 1994, involved a cost of ₹300 crore, and India tested a full cryogenic stage in 2006.
36.tq: Treat the project date, cost and test milestone as independent factual checks.

36.s: What was the outcome of the 1991 Glavkosmos agreement concerning cryogenic technology?
o: Russia transferred all cryogenic technology without restriction.
The United States supplied seven cryogenic engines to India.
US MTCR-based sanctions stopped technology transfer, although Russia supplied seven engines.
The agreement was cancelled by India before any engines were supplied.
36.x: Glavkosmos agreed to sell engines and technology in 1991, but US MTCR-based sanctions in 1992 stopped technology transfer; Russia supplied seven engines only.
36.tq: Separate the original agreement, the later sanctions and the limited engine supply.

36.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Glavkosmos agreed to sell cryogenic engines and technology.
B. MTCR-based sanctions stopped the technology transfer.
C. India tested a full cryogenic stage.
D. GSLV Mk II flew with the indigenous CE-7.5 stage.
36.x: The sequence is 1991 agreement, 1992 sanctions, 2006 full-stage test and 2014 GSLV Mk II flight with the indigenous stage.
36.tq: Fix the first and last events by year, then place the sanctions and test between them.

36.s: GSLV Mk II flew with the indigenous CE-7.5 cryogenic stage on:
36.x: The indigenous CE-7.5 cryogenic stage was flown by GSLV Mk II on 5 January 2014.
36.tq: Distinguish adjacent-year options using the exact milestone date.

36.s: Which engine is correctly matched with its propellant combination and application?
o: Vikas — UH25 and N2O4 — PSLV second stage
CE-7.5 — kerosene and LOX — GSLV Mk II upper stage
CE-20 — solid fuel and liquid oxidiser — LVM3 C25 stage
SE2000 — LOX and LH2 — NGLV upper stage
36.x: Vikas uses UH25 and N2O4 and is used in the PSLV second stage. CE-7.5 and CE-20 use LOX and LH2, while SE2000 uses kerosene and LOX.
36.tq: Start with the engine–propellant pair and then verify its vehicle stage.

36.s: The CE-7.5 engine is associated with which combination?
o: 75 kN, LOX–LH2 staged-combustion engine for the GSLV Mk II cryogenic upper stage
UH25–N2O4 engine for the PSLV second stage
200 kN, LOX–LH2 gas-generator engine for the LVM3 C25 stage
Semi-cryogenic kerosene–LOX engine for the NGLV
36.x: CE-7.5 is a 75 kN staged-combustion LOX–LH2 engine used in the GSLV Mk II cryogenic upper stage.
36.tq: Combine thrust rating, engine cycle and stage application to reject mixed attributes.

36.s: Which statement regarding CE-20 is correct?
o: It is a 75 kN staged-combustion engine used in GSLV Mk II.
It is a solid motor used in the PSLV first stage.
It is a kerosene–LOX engine replacing the L110 core.
It is a 200 kN-class gas-generator LOX–LH2 engine used in the LVM3 C25 upper stage.
36.x: CE-20 is a 200 kN-class gas-generator LOX–LH2 engine for the LVM3 C25 upper stage.
36.tq: Separate CE-20 from CE-7.5 using cycle, thrust and vehicle-stage clues.

36.s:
The CE-20 engine has been used for which of the following missions or flight categories?
1. Chandrayaan-2
2. Chandrayaan-3
3. All LVM3 commercial flights
36.x: CE-20 powers the LVM3 C25 upper stage used for Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3 and all LVM3 commercial flights.
36.tq: Check whether the engine association extends across all three listed applications.

36.s: What is the significance of the CE-20 bootstrap-mode start test?
o: It eliminates the need for liquid oxygen in the engine.
It proves that CE-20 can operate only with solid propellant.
It demonstrates starting on the engine’s own propellant flow without external gas, supporting in-space restart.
It converts CE-20 into a hypergolic engine.
36.x: Bootstrap mode starts the engine using its own propellant flow without external gas and is important for in-space restart capability.
36.tq: Connect the test method with its operational consequence rather than with a propellant change.

36.s: Which propellant combination is planned for the SE2000 engine?
36.x: SE2000 is a semi-cryogenic engine using refined kerosene and LOX.
36.tq: Distinguish the semi-cryogenic combination from the cryogenic and earth-storable pairs.

36.s: SE2000 is planned for which applications?
o: Replacing the C25 in GSLV Mk II only
The PSLV first stage and S200 booster only
Replacing the L110 in LVM3-SC and for the NGLV
36.x: SE2000 is planned for LVM3-SC, replacing the L110, and for the NGLV.
36.tq: Match the engine with its planned vehicle-stage applications.

36.s: Which propellant category is correctly matched with its characteristic?
o: Solid — high initial thrust but cannot normally be throttled or stopped
Hybrid — cannot be stopped or restarted
Hypergolic — requires an external ignition system at every start
Cryogenic — least efficient but simplest to handle
36.x: Solid propellants provide high initial thrust but generally cannot be throttled or stopped. Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact, hybrids can be stopped or restarted, and cryogenic systems are highly efficient but complex.
36.tq: Compare the operational feature of each propellant category instead of relying on the category name alone.

36.s: Which one of the following is an earth-storable liquid propellant combination?
36.x: UH25 and N2O4 are listed as earth-storable liquid propellants. Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.
36.tq: Separate earth-storable liquid propellants from cryogenic and semi-cryogenic combinations.

36.s: Hydrazine-family propellants combined with N2O4 are classified as hypergolic because they:
o: Are non-toxic and suitable for large reusable boosters
Require cryogenic storage and have the highest specific impulse
Ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
36.x: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring, although they are highly toxic.
36.tq: Use the defining property of hypergolic propellants to identify the correct application.

36.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. HTPB — solid propellant example
2. Hydrazine, MMH and UDMH — earth-storable liquid examples
3. Kerosene and LOX — semi-cryogenic combination
4. Solid fuel and liquid oxidiser — hybrid combination
36.x: All four pairings are correct examples of the respective propellant categories.
36.tq: Verify each category–example pair before selecting the complete combination.

36.s: Which propellant category has an approximate specific impulse of 260 seconds and is associated with high initial thrust?
36.x: Solid propellants have an approximate specific impulse of 260 seconds and provide high initial thrust.
36.tq: Use the specific-impulse figure as the discriminator among propellant categories.

36.s: Which statement best describes hybrid propulsion?
o: It uses solid fuel and a liquid oxidiser and can be stopped or restarted.
It uses hydrazine and N2O4 and ignites on contact.
It uses liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen and is the most efficient category.
It uses UH25 and N2O4 and cannot be restarted.
36.x: Hybrid propulsion combines solid fuel with a liquid oxidiser and can be stopped or restarted.
36.tq: Identify the category from its distinctive two-phase propellant arrangement and controllability.

36.s: The SE2000 semi-cryogenic engine uses:
o: Refined kerosene as fuel and LOX as oxidiser
Liquid hydrogen as fuel and LOX as oxidiser
HTPB as fuel and liquid oxygen as oxidiser
UH25 as fuel and N2O4 as oxidiser
36.x: SE2000 uses refined kerosene and liquid oxygen.
36.tq: Test the exact fuel–oxidiser pairing of the named semi-cryogenic engine.

36.s: What did the third hot test of the SE2000 Power Head Test Article validate?
o: Autonomous landing of a reusable vehicle
Ignition and start-up at 60 percent power
Operation with liquid hydrogen at 100 percent power
In-space restart at full power without propellant flow
36.x: The third hot test of the PHTA at 60 percent power validated ignition and start-up.
36.tq: Combine the test number, power level and validated functions to avoid partial matches.

36.s: Which private company conducted a static test of the KALAM 1200 solid motor?
36.x: Skyroot’s KALAM 1200 solid motor was static-tested at SDSC-SHAR.
36.tq: Match the private company with its specific motor and test activity.

36.s: Which of the following correctly describes Skyroot’s KALAM 1200 motor?
o: An 11-metre solid motor containing 30 tonnes of propellant
A 30-metre semi-cryogenic engine containing 11 tonnes of propellant
An 11-metre cryogenic engine containing 30 tonnes of liquid hydrogen
A 1200 kN Hall thruster tested with xenon
36.x: KALAM 1200 is described as an 11-metre solid motor with 30 tonnes of propellant.
36.tq: Watch for reversal of the dimensions and propellant quantity in the options.

36.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding air-breathing engines:

List-I (Engine)
a. Ramjet
b. Scramjet

List-II (Characteristic)
i. Combustion with subsonic airflow
ii. Combustion with supersonic airflow
iii. Speed generally above Mach 2
iv. Speed generally in the Mach 5–6 and above range

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–i and iii; b–ii and iv
a–ii and iii; b–i and iv
a–i and iv; b–ii and iii
a–ii and iv; b–i and iii
36.x: A ramjet uses forward speed for compression, has subsonic combustion and operates above Mach 2. A scramjet has supersonic combustion and is designed for speeds of about Mach 5–6 and above.
36.tq: Start from the sure pair linking scramjet with supersonic combustion, then eliminate codes.

36.s: Which one of the following best explains the principal advantage of a scramjet over a conventional rocket during atmospheric flight?
o: It operates with subsonic airflow at speeds below Mach 2.
It eliminates the need for fuel during hypersonic flight.
It carries atmospheric oxygen, thereby reducing the weight of the onboard oxidiser.
It uses a compressor to compress atmospheric air before combustion.
36.x: A scramjet uses oxygen from the atmosphere, so it need not carry the entire oxidiser required by a rocket. It still requires fuel and works with supersonic airflow.
36.tq: Use the function-based option; distinguish an air-breathing engine from a rocket.

36.s: The major operational challenge in sustaining combustion in a scramjet is popularly compared with which of the following situations?
o: Boiling water in a pressure cooker
Lighting a candle in a hurricane
Starting a diesel engine in winter
Flying a glider in still air
36.x: Maintaining stable combustion in the extremely fast supersonic airflow of a scramjet is likened to trying to keep a candle alight in a hurricane.
36.tq: Recognise the distinctive analogy associated with the technical difficulty.

36.s: India's Advanced Technology Vehicle (ATV) flight-tested scramjet engines in August 2016 from:
36.x: ISRO's Advanced Technology Vehicle flight-tested scramjet engines in August 2016 from Sriharikota.
36.tq: Separate the vehicle, testing year and launch location in a direct location-date question.

36.s: India became the fourth country to demonstrate scramjet flight after which sequence of countries?
o: China, France and the United Kingdom
36.x: The countries identified as having demonstrated scramjet flight before India are the United States, Russia and China.
36.tq: Use the stated ordinal rank and identify all the countries preceding India.

36.s:
Consider the following statements regarding hypersonic propulsion:
1. HSTDV is a scramjet vehicle of DRDO.
2. DRDO tested an actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor for 20 minutes.
3. The combustor used an indigenous endothermic hydrocarbon fuel.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: HSTDV is DRDO's scramjet vehicle. DRDO's actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor operated for 20 minutes using an indigenous endothermic hydrocarbon fuel.
36.tq: Check each statement against the vehicle, duration and fuel details before selecting the combined code.

36.s: On which date was the operation of DRDO's actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor reported?
36.x: The reported operation of the actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor occurred on 12 May 2026.
36.tq: Distinguish the closely placed dates associated with different space and propulsion developments.

36.s:
With reference to the proposed NGLV 'Soorya', consider the following statements:
1. It is planned as a reusable heavy-lift rocket.
2. It is designed to carry about 20,000 kg to low Earth orbit.
3. It is planned to use semi-cryogenic propulsion.
4. Its projected payload to low Earth orbit is about 2.5 times that of LVM3.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Soorya is planned as a reusable heavy-lift NGLV using semi-cryogenic propulsion, with a payload of about 20,000 kg to LEO—approximately 2.5 times the LVM3 capacity.
36.tq: Treat the payload, propulsion, reusability and comparison figures as separate statements and verify all four.

36.s: The approximate payload capacity of the proposed NGLV 'Soorya' to low Earth orbit is:
36.x: The proposed NGLV 'Soorya' is intended to place approximately 20,000 kg into low Earth orbit.
36.tq: Use the payload-class figure rather than confusing it with the vehicle's lift-off mass.

36.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to NGLV 'Soorya'?
o: Launch site — Third Launch Pad, Sriharikota
36.x: Soorya is planned to use semi-cryogenic propulsion, not exclusively solid propulsion. Its projected height is about 90 metres, lift-off mass about 1,000 tonnes, and launch site the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota.
36.tq: Find the option that reverses the propulsion detail while retaining the correct vehicle specifications.

36.s:
The proposed NGLV 'Soorya' is intended to support which of the following future objectives?
1. Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035
2. Crewed lunar landing by 2040
3. Scramjet testing from Sriharikota in August 2016

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
36.x: Soorya is intended to support the Bharatiya Antariksh Station planned for 2035 and a crewed lunar landing planned for 2040. Scramjet testing in August 2016 was a separate ATV activity.
36.tq: Separate the NGLV's future mission objectives from the unrelated scramjet demonstration.

36.s: Which of the following correctly describes Skyroot's Vikram-1 on Mission Aagaman?
o: A reusable heavy-lift vehicle using semi-cryogenic propulsion for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station
A single-stage suborbital vehicle designed for a crewed lunar landing
A three-stage vehicle using only liquid propulsion, designed to place 20,000 kg into LEO
A four-stage vehicle with three solid stages and one liquid stage, designed to place 290 kg into a 500 km SSO
36.x: Skyroot's Vikram-1 has three solid stages and one liquid stage and is designed for a 290 kg payload to a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit. It reached orbit on Mission Aagaman as India's first private orbital rocket.
36.tq: Match the vehicle with its stage composition and payload class, avoiding the specifications of NGLV.

36.s: Mission Aagaman is associated with which significant development in India's space programme?
o: The first flight of the NGLV from the Third Launch Pad
India's first private orbital rocket reaching orbit
The first cryogenic propellant transfer by Starship in orbit
India's first demonstration of a scramjet engine by ISRO
36.x: Skyroot's Vikram-1 reached orbit on Mission Aagaman, marking India's first private orbital rocket. The other options refer to different or unreported developments.
36.tq: Identify the mission by linking it to its distinctive milestone.

36.s: Why are reusability and advanced propulsion considered important for India's future space activities?
o: They can help India compete in commercial launch services and enable more cost-effective human spaceflight.
They restrict launch vehicles to suborbital missions only.
They remove the need for all atmospheric flight tests.
They make every launch vehicle independent of fuel and oxidiser.
36.x: Reusability and advanced propulsion can reduce launch costs, improve commercial competitiveness and support cost-effective human spaceflight. They do not eliminate the need for propellants or testing.
36.tq: Select the option that links the technology to both stated economic and human-spaceflight outcomes.

36.s: NASA has flagged which of the following as a top risk to Starship's Moon-landing plan?
o: The use of an endothermic hydrocarbon fuel in an HSTDV combustor
The absence of a solid stage in Vikram-1
36.x: Cryogenic propellant transfer in orbit has been identified as a top risk to Starship's Moon-landing plan.
36.tq: Use the distinctive risk-technology association rather than confusing it with propulsion tests on other vehicles.

36.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Engine — Application
36.x: CE-7.5, using liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, is used in the upper stage of GSLV Mk-II. CE-20 is used in the LVM3 C25 stage, while SCE-200 is intended for the LVM3 upgrade and NGLV.
36.tq: Start from the sure engine–application pair and eliminate the swapped-stage options.

36.s: The C25 stage of LVM3 is powered by which of the following engines?
o: A cryogenic engine developed by Russia
36.x: The CE-20 engine, using liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, is used in the LVM3 C25 stage.
36.tq: Directly identify the engine associated with the named launch-vehicle stage.

36.s: POEM is best described as:
o: A crew escape module for human spaceflight
The spent fourth stage of PSLV reused as an orbital platform
A radar network for tracking aircraft
A lunar rover operated by ISRO
36.x: POEM, or PSLV Orbital Experimental Module, reuses the spent PS4, the fourth stage of the PSLV, as an orbital platform.
36.tq: Break the acronym and connect it with the correct launch-vehicle stage.

36.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: EVEREST — Astrobase’s first private Indian 800 kN full-flow staged-combustion methane engine
36.x: EVEREST is associated with Astrobase’s first private Indian 800 kN full-flow staged-combustion methane engine.
36.tq: Use the company–technology pairing and eliminate cross-swapped organisations.

36.s: Agnikul’s distinction in the Indian private space sector is that it achieved:
o: The first launch from a private pad named Dhanush using a single-piece 3D-printed engine
The first 4G stack with a C-DOT core
The first satellite launch on Falcon 9 from a government launch site
The first domestic memory-chip packaging operation
36.x: Agnikul achieved the first launch from a private pad, named Dhanush, using a single-piece 3D-printed engine.
36.tq: Identify the distinctive achievement rather than the organisation’s general sector.

37.s: Which satellite is correctly matched with its principal use?
o: GSAT-6 — Large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic communication
GSAT-11 — First operational satellite of the INSAT system
37.x: GSAT-6, launched in 2015, has a large deployable antenna and supports mobile and strategic communication. GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A serves the Air Force, and INSAT-1B marked operationalisation of INSAT.
37.tq: Start with the satellite-use pair and watch for swapped defence roles and chronology.

37.s:
Arrange the following satellites in chronological order of the years stated for them:
A. GSAT-7
B. GSAT-6
C. GSAT-7A
D. GSAT-11
37.x: The sequence is GSAT-7 (2013), GSAT-6 (2015), GSAT-7A (2018) and GSAT-11 (2018).
37.tq: Fix the earliest satellite first and then distinguish the two 2018 entries by their stated sequence.

37.s: Which one of the following statements about GSAT-11 is correct?
o: It is a dedicated Navy satellite launched in 2013.
It was the first operational satellite of the INSAT system in 1983.
It is a 2015 satellite with a large deployable antenna for mobile communication.
It is India’s heaviest communication satellite, weighing approximately 5.8 tonnes, and supports high-speed rural broadband.
37.x: GSAT-11 is India’s heaviest communication satellite at approximately 5.8 tonnes and is associated with high-speed rural broadband.
37.tq: Use the distinctive weight and broadband function to separate GSAT-11 from the other satellites.

37.s: The INSAT system became operational with:
37.x: The INSAT system became operational with INSAT-1B in 1983.
37.tq: Identify the system’s first operational milestone rather than a later GSAT satellite.

37.s: Satellite communication is particularly significant for approximately what share of Indians who are outside easy terrestrial coverage?
37.x: Satellite communication reaches approximately 20–25 percent of Indians who are outside easy terrestrial coverage.
37.tq: Retain the stated range and reject the tempting rounded alternatives.

37.s: Which of the following best describes the stated role of Starlink’s proposed Indian satellite internet service in 2025?
o: Registering newspapers through a satellite-based portal
Replacing all terrestrial fibre networks in urban areas
Providing broadband to remote, disaster-hit and mobile areas
37.x: Starlink’s India launch was imminent in 2025 and its stated advantage was broadband access for remote, disaster-hit and mobile areas.
37.tq: Apply the service’s coverage advantage to the locations and situations described.

37.s:
Consider the following statements regarding INSAT-1 series:
1. The first INSAT satellites were bought abroad.
2. The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983.
3. The series began from 1992 with INSAT-2A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: The INSAT-1 satellites were procured from abroad and the INSAT system was commissioned in 1983. Statement 3 is false because the INSAT-2 series began in 1992.
37.tq: Split the options by checking the series start dates before considering the combined code.

37.s: KALPANA-1, originally known as METSAT, was primarily designed as a/an
37.x: KALPANA-1, earlier called METSAT, was an exclusive meteorological satellite and was launched by PSLV in September 2002.
37.tq: Match the satellite’s distinctive name with its specialised purpose.

37.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: GSAT-8 — Cyclone-warning satellite without communication payloads
37.x: EDUSAT, also designated GSAT-3, was intended for education and provided two-way classroom links. The other satellites have been matched with incorrect functions.
37.tq: Start with the sure purpose-satellite pair and reject swapped applications.

37.s: EDUSAT (GSAT-3) was launched on 20 September 2004 by
o: LVM3-M5 from Sriharikota into a sub-GTO
Ariane-5 from Kourou into a geostationary transfer orbit
37.x: EDUSAT was launched on 20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01, had a mass of 1,950.5 kg and was positioned at 74°E.
37.tq: Combine the date, launcher and orbital-position clues rather than relying on the satellite’s name alone.

37.s: Which one of the following combinations regarding INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR is correct?
o: INSAT-3D—1983; television broadcasting; INSAT-3DR—1992; mobile communication
INSAT-3D—2013; advanced meteorology; INSAT-3DR—2016; advanced meteorology
37.x: INSAT-3D was launched in 2013 and INSAT-3DR in 2016; both serve advanced meteorological purposes.
37.tq: Compare the two closely named satellites by year and common application.

37.s: The principal purpose of INSAT-3D includes advanced monitoring of
37.x: INSAT-3D provides advanced meteorological observations relating to cyclones, monsoon and rainfall.
37.tq: Identify the application cluster that belongs to meteorological satellites.

37.s: Which one of the following statements about GSAT-8 is correct?
o: It was launched on 21 May 2011 by Ariane-5 and carried a GAGAN payload.
It was launched in 2020 by GSLV-F01 for two-way classroom links.
It was launched in 2018 by Falcon 9 and carried only a military payload.
It was launched in 2004 by PSLV and functioned as an exclusive weather satellite.
37.x: GSAT-8 was launched on 21 May 2011 by Ariane-5 and carried a GAGAN payload; GSAT-10 and GSAT-15 also carried GAGAN payloads.
37.tq: Use the date-launcher-payload combination to distinguish GSAT-8 from nearby GSAT missions.

37.s: Which of the following statements regarding GSAT-11 is correct?
o: It is an experimental satellite launched in 1981 for communication testing.
It is a navigation satellite carrying only search-and-rescue transponders.
It is an approximately 5.8-tonne ISRO-built communication satellite intended to support high-speed internet and rural broadband.
It is a meteorological satellite exclusively used for cyclone warnings.
37.x: GSAT-11 is the heaviest ISRO-built communication satellite, weighing approximately 5.8 tonnes, and supports high-speed internet, rural broadband and Digital India.
37.tq: Use the distinctive largest/heaviest description and application pair.

37.s:
Arrange the following satellites in chronological order of their stated launch dates:
A. GSAT-30
B. KALPANA-1
C. EDUSAT
D. GSAT-8
37.x: KALPANA-1 was launched in 2002, EDUSAT in 2004, GSAT-8 in 2011 and GSAT-30 in 2020.
37.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the middle satellites by year.

37.s: GSAT-N2, also designated GSAT-20, is associated primarily with
37.x: GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20), listed with a November 2024 launch, is intended for broadband and in-flight connectivity.
37.tq: Discriminate the newer GSAT designation from similarly numbered communication satellites.

37.s: CMS-03, also referred to as GSAT-7R, is intended primarily for the
37.x: CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is a Navy satellite, listed as a November 2025 LVM3-M5 launch with a mass of about 4,410 kg.
37.tq: Use the service-specific role to separate CMS-03 from GSAT-7A and GSAT-7B.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-7, known as Rukmini, serves the Navy.
2. GSAT-7A, known as Angry Bird, serves the Indian Air Force.
3. GSAT-7B was proposed for the Army.
4. GSAT-6 has a large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic use.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: All four statements are correct. GSAT-7, GSAT-7A and proposed GSAT-7B are associated respectively with the Navy, Air Force and Army, while GSAT-6 has a large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic applications.
37.tq: Check each service assignment independently before selecting the comprehensive code.

37.s: In the Disaster Warning System, cyclone warnings from the Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai are
o: sent upward through S-band and received through C-band by all receivers without selection
sent upward through UHF and received through MF by television households
sent upward through C-band and received through S-band by selectively addressable receivers
sent upward through Ku-band and received through Ka-band only by military stations
37.x: The warning signal goes up on C-band and comes down on S-band to selectively addressable DWS receivers along the coast.
37.tq: Trace the communication path in order: uplink band, downlink band and receiver type.

37.s: Which organisation receives Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data supplied by SDSC-SHAR for disaster-management purposes?
37.x: SDSC-SHAR supplies Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA).
37.tq: Identify the receiving disaster-management authority rather than the supplying centre.

37.s: INSAT’s search-and-rescue transponders operate under the international programme known as
37.x: INSAT carries search-and-rescue transponders under the international COSPAS-SARSAT programme.
37.tq: Separate search-and-rescue terminology from navigation and education programmes.

37.s: Which one of the following statements about a geostationary satellite is NOT correct?
o: Its orbital plane is the equatorial plane with zero inclination.
Its orbital period is approximately 24 hours.
It orbits at approximately 35,786 km above the equator.
Its fixed orbital height varies according to the mass of the satellite.
37.x: The geostationary orbital height is fixed and does not depend on the satellite’s mass. The other statements correctly describe geostationary orbit.
37.tq: Find the exception by checking the physical condition that does not affect orbital height.

37.s: A geostationary satellite appears stationary to an observer because it
o: moves from east to west in a polar plane
moves from west to east in the equatorial plane with a period matching Earth’s rotation
remains permanently fixed above the North Pole
moves randomly around the Earth at a very low altitude
37.x: A geostationary satellite moves west to east in the equatorial plane and has a 24-hour period, matching Earth’s rotation.
37.tq: Combine direction, plane and period to explain the apparent stationary position.

37.s: Which of the following correctly describes the usual process of placing a communication satellite in geostationary orbit?
o: The launcher places it in an elliptical GTO, after which the satellite’s own motor raises it to GEO.
The satellite first descends into the atmosphere and is then lifted by solar radiation.
The launcher directly places it in a circular polar orbit and the satellite remains there.
The launcher places it directly in a sub-GTO and no onboard propulsion is required.
37.x: Launch vehicles generally inject satellites into an elliptical geostationary transfer orbit (GTO); the satellite’s own motor raises it to geostationary orbit (GEO).
37.tq: Distinguish the transfer orbit from the final geostationary orbit.

37.s: Which one of the following sets contains only Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane?
37.x: INSAT-3A, INSAT-4A, INSAT-4B and GSAT-8 are among the Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane.
37.tq: Group the satellites by launcher and location, rejecting satellites associated with Indian or US launchers.

37.s: GSAT-N2 was launched by
o: US Space Shuttle from Kennedy Space Center
37.x: GSAT-N2 was launched by SpaceX’s Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral.
37.tq: Separate the recent commercial foreign launch from the earlier Ariane launches.

37.s: Which one of the following correctly explains APPLE?
o: Asian Public Platform for Long-distance Education, launched in 2004 as EDUSAT
Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment, launched in 1981 as India’s first experimental communication satellite
Aerial Payload and Propulsion Laboratory Experiment, launched in 2002 as a navigation satellite
Advanced Polar Payload Launch Experiment, launched in 1992 as India’s first meteorological satellite
37.x: APPLE stands for Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment and was India’s first experimental communication satellite, launched in 1981.
37.tq: Expand the acronym and match it with its historical role.

37.s: Which of the following is a feature of the multipurpose INSAT design?
o: Telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster warning and search-and-rescue are integrated on one geostationary platform.
Only military communication is provided through a network of polar satellites.
Only weather imaging is performed, without broadcasting or disaster services.
Education and telemedicine are excluded from the satellite-based service framework.
37.x: INSAT integrates telecommunications, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster warning and search-and-rescue on one geostationary platform. It is regarded as one of the largest domestic systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
37.tq: Select the option that captures the full multipurpose design rather than a single service.

37.s: The INSAT system is a joint venture involving which of the following groups of organisations?
o: DoS, DoT, IMD, All India Radio and Doordarshan
DRDO, RBI, SEBI, NITI Aayog and Election Commission
ISRO, WHO, UNESCO, IMF and World Bank
Ministry of Defence, Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard only
37.x: The INSAT system is a joint venture of the Department of Space, Department of Telecommunications, India Meteorological Department, All India Radio and Doordarshan.
37.tq: Check institutional composition carefully; the trap is substitution of unrelated national bodies.

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the management of the INSAT system is correct?
o: The system is coordinated by Doordarshan alone and controlled from Sriharikota.
The system is coordinated by the INSAT Coordination Committee and controlled from the Master Control Facility at Hassan.
The system is coordinated by the Cyclone Warning Centre and controlled from Kourou.
The system is coordinated by NSIL alone and controlled from Cape Canaveral.
37.x: The INSAT Coordination Committee (ICC) coordinates the system, while control is exercised from the Master Control Facility at Hassan in Karnataka.
37.tq: Distinguish the coordinating body from the operational control facility.

37.s: INSAT-4C was lost because
o: GSLV-F01 failed during the EDUSAT mission
Falcon 9 failed during the GSAT-N2 mission
37.x: INSAT-4C was lost in 2006 when GSLV-F02 failed. It was replaced by INSAT-4CR, launched in September 2007 by GSLV-F04.
37.tq: Link the failed satellite with the correct launch vehicle and year.

37.s: Which one of the following statements about the C and extended-C bands is correct?
o: They are used only for mobile satellite services and DWS downlink.
They are typically used for telecommunications and television distribution in the 4–8 GHz range.
They are used mainly for DTH and VSAT in the 12–18 GHz range.
They are used exclusively for high-throughput broadband in the 26–40 GHz range.
37.x: C and extended-C bands are typically used for telecommunications and television distribution and operate in the 4–8 GHz range.
37.tq: Match each frequency range with its characteristic service before eliminating the swapped bands.

37.s: Ku-band transponders are commonly associated with
o: DWS downlink and mobile satellite services only in the S-band range
military services only in the UHF range
high-throughput broadband only in the Ka-band range
DTH and VSAT services in the 12–18 GHz range
37.x: Ku-band operates typically in the 12–18 GHz range and is used for Direct-to-Home (DTH) and VSAT services.
37.tq: Use the service-frequency pair to distinguish Ku from C, Ka and S bands.

37.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: S-band — television distribution in the 4–8 GHz range
C-band — DTH in the 12–18 GHz range
UHF — education channels through Swayam Prabha
37.x: Ka-band is used for high-throughput broadband, including applications associated with GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2. S-band is associated with mobile satellite services and DWS downlink, while UHF has military applications.
37.tq: Start from the distinctive high-throughput broadband pair and identify the band swap in the distractors.

37.s: Which of the following satellites is associated with UHF, S and C bands in the stated communication configuration?
37.x: CMS-03 has UHF, S and C bands in the stated configuration; UHF is associated with military applications.
37.tq: Identify the satellite from the unusual combination of three transponder bands.

37.s: Which of the following sets contains only high-throughput or broadband satellites?
37.x: GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 are identified with high-throughput broadband services for underserved areas, in-flight links and defence, complementing BharatNet.
37.tq: Group satellites by service category and reject meteorological, educational and strategic-only sets.

37.s: Which of the following is NOT an application served by the INSAT/GSAT system?
o: Extraction of petroleum directly from underground reservoirs
37.x: INSAT/GSAT applications include DSNG, mobile satellite services and satellite-aided search and rescue, but satellites do not directly extract petroleum from underground reservoirs.
37.tq: Find the unrelated activity among the recognised communication and service applications.

37.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Application)
A. DTH
B. VSAT
C. DSNG
D. MSS

List-II (Description)
I. Mobile satellite services
II. Satellite news gathering
III. Direct-to-Home broadcasting
IV. Business networks through very small aperture terminals

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: DTH means Direct-to-Home broadcasting, VSAT supports business networks, DSNG means satellite news gathering, and MSS means mobile satellite services.
37.tq: Begin with the unambiguous acronym expansions and complete the matching code.

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Swayam Prabha is correct?
o: It uses INSAT-4CR to provide satellite-aided search-and-rescue services.
It uses KALPANA-1 to transmit cyclone warnings to coastal receivers.
It uses GSAT-11 to provide only military broadband channels.
It uses GSAT-15 to beam 40 free DTH education channels.
37.x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free Direct-to-Home education channels.
37.tq: Match the named education initiative with its satellite and channel count.

37.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with an INSAT/GSAT service?
o: GRAMSAT — rural development and village-oriented communication support
EDUSAT — military-only communication for the Navy
DTH — launch vehicle guidance from GTO
37.x: GRAMSAT is associated with rural and village-oriented communication support. EDUSAT serves education, while DSNG and DTH are communication applications rather than orbital functions.
37.tq: Distinguish application acronyms from orbital and launch-vehicle terminology.

37.s: The South Asia Satellite is designated as which of the following?
37.x: The South Asia Satellite is designated as GSAT-9.
37.tq: Direct identification of a satellite designation.

37.s: GSAT-9, the South Asia Satellite, was launched in which month and year using GSLV-F09?
37.x: GSAT-9 was launched in May 2017 by the GSLV-F09 launch vehicle.
37.tq: Distinguish the closely placed launch year and vehicle details.

37.s: Which one of the following correctly describes CMS-03, also designated GSAT-7R?
o: A weather satellite launched by GSLV-F09 for cyclone-warning services
A commercial communication satellite placed in low Earth orbit by LVM3-M6
An encrypted satellite providing anti-jam naval links up to 2,000 km from the coast, launched by LVM3-M5
A navigation satellite providing regional positioning services through PSLV
37.x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R is associated with encrypted, anti-jam naval links extending up to 2,000 km from the coast and was launched using LVM3-M5.
37.tq: Match the satellite with its specific defence application and launch vehicle.

37.s: CMS-03/GSAT-7R was associated with which of the following launch and operational details?
o: GSLV-F09, May 2017, regional satellite services for South Asia
LVM3-M6, November 2025, commercial broadband links in low Earth orbit
LVM3-M5, November 2025, encrypted anti-jam naval links up to 2,000 km from the coast
LVM3-M5, November 2024, exclusive weather observation over the east coast
37.x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R is linked with LVM3-M5 in November 2025 and supports encrypted, anti-jam naval links up to 2,000 km from the coast.
37.tq: Split the options by comparing launch vehicle, date and mission purpose.

37.s: The early-warning capability of INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR has had which of the following effects?
o: It sharply reduced cyclone-related deaths on the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
It provided encrypted naval communication up to 2,000 km from the coast.
It made BlueBird Block-2 the largest satellite in low Earth orbit.
It enabled the South Asian countries to opt out of satellite services.
37.x: INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR early warnings sharply reduced cyclone deaths along the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
37.tq: Identify the concrete consequence of a satellite-based warning system.

37.s: KALPANA-1 holds which distinction in the Indian satellite programme?
o: First fully indigenous communication satellite series
First satellite for encrypted naval links
First commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit
37.x: KALPANA-1 was India's first exclusive weather satellite.
37.tq: Direct recall of a first-in-category distinction.

37.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: INSAT-2 — first fully indigenous INSAT series
KALPANA-1 — first South Asia regional communication satellite
INSAT-3DR — first fully indigenous INSAT series
37.x: INSAT-2 was the first fully indigenous INSAT series. KALPANA-1, not GSAT-9 or INSAT-3DR, was the first exclusive weather satellite.
37.tq: Start with the sure satellite-series and first-achievement pair.

37.s: Which satellite is used by Swayam Prabha to provide 40 free DTH educational channels?
37.x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free direct-to-home educational channels.
37.tq: Separate the present educational broadcasting satellite from the original EDUSAT mission.

37.s: Which satellite was described as the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil, weighing 4,410 kg and intended for the Navy?
37.x: CMS-03, also designated GSAT-7R, weighed 4,410 kg and was described as the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil for the Navy.
37.tq: Combine payload mass, satellite identity and user organisation.

38.s: Which company developed India’s first NavIC-based device intended to provide precise directions for infrastructure projects?
38.x: Elena Geo Systems developed India’s first NavIC-based device for precise directions on infrastructure projects.
38.tq: Match the specialised company with its specific technological product.

38.s: Which of the following statements regarding NavIC adoption in mobile devices is correct?
o: NavIC adoption in phones is unrelated to the signals carried by NVS satellites.
The L1 signal was removed from newer NVS satellites to restrict civilian use.
NavIC can be received only through dedicated military terminals.
38.x: Qualcomm Snapdragon chipsets support NavIC. Newer NVS satellites add a civilian L1 signal, making integration with other GNSS-enabled phones easier.
38.tq: Select the positive technology-adoption statement and reject reversed signal claims.

38.s: The AIS-140 requirement relating to NavIC primarily concerns:
o: replacement of all GPS satellites by NavIC satellites
mandatory NavIC-enabled location trackers in public transport vehicles
use of NavIC only in military aircraft
mandatory NavIC receivers for all private household appliances
38.x: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ AIS-140 rule made NavIC-enabled location trackers compulsory in public transport vehicles.
38.tq: Identify the regulatory application from the vehicle-tracking context.

38.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as an application encouraged through NavIC adoption?
38.x: Smart devices, vehicle tracking and fleet management are identified applications. Deep-sea mineral extraction only is not stated as a NavIC adoption application.
38.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated application group.

38.s: The original name of NavIC was:
38.x: NavIC was formerly known as the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, or IRNSS.
38.tq: Separate the former system name from the later public name and related programmes.

38.s: NavIC became fully operational in:
38.x: NavIC became fully operational in 2018.
38.tq: Use the operational milestone rather than the first-launch or second-generation year.

38.s: The genesis of India’s regional navigation system is associated with the denial of GPS data during the:
38.x: The denial of GPS data to India during the 1999 Kargil War encouraged the development of an independent navigation system.
38.tq: Link the triggering event with the correct year and context.

38.s:
With reference to the NavIC constellation, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of seven satellites.
2. Three satellites are in geostationary orbit.
3. Four satellites are in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29° to the equator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: NavIC’s planned constellation has seven satellites: three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29° to the equator.
38.tq: Verify the total and split the constellation into its two orbital groups.

38.s: The primary service area of NavIC extends over India and approximately:
38.x: NavIC provides coverage over India and approximately 1,500 km beyond India’s borders.
38.tq: Distinguish the regional coverage figure from global-system coverage.

38.s: Which frequency bands are associated with the original NavIC services?
38.x: NavIC traditionally provides signals in the L5 and S bands. The NVS series additionally introduces an L1 civilian signal.
38.tq: Avoid importing the familiar GPS bands into the NavIC question.

38.s: The major signal-related improvement introduced by the NVS series is the addition of:
38.x: The NVS series adds a civilian L1 signal compatible with other GNSS systems, helping mobile-phone adoption.
38.tq: Identify the exact new band and its civilian-use implication.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes NavIC’s Standard Positioning Service?
o: It is available only to authorised military users and is encrypted.
It is available only outside India and offers accuracy better than 100 metres.
It is a timing-only service without positioning capability.
It is available to all civilians and offers accuracy better than 20 metres.
38.x: The Standard Positioning Service is available to all civilian users and has a design positioning accuracy better than 20 metres.
38.tq: Contrast civilian SPS with the authorised and encrypted Restricted Service.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about NavIC services:
1. The Restricted Service is intended for authorised or military users.
2. The Restricted Service is encrypted.
3. The Standard Positioning Service is available to all civilians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All three statements are correct. RS is an encrypted service for authorised or military users, while SPS is available to civilians.
38.tq: Use the user-category and encryption distinctions to identify the complete combination.

38.s: The design figure given for the timing accuracy of NavIC’s Standard Positioning Service is better than:
38.x: The timing accuracy of NavIC’s Standard Positioning Service is stated as better than 40 nanoseconds.
38.tq: Read the numerical unit carefully and distinguish timing accuracy from positioning accuracy.

38.s: The GPS programme was initiated by the United States Department of Defense in:
38.x: The GPS programme was initiated by the United States Department of Defense in 1973; its first satellite was launched in 1978.
38.tq: Separate the programme-start year from the first-satellite year.

38.s: Which of the following correctly describes the original GPS constellation design?
o: Seven satellites in three geostationary and four inclined orbits
24 satellites in six orbits at about 20,200 km altitude
12 satellites in two polar orbits at 1,500 km altitude
30 satellites in ten orbits at geostationary altitude
38.x: The original GPS design comprised 24 satellites in six orbits at about 20,200 km altitude.
38.tq: Separate GPS orbital architecture from the seven-satellite NavIC architecture.

38.s: Each satellite in the original GPS constellation circles the Earth approximately:
38.x: Each of the original GPS satellites circles the Earth twice a day.
38.tq: Focus on the orbital-period figure rather than the total satellite count.

38.s: Which of the following statements about GPS signals is correct?
o: GPS signals are confined to marine navigation.
GPS uses signals on L1 at 1,575.42 MHz and on L2.
GPS operates only on NavIC’s S band.
GPS transmits only a civilian L5 signal and no L1 signal.
38.x: GPS uses the L1 signal at 1,575.42 MHz and the L2 signal. Its applications extend well beyond marine navigation.
38.tq: Match the exact frequency and bands while rejecting scope and system swaps.

38.s:
Which of the following is an appropriate application of GPS?
1. Precise timing for power, telecommunications and banking
2. Surveying and geodetic mapping
3. Vehicle tracking and fleet management
4. Precision farming and disaster management
