55.x: MNRE's missions include energy security, a larger share of clean power, energy availability and access, affordability and equity. Exclusive dependence on imported energy is not a mission.
55.tq: Find the option that reverses the objective of an energy ministry.

55.s: The three components of Phase I of the National Bioenergy Programme are:
o: Solar pumps, wind farms and fuel cells
Coal gasification, oil refining and hydrogen storage
55.x: The three parts are waste-to-energy, biomass and biogas.
55.tq: Test the exact composition of the programme rather than its broader renewable-energy context.

55.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MoPNG — exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil and gas
Ministry of Coal — nuclear power and research
Department of Atomic Energy — coal mine allocation
55.x: MoPNG handles exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil and gas. Coal allocation belongs to the Ministry of Coal, nuclear power and research to the Department of Atomic Energy, and BEE deals with energy efficiency.
55.tq: Reject swapped ministry mandates by identifying the sector-specific function.

55.s: OIL India is a Navratna public sector enterprise under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
55.x: OIL India is a Navratna under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
55.tq: Use the public-sector undertaking and parent-ministry association.

55.s:
The Ministry of Coal allots mines under which of the following Acts?
1. Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015
2. Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957
3. Energy Conservation Act, 2001
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: The Ministry of Coal allots mines under the CMSP Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957. The Energy Conservation Act, 2001 is associated with energy efficiency and BEE, not coal-mine allotment.
55.tq: Identify the wrong statutory association by matching each Act with its subject.

55.s: The Department of Atomic Energy is placed directly under the:
55.x: The Department of Atomic Energy, which deals with nuclear power and research, functions directly under the Prime Minister.
55.tq: Apply the authority-identification method to a specialised department.

55.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: BEE — National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under NAPCC
PNGRB — National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under NAPCC
NITI Aayog energy vertical — National Policy on Geothermal Energy
55.x: BEE operates under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 and runs NMEEE under NAPCC. PNGRB is the oil and gas regulator, while the other pairings assign functions to the wrong bodies.
55.tq: Start with the statutory body whose programme linkage is specific and distinctive.

55.s:
The energy vertical of NITI Aayog is associated with which of the following?
1. India Energy Security Scenarios 2047
2. Draft National Energy Policy
3. Methanol Economy
4. IEMI
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: The NITI Aayog energy vertical is associated with IESS 2047, the Draft National Energy Policy, the Methanol Economy and IEMI.
55.tq: Recognise the complete set instead of selecting only the best-known initiative.

55.s: IREDA was established in 1987 under which ministry?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
55.x: The Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency was set up in 1987 under MNRE.
55.tq: Link the specialised finance institution with its parent ministry and establishment year.

55.s: Which of the following best describes the role of IREDA?
o: It publishes the World Energy Outlook.
It regulates petroleum and natural gas pipelines.
It promotes, develops and finances renewable-energy projects and provides technical assistance.
It allocates coal mines under the MMDR Act.
55.x: IREDA is a specialised public-sector financial institution that promotes, develops and finances renewable-energy projects and also provides technical help.
55.tq: Match the institution with its combined financing, development and technical-support functions.

55.s: Which of the following correctly states two recent developments concerning IREDA?
o: It was listed on stock exchanges in November 2023 and received Navratna status in April 2024.
It was listed in April 2024 and received Navratna status in November 2023.
It was established in November 2023 and received Navratna status in 1987.
It received both listing and Navratna status in January 2023.
55.x: IREDA was listed on stock exchanges in November 2023 and received Navratna status in April 2024.
55.tq: Keep the two close developments in their correct time sequence.

55.s: Green bonds are instruments in which:
o: The issuer guarantees a fixed carbon-emission reduction in every project.
The funds are reserved only for foreign exchange reserves.
The proceeds can be used exclusively for coal mining.
The proceeds are ring-fenced for projects with climate or environmental benefits.
55.x: Green bonds raise money for projects with climate or environmental benefits, and their proceeds are ring-fenced for such use.
55.tq: Focus on the defining use-of-proceeds condition.

55.s: Sovereign green bonds for the Government were first issued by the RBI in:
55.x: The RBI first issued sovereign green bonds for the Government in January 2023.
55.tq: Distinguish the first sovereign issuance date from later green-finance developments.

55.s: Which of the following statements about sovereign and municipal green bonds is correct?
o: They have been growing, but the greenium remains modest and access to global climate finance is limited.
They have eliminated the need for all other climate-finance sources.
They are issued only for coal and lignite projects.
They provide unlimited access to global climate finance.
55.x: Sovereign and municipal green bonds are growing, but the greenium is modest and access to global climate finance remains limited.
55.tq: Avoid extreme claims and select the carefully qualified comparison.

55.s: The estimated net-zero financing requirement by 2070 is stated as being:
55.x: The net-zero financing need is estimated at over 20 trillion US dollars by 2070.
55.tq: Recall the scale of the requirement and distinguish it from lower nearby estimates.

55.s: Which of the following set consists entirely of distributed energy resources?
o: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV
Large hydropower dams, coal plants, fuel cells and refineries
Battery storage, oil terminals, nuclear reactors and rooftop solar PV
Coal mines, biomass generators, gas pipelines and fuel cells
55.x: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV all qualify as distributed energy resources.
55.tq: Check every item against the small, consumer-near generation or storage concept.

55.s: Distributed energy resources are best described as:
o: Centralised fuel-import terminals owned by the Union Government
Transmission networks located far from electricity consumers
Small generation or storage units located near the consumer
Only large power stations connected to interstate transmission lines
55.x: DERs are small generation or storage units sited near consumers. They can turn users into prosumers and ease the load on the grid.
55.tq: Use the location-and-scale definition to distinguish distributed from centralised resources.

55.s: A household installs rooftop solar panels and battery storage, produces part of its own electricity and supplies surplus power to the grid. In the context of distributed energy resources, the household is functioning as a:
55.x: A consumer who also produces or stores electricity is a prosumer. DERs can make consumers prosumers and help ease the load on the grid.
55.tq: Apply the concept to a consumer who both produces and consumes electricity.

55.s: Which of the following correctly matches the policy vehicle with its principal focus?
o: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — rooftop solar for one crore households
PM-KUSUM — strategic oil stocks for 90 days of imports
PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — coal-mine allocation
PM-KUSUM — nuclear research under the Prime Minister
55.x: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana focuses on rooftop solar for one crore households. PM-KUSUM concerns solar pumps and decentralised plants.
55.tq: Match each scheme with its target beneficiary and technology.

55.s: PM-KUSUM is associated with:
o: Only urban rooftop solar for one crore households
55.x: PM-KUSUM promotes solar pumps and decentralised plants, whereas PM Surya Ghar focuses on rooftop solar for one crore households.
55.tq: Separate the two solar schemes by their beneficiary and deployment model.

55.s: In Andhra Pradesh, virtual net metering associated with distributed energy policy has a particular focus on:
o: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households
55.x: Andhra Pradesh has introduced virtual net metering with a focus on SC/ST households.
55.tq: Identify the targeted beneficiary group rather than the technology alone.

55.s: The Integrated Energy Policy was prepared by which body and in which year was it issued?
o: Planning Commission expert committee under Kirit Parikh, 2006
55.x: The Integrated Energy Policy was prepared in 2006 by an expert committee of the Planning Commission under Kirit Parikh. It was approved in 2008.
55.tq: Match the document with its drafting body and distinguish the preparation year from the approval year.

55.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 — NITI Aayog — 2014–15
Draft National Energy Policy — Ministry of Power — 2017
Integrated Energy Policy — Ministry of Power — 2008
55.x: India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 was prepared by NITI Aayog in 2014–15. The Draft National Energy Policy was prepared by NITI Aayog in 2017, while the National Electricity Policy 2005 was issued by the Ministry of Power.
55.tq: Use document–year–body association and reject swapped institutional authorities.

55.s:
The Draft National Energy Policy prepared by NITI Aayog has which of the following as its objectives?
1. Access to energy at affordable prices
2. Improved energy security and independence
3. Greater sustainability
4. Economic growth

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: The four objectives are affordable access, improved security and independence, greater sustainability and economic growth.
55.tq: Recognise a complete objectives list; the comprehensive option contains all four stated objectives.

55.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the major areas of intervention identified in the energy policy framework?
o: Exclusive expansion of urban metro rail networks
Oil and gas supply, including domestic exploration and production and overseas acreage
55.x: The listed interventions include energy consumption, demand-side efficiency and decarbonisation, coal, electricity, oil and gas supply, and oil refining and distribution. Exclusive expansion of urban metro rail networks is not listed as an intervention.
55.tq: Find the option outside the stated intervention list rather than selecting a merely related energy activity.

55.s: Fossil fuels account for approximately what share of India’s commercial primary energy supply, and what associated trend is highlighted?
o: Nearly 90%, with increasing dependence on imports
55.x: Fossil fuels constitute nearly 90% of commercial primary energy supply and are increasingly imported. Reducing fossil-fuel use therefore supports both sustainability and energy security.
55.tq: Combine the approximate share with the direction of import dependence; reject extreme percentage claims.

55.s: Primary energy import dependence was projected to change from 31% in 2012 to which range by 2040?
55.x: The projection placed primary energy import dependence at 31% in 2012 and 36–55% by 2040.
55.tq: Test the starting value and projected range together, with nearby percentage distractors.

55.s: The projected target for the manufacturing sector’s share in GDP was to increase from 16% to:
55.x: The projection of that period aimed to raise manufacturing’s share of GDP from 16% to 25% by 2022.
55.tq: Distinguish the target percentage from the target year in a time-bound projection.

55.s: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas target concerning oil imports was to reduce them by what amount from the 2014–15 level by 2022?
55.x: The target was to reduce oil imports by 10% from the 2014–15 level by 2022.
55.tq: Identify the exact percentage and base year rather than confusing it with a broader import-dependence projection.

55.s: Which of the following pairs concerning electricity-sector policy is correctly matched?
o: Electricity Act — 2003; National Electricity Policy — 2005; Tariff Policy — 2006, revised in 2016
Electricity Act — 2005; National Electricity Policy — 2003; Tariff Policy — 2017
Electricity Act — 2006; National Electricity Policy — 2008; Tariff Policy — 2014, revised in 2022
Electricity Act — 2017; National Electricity Policy — 2016; Tariff Policy — 2005, revised in 2006
55.x: The relevant sequence is the Electricity Act 2003, National Electricity Policy 2005 and Tariff Policy 2006, with the Tariff Policy revised in 2016.
55.tq: Arrange and associate closely related legislation and policies by year, including the later revision.

55.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the new and earlier electricity policies?
o: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005.
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2017 replaced the Tariff Policy 2006.
The National Electricity Policy 2005 replaced the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026.
The Tariff Policy 2016 replaced the Electricity Act 2003.
55.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, issued by the Ministry of Power, is intended to replace the National Electricity Policy 2005.
55.tq: Discriminate between a policy, a tariff policy and an Act by testing the direction of replacement.

55.s: The energy-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 are intended to feed into which mechanism?
o: The National Green Hydrogen Mission alone
The State Energy and Climate Index
55.x: Greenhouse-gas emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 feed into the domestic carbon market.
55.tq: Link the statutory target, the number of industrial units and the specific market mechanism.

55.s:
The Panchamrit commitments announced at COP26 in Glasgow include which of the following?
1. 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030
2. Meeting 50% of energy needs from renewable energy by 2030
3. Achieving net zero emissions by 2070

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: The Panchamrit commitments include 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, 50% of energy needs from renewable energy by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2070. They were announced at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
55.tq: Use the complete set of three headline commitments and distinguish energy share from installed-capacity targets.

55.s: As of 30 November 2025, which of the following correctly describes India’s installed power capacity and non-fossil capacity?
o: 509.64 GW total and 246.90 GW non-fossil, constituting 48.45%
470 GW total and 262.74 GW non-fossil, constituting 47%
542 GW total and 283.46 GW non-fossil, constituting 52.27%
509.64 GW total and 262.74 GW non-fossil, constituting 51.55%
55.x: As of 30 November 2025, total installed capacity was 509.64 GW and non-fossil capacity was 262.74 GW, or 51.55%. The 542 GW and 283.46 GW figures relate to 2026.
55.tq: Separate closely spaced status dates and reject figures belonging to a different year.

55.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the 30 November 2025 installed-capacity data?
o: Renewable energy including large hydro — 153.96 GW
55.x: The 30 November 2025 capacity composition included 246.90 GW thermal, 8.78 GW nuclear and 253.96 GW renewable energy including large hydro, making 262.74 GW non-fossil capacity.
55.tq: Start with the sure capacity pair and identify the options that alter a component figure.

55.s: By 2026, India’s installed capacity and non-fossil capacity were reported as approximately:
55.x: By 2026, installed capacity was reported at 542 GW and non-fossil capacity at 283.46 GW, constituting 52.27%. Renewable energy had crossed 200 GW.
55.tq: Keep total capacity, non-fossil capacity and percentage in their proper order.

55.s: The new NDC for 2031–35 proposes which combination of targets?
o: 70% non-fossil capacity and a 35% reduction in emissions intensity by 2030
50% non-fossil capacity and a 45% reduction in emissions intensity by 2030
47% non-fossil capacity and a 60% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035
60% non-fossil capacity and a 47% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035
55.x: The new NDC for 2031–35 proposes 60% non-fossil capacity and a 47% cut in emissions intensity by 2035.
55.tq: Match both the target percentages and the common target year instead of mixing them with the updated 2022 NDC.

55.s: India’s stated goal of achieving energy independence is associated with which year?
55.x: India has set the goal of achieving energy independence by 2047. Net zero emissions is the separate 2070 target.
55.tq: Distinguish the energy-independence year from the net-zero year.

55.s: The Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy of India was submitted to which body at which event?
55.x: India submitted its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy to the UNFCCC at COP27 in 2022.
55.tq: Discriminate between the international body, conference number and year.

55.s: Under the Renewable Purchase Obligation mechanism, which entities are required to purchase a prescribed share of electricity from renewable energy sources?
o: DISCOMs and open-access or captive users
Only generating companies owned by the Union Government
Only households consuming less than 100 kW
55.x: RPO requires DISCOMs and open-access or captive users to purchase a prescribed share of power from renewable energy sources. State Electricity Regulatory Commissions fix the obligation.
55.tq: Identify the obligated entities separately from the authority that sets the obligation.

55.s: Which body is empowered under the Electricity Act, 2003 to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations?
o: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy alone
55.x: The Electricity Act 2003 enables State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.
55.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the regulator from ministries and technical bodies.

55.s: Fiscal incentives for States linked to renewable-energy adoption are intended primarily to:
o: Discourage power-purchase agreements for renewable energy
Promote greater renewable-energy adoption and more power-purchase agreements
Replace all State electricity regulators with a central body
55.x: Linking fiscal incentives to renewable-energy adoption is intended to promote adoption and encourage more power-purchase agreements. The policy was accepted by the Finance and Power ministries.
55.tq: Infer the policy purpose from the incentive design and reject options that reverse its effect.

55.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Integrated Energy Policy:
1. The report was prepared in 2006.
2. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in December 2008.
3. Its core objective was to meet India's energy needs up to 2031-32.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: The report was prepared in 2006, approved in December 2008, and aimed to meet energy needs reliably, sustainably and at least cost up to 2031-32.
55.tq: Use the dates and the policy horizon together to identify the complete combination.

55.s: The core aim of the Integrated Energy Policy was to ensure that energy needs are met:
o: for all, at least cost, reliably and sustainably until 2031-32
through imported fuels at the lowest possible short-term price
55.x: The policy aimed to meet the energy needs of all at least cost, reliably and sustainably up to 2031-32.
55.tq: Select the option that combines the policy's beneficiaries, cost objective, reliability and sustainability.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the Integrated Energy Policy's recommendation on tradable fuels?
o: Market-determined or trade-parity pricing with subsidies targeted to the poor
Free pricing only for imported petroleum products
Administrative pricing of all fuels without competition
Universal price subsidy irrespective of income
55.x: The policy recommended market-determined or trade-parity pricing for tradable fuels and targeted subsidies instead of a general price subsidy.
55.tq: Distinguish targeted subsidy from a general price subsidy.

55.s: Which of the following is NOT a recommendation associated with the Integrated Energy Policy?
o: Exclusive dependence on a single domestic fuel source
55.x: The policy recommended diversification, efficiency, demand-side management, independent regulation and competition; it did not support exclusive dependence on one fuel source.
55.tq: Find the option that reverses the policy's diversification principle.

55.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the supply-diversification approach recommended under the Integrated Energy Policy?
o: Coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables and overseas assets
Petrol, diesel, LPG and imported coal only
55.x: The policy proposed diversification through coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables and overseas assets, along with strategic oil reserves.
55.tq: Start from the distinctive combination of conventional, renewable and overseas sources.

55.s: In addition to diversifying energy supply, the Integrated Energy Policy recommended building:
o: exclusive gas import terminals in every district
55.x: Building strategic oil reserves was one of the policy's recommendations for energy security.
55.tq: Test the specific security measure linked with supply diversification.

55.s: India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 (IESS 2047) is best described as:
o: an open-access energy modelling and scenario tool of NITI Aayog
a closed database of petroleum subsidies
a scheme for rural LPG distribution
a constitutional body regulating electricity tariffs
55.x: IESS 2047 is NITI Aayog's open-access energy modelling and scenario tool used for projections up to 2047.
55.tq: Match the named instrument with its institutional character and function.

55.s: IESS 2047 was launched in:
55.x: The India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 tool was launched in 2014.
55.tq: Use the year-based options and identify the middle-period launch date.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about IESS 2047:
1. It models both energy supply and energy demand.
2. Its modelling horizon extends to 2047.
3. Business-As-Usual and Ambitious are among its scenarios.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: IESS 2047 models supply and demand up to 2047 and includes scenarios such as Business-As-Usual and Ambitious.
55.tq: Combine the tool's scope, time horizon and named scenarios.

55.s: According to the domestic coal production projections, which of the following is correctly matched?
55.x: Domestic coal production was listed as 582 Mtce for 2012; the 2040 BAU and Ambitious projections were 1190 and 1385 Mtce respectively.
55.tq: Anchor the table by matching the historical base year before comparing projections.

55.s:
Arrange the following domestic coal production figures in ascending order:
A. 2012 level
B. 2040 Ambitious projection
C. 2040 BAU projection
55.x: The figures are 582 Mtce in 2012, 1190 Mtce under 2040 BAU and 1385 Mtce under 2040 Ambitious; hence A, C, B.
55.tq: Arrange numerical values by magnitude rather than by date alone.

55.s: The newer NITI Aayog scenario study titled Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero recommends approximately what nuclear capacity by 2047?
55.x: The study recommends approximately 100 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047.
55.tq: Separate the 2047 target from the higher 2070 range.

55.s:
Which of the following measures is associated with NITI Aayog's newer scenario study on Viksit Bharat and Net Zero?
1. Nuclear capacity of about 200-300 GW by 2070
2. Promotion of small modular reactors
3. Private participation in the nuclear sector
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: The study recommends about 200-300 GW of nuclear capacity by 2070, small modular reactors and private participation.
55.tq: Use the complete policy package rather than selecting only the numerical target.

55.s: Which programme was launched in 2014 with the objective of rural feeder separation and village electrification?
55.x: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) was launched in 2014 for rural feeder separation and village electrification.
55.tq: Link the launch year with the programme's distinctive rural electricity objectives.

55.s: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016 at:
55.x: PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016 at Ballia in Uttar Pradesh.
55.tq: Test the place-year pair, a common location trap in scheme questions.

55.s: PM Ujjwala Yojana primarily aimed to provide:
o: electricity connections to all urban households
LPG connections to women from BPL households
55.x: PMUY aimed to provide LPG connections to women belonging to below-poverty-line households.
55.tq: Discriminate the clean-cooking objective of PMUY from the electricity objectives of other programmes.

55.s: Saubhagya, formally known as the PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, was launched in:
55.x: Saubhagya was launched in 2017 to promote last-mile household electrification.
55.tq: Distinguish the launch year of Saubhagya from the earlier DDUGJY and PMUY dates.

55.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. DDUGJY
b. PM Ujjwala Yojana
c. Saubhagya

List-II (Primary aim)
i. Last-mile household electrification
ii. LPG connections to BPL women
iii. Rural feeder separation and village electrification

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: DDUGJY is associated with feeder separation and village electrification, PMUY with LPG connections to BPL women, and Saubhagya with household electrification.
55.tq: Start from the sure pair PMUY–LPG and complete the programme-purpose mapping.

55.s: Before the expansion of electricity and clean cooking access, approximately how many people in India were without electricity and how many relied on solid biomass for cooking?
55.x: The earlier baseline was approximately 304 million people without electricity and 500 million relying on solid biomass for cooking.
55.tq: Avoid reversing the two baseline figures by matching each number with its sector.

55.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported present energy-access position?
o: Household electrification is near-universal and clean cooking access has expanded.
Solid biomass use has become universal despite LPG expansion.
Household electrification remains limited to urban areas only.
Rural electricity supply is lower than 10 hours per day on average.
55.x: The reported position is near-universal household electrification along with expanded access to clean cooking.
55.tq: Select the carefully worded broad outcome instead of an extreme or reversed claim.

55.s: The reported average electricity supply was approximately:
o: 23.4 hours in rural areas and 22.6 hours in urban areas
22.6 hours in rural areas and 23.4 hours in urban areas
20.6 hours in rural areas and 21.4 hours in urban areas
24 hours in rural areas and 23.4 hours in urban areas
55.x: Average supply was reported at 22.6 hours in rural areas and 23.4 hours in urban areas.
55.tq: Check the rural-urban order carefully; the values are close and easily reversed.

55.s: India's reported peak electricity shortage was approximately:
55.x: The reported peak shortage was only 0.03 percent.
55.tq: Distinguish the decimal percentage from its tenfold and hundredfold distractors.

55.s: Petrol prices in India were deregulated in June 2010, whereas diesel prices were deregulated in:
55.x: Petrol prices were deregulated in June 2010 and diesel prices in October 2014.
55.tq: Discriminate the two closely related deregulation dates rather than pairing both with 2010.

55.s: The LPG subsidy mechanism introduced through PAHAL in 2015 primarily used:
o: free LPG distribution through local bodies
universal price control at the refinery gate
55.x: PAHAL implemented LPG subsidy transfer through the Direct Benefit Transfer mechanism.
55.tq: Match the named reform with its delivery mechanism.

55.s: Which of the following statements about fuel pricing reforms is correct?
o: Excise duty was reduced only on LPG and never on petrol or diesel.
Petrol and diesel prices continue to be fixed exclusively by the Planning Commission.
Fuel subsidies were completely abolished in every circumstance.
The Government has, at times of price spikes, reduced excise duty on petrol and diesel.
55.x: The Government has reduced excise duty on petrol and diesel on occasions when prices spiked; this does not mean that all subsidies were abolished.
55.tq: Reject the absolute claim and identify the carefully qualified fiscal response.

55.s: The pricing logic of the Integrated Energy Policy combines:
o: general price subsidy with exclusive administrative pricing
import prohibition with fixed domestic prices
free fuel distribution with universal cash transfers
55.x: The policy favours trade-parity pricing for tradable fuels while targeting subsidies towards the poor.
55.tq: Test the policy pair by contrasting targeted support with universal subsidy.

55.s:
Under the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, which combination of measures is associated with the stated current-policy direction?
1. 100 GW of pumped storage hydropower by 2047
2. Time-of-Day tariffs
3. A target of 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 includes 100 GW of pumped storage hydropower by 2047 and Time-of-Day tariffs. The 100 GW nuclear target by 2047 belongs to the newer NITI Aayog scenario study, not the stated policy combination here.
55.tq: Separate similarly dated policy proposals and avoid transferring a target from one document to another.

55.s: The Entropy Effect, as discussed in energy-sector debates, refers to the risk that:
o: nuclear expansion automatically eliminates all import dependence
rapid decarbonisation without adequate buffers may increase grid volatility
slow electrification always reduces grid volatility
fuel subsidies cause a permanent fall in renewable generation
55.x: The Entropy Effect describes the possibility that rapid decarbonisation without sufficient buffers can raise grid volatility, as observed in the Netherlands and Spain.
55.tq: Apply the definition to the cause-effect relationship rather than selecting a general decarbonisation statement.

55.s: Which country pair was cited in connection with the grid-volatility concerns associated with the Entropy Effect?
55.x: The Netherlands and Spain were cited as examples in the discussion of grid volatility during rapid decarbonisation without adequate buffers.
55.tq: Recall the specific examples used to illustrate the policy criticism.

55.s: SAEL's 600 MW solar project in Kadapa was described as the first project commissioned under:
55.x: The 600 MW SAEL solar project in Kadapa was the first project commissioned under the Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024.
55.tq: Match the project with the policy framework under which it was commissioned.

55.s: The SAEL solar project in Kadapa was built in approximately:
55.x: The project was reported to have been built in 11 months.
55.tq: Identify the precise project-completion period among nearby numerical distractors.

55.s: Under the NITI-blueprint ASSET programme, Andhra Pradesh aims to reduce its power purchase cost to:
55.x: The ASSET programme sets targets of ₹4.20 per unit by 2030 and ₹3.90 per unit by 2035.
55.tq: Track both the values and their respective target years without reversing the sequence.

55.s: Which of the following correctly states the import dependence figures highlighted in the energy debate?
55.x: The figures highlighted were approximately 88 percent import reliance for crude and 51 percent for gas.
55.tq: Avoid reversing the two fuel categories while retaining their approximate shares.

55.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly associated with the energy-sector challenges highlighted in recent debates?
o: 25 GW of stranded gas capacity and net-zero investment needs exceeding $20 trillion
88 GW of stranded gas capacity and no major investment requirement
51 GW of stranded gas capacity and investment needs of $5 trillion
25 GW of stranded nuclear capacity and investment needs below $2 trillion
55.x: The highlighted challenges include approximately 25 GW of stranded gas capacity and net-zero investment requirements exceeding $20 trillion.
55.tq: Match the two challenge figures and reject exaggerated or reversed values.

55.s: The Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 sets the State's net-zero target for:
55.x: The Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 targets net zero by 2047.
55.tq: Distinguish the State target of 2047 from the national net-zero target of 2070.

55.s: The first project under the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 was the 600 MW SAEL solar project located in:
55.x: The first project was the 600 MW SAEL solar project in Rayalaseema, commissioned on 22 May 2026.
55.tq: Use the project-location association and distinguish the regional name from the district-level reference to Kadapa.

55.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The SAEL solar project under the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 had a capacity of 600 MW.
2. It was commissioned on 22 May 2026.
3. It was the first project under that policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: The project had a 600 MW capacity, was commissioned on 22 May 2026, and was identified as the first project under the policy.
55.tq: Combine capacity, date and status to verify the complete project description.

55.s: Under the Updated Nationally Determined Contribution of August 2022, India committed to reducing the emissions intensity of GDP by what percentage by 2030 from the 2005 level?
55.x: The Updated NDC set a target of reducing GDP emissions intensity by 45% by 2030 from the 2005 level.
55.tq: Distinguish the emissions-intensity target from the non-fossil-capacity target.

55.s: India’s share of non-fossil installed capacity was reported as 51.93% in December 2025 and more than ____ in August 2026.
55.x: The share was 51.93% in December 2025 and exceeded 54% in August 2026.
55.tq: Read the time-linked progression and distinguish an exact percentage from a greater-than figure.

55.s: Which of the following is NOT a Panchamrit commitment announced in the context of COP26?
o: 45% reduction in GDP emissions intensity by 2030 from the 2005 level
50% of energy needs from renewables by 2030
55.x: The 45% emissions-intensity reduction is an Updated NDC target. Panchamrit includes 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, 50% energy from renewables by 2030 and Net Zero by 2070.
55.tq: Separate the Panchamrit commitments from the later Updated NDC targets.

55.s: The Ministry of Power became an independent ministry with effect from:
55.x: The Ministry of Power became independent from 2 July 1992.
55.tq: Use the exact date and reject nearby decade-based distractors.

55.s: India has set a target of achieving non-fossil fuel capacity of how much by 2030?
55.x: India's target is 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
55.tq: Test the headline national energy target directly.

55.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India reached a 50 per cent non-fossil share about five years ahead of schedule.
2. Coal's share fell for the first time in 50 years.
3. India's non-fossil capacity target for 2030 is 500 GW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All three statements are correct. India reached the 50 per cent non-fossil share early, coal's share declined for the first time in five decades, and the 2030 target is 500 GW.
55.tq: Combine milestone, trend and target statements in a coded option.

55.s: Fossil fuels constitute nearly what proportion of India’s commercial primary energy supply?
55.x: Fossil fuels account for nearly 90% of India’s commercial primary energy supply.
55.tq: Distinguish the commercial primary-energy share from the separate coal shares.

55.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's energy-transition challenges:
1. Achieving net-zero may require more than 20 trillion dollars.
2. Approximately 25 GW of gas capacity is stranded.
3. These issues illustrate both the financial and asset-utilisation challenges of the transition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All three statements are correct. The transition involves very large investment requirements and the problem of stranded gas-generation capacity.
55.tq: Link the numerical facts with their broader policy implication.

55.s: The INSA policy brief proposed a Unified National Energy Policy Framework aimed at achieving:
o: energy self-reliance by 2047 and net zero by 2070
energy self-reliance by 2030 and net zero by 2047
energy self-reliance by 2070 and net zero by 2047
energy self-reliance by 2026 and net zero by 2050
55.x: The proposed framework seeks energy self-reliance by 2047 and net zero by 2070.
55.tq: Keep the two target years aligned with their respective objectives.

55.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to India's institutional framework for non-conventional energy in chronological order:
A. MNRE was renamed from MNES
B. Commission for Additional Sources of Energy was set up
C. Department of Non-Conventional Energy Sources was created
D. A separate Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources was established
55.x: CASE was established in 1981, DNES in 1982, MNES in 1992 and the Ministry was renamed MNRE in 2006.
55.tq: Use the first and last milestones, then place the intermediate years.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about institutions associated with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy:
1. NISE is located in Gurugram and serves as a technical focal point for solar research and development.
2. NIWE is located in Chennai and is associated with wind research and the wind roadmap.
3. NIBE is located in Kapurthala and is concerned with bio-energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: All three statements are correct: NISE-Gurugram concerns solar R&D, NIWE-Chennai concerns wind R&D and NIBE-Kapurthala concerns bio-energy.
55.tq: Check each institution against its location and specialised field.

56.s: The National Clean Energy Fund was primarily established to fund:
o: Oil and gas exploration by private companies
Research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies
56.x: The NCEF was intended to fund research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies, promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions.
56.tq: Match the fund with its stated purpose rather than its revenue source.

56.s: The principal source of the National Clean Energy Fund was:
o: A clean energy cess on coal, lignite and peat
A cess on electricity consumption alone
56.x: The NCEF was financed through a clean energy cess imposed on coal, including lignite and peat, from 2010-11.
56.tq: Distinguish the fund's dedicated cess from other energy-related levies.

56.s: The clean energy cess that supported the National Clean Energy Fund was initially levied at ₹50 per tonne and was later raised to:
56.x: The clean energy cess started at ₹50 per tonne and was subsequently raised to ₹400 per tonne.
56.tq: Track the original and revised values rather than confusing the two rates.

56.s: What was the effect of the introduction of GST on the National Clean Energy Fund?
o: The cess was shifted from coal to petroleum products.
The clean energy cess was doubled and the NCEF received a dedicated inflow.
The NCEF was converted into a sovereign green bond account.
The clean energy cess was replaced by GST compensation cess, causing the NCEF to lose its dedicated inflow.
56.x: When GST was introduced in 2017, the clean energy cess was replaced by the GST compensation cess. Consequently, the NCEF lost its dedicated inflow.
56.tq: Link the policy change to its direct fiscal consequence.

56.s: The Commission for Additional Sources of Energy (CASE) was set up in:
56.x: CASE was set up in 1981 as an early institutional milestone in India's non-conventional energy framework.
56.tq: Direct year recall using closely spaced institutional milestones as distractors.

56.s: The Department of Non-Conventional Energy Sources (DNES) was created in 1982 in the:
56.x: DNES was created in 1982 within the Ministry of Energy.
56.tq: Identify the correct parent Ministry rather than only the year.

56.s: In which year was the Department of Non-Conventional Energy Sources upgraded to a separate Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources?
56.x: The Department was upgraded to a separate Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources in 1992.
56.tq: Distinguish the creation of a department from its later elevation to a Ministry.

56.s: India became the first country in the world to establish a Ministry specifically for:
56.x: India was the first country in the world to set up a ministry for non-conventional energy sources.
56.tq: Direct recall of a distinctive international first.

56.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
56.x: NIBE is an autonomous institution located at Kapurthala in Punjab and is associated with bio-energy. NISE, NIWE and SECI have different roles.
56.tq: Start from the institution-field-location pair that is uniquely correct.

56.s: Which institution functions as a PSU and implementing arm for the National Solar Mission and wind projects?
56.x: The Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) is a PSU and serves as the implementing arm for the National Solar Mission and wind projects.
56.tq: Distinguish an implementing agency from research and financing institutions.

56.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding IREDA?
o: It is an academic department under IIT Roorkee.
It is an autonomous solar research institution in Gurugram.
It is the nodal agency for the wind roadmap.
It is a PSU and NBFC providing term loans for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency projects.
56.x: IREDA is a PSU and non-banking financial company that provides term loans for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency projects.
56.tq: Match the institution with its organisational type and core function.

56.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. DHRE, IIT Roorkee provides technical support for small hydro.
2. DHRE is under the administrative control of MNRE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: DHRE, IIT Roorkee provides technical support for small hydro, but it is not under MNRE's control.
56.tq: Test the distinction between technical association and administrative control.

56.s: Who publishes the Renewable Energy Country Attractiveness Index (RECAI)?
56.x: The Renewable Energy Country Attractiveness Index is published by EY, formerly Ernst & Young.
56.tq: Publisher-identification question using closely related energy organisations as distractors.

56.s: The report ‘Renewables Integration in India’ released in 2021 was prepared by:
56.x: The 2021 report on Renewables Integration in India was issued by the International Energy Agency with NITI Aayog.
56.tq: Identify both members of a joint publishing partnership.

56.s: Which of the following reports is published by the International Energy Agency?
56.x: The World Energy Outlook and India Energy Outlook are published by the IEA. Renewable Capacity Statistics is published by IRENA, RECAI by EY and Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025 by IRENA.
56.tq: Use publisher-report matching to separate similar international energy publications.

56.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Report or index)
a. Renewable Capacity Statistics
a. Renewable Energy Country Attractiveness Index
c. Renewables Integration in India (2021)
d. Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025

List-II (Publisher)
i. EY
ii. IRENA
iii. IEA with NITI Aayog
iv. IRENA

Select the correct answer using the code below.
56.x: Renewable Capacity Statistics and Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025 are IRENA publications; RECAI is published by EY and Renewables Integration in India by IEA with NITI Aayog.
56.tq: Start with the sure publisher pair and eliminate codes that repeat the wrong association.

56.s: According to the July 2026 finding cited for ‘Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025’, more than what proportion of new utility-scale renewable-energy capacity was cheaper than the cheapest fossil-fuel option?
56.x: IRENA reported that more than 90% of new utility-scale renewable-energy capacity was cheaper than the cheapest fossil-fuel alternative.
56.tq: Distinguish a high but non-total proportion from the absolute option.

56.s: The renewable-energy cost reductions reported for 2025 were stated to have avoided approximately what fossil-fuel cost?
56.x: The reported renewable-energy cost advantage was associated with an avoided fossil-fuel cost of approximately 480 billion US dollars.
56.tq: Read the scale of the reported figure carefully rather than confusing millions and billions.

56.s: Which one of the following sets correctly represents India's positions in the cited renewable-energy indicators?
o: Second in total renewable capacity, fourth in wind, and third-largest solar-growth market in 2025
Fourth in total renewable capacity, third in wind, and largest solar-growth market in 2025
Third in total renewable capacity, fourth in wind, and second-largest solar-growth market in 2025
Third in total renewable capacity, second in wind, and fourth-largest solar-growth market in 2025
56.x: The cited findings place India third in total renewable-energy capacity, fourth in wind and as the second-largest solar-growth market in 2025.
56.tq: Keep the three rank indicators together and reject reversed comparisons.

56.s: India overtook which country to become the third-largest solar power producer?
56.x: India overtook Japan and became the third-largest solar power producer according to the cited August 2026 finding.
56.tq: Direct recall of the country involved in a rank change.

56.s: The National Clean Energy Fund was created in 2010–11 primarily from a cess imposed on:
56.x: The NCEF was created in 2010–11 from a clean-energy cess on domestic and imported coal.
56.tq: Identify the correct revenue source rather than the fund's purpose.

56.s: The initial clean-energy cess associated with the National Clean Energy Fund was:
56.x: The initial cess was ₹50 per tonne on both domestic and imported coal.
56.tq: Test the exact levy amount with adjacent numerical distractors.

56.s: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the National Clean Energy Fund?
o: To regulate electricity tariffs in States
To provide free electricity to all households
To finance research and innovative projects in clean-energy technologies
56.x: The NCEF was intended to fund research and innovative projects in clean-energy technologies, promote renewable technologies and reduce carbon emissions.
56.tq: Match the fund with its functional purpose, not a general energy-sector activity.

56.s: Which development ended the dedicated inflow to the National Clean Energy Fund?
o: The conversion of MNRE into MNES
The subsuming of the coal cess into the GST Compensation Cess in July 2017
The replacement of coal by natural gas
56.x: The coal cess was subsumed into the GST Compensation Cess in July 2017, thereby ending the NCEF's dedicated inflow.
56.tq: Link the fund's status to the specific fiscal change and date.

56.s: IREDA was established in:
56.x: The Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency was established in 1987.
56.tq: Distinguish the financing agency's establishment year from MNRE's institutional milestones.

56.s: Which of the following is NOT a financing activity associated with IREDA?
o: Issuing wind-roadmap guidelines as its principal statutory function
56.x: IREDA provides term, bridge and working-capital loans for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency projects. The wind roadmap is associated with NIWE, not IREDA's principal financing role.
56.tq: Find the activity belonging to a neighbouring institution rather than the financing agency.

56.s:
IREDA obtains funds from which of the following sources?
1. Government sources
2. Multilateral institutions
3. Capital markets, including green bonds
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: IREDA's funding sources include the Government, multilateral institutions and capital markets, including green bonds.
56.tq: Test a complete list through the coded-options format.

56.s: The 8th Mission Innovation ministerial meeting held with the 14th Clean Energy Ministerial in July 2023 was hosted at:
56.x: The combined MI-8 and 14th Clean Energy Ministerial event was held in Goa in July 2023.
56.tq: Match the energy event with its host city.

56.s: Which one of the following correctly matches an event with its host city?
56.x: The fourth edition of RE-INVEST in September 2024 was hosted at Gandhinagar. India Energy Week was held in Bengaluru in 2023, Goa in 2024 and New Delhi in 2025.
56.tq: Use event-year matching before checking the city.

56.s:
Which of the following initiatives was launched in connection with the 8th ISA Assembly?
1. OSOWOG roadmap was operationalised.
2. ISA Global Capability Centre was launched.
3. ISA Academy and SUNRISE were launched.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: The 8th ISA Assembly operationalised the OSOWOG roadmap and launched the ISA Global Capability Centre, ISA Academy and SUNRISE.
56.tq: Recognise the complete cluster of initiatives associated with one event.

56.s: A two-year biodiesel project by the Belgian firm VITO, initiated in April 2023, was associated with:
56.x: The two-year biodiesel project by VITO was associated with Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh.
56.tq: Match a clean-energy first with its location while separating similar firsts.

56.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First 24x7 solar-powered village — Cochin International Airport
56.x: Diu was the first 100% solar-powered Union Territory during daytime. Modhera was the first 24x7 solar-powered village, Cochin International Airport the first fully solar-powered airport, and Aditya the first solar ferry.
56.tq: Start with the distinctive Union Territory-location pair and eliminate crossed firsts.

56.s: Modhera, known for a clean-energy first in India, is located in:
56.x: Modhera in Gujarat became India's first 24x7 solar-powered village in 2022.
56.tq: Combine the achievement with its State location.

56.s: The solar ferry ‘Aditya’, introduced in 2017, operates on the:
56.x: The first solar ferry, Aditya, was introduced in 2017 on the Vaikom–Thavanakkadavu route in Kerala.
56.tq: Test the precise route associated with a named clean-energy first.

56.s: The target capacity under Phase-II of the Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme, subsequently subsumed in PM Surya Ghar, is:
56.x: Phase-II of the Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme had a target of 40,000 MW and was subsumed in PM Surya Ghar.
56.tq: Recall the exact programme target and distinguish it from broader solar-capacity figures.

56.s: According to the cited IRENA finding for 2025, approximately what share of new utility-scale solar capacity was paired with batteries?
56.x: The cited IRENA finding states that 25% of new utility-scale solar capacity was paired with batteries.
56.tq: Test the specific storage proportion rather than total renewable capacity.

56.s: PM Surya Sarovar projects are required to add battery energy storage systems (BESS) having a minimum duration of:
56.x: PM Surya Sarovar projects must add BESS with a minimum storage duration of two hours.
56.tq: Identify the minimum technical specification from close duration options.

56.s: Which statement correctly compares green-hydrogen fuel cells and combustion engines?
o: Fuel cells convert electricity exclusively into biomass.
Fuel cells can operate only with coal-derived hydrogen.
Green-hydrogen fuel cells are generally more efficient than combustion engines.
Combustion engines are always more efficient than fuel cells.
56.x: Green-hydrogen fuel cells are more efficient than combustion engines in the comparison stated.
56.tq: Use the direct efficiency comparison and reject absolute reversals.

56.s: Which programme is associated with family biogas plants?
o: National Biogas and Manure Management Programme
Biomass Power and Bagasse Co-generation Programme
56.x: The National Biogas and Manure Management Programme is associated with family biogas plants.
56.tq: Match the programme with its specific distributed-energy application.

56.s: The Biomass Power and Bagasse Co-generation Programme is concerned with:
56.x: The programme supports biomass power and co-generation using bagasse.
56.tq: Identify the technology named in the programme title and purpose.

56.s: The approximate bio-power capacity cited for India is:
56.x: The cited bio-power capacity is approximately 11.75 GW.
56.tq: Recall the exact capacity figure and its unit scale.

56.s: The New Solar Power Scheme under PM JANMAN and DA JGUA had electrified how many households in 2025?
56.x: The off-grid tribal solar initiative electrified 4,919 households in 2025.
56.tq: Distinguish the exact household count from digit-shifted options.

56.s: The International Solar Alliance was established as a joint initiative of:
56.x: The International Solar Alliance was jointly initiated by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015.
56.tq: Use the founding-country pair to distinguish similar international initiatives.

56.s: The principal purpose of the International Solar Alliance is to function as a platform for:
56.x: The International Solar Alliance serves as a platform to promote and facilitate solar deployment.
56.tq: Identify the initiative from its functional objective rather than its founding event.

56.s: One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG) refers to:
o: A national coal transmission grid under the Ministry of Coal
A transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance
A biofuel blending programme under the Global Biofuels Alliance
A global wind-purchasing platform operated by IREDA
56.x: OSOWOG is a transnational solar grid concept under the International Solar Alliance. Its roadmap was operationalised at the 8th ISA Assembly in 2026.
56.tq: Distinguish the grid concept from other renewable-energy programmes by its transnational scope.

56.s: The Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG was launched by India and the United Kingdom at:
o: The G20 Summit, New Delhi, in 2023
The UN Climate Action Summit, in 2019
56.x: The Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG was launched by India and the United Kingdom at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
56.tq: Use the event-location-year combination to separate related climate initiatives.

56.s: As reported on 15 August 2026, India’s approximate installed power capacity and non-fossil share were respectively:
56.x: The reported figures were approximately 552 GW of installed capacity and more than 54% from non-fossil sources.
56.tq: Keep the latest aggregate figures distinct from earlier and target figures.

56.s: Which of the following correctly represents India’s reported renewable capacity figures as of 15 August 2026?
56.x: The reported installed capacities were 164.59 GW of solar and 58.14 GW of wind.
56.tq: Avoid reversing paired sectoral figures in a comparison question.

56.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India’s target is to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
2. The COP26 Panchamrit goal of 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030 was reported as having been achieved five years early.
3. The non-fossil share was reported as 51.93% by December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: India has a 500 GW non-fossil capacity target for 2030; the 50% Panchamrit capacity goal was reported as achieved five years early, and the share was 51.93% by December 2025.
56.tq: Separate a long-term capacity target from an already-reported milestone and percentage.

56.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported wind-energy targets?
56.x: The reported wind-energy targets are 100 GW by 2030 and 155 GW by 2035.
56.tq: Check the order of milestones before selecting the numerical pair.

56.s: India’s solar module manufacturing capacity was reported as approximately how much in March 2026?
56.x: Solar module manufacturing capacity was reported as approximately 172 GW in March 2026.
56.tq: Distinguish manufacturing capacity from installed generation capacity.

56.s:
Consider the following statements regarding renewable-energy initiatives in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Tata Renewable has a planned 800 MW hybrid project involving an investment of ₹5,750 crore.
2. A solar Centre of Excellence is associated with IIT Tirupati and the University of New South Wales.
3. The reported hybrid project is a 5,000 MW floating solar project implemented by SECI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: The Andhra Pradesh-related initiatives include Tata Renewable’s 800 MW hybrid project costing ₹5,750 crore and a solar Centre of Excellence with IIT Tirupati and UNSW. Statement 3 describes the PM Surya Sarovar target, not the Tata Renewable project.
56.tq: Separate the State-specific project from a similarly worded national scheme.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance:
1. It had 125 member and signatory countries as reported in March 2026.
2. The 8th ISA Assembly drew 137 nations.
3. The number of nations attending the 8th Assembly was lower than the number of member and signatory countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: The ISA had 125 member and signatory countries, while the 8th Assembly drew 137 nations. Therefore, statement 3 is false because 137 is higher than 125.
56.tq: Compare two close numerical figures and reject the reversed comparison.

56.s: India achieved its 50% non-fossil capacity goal:
56.x: India achieved the 50% non-fossil capacity goal five years ahead of schedule.
56.tq: Recall the time advantage attached to a policy milestone.

57.s: Raniganj coalfield is located in which State and associated with which river valley?
57.x: Raniganj coalfield is located in West Bengal and lies in the Damodar Valley. The first coal mine in India was opened at Raniganj in 1774.
57.tq: Start from the sure location–river pair.

57.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
57.x: Jharia is in Jharkhand and forms part of the Damodar Valley. Korba is in Chhattisgarh, Talcher in Odisha and Singareni in Telangana.
57.tq: Use the state–valley combination to eliminate swapped locations.

57.s: Jharia coalfield is particularly noted for which of the following?
o: Lignite deposits in the Satpura Basin
The first commercial coal mine in India
57.x: Jharia in Jharkhand is the largest coking-coal field and is situated in the Damodar Valley.
57.tq: Directly distinguish the coalfield by its special characteristic.

57.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Karanpura — Jharkhand — Damodar Valley
b. Korba — Chhattisgarh — Hasdeo
c. Umaria — Madhya Pradesh — Son
d. Singareni — Telangana — Godavari
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
57.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Karanpura is in the Damodar Valley, Korba in the Hasdeo basin, Umaria in the Son Valley and Singareni in the Godavari Valley.
57.tq: Check each pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

57.s: Which one of the following coalfields is correctly matched with its State and distinctive feature?
57.x: Mawlong is located in Meghalaya and is associated with Tertiary coal. Satpura and Umaria are in Madhya Pradesh, while Talcher is in Odisha.
57.tq: Use the distinctive geological term as the anchor pair.

57.s: The Satpura coalfield, including the Pench-Kanhan and Pathakhera fields, is located in which State?
57.x: The Satpura coalfield, including Pench-Kanhan and Pathakhera, is located in Madhya Pradesh and belongs to the Satpura Basin.
57.tq: Direct state identification from a grouped coalfield name.

57.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Gondwana coal-bearing valleys listed for India?
57.x: The listed Gondwana coal-bearing valleys are Damodar, Son, Mahanadi, Godavari and Wardha. Narmada is not included in this list.
57.tq: Find the odd geographical member in a named group.

57.s: In coal gasification, coal is converted into syngas by partial oxidation with which of the following at high temperature and pressure?
57.x: Coal is partly oxidised with oxygen and steam at high temperature and pressure to produce syngas.
57.tq: Identify the process inputs rather than the products.

57.s: Which one of the following is NOT a constituent of the syngas produced through coal gasification?
57.x: Syngas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide. Ammonia is a product that can be manufactured using syngas, not a stated constituent of syngas.
57.tq: Separate the composition of syngas from products made using syngas.

57.s:
Which of the following products can be manufactured using coal gasification?
1. Synthetic natural gas
2. Methanol
3. Ammonia for fertilisers
4. Dimethyl ether
Select the correct answer using the code below.
57.x: Coal gasification can produce synthetic natural gas, methanol, ammonia for fertilisers, hydrogen, dimethyl ether, ammonium nitrate and petrochemicals.
57.tq: Use the complete product list to identify the all-inclusive combination.

57.s: Syngas produced through coal gasification can also be used to operate which of the following power-generation systems?
o: Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle power plants
57.x: Syngas can be used to run Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC) power plants.
57.tq: Match the specialised fuel product with its stated power-generation application.

57.s:
Consider the following substances:
1. Ethanol
2. Nitroglycerine
3. Urea
Which of the substances listed above can be produced through coal gasification?
57.x: Ethanol and urea can be produced through coal gasification. Nitroglycerine is not included among the stated products.
57.tq: Discriminate between direct gasification products and an unrelated chemical.

57.s: The National Coal Gasification Mission aims to gasify how much coal by 2030?
57.x: The National Coal Gasification Mission has a target of gasifying 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
57.tq: Recall the mission target and distinguish it from the sub-target under the incentive scheme.

57.s: What was the outlay approved for the Coal Gasification Incentive Scheme introduced in 2024?
57.x: The Coal Gasification Incentive Scheme of 2024 has an outlay of ₹8,500 crore for public and private projects.
57.tq: Distinguish the outlay of the 2024 scheme from the later surface coal and lignite scheme.

57.s:
With reference to the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved by the Cabinet on 13 May 2026.
2. Its outlay is ₹37,500 crore.
3. The incentive may be up to 20% of plant and machinery cost.
4. The incentive is capped at ₹5,000 crore per project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All four statements correctly describe the scheme approved on 13 May 2026, including its outlay, incentive rate and project-wise ceiling.
57.tq: Check the date, outlay, percentage and cap as separate components of one scheme.

57.s: The Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification is intended to contribute approximately how much coal gasification capacity towards the 100-million-tonne mission target?
57.x: The scheme targets about 75 million tonnes of coal gasification capacity towards the 100-million-tonne mission goal.
57.tq: Distinguish the scheme contribution from the overall mission target.

57.s: Under the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, the coal linkage tenure was extended to:
57.x: The coal linkage tenure under the scheme was extended to 30 years.
57.tq: Recall the exact duration of the policy provision.

57.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the status of the ₹37,500-crore coal gasification scheme?
o: Bidding was permanently closed after one unsuccessful round.
All eligible projects had already received the incentive.
The scheme was withdrawn because the mission target had been achieved.
No bidders had turned up, and bid windows were planned every two months.
57.x: No bidders had turned up for the scheme, and bid windows were planned at intervals of two months.
57.tq: Use the current-status detail rather than confusing it with scheme approval or implementation.

57.s: The import bill for substitutable products such as LNG, urea, ammonia, coking coal, methanol and DME was approximately what amount in FY2025?
57.x: The import bill for these substitutable products was about ₹2.77 lakh crore in FY2025.
57.tq: Read the unit carefully and distinguish lakh crore from crore figures.

57.s: Which of the following is the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant identified in the sector?
o: The Talcher fertiliser plant in Odisha
MCL's IB Valley Washery in Odisha
57.x: JSPL's plant at Angul, Odisha, is identified as the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant.
57.tq: Match the project with its distinctive status and location.

57.s: The first gasification-based fertiliser plant at Talcher is due to be completed by:
57.x: The first gasification-based fertiliser plant at Talcher is due by December 2027.
57.tq: Recall the project timeline without confusing it with the mission target year.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about BCGCL:
1. It is a joint venture of BHEL and CIL.
2. It was formed on 21 May 2024.
3. It is building a commercial coal-to-ammonium-nitrate plant at Lakhanpur in Jharsuguda district.
4. The plant is located in Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: BCGCL is a BHEL-CIL joint venture formed on 21 May 2024, and it is constructing the plant at Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda, Odisha.
57.tq: Verify the organisation, formation date, project and location independently.

57.s: The Lakhanpur coal-to-ammonium-nitrate plant being built by BCGCL is designed for which of the following capacities?
o: 2,500 TPD of coal input and 2,000 TPD of ammonium nitrate output
2,000 TPD of coal input and 2,500 TPD of ammonium nitrate output
2,000 TPD each of coal input and ammonium nitrate output
2,500 TPD each of coal input and ammonium nitrate output
57.x: The plant is designed to use 2,500 tonnes per day of coal and produce 2,000 tonnes per day of ammonium nitrate.
57.tq: Avoid reversing input and output figures in a capacity question.

57.s: Commercial coal blocks receive a 50% rebate on revenue share when at least what proportion of their output is used for gasification?
57.x: A 50% rebate on revenue share is available when at least 10% of the commercial block's output is used for gasification.
57.tq: Separate the rebate percentage from the qualifying output percentage.

57.s: Which of the following correctly describes Indian coal?
o: High ash, high calorific value, low ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
High ash, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur
Low ash, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
Low ash, high calorific value, low ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
57.x: Indian coal generally has high ash content, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur content.
57.tq: Track all four quality characteristics without reversing paired properties.

57.s: The ash content of Indian coal is generally in which range?
57.x: Indian coal is characterised by a high ash content of approximately 35–45%.
57.tq: Recall the stated range and reject lower, more typical-quality coal figures.

57.s: The sulphur content of Indian coal is approximately:
57.x: Indian coal generally has low sulphur content of about 0.5%.
57.tq: Use the decimal carefully; the major trap is a tenfold change in magnitude.

57.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a problem affecting the Indian coal sector?
o: Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal
57.x: The identified problems include poor quality, movement bottlenecks, low washery use, rising coking-coal imports and administrative issues. Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal is not a stated problem.
57.tq: Find the option that reverses the sectoral problem described.

57.s: Disruption of thermal power generation due to rail and logistics delays primarily reflects which problem in the coal sector?
57.x: Rail and logistics delays create movement and evacuation bottlenecks, which can disrupt thermal power generation.
57.tq: Translate the practical situation into the underlying sectoral problem.

57.s: Coking coal is imported mainly from which country, while non-coking coal is obtained mainly from Indonesia and South Africa?
57.x: Coking coal is imported mainly from Australia, whereas non-coking coal comes mainly from Indonesia and South Africa.
57.tq: Keep the source countries of coking and non-coking coal separate.

57.s: APGENCO procures washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery for which of the following power stations or units?
o: RTPP 600 MW and Dr NTTPS 500/800 MW units
RTPP 500 MW and Dr NTTPS 600/1000 MW units
57.x: APGENCO buys washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery for the 600 MW RTPP and the 500/800 MW units of Dr NTTPS.
57.tq: Match the washery supply arrangement with both recipient stations and capacities.

57.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reserve and leading-State position of lignite?
o: 15.000 billion tonnes; Rajasthan led by Singrauli
47.295 billion tonnes; Odisha led by Talcher
47.295 billion tonnes; Tamil Nadu led by Neyveli
389.421 billion tonnes; Jharkhand led by Jharia
57.x: Lignite resources are estimated at 47.295 billion tonnes, with Tamil Nadu leading through the Neyveli region, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat.
57.tq: Match the resource figure with the correct leading State and field.

57.s: Which of the following coalfield–State pairs is correctly matched?
57.x: Raniganj is located in West Bengal. Talcher is in Odisha, Singrauli is in Madhya Pradesh and Makum is in Assam.
57.tq: Start with the sure location and eliminate swapped State associations.

57.s: The first coal mine at Raniganj was established in 1774 at:
57.x: The first mine at the Raniganj coalfield was established in 1774 at Sitarampur.
57.tq: Link the historical date with the specific place within the coalfield.

57.s: Which of the following pairs of coalfields is correctly associated with Odisha?
57.x: Talcher and Deogarh, including the IB Valley, are coalfields of Odisha. Jharia and Bokaro are in Jharkhand, Korba and Raigarh in Chhattisgarh, and Singareni and Makum in Telangana and Assam respectively.
57.tq: Group coalfields by State and reject cross-State substitutions.

57.s: Which of the following coalfield–State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
57.x: Deogarh is in Odisha, not Madhya Pradesh. Jharia, Korba and Singareni are correctly associated with Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Telangana respectively.
57.tq: Find the single location swap among neighbouring coal-producing regions.

57.s: India recorded coal production of how much in 2024–25, marking the first year in which production exceeded one billion tonnes?
57.x: India recorded 1,047.50 MT of coal production in 2024–25, the first time production crossed one billion tonnes.
57.tq: Use the exact production figure and distinguish it from the target and import figures.

57.s:
With reference to India’s coal sector in 2024–25, consider the following statements:
1. Coal imports declined by 7.9%.
2. Coal imports stood at 243.62 MT.
3. The reduction in imports resulted in savings of about $7.13 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three statements are correct. Imports fell by 7.9% to 243.62 MT, producing estimated savings of about $7.13 billion.
57.tq: Check whether the percentage, absolute quantity and consequence belong to the same data set.

57.s: What was India’s coal production target for 2025–26?
57.x: India’s coal production target for 2025–26 was fixed at 1,157 MT.
57.tq: Separate the future target from the previous year’s actual production.

57.s: By August 2025, how much coal production had been achieved against the 2025–26 target?
57.x: Coal production by August 2025 was reported as 381.749 MT against the 2025–26 target.
57.tq: Match the partial-year achievement with the correct target-year data.

57.s: India ranks where in the world in terms of coal production and consumption, after China?
o: First in production and second in consumption
Third in production and second in consumption
Second in production and third in consumption
57.x: India is the world’s second-largest producer and consumer of coal, after China.
57.tq: Test the paired ranking without reversing production and consumption.

57.s: Coal accounts for approximately what share of India’s commercial energy needs?
57.x: Coal meets about 55% of India’s commercial energy needs.
57.tq: Distinguish the share in commercial energy needs from the higher share in power generation.

57.s: Which of the following is the planning arm of Coal India Limited?
57.x: Central Mine Planning and Design Institute, abbreviated as CMPDI, functions as Coal India Limited’s planning arm.
57.tq: Test the exact institutional abbreviation rather than the producing subsidiaries.

57.s: How many producing subsidiaries does Coal India Limited have according to the stated organisational structure?
57.x: Coal India Limited has seven producing subsidiaries.
57.tq: Use the count first, then verify it against the listed entities.

57.s: Which one of the following sets contains all the seven producing subsidiaries of Coal India Limited?
o: ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL
ECL, CMPDI, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and SCCL
BCCL, CCL, MCL, SCCL, NCL, WCL and CMPDI
ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, MCL, SCCL and CMPDI
57.x: The seven producing subsidiaries are ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL. CMPDI is the planning arm and SCCL is not one of these seven subsidiaries.
57.tq: Start with the sure list items and eliminate options containing the planning arm or SCCL.

57.s: The ownership pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is:
57.x: SCCL is owned 51% by Telangana and 49% by the Government of India.
57.tq: Watch for the reversed ownership percentages and the swapped governments.

57.s: The SHAKTI policy of 2017 replaced which coal linkage regime?
57.x: The SHAKTI policy, introduced in 2017, replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime.
57.tq: Distinguish a policy regime from the Acts governing coal allocation and mining.

57.s: Under the SHAKTI policy, coal linkages are provided through:
57.x: SHAKTI introduced auction or tariff-based bidding for coal linkages in place of the earlier NCDP-2007 regime.
57.tq: Identify the operational mechanism associated with the policy rather than its year or parent legislation.

57.s: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions in India began in:
57.x: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began in 2020.
57.tq: Place the auction mechanism in time against the nearby years of the CMSP Act, SHAKTI policy and later auction rounds.

57.s: After twelve rounds of commercial coal auctions, which of the following was the position regarding mines and peak rated capacity?
57.x: After twelve rounds, 134 mines had been sold, with a peak rated capacity of 277.04 MTPA.
57.tq: Pair the round count with both the mine count and capacity instead of mixing figures from other stages.

57.s: The 13th round of commercial coal mine auctions opened on:
57.x: The 13th round opened on 21 August 2025.
57.tq: Use the exact day, month and year to distinguish the auction round from later agreements.

57.s: How many mines were offered in the 13th round of commercial coal auctions?
57.x: The 13th round opened with 14 mines.
57.tq: Separate the number offered in one round from the cumulative number sold after twelve rounds.

57.s: In the 14th round of commercial coal mine auctions, mines went to:
57.x: The 14th round awarded mines to Reliance Industries and Axis Energy.
57.tq: Apply the wrong-owner trap by distinguishing auction awardees from coal-producing public sector entities.

57.s: The agreements in the 14th round were significant because they were the first agreements to include clauses relating to:
57.x: The 14th-round agreements were the first to include underground coal gasification clauses.
57.tq: Link the special contractual clause with the correct technology rather than with the auction mechanism itself.

57.s: A total of 199 coal mines have been allocated under:
o: The CMSP Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957
The Energy Conservation Act and the Electricity Act
57.x: The 199 mines were allocated under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957.
57.tq: Distinguish the two statutory routes of allocation from the separate linkage policy.

57.s: Which mineral was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral through an amendment to the MMDR framework, enabling the Centre to auction its leases?
57.x: Coking coal was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral, allowing the Centre to auction its leases.
57.tq: Identify the specific coal variety and avoid substituting the broader category of coal.

57.s: Coal bed methane is best described as methane that is:
o: Stored only in large underground cavities
Only dissolved in groundwater below coal seams
Produced exclusively by surface combustion of coal
Held in coal seams, partly free in joints and partly adsorbed in micropores
57.x: CBM is methane held in coal seams; part of it is free in joints and part is adsorbed in micropores.
57.tq: Break the definition into its two storage forms—free gas in joints and adsorbed gas in micropores.

57.s: Commercial recovery of coal bed methane generally involves:
o: Drilling wells and pumping out water
Mining only the surface layer of coal
Burning the coal seam in situ without wells
Injecting only nitrogen into coal seams
57.x: CBM is released by drilling wells and pumping out water from the coal seam.
57.tq: Match the resource-recovery process with the correct operational steps.

57.s: Coal bed methane is also known as “sweet gas” because it:
o: Has a high concentration of heavier hydrocarbons
Is produced only from sweet-water aquifers
57.x: CBM is called sweet gas because it carries few heavier hydrocarbons.
57.tq: Use the exact defining chemical distinction instead of interpreting “sweet” literally.

57.s: Which one of the following correctly describes underground coal gasification?
o: It uses water alone to convert coal into liquid fuel.
It is an in-situ process in which air or oxygen and steam are injected into coal seams to produce syngas underground.
It extracts only methane from micropores without altering the coal seam.
It is an ex-situ process in which coal is transported to a surface furnace.
57.x: UCG is an in-situ process. Air or oxygen and steam are injected into the coal seam to produce syngas underground.
