57.tq: Contrast in-situ and ex-situ processes and identify the correct reactants and product.

57.s: Underground coal gasification is particularly applicable to coal that is:
57.x: UCG can be used for deep, thin or unmineable coal seams.
57.tq: Identify the resource characteristic that makes underground conversion useful.

57.s: Which of the following is a stated environmental risk of underground coal gasification?
o: Immediate destruction of all surface vegetation
Formation of heavier hydrocarbons in all coal seams
57.x: Groundwater contamination is a recognised risk associated with UCG.
57.tq: Select the specifically stated risk and reject broader unsupported environmental claims.

57.s: What was the position of the MoEFCC expert panel regarding the minimum depth for UCG pilot projects?
o: It refused to waive the 300 m minimum depth.
It waived the 300 m minimum depth.
It increased the minimum depth to 600 m.
57.x: The MoEFCC expert panel refused to waive the 300 m minimum depth requirement for UCG pilot projects.
57.tq: Watch the NOT-waiver distinction and retain the exact 300 m threshold.

57.s: The ₹37,500-crore scheme currently associated with coal gasification drew:
o: No policy attention during the West Asia conflict
Bids only from Reliance Industries in May 2026
57.x: The ₹37,500-crore gasification scheme drew no bids in September 2026. The West Asia conflict nevertheless pushed gasification higher on the policy agenda.
57.tq: Separate the policy objective and relevance from the actual response received in the bidding process.

57.s: Which development pushed coal gasification higher on the policy agenda?
o: The replacement of NCDP-2007 by SHAKTI
The achievement of 1,047.50 MT coal production
57.x: The West Asia conflict increased the policy emphasis on coal gasification.
57.tq: Identify the stated current-affairs trigger rather than a related coal-sector reform.

57.s: Why has the 100 MT coal-gasification goal been viewed with doubt?
o: Because few projects have reached an advanced stage
Because all commercial auctions were cancelled
Because UCG uses only shallow coal
Because coal production crossed one billion tonnes in 2024–25
57.x: The 100 MT goal is considered doubtful because few coal-gasification projects have reached an advanced stage.
57.tq: Link the criticism to project maturity rather than to total coal production or auction numbers.

57.s:
Which of the following measures has been recommended by LENS in relation to coal gasification?
1. Use of CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal
2. Zero liquid discharge
3. Mandatory CCUS
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: LENS has called for CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal, zero liquid discharge and mandatory carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS).
57.tq: Recognise a complete recommendation set and avoid dropping the environmental safeguards.

57.s: BHEL commissioned the first IGCC plant in:
57.x: BHEL commissioned the first Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC) plant in 1985.
57.tq: Expand the technology abbreviation and associate the correct year with the commissioning event.

57.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First coal mine established at Raniganj
B. BHEL commissioned the first IGCC plant
C. Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began
D. The 13th round of commercial coal auctions opened
57.x: The correct sequence is 1774, 1985, 2020 and 21 August 2025: A, B, C, D.
57.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two intermediate milestones by year.

57.s:
Arrange the following coal types in descending order of carbon content:
A. Lignite
B. Anthracite
C. Peat
D. Bituminous
E. Sub-bituminous
57.x: The descending order is anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, lignite and peat.
57.tq: Arrange the grades by the carbon-content hierarchy, not by age or colour.

57.s: Which type of coal contains the highest carbon content, generally about 80–95%?
57.x: Anthracite contains approximately 80–95% carbon and is the best-quality coal.
57.tq: Match the highest carbon range with the highest-grade coal type.

57.s: Which one of the following statements about anthracite is correct?
o: It is known as brown coal and is centred on Neyveli.
It is the first stage in the transformation of wood into coal.
Small amounts occur in Jammu and Kashmir.
It is found in large quantities throughout India.
57.x: Anthracite is found only in small amounts in Jammu and Kashmir. Peat is the first stage, while lignite is brown coal associated with places such as Neyveli.
57.tq: Use the distinctive occurrence of anthracite to reject descriptions of other coal types.

57.s: Which type of coal is most widely used and is also the coking grade?
57.x: Bituminous coal is the most widely used type and includes the coking grade.
57.tq: Identify the coal type by its use and industrial grade.

57.s: Sub-bituminous coal is best described as coal that:
o: Is a brown coal found only in Jammu and Kashmir
Lies between bituminous coal and lignite and is used in power plants
Contains under 40% carbon and represents the first stage of coal formation
Contains 80–95% carbon and is the best-quality coal
57.x: Sub-bituminous coal lies between bituminous coal and lignite in rank and is used in power plants.
57.tq: Distinguish the intermediate coal type from both higher- and lower-rank varieties.

57.s: Lignite generally contains approximately what percentage of carbon and is also known as:
57.x: Lignite generally contains about 40–55% carbon and is commonly called brown coal.
57.tq: Pair the numerical range with the accepted descriptive name.

57.s: Which of the following set of places is associated with lignite occurrences mentioned in the classification?
57.x: Neyveli, Palana and Lakhimpur are identified with lignite occurrences. The other groups are associated with major coalfields of higher-rank coal regions.
57.tq: Recognise the lignite-location group instead of a group of Gondwana coalfields.

57.s: Peat is characterised by which of the following?
o: 60–80% carbon and use as coking coal
Less than 40% carbon and being the first stage in the transformation of wood into coal
40–55% carbon and occurrence mainly at Neyveli
57.x: Peat contains under 40% carbon and represents the first stage in the change from wood to coal.
57.tq: Use the defining formation-stage description to identify the lowest-rank material.

57.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Coal type)
A. Anthracite
B. Bituminous
C. Lignite
D. Peat

List-II (Carbon content)
1. Less than 40%
2. 80–95%
3. 40–55%
4. 60–80%

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
57.x: Anthracite contains 80–95% carbon, bituminous 60–80%, lignite 40–55%, and peat less than 40%.
57.tq: Begin with the extreme values and then match the intermediate coal categories.

57.s: Anthracite coal in India occurs in small quantities only in
57.x: Anthracite occurs only in small quantities in Jammu and Kashmir.
57.tq: Use the unique state association for the rarest coal type.

57.s: Which of the following states is NOT listed among the principal occurrences of bituminous coal?
57.x: Bituminous coal occurs in Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. Tamil Nadu is associated with Neyveli lignite.
57.tq: Separate the bituminous-coal states from the lignite-producing state.

57.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
57.x: Lignite contains approximately 40–55% carbon. Peat has less than 40%, anthracite 80–95%, and bituminous coal about 60–80% according to the stated classification.
57.tq: Check each coal type against its carbon range rather than relying on names alone.

57.s: Lignite is also known as
57.x: Lignite is commonly called brown coal.
57.tq: Discriminate between descriptive names of different coal grades.

57.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the first stage in the transformation of wood into coal?
57.x: Peat, with less than 40% carbon, is identified as the first stage in the transformation of wood into coal.
57.tq: Test the sequence of coal formation from the earliest stage.

57.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
57.x: Talcher is in Odisha, whereas Singareni is in Telangana. Jharia is in Jharkhand, Raniganj in West Bengal and Korba in Chhattisgarh.
57.tq: Use the coalfield-state association and catch the swapped eastern-India location.

57.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bokaro — Jharkhand
2. Giridih — Jharkhand
3. Raigarh — Chhattisgarh
4. Neyveli — Tamil Nadu
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
57.x: Bokaro and Giridih are in Jharkhand, Raigarh is in Chhattisgarh and Neyveli lignite field is in Tamil Nadu.
57.tq: Verify each location pair before selecting the complete combination.

57.s: Singareni coalfield is located in
57.x: The Singareni coalfield is located in Telangana.
57.tq: Use the distinctive coalfield-state pair as an anchor for elimination.

57.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
57.x: Palana lignite field is in Rajasthan. Lakhimpur is in Assam, Neyveli in Tamil Nadu and Barmer in Rajasthan.
57.tq: Compare similarly named lignite locations across states.

57.s: The maximum lignite reserves in India are associated with
57.x: Tamil Nadu, particularly Neyveli, has the maximum lignite reserves among the locations listed.
57.tq: Separate the largest occurrence from other listed lignite fields.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about Gondwana coal:
1. It is approximately 250–300 million years old.
2. It accounts for about 98% of India’s coal reserves.
3. It occurs in the Damodar, Mahanadi, Son and Godavari valleys.
4. It consists predominantly of Tertiary lignite deposits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Gondwana coal is not predominantly Tertiary lignite; Tertiary deposits are younger and include lignite.
57.tq: Reject the statement that swaps Gondwana characteristics with Tertiary characteristics.

57.s:
Assertion (A): Gondwana coal is the principal source of India’s coal reserves.
Reason (R): Gondwana coal accounts for about 98% of India’s coal reserves and includes most of its coking coal.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
57.x: Both statements are true, and the approximately 98% share of reserves and concentration of coking coal directly explain why Gondwana coal is the principal source.
57.tq: Check whether the quantitative reason directly explains the assertion.

58.s: Which of the following correctly states the sequence of coal-sector nationalisation in India?
o: Non-coking coal in 1971–72 followed by coking coal in 1973
Coking coal in 1971–72 followed by non-coking coal in 1973
Both coking and non-coking coal in 1971–72
Coking coal in 1973 followed by non-coking coal in 1975
58.x: Coking coal was nationalised in 1971–72, followed by non-coking coal in 1973.
58.tq: Use the order of two closely related nationalisation events to eliminate reversed sequences.

58.s: The Supreme Court’s cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 was followed by which legislative measure for auction-based allocation?
o: Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, without amendment
58.x: The cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 led to the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, which enabled auction-based allocation.
58.tq: Match the judicial event with the specific corrective legislation that followed it.

58.s:
Which of the following functions is performed by the Coal Controller’s Organisation?
1. Compilation of coal statistics
2. Monitoring of captive coal blocks
3. Hearing objections relating to acquisition of coal-bearing land

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The Coal Controller’s Organisation performs all three functions: maintaining coal statistics, monitoring captive blocks and hearing objections concerning acquisition of coal-bearing land.
58.tq: Group the body’s technical, monitoring and quasi-adjudicatory functions before choosing the code.

58.s: The ownership pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is:
o: 51 per cent Telangana Government and 49 per cent Government of India
49 per cent Telangana Government and 51 per cent private companies
51 per cent Government of India and 49 per cent Telangana Government
58.x: Singareni Collieries Company Limited is owned 51 per cent by Telangana and 49 per cent by the Government of India.
58.tq: Watch for reversal of majority and minority ownership shares.

58.s: The publication titled ‘Energy Statistics’ is brought out by the:
o: Coal Controller’s Organisation under the Ministry of Coal
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power
National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
58.x: Energy Statistics is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
58.tq: Identify the publishing authority and avoid swapping it with a sectoral regulator or ministry.

58.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Basin — State
1. Cambay — Gujarat
2. Krishna-Godavari — Andhra Pradesh
3. Cauvery — Tamil Nadu
4. Rajasthan Basin — Rajasthan
58.x: Cambay is in Gujarat, Krishna-Godavari in Andhra Pradesh, Cauvery in Tamil Nadu and the Barmer-Jaisalmer basin in Rajasthan.
58.tq: Use the state-basin association and eliminate options containing a swapped location.

58.s: Ankleshwar and Kalol are important fields of which sedimentary basin?
58.x: Ankleshwar and Kalol are key fields of the Cambay Basin in Gujarat.
58.tq: Test the field-to-basin association directly.

58.s: Bombay High is associated with which one of the following basins?
58.x: Bombay High is the principal field associated with the Mumbai Offshore Basin off the Maharashtra coast. It was developed after the 1973 oil shock.
58.tq: Distinguish a well-known offshore field from onshore basin fields.

58.s:
Which of the following fields are associated with the Krishna-Godavari Basin?

1. Ravva
2. KG-D6
3. Narimanam
4. Mangala

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Ravva and KG-D6 are associated with the Krishna-Godavari Basin. Narimanam belongs to the Cauvery Basin and Mangala to the Rajasthan Basin.
58.tq: Separate neighbouring basin fields by matching each field to its basin.

58.s: Narimanam is a key field of the
58.x: Narimanam is a key field of the Cauvery Basin, which extends across onshore and offshore areas of Tamil Nadu.
58.tq: Use a single distinctive field as the identifying clue.

58.s:
Consider the following fields:

1. Digboi
2. Naharkatiya
3. Moran

They are associated with which one of the following regions or basins?
58.x: Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran are key fields of the Assam-Arakan or Assam Shelf region.
58.tq: Group the three fields that belong to the same basin before checking the options.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
58.x: Moran is associated with the Assam-Arakan or Assam Shelf region, not the Cauvery Basin. Mangala and Dandewala are in Rajasthan, while Trishna is in Tripura.
58.tq: Find the incorrectly paired field and basin by checking the location of each field.

58.s: Trishna gas project is located in
58.x: The Trishna gas project is located in Tripura and is associated with the Tripura Fold Belt.
58.tq: Test the project-to-state association directly.

58.s: Which of the following basins is NOT included among Category I basins in commercial production?
58.x: Category I basins listed as being in commercial production are Cambay, Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery, Assam Shelf, Assam-Arakan and Rajasthan. Tripura Fold Belt is not included in that list.
58.tq: Use the listed-category method and identify the basin outside the specified group.

58.s: The Dandewala gas field is located in the
58.x: Dandewala is a gas field in the Jaisalmer Basin of Rajasthan.
58.tq: Distinguish the Rajasthan gas field from similarly named fields in other basins.

58.s: In May 2026, Oil India Limited struck gas in the shallower Sanu Formation at Dandewala. The formation belongs to which geological age?
58.x: The Sanu Formation at Dandewala is identified as Tertiary and lower Eocene.
58.tq: Link the dated discovery with the geological-age detail rather than treating the date as the answer.

58.s: Which one of the following statements regarding petroleum occurrence is correct?
o: Oil is formed only in Precambrian rocks and occurs chiefly in river valleys.
Oil is formed mainly in the Quaternary period and occurs only in volcanic rocks.
Oil formed in the Tertiary period, and most reserves occur in anticlines and fault traps.
Oil formed in the Jurassic period and is confined exclusively to synclines.
58.x: The material identifies the Tertiary period as the period of oil formation and anticlines and fault traps as the principal settings of most reserves.
58.tq: Combine the geological age with the structural-trap concept in the precise option.

58.s: Shale gas and oil are primarily held in
o: permeable sandstone and extracted without stimulation
coal seams and released mainly by pumping water
fine-grained shale and generally require hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling
58.x: Shale hydrocarbons occur in fine-grained shale and require fracking and horizontal drilling. Coal seams hold coal bed methane, while gas hydrates occur as methane-water crystals.
58.tq: Discriminate unconventional resources by their host formation and extraction method.

58.s: Coal bed methane is best described as methane that is
o: adsorbed in coal seams and released by pumping water
dissolved in seawater and frozen below the seabed
mixed with propane and butane during petroleum refining
trapped in permeable sandstone and extracted by ordinary wells
58.x: Coal bed methane is methane held or adsorbed in coal seams and is released by pumping out water.
58.tq: Separate CBM from shale gas and gas hydrates by identifying both its host and release method.

58.s: The first commercial output of coal bed methane in India was obtained at
58.x: The first commercial output of coal bed methane was obtained at Raniganj. Jharia, Bokaro and Sohagpur are also important CBM areas.
58.tq: Distinguish the first commercial site from the wider list of CBM areas.

58.s:
Which of the following are identified as important areas for coal bed methane?

1. Raniganj
2. Jharia
3. Bokaro
4. Sohagpur

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Raniganj, Jharia, Bokaro and Sohagpur are all identified as key coal bed methane areas.
58.tq: Check whether the complete list is covered rather than selecting only the best-known area.

58.s: Gas hydrates consist principally of
o: carbon dioxide trapped in coal seams
58.x: Gas hydrates are ice-like methane-water crystals occurring in deep-sea sediments.
58.tq: Use the physical description to distinguish gas hydrates from other unconventional hydrocarbons.

58.s:
Which of the following locations are associated with gas hydrates?

1. Krishna-Godavari
2. Mahanadi
3. Andaman offshore
4. Damodar Valley

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Gas hydrates are associated with the Krishna-Godavari, Mahanadi and Andaman offshore areas. Damodar Valley is a major coal bed methane region.
58.tq: Avoid confusing offshore gas-hydrate locations with the coalfield locations of CBM.

58.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes conventional gas from unconventional gas?
o: Conventional gas occurs in impermeable shale only, whereas unconventional gas occurs in permeable sandstone only.
Conventional gas generally occurs in permeable sandstone, whereas unconventional gas occurs in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams and requires costly technology.
Both types occur only in coal seams and are extracted by pumping water.
Neither type requires drilling or specialised technology.
58.x: Conventional gas is found in permeable sandstone. Unconventional gas occurs in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams and generally needs costly extraction technology.
58.tq: Compare the host formations and technological requirements rather than the fuel name alone.

58.s:
Which of the following are identified as major gas basins?

1. Mumbai Offshore
2. Krishna-Godavari
3. Assam
4. Cambay

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay are all identified as major gas basins.
58.tq: Recognise a complete four-item list and reject partial-list distractors.

58.s: Gas was first found in India in the 1960s in which two states?
58.x: The first gas discoveries referred to in the material were in Assam and Maharashtra during the 1960s.
58.tq: Match the decade with the correct pair of states.

58.s: Regasified LNG can be used for supplying
o: only coal gas to thermal plants
58.x: After regasification, LNG can be supplied for use as piped natural gas and compressed natural gas.
58.tq: Follow the conversion chain from liquefied gas to its end-use forms.

58.s: India's targeted share of gas in the energy mix by 2030 is approximately
58.x: The target is to raise the share of gas in the energy mix from about 6.7 percent to 15 percent by 2030.
58.tq: Distinguish the present approximate share from the future target.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the indicated present gas-sector position?
o: Gas imports are below 5 percent and no gas-based power capacity is stranded.
Gas imports are about 80 percent and stranded gas power capacity is about 250 GW.
Gas imports are about 15 percent and stranded gas power capacity is about 2.5 GW.
Gas imports are about 47–51 percent and about 25 GW of gas-based power capacity is stranded.
58.x: The indicated figures are gas imports of approximately 47–51 percent and around 25 GW of stranded gas-based power capacity.
58.tq: Check both the percentage range and the capacity figure together to avoid scale errors.

58.s: The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline passes through which states?
o: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal
58.x: The HVJ pipeline of GAIL connects Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; Maharashtra is not on this route.
58.tq: Use route sequencing and the excluded-state trap to identify the correct corridor.

58.s:
Which of the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga project is correct?

1. It is also known as the Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra pipeline.
2. Its authorised length is 3,546 km.
3. Its running length is 3,272 km.
4. It links the eastern and north-eastern regions to the gas grid.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: All four statements correctly describe Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga, including its JHBDPL identity, authorised and operating lengths, and regional linkage function.
58.tq: Check the project name, both numerical lengths and its stated connectivity before selecting the complete combination.

58.s: The Indradhanush North-East Gas Grid extends for approximately
58.x: The Indradhanush North-East Gas Grid is approximately 1,656 km long and spans the eight North-Eastern States.
58.tq: Distinguish the NE grid length from the longer national and Urja Ganga figures.

58.s:
Which of the following organisations constitute the joint venture for the Indradhanush North-East Gas Grid?

1. IOCL
2. ONGC
3. GAIL
4. OIL
5. NRL

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The joint venture comprises IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL.
58.tq: Verify the full institutional composition instead of stopping at the first three familiar entities.

58.s: One Nation One Gas Grid was initiated in
58.x: The One Nation One Gas Grid initiative began in 2014.
58.tq: Distinguish the initial year of the gas-grid idea from the later implementation dates.

58.s: As on 31 March 2025, which combination correctly represents the pipeline network authorised by PNGRB and the portion operating?
58.x: PNGRB had authorised 34,223 km of pipeline, of which 25,429 km was operating as on 31 March 2025.
58.tq: Keep the authorised and operating figures in the correct order.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly states the target associated with One Nation One Gas Grid?
o: A network of 25,429 km linking all districts by 2025
A national network of 3,200 km linking only the eastern States by 2030
A national network of more than 32,000 km linking all States by 2027
A network of 34,223 km restricted to the eight North-Eastern States by 2027
58.x: The target is a national pipeline network exceeding 32,000 km and linking all States by 2027.
58.tq: Combine the target length, coverage and deadline in one precise option.

58.s: The idea of a national gas grid was first proposed in 1955 by
58.x: S. H. Zaheer first proposed the idea of a national gas grid in 1955.
58.tq: Test the person-year association without confusing the proposal with later implementation.

58.s: S. H. Zaheer was associated with the institution in Hyderabad that is now known as
58.x: The proposal was associated with the Regional Research Laboratory at Hyderabad, now known as CSIR-IICT.
58.tq: Use the former-name and present-name relationship to identify the institution.

58.s:
With reference to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), consider the following statements:

1. It is a statutory body under the PNGRB Act, 2006.
2. It authorises geographical areas for city gas distribution.
3. It sets pipeline tariffs.
4. It regulates crude oil production.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: PNGRB is a statutory body under the 2006 Act, authorises CGD geographical areas and sets pipeline tariffs. It does not regulate crude oil production among the activities specified here.
58.tq: Apply the authority test: identify the powers expressly assigned to PNGRB and reject the overextended production claim.

58.s:
According to the specified regulatory division, PNGRB regulates which two activities among the following?

1. Production of crude oil
2. Refining, storage and distribution of petroleum
3. Marketing and sale of petroleum products
4. Production of natural gas

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The two regulated activities specified are refining, storage and distribution of petroleum, and marketing and sale of petroleum products. Crude oil and natural gas production are not included in these two activities.
58.tq: Separate regulated downstream activities from upstream production activities.

58.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. HVJ — Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
2. Trishna gas project — Tripura
3. East-West pipeline — Kakinada to Bharuch
4. PM Urja Ganga — Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha
58.x: All four pairings are correct. The East-West pipeline runs from Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh to Bharuch in Gujarat, while PM Urja Ganga covers the five listed eastern and north-central States.
58.tq: Check each route against its states and endpoints before selecting the complete matching set.

58.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of the dates or years associated with them:

A. Proposal of a national gas grid by S. H. Zaheer
B. Beginning of One Nation One Gas Grid
C. Establishment of IIPE Visakhapatnam
D. IIPE becoming an Institute of National Importance

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The order is 1955 proposal, 2014 beginning of ONOGG, 2016 establishment of IIPE and 2017 recognition as an Institute of National Importance. However, among the provided options, the sequence that places A before C, D and B is not chronologically accurate because B precedes C and D.
58.tq: Place the dated milestones first and verify the middle events carefully.

58.s: Oil marketing companies had established how many Energy Stations by 1 August 2025?
58.x: Oil marketing companies had established 799 Energy Stations by 1 August 2025.
58.tq: Retain the exact count and date together; nearby figures are scale-based distractors.

58.s: Which one of the following was introduced under the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) of 2016?
o: A single licence for all hydrocarbons
Government-controlled pricing of all petroleum products
Separate licences for each type of hydrocarbon
58.x: HELP introduced a single uniform licence covering conventional and unconventional hydrocarbons. It also provided open acreage and marketing and pricing freedom.
58.tq: Direct recall of the distinctive feature of a policy.

58.s: Under HELP, the Government's revenue is obtained through which of the following arrangements?
o: A profit-sharing contract determined after production
58.x: HELP replaced the production-sharing contract system under NELP with a biddable revenue-sharing contract.
58.tq: Confusable-policy discrimination between production sharing and revenue sharing.

58.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP):
1. Companies may choose the blocks they wish to bid for.
2. Bidding for blocks is permitted throughout the year.
3. The National Data Repository supports identification of blocks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: OALP allows companies to select blocks and bid year-round, using data available through the National Data Repository. The policy is intended to promote domestic exploration and production.
58.tq: Statement elimination using a policy's operational features.

58.s: The Discovered Small Fields policy primarily relates to the auction of small fields held by which entities?
58.x: Under the Discovered Small Fields policy of 2015, small fields held by ONGC and OIL are auctioned to increase domestic output.
58.tq: Direct recall of the concerned public-sector entities.

58.s:
With reference to Samudra Manthan, consider the following statements:
1. It is the National Offshore Exploration Scheme.
2. Its outlay extends up to 2030-31.
3. It is a 100 per cent Central Sector scheme.
4. It is restricted to blocks held by ONGC alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Samudra Manthan is the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, with an outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to 2030-31 and 100 per cent central funding. It is open to OALP block holders, not only ONGC.
58.tq: Find the wrongly restricted statement in a scheme description.

58.s: The outlay approved for Samudra Manthan up to 2030-31 is:
58.x: The approved outlay for Samudra Manthan up to 2030-31 is ₹84,084 crore.
58.tq: Numerical recall with closely spaced figures.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the exploration activities supported under Samudra Manthan?
o: Coal-bed methane extraction, with support capped at ₹675 lakh per well
Only offshore production, with complete reimbursement of drilling expenditure
Seismic mapping and risk drilling, with 50 per cent support capped at ₹675 crore per well
Refinery modernisation and pipeline construction, with 50 per cent support
58.x: The scheme covers seismic mapping and risk drilling. Risk drilling receives 50 per cent support, capped at ₹675 crore per well, and about 60 deep-water wells are envisaged.
58.tq: Match the scheme's purpose, support rate and ceiling precisely.

58.s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is best described as a:
o: Public-sector company under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Constitutional body under the Ministry of Finance
Statutory body established under the PNGRB Act, 2006
Advisory body created under the Companies Act, 2013
58.x: PNGRB is a statutory body established under the PNGRB Act, 2006, functioning under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
58.tq: Distinguish statutory bodies from constitutional bodies and companies.

58.s: Which of the following activities falls outside the regulatory scope of PNGRB?
o: Marketing and sale of petroleum products and gas
Authorisation of City Gas Distribution geographical areas
Production of crude oil and natural gas
58.x: PNGRB regulates refining, storage, distribution, marketing and sale, and authorises CGD geographical areas. Production of crude oil or gas is outside the stated scope.
58.tq: Identify the excluded activity by separating production from downstream regulation.

58.s: Foreign Direct Investment in many segments of India's petroleum and natural gas sector is permitted up to:
58.x: FDI is permitted up to 100 per cent in many petroleum and natural gas segments. In PSU refining, the limit is 49 per cent without disinvestment.
58.tq: Contrast the general ceiling with the sector-specific exception.

58.s: In petroleum geology, the rock in which oil is formed is generally the:
58.x: Source rock is generally organic-rich shale in which petroleum is formed. Reservoir and cap rocks perform different functions in petroleum accumulation.
58.tq: Direct recall of the source-reservoir-cap rock distinction.

58.s: Which one of the following is the most suitable description of a petroleum reservoir rock?
o: A porous and permeable sandstone or fissured limestone
A salt dome containing only natural gas
An impervious bed that seals the trap
An organic-rich shale in which oil originates
58.x: Reservoir rocks are porous and permeable, commonly sandstone or fissured limestone, allowing hydrocarbons to accumulate and flow.
58.tq: Discriminate reservoir rock from source rock and cap rock by function.

58.s: The principal function of a cap rock in a petroleum trap is to:
o: Seal the trap because it is impervious
Separate gas from crude oil during refining
58.x: Cap rock is an impervious bed that prevents hydrocarbons from escaping and thereby seals the petroleum trap.
58.tq: Apply the geological function rather than memorising the name alone.

58.s: Commercial accumulations of petroleum are generally found at the crests of:
58.x: Commercial oil commonly accumulates at the crests of anticlines. Other recognised traps include fault traps and salt domes.
58.tq: Direct recall of the principal structural trap.

58.s: Which of the following lists contains only recognised petroleum traps?
o: Anticlines, fault traps and salt domes
Fault traps, dunes and volcanic cones
58.x: Anticlines, fault traps and salt domes are recognised petroleum traps. The other alternatives include landforms that are not listed as petroleum traps here.
58.tq: Odd-group identification using a complete technical list.

58.s: In a petroleum reservoir, the usual vertical arrangement from the top downward is:
58.x: Because of differences in density, gas is found above oil, and water is generally below oil.
58.tq: Use density to determine the correct vertical sequence.

58.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
o: Gas rich in hydrogen sulphide — sour gas
Gas with no hydrocarbons — sour gas
58.x: Gas rich in hydrogen sulphide is called sour gas. Associated gas is termed wet gas, while non-associated gas is termed dry gas.
58.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination among petroleum gas terms.

58.s: Petroleum generally consists of approximately what proportion of hydrocarbons?
58.x: Petroleum is composed of approximately 90–95 per cent hydrocarbons.
58.tq: Direct quantitative recall using percentage ranges.

58.s: The Andhra Pradesh Gas Infrastructure Corporation holds what share in a consortium with ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks?
58.x: APGIC holds a 10 per cent share in the consortium involving ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks.
58.tq: Direct recall of consortium participation and percentage.

58.s: Which of the following pairs of KG-basin fields and participating entities is correctly matched?
58.x: Ravva is an offshore KG field associated with Cairn-ONGC, whereas KG-D6 is associated with Reliance-BP.
58.tq: Swap-the-owner trap involving two prominent KG-basin fields.

58.s: The coal associated with the Godavari valley is:
58.x: The Godavari valley coalfields are associated with Singareni, which is now in Telangana. The historical observation was that Andhra lacked coal and would draw on Singareni.
58.tq: Location-resource association using a nearby regional distractor.

58.s: Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) is produced by:
o: Compressing natural gas to 200–250 kg/cm² only
Mixing natural gas with propane and butane
58.x: LNG is natural gas cooled below −160°C. This reduces its volume approximately 1,000 times, and LNG is lighter than air.
58.tq: Distinguish liquefaction by cooling from compression and blending.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly describes CNG?
o: Natural gas compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm² and used as a vehicle fuel
Natural gas cooled below −160°C and transported as a liquid
A heavy residual fuel used in boilers
A mixture of propane and butane used in domestic cylinders
58.x: CNG is natural gas compressed to approximately 200–250 kg/cm² and is widely used as a vehicle fuel.
58.tq: Identify the fuel from its preparation, pressure and principal use.

58.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. LPG mainly contains propane and butane.
2. LPG is a by-product of oil refining and gas processing.
3. LPG is heavier than air.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: LPG mainly consists of propane and butane, is obtained as a by-product of oil refining and gas processing, and is heavier than air.
58.tq: Combine composition, origin and physical-property statements.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Piped Natural Gas (PNG)?
o: It contains 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied continuously through CGD networks
It contains mainly propane and butane and is stored in cylinders
It is natural gas liquefied below −160°C and transported by tankers
It is a heavy residual fuel supplied only to boilers
58.x: PNG contains approximately 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied through City Gas Distribution networks on a continuous basis.
58.tq: Separate PNG from LPG, LNG and furnace oil using composition and delivery mode.

58.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Furnace oil — light fuel for household cooking
58.x: Brent is the North Sea crude-price benchmark, while WTI is the United States benchmark. Furnace oil is a heavy residual fuel used in boilers.
58.tq: Discriminate between two commonly confused crude-price benchmarks.

58.s: A domestic consumer shifting from LPG to PNG would be using a fuel supplied through:
58.x: PNG is supplied continuously through City Gas Distribution networks. Domestic gas could potentially supply 30 crore consumers if they shifted from LPG to PNG.
58.tq: Apply the fuel's distribution method to a practical situation.

58.s: India has approximately how many LPG connections?
58.x: India has approximately 33 crore LPG connections. Domestic gas could supply around 30 crore consumers if they switched to PNG.
58.tq: Direct recall of a large sectoral figure.

58.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Phase I locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
58.x: Phase I of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves comprises Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur in Karnataka.
58.tq: Use location-based elimination among closely related energy projects.

58.s: The import cover provided by Phase I of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves is approximately
58.x: Phase I provides approximately 9.5 days of import cover.
58.tq: Separate the domestic reserve figure from the international benchmark.

58.s: The International Energy Agency norm for strategic petroleum reserve cover is
58.x: The IEA norm mentioned for strategic petroleum reserves is 90 days of import cover.
58.tq: Test the benchmark figure against smaller domestic reserve values.

58.s:
Under the new strategic fuel reserve plan, which of the following combinations is correct?
1. It is planned to hold about two months of crude and LNG.
2. It is planned to hold about six weeks of LPG.
3. It is proposed to be funded partly through levies on LPG and gas.
58.x: The proposed reserve covers about two months of crude and LNG and about six weeks of LPG, with funding through levies on LPG and gas.
58.tq: Use the coverage periods and financing mechanism together to test a policy proposal.

58.s: The proposed levy on LPG under the new strategic fuel reserve plan is approximately
58.x: The proposed levy is ₹1.29 per kg of LPG, equivalent to about ₹18 per cylinder.
58.tq: Distinguish the per-kilogram levy from its approximate per-cylinder equivalent.

58.s: The proposed levy on gas for financing the new strategic fuel reserve is
58.x: The proposed gas levy is ₹1.43 per standard cubic metre.
58.tq: Check the unit and decimal place carefully in numerical options.

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Product)
A. LPG
B. CNG
C. Naphtha
D. Furnace oil

List-II (Main use)
1. Petrochemicals and fertilisers
2. Household cooking
3. Industrial boilers and furnaces
4. Vehicles

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
58.x: LPG is mainly used for household cooking, CNG for vehicles, naphtha for petrochemicals and fertilisers, and furnace oil in industrial boilers and furnaces.
58.tq: Start with the sure product-use pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Petrochemicals — Plastics, synthetic fibres and rubber
Furnace oil — Industrial boilers and furnaces
58.x: CNG is mainly used in vehicles and produces lower pollutants. Industrial boilers and furnaces mainly use furnace oil in the given classification.
58.tq: Identify the product whose stated use has been swapped with a neighbouring product.

58.s: The Coal Council of India was set up in
58.x: The Coal Council of India was established in 1956.
58.tq: Distinguish institutional formation dates from later nationalisation dates.

58.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of coal-sector nationalisation?
o: Non-coking coal in 1971-72, coking coal in 1973, Coal India Ltd in 1975
Coking coal in 1971-72, non-coking coal in 1973, Coal India Ltd in 1975
Coking coal in 1973, non-coking coal in 1975, Coal India Ltd in 1971-72
Coal India Ltd in 1971-72, coking coal in 1973, non-coking coal in 1975
58.x: Coking coal was nationalised in 1971-72, non-coking coal in 1973, and Coal India Ltd was established in 1975.
58.tq: Fix the first and last milestones before checking the middle event.

58.s: Following the cancellation of coal blocks by the Supreme Court in 2014, coal-block auctions were conducted under the
58.x: Auctions after cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 were conducted under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015.
58.tq: Use the correct statute-name trap in a policy and legislation question.

58.s: Commercial mining auctions for coal commenced from
58.x: Commercial mining auctions for coal began in 2020.
58.tq: Separate the year of the special-provisions legislation from the year commercial auctions began.

58.s:
The Coal Controller's Organisation is associated with which of the following functions?
1. Coal grading
2. Quality checks
3. Compilation of coal statistics
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: The Coal Controller's Organisation undertakes coal grading, quality checks and maintenance of coal statistics.
58.tq: Recognise the common administrative functions of the designated regulatory organisation.

58.s: The Coal Controller's Organisation functions under the Ministry of Coal and is headquartered at
58.x: The Coal Controller's Organisation is under the Ministry of Coal and is located in Kolkata.
58.tq: Test the ministry-location pair, a common APPSC trap.

58.s: Which of the following is NOT a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Coal mentioned in the context of the coal sector?
58.x: The listed Ministry of Coal PSUs are Coal India Limited, NLC India and Singareni Collieries Company Limited. Oil India Limited belongs to the petroleum sector.
58.tq: Find the organisation belonging to the neighbouring petroleum sector.

58.s: The reduction in coal imports for thermal plants was approximately
58.x: Coal imports for thermal plants declined by approximately 27.4%.
58.tq: Distinguish the reported percentage change from nearby rounded alternatives.

58.s: Coal gasification primarily produces syngas containing
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide
58.x: Coal gasification produces syngas containing carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide.
58.tq: Break the process output into its named chemical constituents.

58.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a possible product or downstream application of coal gasification?
58.x: Coal gasification can support production of SNG, methanol, ethanol, ammonia or urea, hydrogen and petrochemicals. Nuclear fuel enrichment is not a stated application.
58.tq: Identify the unrelated industrial application among the gasification products.

58.s: The target of the National Coal Gasification Mission for 2030 is
58.x: The National Coal Gasification Mission has a target of 100 million tonnes by 2030.
58.tq: Match the mission with its target year and quantity.

58.s: The first gasification fertiliser plant under the stated coal-gasification plan is associated with
58.x: The first gasification fertiliser plant is planned at Talcher in Odisha by December 2027.
58.tq: Combine the project location with its target completion date.

58.s: Which company is identified as having the only commercial-scale coal-gasification plant?
58.x: JSPL's Angul facility is identified as the only commercial-scale coal-gasification plant.
58.tq: Use the company-project association rather than the location alone.

58.s: Under the coal-gasification incentive arrangement, a 50% revenue-share rebate is available when
o: The plant uses only imported coal
At least 10% of output is gasified

59.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Southern Grid synchronisation
B. PGCIL study for the Green Energy Corridor
C. Implementation of the Green Energy Corridor
D. APERC approval for procurement of 1,600 MW of coal power
59.x: The PGCIL study was conducted in 2012, the Southern Grid was synchronised in December 2013, the Green Energy Corridor was implemented from 2015, and the APERC approval came in 2026.
59.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle events.

59.s: The Green Energy Corridor began with a PGCIL study in 2012 and was implemented from
59.x: The Green Energy Corridor began with a PGCIL study in 2012 and was implemented from 2015.
59.tq: Distinguish the preparatory study year from the implementation year.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I:
1. It covers eight States, including Andhra Pradesh.
2. It involves about 9,700 circuit km of lines.
3. It involves 22,600 MVA of capacity.
4. It is associated with 24 GW of renewable energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All four statements correctly describe the scope and capacity of Intra-State GEC-I.
59.tq: Verify coverage, line length, transformation capacity and renewable-energy capacity separately.

59.s: Which of the following gives the correct funding pattern for Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I?
59.x: The funding pattern is MNRE 40%, KfW 40% and the State Transmission Utility 20%.
59.tq: Compare the percentages while preserving the order of the funding agencies.

59.s: The estimated cost of Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I is
59.x: The estimated cost of Intra-State GEC-I is ₹10,141.68 crore.
59.tq: Identify the exact project-cost figure among close alternatives.

59.s: Which organisation functions as the Central Transmission Utility of India?
59.x: POWERGRID, or PGCIL, functions as the Central Transmission Utility.
59.tq: Match the statutory transmission role with the correct organisation.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh’s transmission network:
1. It has 376 extra-high-voltage substations.
2. Its transmission network extends to 33,379.72 circuit km.
3. Its transmission and distribution losses are 9.25%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: The Andhra Pradesh network has 376 EHT substations, 33,379.72 circuit km of transmission and T&D losses of 9.25%.
59.tq: Check whether the network-size and loss figures are all retained accurately.

59.s: An oscillation that began in Rajasthan was reportedly felt at which power facility, illustrating the interconnected nature of the grid?
59.x: The grid oscillation that began in Rajasthan was felt at Kudankulam.
59.tq: Apply the interconnected-grid concept to identify the affected facility.

59.s: India recorded a peak power demand of 270.82 GW on
59.x: The record peak demand was 270.82 GW on 21 May 2026.
59.tq: Match the record figure with its precise date.

59.s: According to the Economic Survey reference, the demand–supply gap in electricity had become zero by
59.x: The demand–supply gap was reported to be zero by November 2025.
59.tq: Distinguish the zero-gap date from the separate shortage figures.

59.s: The transmission network associated with India’s One Nation-One Grid-One Frequency system exceeds
59.x: The network exceeds 5 lakh circuit km.
59.tq: Identify the order of magnitude rather than confusing it with recent additions.

59.s: The Electricity Act, 2003 was notified on which date?
59.x: The Electricity Act, 2003 was notified on 10 June 2003.
59.tq: Use the precise date rather than the year alone.

59.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Electricity Act, 2003?
59.x: The Act introduced or facilitated electricity trading; it did not abolish it. It also delicensed generation, required unbundling of SEBs and introduced open access and SERCs.
59.tq: Find the option that reverses a major provision of the Act.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Electricity Act, 2003:
1. It consolidates laws relating to generation, transmission, distribution and trading of electricity.
2. It established the Central Electricity Authority, regulatory commissions and an appellate tribunal.
3. It required State Electricity Boards to remain fully integrated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Act required SEBs to be unbundled.
59.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the unbundling provision.

59.s: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission was established under which legislation?
59.x: APERC was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.
59.tq: Distinguish the state reform legislation from the later central Electricity Act.

59.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, APERC served both successor States for a period of
59.x: Following bifurcation, APERC served both States for up to six months under the AP Reorganisation Act.
59.tq: Test the exact transitional period attached to reorganisation.

59.s: The Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 primarily provide for
o: allocation of coal to thermal plants
time limits for new connections and service standards
59.x: The 2020 Rules prescribe time limits for new electricity connections and service standards for consumers.
59.tq: Match the consumer-rights rules with their service-delivery function.

59.s: With reference to renewable energy under the Electricity Act, 2003, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: CEA asked Parliament to be treated as the Central Government.
MNRE asked a parliamentary committee to be treated as the Central Government.
APERC was treated as the Central Government by the Act.
CERC asked a parliamentary committee to be treated as the Central Government.
59.x: MNRE asked a parliamentary committee to be treated as the “Central Government” for renewables under the Act.
59.tq: Use the who-requested-what formulation to distinguish authorities.

59.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
a. CERC
a. SERCs
c. APTEL
d. CEA
List-II (Function or feature)
i. Reports on installed capacity and National Electricity Plan
 ii. Central tariffs and inter-State matters
 iii. State retail tariffs, licensing and standards
 iv. Appeals against CERC and SERC orders
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: CERC handles central tariffs and inter-State matters; SERCs handle State retail tariffs and licensing; APTEL hears appeals; CEA publishes technical power-sector reports.
59.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched regulatory functions.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission?
o: It fixes retail tariffs for all consumer classes in every State.
It deals with central tariffs and inter-State matters and regulates power exchanges such as IEX.
It is a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Finance.
It hears appeals against orders of all courts in electricity matters.
59.x: CERC deals with central tariffs and inter-State matters and regulates power exchanges such as IEX. SERCs generally fix State retail tariffs.
59.tq: Separate central and State regulatory jurisdictions.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about State Electricity Regulatory Commissions:
1. Their members are appointed by the State Government.
2. They fix retail tariffs for all consumer classes.
3. They can license, enforce standards and settle disputes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All three statements correctly describe the functions or composition of SERCs.
59.tq: Check whether all listed functions belong to the State-level regulator.

59.s: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity was established on
59.x: APTEL was established on 24 August 2004.
59.tq: Distinguish the establishment date of the appellate body from the Act’s notification date.

59.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity?
o: Regulates only renewable-energy exchanges; its Chairperson is the Union Finance Minister.
Publishes the National Electricity Plan; its Chairperson heads the CEA.
Fixes retail tariffs in all States; its Chairperson is appointed by a State Government.
Hears appeals against CERC and SERC orders; its Chairperson is usually a retired Supreme Court judge.
59.x: APTEL hears appeals against CERC and SERC orders, and its Chairperson is usually a retired Supreme Court judge.
59.tq: Use the body-function-authority combination to reject swapped roles.

59.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the following developments?
A. Establishment of CERC
B. Notification of the Electricity Act, 2003
C. Establishment of APTEL
D. Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020
59.x: CERC was set up in 1998, the Electricity Act was notified in 2003, APTEL was established in 2004, and the Consumer Rules were issued in 2020.
59.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intervening dates.

59.s:
Which of the following are recognised power exchanges in India?
1. Indian Energy Exchange
2. Power Exchange India Limited
3. Hindustan Power Exchange
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: IEX, PXIL and HPX are the power exchanges identified in the electricity market framework.
59.tq: Use the complete-list option when all three named exchanges belong to the group.

59.s: The Real-Time Market in the Indian electricity market was introduced in
59.x: The Real-Time Market started in 2020.
59.tq: Discriminate between the adjacent years of RTM and GDAM.

59.s: The Green Day-Ahead Market was introduced in
59.x: The Green Day-Ahead Market started in 2021.
59.tq: Use the one-year sequence between RTM and GDAM.

59.s: The Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and Related Matters) Rules, 2022 enable discoms to
o: fix tariffs without approval of the regulator
obtain free power from renewable generators
clear old dues in instalments and face restriction of power-exchange access for defaulting entities
59.x: The 2022 Rules permit discoms to clear old dues in instalments and provide for cutting power-exchange access for defaulters.
59.tq: Apply the rule to a defaulting discom rather than confuse it with tariff regulation.

59.s: Energy Statistics (India) is published by
o: Energy Institute of the United Kingdom
National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power
59.x: Energy Statistics (India) is published by the CSO, now the National Statistics Office, under MoSPI.
59.tq: Distinguish the national statistical publication from power-sector and international reports.

59.s: Which one of the following publications is correctly matched with its publisher?
o: World Energy Outlook — Central Electricity Authority
Statistical Review of World Energy — International Energy Agency
World Energy Outlook — International Energy Agency
59.x: The World Energy Outlook is published by the International Energy Agency in Paris. The Statistical Review of World Energy is published by the Energy Institute.
59.tq: Identify the publication whose publisher is correctly paired rather than swapping international agencies.

59.s: The Statistical Review of World Energy is published by the
o: Energy Institute of the United Kingdom
59.x: The Statistical Review of World Energy is published by the Energy Institute of the UK; it was formerly associated with BP.
59.tq: Use the publisher’s institutional identity, not the former publisher’s name.

59.s:
Which of the following publications are associated with NITI Aayog?
1. India Energy Security Scenarios 2047
2. Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero
3. National Electricity Plan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: NITI Aayog is associated with India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 and the 2026 Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero. The National Electricity Plan is a CEA report.
59.tq: Reject the statement that assigns a CEA publication to NITI Aayog.

59.s: India is the world’s ____ largest producer of electricity.
59.x: India is the third-largest electricity producer in the world.
59.tq: Test the global rank directly without confusing production with renewable capacity.

59.s: India’s electricity generation increased from 1,020.2 billion units in 2013–14 to approximately how much in 2024–25?
59.x: Electricity generation rose from 1,020.2 BU in 2013–14 to 1,830 BU in 2024–25.
59.tq: Use the two-endpoint comparison and identify the later value.

59.s: Which of the following correctly states India’s recent global positions in renewable energy?
o: Third in renewable capacity, fourth in wind and third in solar
Third in renewable capacity, second in wind and fourth in solar
Fifth in renewable capacity, fourth in wind and third in solar
Fourth in renewable capacity, third in wind and fifth in solar
59.x: The recent figures place India third in renewable capacity, fourth in wind and third in solar.
59.tq: Keep the three rankings in their respective categories and avoid cross-swapping them.

59.s: Solar power was the world’s second-largest growth market in
59.x: Solar was the second-largest growth market in 2025.
59.tq: Separate the market-growth year from the renewable-ranking years.

59.s: Which statement correctly describes the older and newer figures relating to India’s renewable-energy rankings?
o: Older figures placed India third in renewable energy and fourth in solar; newer figures place it fifth in both.
Older figures placed India fifth in renewable energy and third in solar; newer figures place it fourth in both.
Older figures placed India fourth in renewable energy and fifth in solar; newer figures place it third in renewable capacity and third in solar.
The ranking remained unchanged at fourth in renewable energy and fifth in solar.
59.x: Older figures cited fourth in renewable energy and fifth in solar, while newer figures cite third in renewable capacity and third in solar; another recent source also reports fourth for renewable capacity, reflecting the stated source variation.
59.tq: Track changing rankings by separating older and newer reference figures.

59.s: Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY), launched in November 2015, was primarily intended for which of the following purposes?
o: Financial turnaround and revival of DISCOMs
Universal installation of nuclear power plants
Privatisation of all State Electricity Boards
59.x: UDAY was launched in November 2015 to achieve the financial turnaround and revival of distribution companies.
59.tq: Directly identify the purpose associated with the named scheme.

59.s: Which one of the following is a demand-side intervention under UDAY?
59.x: The use of energy-efficient LED bulbs is a demand-side intervention. Coal swapping, transformer upgrades and feeder metering are operational interventions.
59.tq: Separate operational measures from measures that reduce consumer-side energy demand.

59.s: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) was conveyed on 3 December 2014. Which one of the following correctly describes it?
o: A scheme exclusively for nuclear-power generation
A scheme for last-mile household connections in urban areas only
A rural power scheme that subsumed RGGVY and aimed at 24x7 power in rural India
A scheme for privatisation of rural DISCOMs
59.x: DDUGJY was conveyed on 3 December 2014, subsumed the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana and aimed at providing 24x7 power in rural India.
59.tq: Combine the date, predecessor scheme and principal objective of a government programme.

59.s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for DDUGJY?
59.x: Rural Electrification Corporation, or REC, is the nodal agency for DDUGJY.
59.tq: Use the institutional-association approach to identify the nodal agency.

59.s:
Consider the following components of DDUGJY:
1. Separation of agricultural and non-agricultural feeders
2. Strengthening of sub-transmission and distribution systems
3. Development of micro-grids and off-grid systems
4. Metering of distribution transformers, feeders and consumers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All four are components of DDUGJY. The scheme also includes rural electrification as a major component.
59.tq: Test the completeness of a scheme by checking whether each listed component belongs to its design.

59.s: Under DDUGJY, the normal grant component and the additional milestone-linked support are respectively:
59.x: DDUGJY provides a 60% grant and additional support of up to 15% linked to milestones. For special-category States, the corresponding figures are 85% and 5%.
59.tq: Recall the paired percentage structure and distinguish ordinary from special-category States.

59.s: Approximately how many households had been electrified under Saubhagya?
59.x: Approximately 2.86 crore households were electrified under Saubhagya.
59.tq: Distinguish close numerical alternatives by retaining the exact crore figure.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between feeder separation, RDSS and PM-KUSUM?
o: Feeder separation ended with DDUGJY and has no connection with later schemes.
Feeder separation continues under RDSS, and separated agricultural feeders are subsequently solarised under PM-KUSUM.
PM-KUSUM separates urban commercial feeders under RDSS.
RDSS replaced feeder separation with only off-grid micro-grids.
59.x: Feeder separation continues under RDSS, while separated agricultural feeders can subsequently be solarised under PM-KUSUM.
59.tq: Trace the policy sequence from an infrastructure intervention to its later application.

59.s: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) was introduced in which year, and what is its stated total outlay?
59.x: RDSS was introduced in 2021 with an outlay of ₹3.03 lakh crore.
59.tq: Match the programme year with its distinctive outlay figure.

59.s:
Which of the following features characterises RDSS?
1. It is reform-based.
2. It is results-linked.
3. It has been extended by two years up to FY 2027-28.
4. REC and PFC are its nodal agencies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All four statements are correct. RDSS is reform-based and results-linked, has been extended to FY 2027-28, and uses REC and PFC as nodal agencies.
59.tq: Use a four-part scheme profile rather than relying on its name alone.

59.s:
Under RDSS, smart metering is implemented on which model, with priority given to which consumers?

1. TOTEX model under a public-private partnership framework
2. Government offices
3. Commercial consumers
4. Commercial and industrial consumers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: RDSS smart metering follows the TOTEX model under PPP, with priority for government offices and commercial and C&I consumers.
59.tq: Link the implementation model with the priority consumer categories.

59.s: Which of the following correctly represents the smart-metering figures under RDSS?
59.x: Approximately 4.7 crore smart meters had been installed, while 20.34 crore had been sanctioned under RDSS.
59.tq: Compare installed and sanctioned quantities without reversing their status.

59.s: Which statement regarding the metering technology requirements under RDSS is correct?
o: One hundred per cent Indian HES and MDMS systems are mandated.
HES and MDMS are excluded from the scheme.
At least 50% Indian HES and MDMS systems are mandated.
Only imported HES and MDMS systems are permitted.
59.x: RDSS mandates 100% Indian HES and MDMS systems for the specified smart-metering programme.
59.tq: Watch for the exact percentage in a technology-procurement requirement.

59.s: What is the role of Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) in the smart-metering context?
o: It replaces REC as the nodal agency of RDSS.
It certifies all nuclear power plants.
It acts as the regulator for electricity tariffs.
It undertakes demand aggregation for large smart-metering programmes.
59.x: EESL undertakes demand aggregation for large smart-metering programmes.
59.tq: Identify the specific operational role rather than confusing it with a regulatory or nodal role.

59.s: EESL entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with PNGRB for smart meters relating to:
59.x: EESL entered into an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters, where PNG means piped natural gas.
59.tq: Expand the abbreviation and match the organisation with the correct utility sector.

59.s: Under the Rights of Consumers Rules, a new electricity connection is to be provided within which maximum periods in metropolitan, municipal and rural areas respectively?
59.x: The prescribed periods are 3 days in metropolitan areas, 7 days in municipal areas and 15 days in rural areas.
59.tq: Retain the geographical order while matching each area with its time limit.

59.s: The Rights of Consumers Rules had been adopted by how many States and Union Territories?
59.x: The Rights of Consumers Rules had been adopted by all 36 States and Union Territories.
59.tq: Distinguish the total number of adopting units from the number of States alone.

59.s: Under the Late Payment Surcharge Rules, 2022, legacy electricity dues were to be cleared through:
o: Waiver by the Central Electricity Authority
A single cash payment with penal interest
Conversion into equity of generating companies
59.x: The rules provided for clearance of legacy dues through interest-free equated monthly instalments.
59.tq: Identify the consumer-relief mechanism that follows from the rule’s purpose.

59.s: The dues payable to generating companies declined from approximately ₹1.35–1.39 lakh crore in 2022 to which amount in January 2026?
59.x: The dues fell to ₹4,927 crore by January 2026, representing an approximately 96% reduction from the 2022 level.
59.tq: Handle Indian-numbering figures carefully and avoid shifting a zero or decimal place.

59.s: The payment cycle for electricity-sector dues changed from 178 days in FY 2020-21 to how many days in FY 2024-25?
59.x: The payment cycle declined from 178 days in FY21 to 113 days in FY25.
59.tq: Compare the initial and latest values in the stated time sequence.

59.s: The amended Electricity Rules provide for automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes. What is the principal intended effect of this provision?
o: It prevents generating companies from changing fuel sources.
It prevents new deficits from arising due to unrecovered fuel-cost changes.
It abolishes all electricity tariffs for agricultural consumers.
It transfers all distribution losses to consumers without regulation.
59.x: Automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes is intended to prevent new deficits caused by delays in recovering such costs.
59.tq: Infer the financial consequence from the mechanism described in the rule.

59.s: AT&C loss in the electricity sector refers to:
o: The difference between average cost and average revenue per unit
The unpaid subsidy released by the State Government
Technical and commercial losses, including theft, billing and collection inefficiency
Only technical losses in transmission lines
59.x: AT&C loss combines technical and commercial losses, including losses from theft, billing inefficiency and collection inefficiency.
59.tq: Distinguish a composite loss metric from the separate ACS-ARR financial gap.

59.s: AT&C losses declined from 22.62% in FY 2013-14 to what level in FY 2024-25?
59.x: AT&C losses declined to 15.04% in FY25 from 22.62% in FY14. The figure of 16.12% relates to FY24 in an older set of values.
59.tq: Match the exact percentage with the correct financial year and reject the nearby-year figure.

59.s: The ACS-ARR gap is defined as:
o: Average cost of supply minus average revenue realised per unit
Average revenue realised minus average cost of supply per consumer
Average subsidy received minus total generation cost
Annual commercial loss minus annual technical loss
59.x: ACS-ARR gap means average cost of supply minus average revenue realised per unit.
59.tq: Expand both components of the abbreviation and preserve their order in the subtraction.

59.s: The ACS-ARR gap decreased from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY 2013-14 to what level in FY 2024-25?
59.x: The ACS-ARR gap fell to ₹0.06 per kWh in FY25 from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY14. This equals 6 paise per unit, not 0.06 paise.
59.tq: Check both the unit and the decimal placement in a small financial figure.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the financial performance of DISCOMs?
o: They posted a profit of ₹67,962 crore in FY25 after a loss of ₹2,701 crore in 2013-14.
They posted identical profits in both years.
They posted a loss of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 after a profit of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
They posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 after a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
59.x: DISCOMs posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25, compared with a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
59.tq: Track both the direction of change and the year attached to each amount.

59.s: The PFC Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise grades DISCOMs annually on which basis?
o: Only the number of rural households connected
59.x: PFC annually grades DISCOMs on their financial and operational performance through its Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise.
59.tq: Identify the two-dimensional basis of the institutional rating.

59.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Delhi DISCOMs — Privatised in 2002
2. Odisha DISCOMs — Taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21
3. Bhiwandi input-based franchise model — Torrent, 2007
4. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Recommendation for active DISCOM privatisation by States

Select the correct answer using the code below.
59.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Delhi’s DISCOMs were privatised in 2002, Odisha’s were taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21, Bhiwandi pioneered the cited franchise model in 2007, and the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended active State-led privatisation.
59.tq: Start with the sure historical pair and verify the remaining institutional associations.

59.s: The input-based franchisee model in electricity distribution was first implemented at Bhiwandi by:
59.x: The input-based franchisee model was first implemented at Bhiwandi by Torrent in 2007.
59.tq: Match the place, implementing entity and year in a reform-history question.

59.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh DISCOMs?
o: APSPDCL — Headquartered at Hyderabad after its 2020 re-formation
59.x: APSPDCL is headquartered at Tirupati. APCPDCL was re-formed in 2020 at Vijayawada; the older pre-2014 APCPDCL was associated with Hyderabad.
59.tq: Find the single location and organisational-history mismatch.

59.s: Which statement correctly describes the change involving APSPDCL after bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: It was re-formed at Vijayawada in 2020.
It took over all districts formerly served by APEPDCL.
It took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
59.x: At bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, APSPDCL took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
59.tq: Identify the specific territorial transfer rather than the headquarters of the DISCOM.

59.s: What proportion of APSPDCL’s agricultural feeders had been segregated, based on the reported figures of 312 out of 3,015?
59.x: 312 out of 3,015 is approximately 10.3%, or about 10%.
59.tq: Convert the reported numerator and denominator into an approximate percentage.

59.s: The State stood guarantor for a ₹300 crore HUDCO loan obtained by which entity for rural distribution transformers?
59.x: The State stood guarantor for a ₹300 crore HUDCO loan to AP Power Finance Corporation for rural distribution transformers.
59.tq: Match the guarantor, lender, borrower and purpose in the financing arrangement.

59.s: The National Generation and Availability Plan (NGAP) 2026–27 to 2035–36 envisages a total power-generation capacity of:
59.x: The CEA’s NGAP 2026–27 to 2035–36 plans for 1,121 GW of generation capacity.
59.tq: Direct numerical recall with closely related capacity figures as distractors.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the CEA’s NGAP 2026–27 to 2035–36:
1. It envisages 1,121 GW of generation capacity.
2. About 70% of the planned capacity is to be from non-fossil sources.
3. It covers the period from 2026–27 to 2035–36.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All three statements are correct: the plan covers 2026–27 to 2035–36, targets 1,121 GW of capacity and assigns about 70% of it to non-fossil sources.
59.tq: Statement-combination question requiring the period, total capacity and source composition to be checked together.

59.s: Which one of the following best illustrates the distinction between installed capacity and actual electricity generation in India?
o: Coal accounts for 6–10% of present electricity generation and over 50% of installed capacity.
Non-fossil sources account for about 22% of installed capacity but over 50% of electricity output.
Non-fossil sources account for over 50% of installed capacity but only about 22% of electricity output.
Solar curtailment ensures that installed capacity and generation remain equal.
59.x: Non-fossil sources constitute more than half of installed capacity, but their share in actual output is only about 22%, demonstrating the capacity-generation gap.
59.tq: Comparison-table reasoning: distinguish the capacity share from the generation share.

59.s: Approximately how much renewable-energy capacity is reported to have no power-purchase agreement (PPA)?
59.x: Around 40 GW of renewable-energy projects are reported to have no PPAs.
59.tq: Figure-based recall using nearby electricity-sector numbers as distractors.

59.s: NITI’s long-term projection regarding coal’s share in India’s electricity generation envisages that it may fall from about 74% to:
59.x: NITI projects that coal’s share of electricity generation could decline from about 74% to 6–10% by 2070.
59.tq: Trend-and-end-point trap: match the starting share, projected range and target year.

59.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the target mentioned under ICEP-2024 for renewable-energy capacity is:
59.x: The ICEP-2024 target for renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh is 160 GW.
59.tq: Direct recall of a state-specific target, with national and loss figures as distractors.

59.s:
Assertion (A): An El Niño year can adversely affect wind and hydropower generation.
Reason (R): Variations associated with El Niño can reduce wind availability and hydrological conditions relevant to power generation.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
59.x: Both statements are true, and the reason explains why El Niño conditions can hurt wind and hydropower output.
59.tq: Causal assertion–reason test linking a climate phenomenon with two electricity sources.

59.s:
Which of the following developments is associated with the present electricity-sector debate?
1. Solar curtailment
2. Stranded gas-based power plants of approximately 25 GW
3. A gap between installed capacity and actual generation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: Solar curtailment, approximately 25 GW of stranded gas plants and the capacity-versus-generation gap are all identified as important electricity-sector concerns.

60.s: The plant load factor (PLF) range generally indicated for coal-based power plants is
60.x: Coal-based plants have a PLF range of about 60–85%, compared with 20–35% for wind power.

60.s: During the heatwave-related power stress in April 2026, the peak electricity demand reached approximately
60.x: Peak electricity demand reached approximately 256 GW in April 2026.

60.s: Flue-gas desulphurisation (FGD) scrubbers installed in thermal power plants primarily trap
60.x: FGD scrubbers trap sulphur dioxide in the stacks of thermal power plants.
60.tq: Match the pollution-control equipment with the pollutant it removes.

60.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated characteristic of coal-based power plants?
o: They are a major source of PM2.5.
They are heavy users of water.
They produce no significant air pollution when operated continuously.
They are the largest source of carbon dioxide among the listed power sources.
60.x: Coal plants are major sources of carbon dioxide and PM2.5 and are heavy water users. Continuous operation does not eliminate their air-pollution impacts.
60.tq: Reject the absolute statement that contradicts the stated environmental impacts.

60.s: The projected thermal capacity requirement for the period 2023–2035 was stated as approximately
60.x: The projected thermal capacity requirement for 2023–2035 is approximately 307 GW.

60.s: The policy of mandating biomass co-firing in coal-based power plants specifies a biomass share of

60.x: The 5% biomass co-firing policy was implemented under the SAMARTH mission.
60.tq: Identify the programme directly associated with the stated reform measure.

60.s:
Which of the following are measures associated with flexible operation of the power system?
1. Pumped storage
2. Batteries
3. Cyclical operation of gas plants
4. Hydro optimisation alongside coal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: Flexible operation includes pumped storage, batteries, cyclical operation of gas plants and optimisation of hydro generation alongside coal.
60.tq: Treat the listed flexibility measures as a combined system-management toolkit.

60.s: Under Revised SHAKTI introduced in May 2025, Window-I provides coal to central and State plants at
o: a subsidised price fixed by State electricity regulators
a price determined only through bidding
a premium over the notified price
60.x: Under Window-I of Revised SHAKTI, central and State plants receive coal at the notified price.
