66.s: India added 6.34 GW of wind capacity during calendar year 2025. This addition was approximately what percentage higher than the 3.42 GW added in 2024?
66.x: The 2025 addition of 6.34 GW was reported as 85.4% higher than the 3.42 GW added in 2024.
66.tq: Match the percentage with the directly stated year-on-year comparison.

66.s: Which of the following correctly matches India’s installed wind-capacity milestones?
66.x: India’s installed wind capacity was 54.51 GW at the end of 2025 and 56.09 GW on 31 March 2026.
66.tq: Start with the sure date-value pair and eliminate swapped milestones.

66.s: According to the latest capacity comparison given, wind accounted for what percentage of India’s total power capacity?
66.x: The latest stated wind capacity of 56.81 GW represented 10.47% of the total 542 GW capacity.
66.tq: Separate capacity share from renewable share and capacity-utilisation figures.

66.s: Which renewable energy source had the largest installed capacity in the stated comparison?
66.x: Solar power, at 157.05 GW, was the largest renewable source in the comparison, followed by wind at 56.81 GW and large hydro at 51.96 GW.
66.tq: Rank the comparable values before selecting the largest source.

66.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wind was the second-largest renewable-energy source in the stated capacity comparison.
2. Wind capacity was just ahead of large hydropower.
3. Large hydropower had an installed capacity of 51.96 GW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All three statements are correct: wind ranked second at 56.81 GW, just ahead of large hydro at 51.96 GW.
66.tq: Use the ranking and numerical values together rather than treating them separately.

66.s: What was the record addition to India’s wind capacity during financial year 2025–26?
66.x: The record addition during FY 2025–26 was 6.05 GW. The 6.34 GW figure refers to calendar year 2025.
66.tq: Distinguish the financial-year figure from the calendar-year figure.

66.s: The record wind-capacity addition of 6.05 GW in FY 2025–26 was approximately what percentage above the addition in FY 2024–25?
66.x: The 6.05 GW addition in FY 2025–26 was reported to be 46% above the addition in FY 2024–25.
66.tq: Match the record figure with its stated comparative percentage.

66.s: India’s stated national target for installed wind capacity by 2030 is:
66.x: The national target is to reach 100 GW of installed wind capacity by 2030.
66.tq: Distinguish the wind-specific target from the broader renewable-energy target.

66.s: What is the stated offshore-wind capacity target for India by 2030?
66.x: India’s stated offshore-wind target is 30 GW by 2030.
66.tq: Identify the offshore-specific target rather than the total wind target.

66.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the long-term wind-capacity targets mentioned for India?
o: 100 GW by 2030 and 155 GW by 2035/156 GW by 2036
30 GW offshore by 2030 and 500 GW wind by 2035
66.x: The stated targets are 100 GW by 2030 and either 155 GW by 2035 or 156 GW by 2036, depending on the cited projection.
66.tq: Keep near-identical long-term target figures tied to their correct years.

66.s: India’s reported non-fossil capacity was 283.46 GW, representing what share of total capacity in the stated comparison?
66.x: The reported non-fossil capacity was 283.46 GW, equal to 52.27% in the stated comparison.
66.tq: Distinguish the December 2025 percentage from the separately reported capacity-share figure.

66.s: India’s annual turbine manufacturing capacity and the approximate degree of indigenisation are respectively:
66.x: The wind-turbine manufacturing base has a capacity of about 24 GW per year, with 70–80% indigenisation.
66.tq: Match the production figure with its corresponding indigenisation range.

66.s: Which of the following is the correct order of the top three countries by installed wind-power capacity?
o: China, Germany, United States of America
United States of America, China, Germany
China, United States of America, Germany
Germany, China, United States of America
66.x: The top three countries are China, the United States of America and Germany, in that order.
66.tq: Treat the ranking as an ordered sequence and check the middle position carefully.

66.s: Global Wind Day is observed on:
66.x: Global Wind Day is observed on 15 June.
66.tq: Use the exact date rather than confusing it with World Environment Day or the summer solstice.

66.s: India hosted the 2026 Global Wind Day conference at which location, with the theme ‘Wind Energy: From Ambition to Acceleration’?
66.x: The 2026 Global Wind Day conference was hosted in Goa with the theme ‘Wind Energy: From Ambition to Acceleration’.
66.tq: Link the event theme with its stated host location.

66.s: In a horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT), the rotor axis is:
o: Independent of wind direction and rotor position
Perpendicular to the wind direction and fixed vertically
66.x: In a HAWT, the rotor axis is parallel to the wind. Such turbines commonly use three blades and require yaw control.
66.tq: Discriminate HAWT from VAWT using the orientation of the rotor axis.

66.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with a vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT)?
o: Its axis is parallel to the wind and it necessarily has three blades
It has higher efficiency than all horizontal-axis turbines
Its axis is vertical and it can accept wind from any direction
It can operate only when wind direction is constant
66.x: A VAWT has a vertical axis and can take wind from any direction. Its efficiency is generally lower than that of standard horizontal-axis utility turbines.
66.tq: Use the defining orientation and directional feature of the turbine type.

66.s: The Betz limit states that the maximum fraction of wind’s kinetic energy that can be captured by a wind turbine is approximately:
66.x: The Betz limit is 16/27, or approximately 59.3% of the wind’s kinetic energy.
66.tq: Recognise the characteristic fraction and convert it to the stated percentage.

66.s: According to the power law for wind turbines, power varies with:
o: The square of wind speed only
The cube of wind speed and the swept area
The inverse of wind speed and rotor diameter
The cube of air pressure only
66.x: Wind-turbine power varies with the cube of wind speed and with the swept area.
66.tq: Focus on the two variables in the power relationship and reject altered exponents.

66.s: Capacity Utilisation Factor of a power plant is best expressed as:
o: Installed capacity divided by annual fuel consumption
Maximum possible output divided by actual output
Annual generation divided by transmission loss
Actual output divided by output at full rated power over the relevant time
66.x: Capacity Utilisation Factor is the ratio of actual output to the output possible at full rated power over the relevant period.
66.tq: Apply the numerator–denominator relationship rather than relying on the term alone.

66.s: Which one of the following statements about onshore and offshore wind power is NOT correct?
o: Offshore projects eliminate all environmental and navigational risks.
Floating turbines can be used in deep water.
Offshore sites generally have stronger and steadier winds.
Onshore projects are generally cheaper and easier to maintain.
66.x: Offshore projects do not eliminate risks; they may involve corrosion, undersea cables, navigation issues and marine-ecology concerns.
66.tq: Identify the absolute claim contradicted by the stated disadvantages of offshore projects.

66.s: Which statement correctly describes IEC wind-turbine classes?
o: The classes are based exclusively on turbine colour and blade number.
Class I is intended for high-wind sites and Class III for low-wind sites.
Class III is designed for the highest wind speeds.
Class I is intended only for offshore sites and Class III only for deserts.
66.x: IEC turbine classes are determined by site wind speed: Class I is for high-wind sites and Class III for low-wind sites.
66.tq: Compare the end classes and watch for reversal of high-wind and low-wind applications.

66.s: Which of the following correctly describes the energy-conversion sequence in a wind turbine?
o: Mechanical energy in the generator → wind energy → electricity
Electrical energy → chemical energy → kinetic energy
Wind’s kinetic energy → blade/rotor rotation → generator → electricity
66.x: Wind’s kinetic energy rotates the blades and rotor; the generator then converts the mechanical energy into electricity.
66.tq: Follow the conversion chain from the natural source to the final output.

66.s: Which of the following correctly matches the hub height with the assessed wind potential?
66.x: The assessed potential is 695.5 GW at a 120-metre hub height and 1,163.9 GW at a 150-metre hub height.
66.tq: Start with the lower hub-height value and check the increase at the higher height.

66.s: The estimated wind-energy potential at a hub height of 150 metres is:
66.x: The estimated potential at a 150-metre hub height is 1,163.9 GW.
66.tq: Match the exact hub-height figure with its corresponding potential.

66.s: The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) is headquartered at:
66.x: NIWE is located in Chennai and functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
66.tq: Use the organisation–headquarters association rather than the locations of major windy states.

66.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Institute of Wind Energy:
1. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
2. It undertakes wind-resource assessment and identification of potential sites.
3. It prepares the Indian Wind Atlas.
4. It provides support for testing and certification of wind technologies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All four statements correctly describe NIWE’s institutional status and functions, including resource assessment, site identification, atlas preparation, testing and certification support.
66.tq: Check the organisation’s status and each listed function before choosing the complete code.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated function or role of NIWE?
o: Formulation of monetary policy for renewable-energy banks
Preparation of the Indian Wind Atlas
66.x: NIWE undertakes wind-resource assessment, site identification, atlas preparation and related testing and certification support. Formulation of monetary policy is not its role.
66.tq: Find the institutional function that belongs to a different policy domain.

66.s:
Assertion (A): Offshore wind projects generally achieve a higher capacity factor than comparable onshore projects.
Reason (R): Offshore locations generally experience stronger and steadier winds.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
66.x: Both statements are true, and stronger and steadier offshore winds explain the generally higher capacity factor of offshore projects.
66.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the comparison in the assertion.

66.s:
Assertion (A): Onshore wind is considered the cheapest new electricity source globally.
Reason (R): Onshore wind projects have no maintenance or land-related costs.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
66.x: The assertion is true as stated. The reason is false because onshore projects still involve land use and maintenance, even though they are generally cheaper than offshore projects.
66.tq: Reject an absolute reason while retaining the supported assertion.

66.s: The nodal agency for offshore wind energy development in India is:
66.x: The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) is the nodal agency for offshore wind energy development.
66.tq: Distinguish the nodal agency from related renewable-energy institutions.

66.s: The National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015 primarily provides a framework for developing offshore wind farms in India's:
66.x: The policy provides the framework for offshore wind farms in India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
66.tq: Test the exact geographical scope of a policy.

66.s: The initial offshore wind development zones identified for India are located off the coasts of:
66.x: The identified zones are off the Gujarat coast and the Tamil Nadu coast, including the Gulf of Mannar.
66.tq: Use location-based elimination among coastal states.

66.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the offshore wind Viability Gap Funding scheme:
1. It was approved in 2024.
2. It covers the first 1 GW of offshore wind projects.
3. It provides 500 MW each off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme approved in 2024 covers 1 GW, divided equally between Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, with an outlay of ₹7,453 crore.
66.tq: Combine the approval year, capacity and geographical split.

66.s: The Viability Gap Funding approved for the first 1 GW of offshore wind projects amounts to:
66.x: The approved VGF scheme provides ₹7,453 crore for the first 1 GW of offshore wind projects.
66.tq: Distinguish the project-specific funding figure from other energy-sector outlays.

66.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Partner)
a. United Kingdom
b. Denmark
c. Belgium

a. Offshore Wind Taskforce, February 2026
b. Agreement of 2019, renewed in May 2025
c. Reaffirmation at WEF 2026

List-II (Cooperation)
i. India-Belgium
 ii. India-Denmark
 iii. India-UK
66.x: The United Kingdom is associated with the Offshore Wind Taskforce, Denmark with the 2019 agreement renewed in May 2025, and Belgium with the WEF 2026 reaffirmation.
66.tq: Start from the distinctive date and institutional pair.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage generally associated with offshore wind energy?
o: Lower maintenance and installation costs than onshore wind
66.x: Offshore wind generally benefits from stronger, steadier winds and less land conflict, but it is costlier and harder to maintain than onshore wind.
66.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the list of advantages and disadvantages.

66.s: Which of the following best describes the National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy, 2018?
o: It replaces wind power with solar power in all renewable-energy parks.
It permits only separate wind and solar plants connected to different grids.
It restricts hybrid projects to off-grid rural applications.
It promotes wind turbines and solar photovoltaic systems at the same grid connection point.
66.x: The policy promotes co-location of wind turbines and solar PV at the same point of grid connection.
66.tq: Test the precise operational definition of a policy.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about wind-solar hybrid projects:
1. They can improve the use of land and transmission infrastructure.
2. They can reduce variability in renewable power generation.
3. They are intended only for isolated micro-grids.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hybrid projects are also designed for large grid-connected systems, so statement 3 is false.
66.tq: Reject the restrictive word 'only' and retain the two stated benefits.

66.s: Round-the-clock renewable-energy tenders generally combine:
66.x: RTC renewable-energy tenders bundle wind, solar and storage to provide a firm supply of electricity.
66.tq: Identify the components of a bundled power-supply model.

66.s: The waiver of ISTS charges for eligible renewable-energy projects applied to projects commissioned by:
66.x: The ISTS-charge waiver applied to eligible projects commissioned by 30 June 2025.
66.tq: Distinguish a specific deadline from nearby policy dates.

66.s: Which of the following correctly represents the financing pattern of Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I?
66.x: The financing pattern is MNRE 40%, KfW 40% and the States 20%.
66.tq: Match each contributor with its precise percentage share.

66.s: Repowering of a wind turbine means:
o: Moving an old turbine to a different State without changing its equipment
Converting a wind farm entirely into a solar park
Reducing the height and capacity of existing turbines
Replacing ageing turbines with larger and modern turbines at the same site
66.x: Repowering replaces ageing, less efficient turbines with more powerful modern units at the same windy site to increase generation.
66.tq: Apply the definition to a practical wind-farm situation.

66.s: The first National Repowering Policy for wind turbines was issued in:
66.x: The National Repowering Policy was issued in 2016.
66.tq: Discriminate between the original policy year and the later revision.

66.s: The National Repowering Policy, 2016 was revised as the:
66.x: The 2016 policy was revised as the Repowering and Life Extension Policy, 2023.
66.tq: Distinguish the exact title of the revised policy from similar-sounding alternatives.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed as a support measure relevant to wind-energy development and repowering?
o: Generation Based Incentive for projects before 31 March 2017
Universal waiver of all transmission charges for projects commissioned after 2030
66.x: Accelerated depreciation, the pre-31 March 2017 GBI, the Wind RPO trajectory up to 2030 and tariff-based bidding are listed support measures. A universal waiver after 2030 is not stated as a support measure.
66.tq: Identify the invented policy condition among genuine incentives.

66.s: The Generation Based Incentive mentioned for wind projects applied to projects established before:
66.x: The Generation Based Incentive referred to projects established before 31 March 2017.
66.tq: Focus on the qualifying cut-off date rather than the general incentive name.

66.s: Andhra Pradesh is recognised as one of how many windy States in India?
66.x: Andhra Pradesh is one of the eight windy States identified for wind-energy development.
66.tq: Test the exact count in a State classification.

66.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for what share of India's renewable-energy potential?
66.x: Andhra Pradesh holds 9.10% of India's renewable-energy potential.
66.tq: Distinguish the precise percentage from nearby plausible shares.

66.s: The principal wind-farm cluster in Andhra Pradesh is located in:
o: North Coastal Andhra around Srikakulam and Vizianagaram
Coastal Andhra around Kakinada and Machilipatnam
Rayalaseema, particularly Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa
66.x: Wind farms are concentrated in Rayalaseema, especially in Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts.
66.tq: Use regional clustering to identify the correct geographical zone.

66.s: Ramagiri in Andhra Pradesh is notable for hosting a:
66.x: Ramagiri hosts a hybrid solar-wind park.
66.tq: Link a specific place with its distinctive energy project.

66.s: Which company is identified as the largest wind developer in Andhra Pradesh, with more than 1,700 MW?
66.x: Suzlon is identified as Andhra Pradesh's largest wind developer, with more than 1,700 MW.
66.tq: Match the company with its State-level development role.

66.s: Suzlon's S144 blade unit in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
66.x: The S144 blade unit is located at Hulikera in Kanekal mandal of Anantapur.
66.tq: Test a precise industrial-location association.

66.s: The S144 blade unit at Hulikera was opened on:
66.x: The S144 blade unit at Hulikera was opened on 25 August 2026.
66.tq: Distinguish the inauguration date from another 2026 energy-sector date.

66.s: The Central Electricity Authority projects Andhra Pradesh's wind capacity at approximately:
66.x: The CEA projects Andhra Pradesh's wind capacity at 8,257 MW and has indicated the need for an additional 4,200 MW to meet the RPO requirement up to 2035–36.
66.tq: Separate a future capacity projection from current installed capacity.

66.s: The CEA has indicated that Andhra Pradesh requires an additional wind capacity of about how much to meet its RPO up to 2035–36?
66.x: The CEA has indicated that Andhra Pradesh needs about 4,200 MW more to meet its RPO requirement up to 2035–36.
66.tq: Identify the incremental requirement rather than the total projected capacity.

66.s: Which climatic phenomenon was expected to reduce wind and hydropower output?
o: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole accompanied by heavy rainfall
Western disturbances accompanied by a cold wave
El Niño accompanied by a weak monsoon
La Niña accompanied by a strong monsoon
66.x: El Niño and a weak monsoon were expected to dent wind and hydro output.
66.tq: Connect the climatic condition with its stated energy-sector impact.

66.s: The quantity of solar-wind electricity reported as curtailed in the preceding year was:
66.x: The reported curtailment of solar-wind electricity was 2.1 TWh.
66.tq: Handle the decimal and unit carefully in a quantitative current-affairs fact.

66.s: A grid-variability incident involving oscillations from renewable energy generation in Rajasthan was reportedly felt at:
66.x: An oscillation originating from renewable-energy variability in Rajasthan was reportedly felt at Kudankulam.
66.tq: Match the reported grid event with its affected power station.

66.s: India's turbine manufacturing capacity is approximately how much per year, with indigenisation of about 70–80%?
66.x: India's turbine manufacturing capacity is about 24 GW per year, with 70–80% indigenisation.
66.tq: Combine the annual manufacturing capacity with its indigenisation context.

66.s: Which of the following demands has been raised by the wind industry?
o: Removal of all renewable purchase obligations
Exclusive government ownership of wind farms
PLI for large forgings and export incentives
A ban on domestic turbine manufacturing
66.x: The industry has sought a Production Linked Incentive for large forgings and export incentives.
66.tq: Identify the genuine industry-policy demand among reversed alternatives.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about wind-energy policy support:
1. Accelerated depreciation is a support measure.
2. Wind RPO has a trajectory up to 2030.
3. Tariff-based bidding is used as a support mechanism.
4. ISTS-charge waiver was linked to projects commissioned by 30 June 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All four statements are correct and represent the listed forms of support or policy facilitation for renewable-energy projects.
66.tq: Check each policy instrument independently before selecting the complete combination.

66.s: Which of the following correctly describes Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I?
o: It covered 8 States, about 9,700 ckm of lines, 22,600 MVA substations and about 24 GW renewable capacity.
It covered 7 States, about 20,000 ckm of lines and 50 GW renewable capacity.
It covered 9 States, about 9,700 ckm of lines and 20 GW renewable capacity.
It covered 8 States, about 20,000 ckm of lines and 24 GW renewable capacity.
66.x: GEC-I covered eight States and involved about 9,700 ckm of transmission lines, 22,600 MVA of substations and approximately 24 GW of renewable-energy integration.
66.tq: Check the phase-specific figures together instead of mixing GEC-I and GEC-II data.

66.s: Which of the following States was NOT included among the eight States covered by Intra-State GEC-I?
66.x: GEC-I included Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu. Telangana was not included in the listed eight-State group.
66.tq: Find the outsider by comparing each option with the complete membership list.

66.s: The financing pattern for Intra-State GEC-I was:
o: MNRE 50%, KfW loan 25% and State utility 25%
MNRE 20%, KfW loan 40% and State utility 40%
MNRE 40%, KfW loan 20% and State utility 40%
MNRE 40%, KfW loan 40% and State utility 20%
66.x: The cost-sharing pattern was MNRE 40%, KfW of Germany loan 40% and State utility contribution 20%.
66.tq: Match each percentage with the correct financing institution or agency.

66.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Intra-State GEC-II is correct?
o: It was approved in 2022 for eight States and about 24 GW of renewable energy.
It was approved in 2015 for eight States and 24 GW of renewable energy.
It was approved in 2025 for seven States and about 50 GW of renewable energy.
It was approved in 2022 for seven States and about 20 GW of renewable energy.
66.x: Intra-State GEC-II was approved in 2022 for seven States and was designed to support about 20 GW of renewable energy.
66.tq: Discriminate the second phase using its approval year, State count and capacity.

66.s:
With reference to renewable-energy deployment, consider the following statements:
1. Gujarat leads installed renewable energy capacity with 42.58 GW.
2. Gujarat's share in the stated installed renewable-energy capacity is 16.5%.
3. The figures refer specifically to the current ranking of installed solar capacity alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Gujarat is stated to lead installed renewable energy with 42.58 GW and a 16.5% share. The figures are for installed renewable energy, not specifically solar capacity alone.
66.tq: Distinguish a broad category from a narrower category in a ranking statement.

66.s: According to the comparative cost assessment stated for 2025, which source was the cheapest new electricity source globally?
66.x: Onshore wind was identified as the cheapest source of new electricity globally, with costs falling by 4% in 2025.
66.tq: Avoid reversing the onshore–offshore cost comparison.

66.s: The cost of onshore wind electricity fell by what percentage in 2025?
66.x: The stated fall in the cost of onshore wind electricity in 2025 was 4%.
66.tq: Select the precise percentage rather than a rounded alternative.

67.s: The primary source of geothermal energy is:
o: Heat from the Earth's interior, largely associated with radioactive decay
Chemical energy released by surface oxidation
67.x: Geothermal energy originates from the internal heat of the Earth, much of which is generated by radioactive decay in its interior.
67.tq: Identify the source-process relationship rather than a surface manifestation.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
67.x: Tattapani geothermal field is located in Chhattisgarh. Puga is in Ladakh, Manikaran is in Himachal Pradesh and Cambay is in Gujarat.
67.tq: Start from the sure site–state pair and eliminate the swapped locations.

67.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Puga Valley and Chhumathang — Ladakh
2. Surajkund — Jharkhand
3. Tapovan — Uttarakhand
4. Godavari Valley — Telangana

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
67.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Godavari Valley field, including Manuguru, is in present-day Telangana, though it was earlier associated with Andhra Pradesh.
67.tq: Check each geographical pair independently, especially the historical-state distinction.

67.s: Which of the following is the correct location of India's first geothermal power project?
67.x: India's first geothermal power project is associated with Puga Valley in Ladakh and is being led by ONGC.
67.tq: Use the first-project clue and distinguish it from other geothermal fields.

67.s: India's first geothermal power project at Puga is being led by:
67.x: The Puga geothermal power project in Ladakh is ONGC-led.
67.tq: Match the project with the implementing organisation, not the surveying agency.

67.s: The world's first geothermal power generation was achieved at:
67.x: The world's first geothermal power generation took place at Larderello in Italy in 1904.
67.tq: Separate the world-first from the India-first project.

67.s: Larderello is associated with the world's first geothermal power generation in:
67.x: Larderello, Italy, recorded the world's first geothermal power generation in 1904.
67.tq: Use the date as the decisive numerical discriminator.

67.s: Which one of the following geothermal fields is located in Himachal Pradesh's Kullu region?
67.x: Manikaran is located in the Parvati Valley of Himachal Pradesh, in the Kullu region.
67.tq: Distinguish closely listed geothermal fields by their regional location.

67.s: Tattapani geothermal springs are noted for having temperatures approximately in the range of:
67.x: The Tattapani springs in Chhattisgarh are described as having temperatures of about 45–90°C.
67.tq: Select the stated range rather than inferring from the field's name.

67.s: Which of the following is NOT a listed geothermal province or region of India?
67.x: The listed geothermal regions include the Himalaya, Godavari Valley, Cambay, SONATA, Mahanadi, West Coast and Andaman-Nicobar. The Indo-Gangetic Plain is not included in that list.
67.tq: Find the option outside the stated geographical classification.

67.s: The Geological Survey of India has estimated India's geothermal potential at approximately:
67.x: India's estimated geothermal potential is about 10,600 MW from 381 hot springs, according to the stated GSI estimate.
67.tq: Match the capacity figure with the corresponding number of sites.

67.s:
Which of the following is a surface expression of geothermal energy?

1. Hot springs
2. Geysers
3. Volcanoes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Hot springs, geysers and volcanoes are all surface expressions of heat originating within the Earth.
67.tq: Recognise the common underlying process behind different surface manifestations.

67.s: Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) are designed to:
o: Prevent all water movement in geothermal fields
Convert solar radiation directly into electricity
Replace radioactive decay with chemical combustion
67.x: EGS technology artificially stimulates geothermal reservoirs to improve access to underground heat.
67.tq: Match the technology with its functional purpose.

67.s: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge associated with geothermal energy?
o: Subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids
67.x: The stated challenges are uneven reservoir distribution, high drilling costs, subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids. Geothermal energy necessarily depends on underground heat.
67.tq: Reject the absolute statement that contradicts the basic principle of the resource.

67.s: The National Policy on Geothermal Energy was notified by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy on:
67.x: India's National Policy on Geothermal Energy was notified by MNRE on 15 September 2025.
67.tq: Use the exact notification date to distinguish adjacent years.

67.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated focus of the National Policy on Geothermal Energy, 2025?
o: Exclusive promotion of coal-based geothermal substitutes
67.x: The policy focuses on research, technology, ecosystem and capacity development and supports the Net Zero 2070 objective. It does not promote the stated coal-based substitute.
67.tq: Identify the option that does not belong to the policy's stated objectives.

67.s: The National Policy on Geothermal Energy, 2025, envisages the development of how many pilot projects?
67.x: The policy provides for five pilot geothermal projects.
67.tq: Test the specific programme count rather than the number of geothermal provinces.

67.s: Which of the following correctly describes biogas?
o: A mixture mainly containing methane and carbon dioxide, produced by anaerobic digestion
A petroleum product obtained from crude oil
A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen produced by electrolysis
A pure methane gas produced in the presence of oxygen
67.x: Biogas is produced through anaerobic digestion of organic matter and mainly contains methane and carbon dioxide, along with small quantities of other gases.
67.tq: Discriminate between composition and production conditions.

67.s: Methane generally constitutes approximately what share of biogas?
67.x: Methane is the major component of biogas and generally accounts for about 50–75 percent.
67.tq: Select the stated composition range rather than the extreme percentage.

67.s: Gobar gas is best described as:
o: Gas produced only from municipal plastic waste
Compressed natural gas extracted from coal seams
67.x: Gobar gas is biogas generated from cattle dung.
67.tq: Distinguish the feedstock-specific term from the broader term biogas.

67.s: The final methane-forming step in biogas production is carried out by:
67.x: Methanogenic archaea, also called methanogens, carry out the final methane-forming step during anaerobic digestion.
67.tq: Identify the specific microbial group associated with the final process step.

67.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the residue left after biogas production is correct?
o: It is a good organic manure
It is suitable only for making petroleum
It is unusable because all nutrients are destroyed
67.x: The slurry remaining after anaerobic digestion is a useful organic manure.
67.tq: Apply the production-process knowledge to the by-product.

67.s: Compressed Biogas (CBG) is:
o: Unpurified biogas stored at atmospheric pressure
Compressed carbon dioxide used as a fuel
Purified and compressed biogas chemically identical to CNG
67.x: CBG is purified and compressed biogas. Chemically, it is identical to compressed natural gas and is considered renewable and carbon-neutral.
67.tq: Separate CBG from raw biogas and from similarly named fossil-fuel gases.

67.s:
Which of the following correctly states the nature of CBG?

1. It is renewable.
2. It is described as carbon-neutral.
3. It is chemically identical to CNG.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: CBG is renewable, is described as carbon-neutral and is chemically identical to CNG after purification and compression.
67.tq: Use the all-correct combination when each characteristic is independently supported.

67.s: SATAT, launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, aims primarily to promote:
o: CBG production from agricultural residue and municipal waste
Ethanol production only from imported crude oil
67.x: SATAT, or Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation, was launched in 2018 by MoPNG to promote CBG from agricultural residue and municipal waste.
67.tq: Expand the acronym and match the initiative with its ministry and objective.

67.s:
GOBARdhan is an umbrella initiative for converting cattle dung and farm solid waste into:

1. Compost
2. Biogas or CBG/bio-CNG
3. Petroleum crude

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung and farm solid waste into compost, biogas and CBG/bio-CNG. Petroleum crude is not an output of the initiative.
67.tq: Find the false output by distinguishing biological conversion from petroleum production.

67.s: GOBARdhan was launched in:
67.x: The GOBARdhan initiative was launched in 2018.
67.tq: Use the programme year as the distinguishing fact among nearby years.

67.s: The expansion of GOBARdhan is:
o: Generating Organic Biomass and Renewable Development
Government Organisation for Bioenergy and Rural Development Network
Green Organic Biogas and Renewable Development
67.x: GOBARdhan stands for Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan.
67.tq: Test the exact official expansion of a look-alike acronym.

67.s: The Biogas Programme is implemented under which programme and period?
67.x: The Biogas Programme is a component of the National Bioenergy Programme for 2021–26.
67.tq: Match the sub-programme with its parent programme and period.

67.s: Which of the following correctly matches a programme with its principal activity?
o: Biomass Power and Bagasse Co-generation Programme — power from agro-residue and sugar-mill bagasse
67.x: The Biomass Power and Bagasse Co-generation Programme supports power generation from agro-residue and sugar-mill bagasse.
67.tq: Match each programme with its stated sector rather than its broad energy category.

67.s: Biomass energy is best understood as:
o: Solar energy stored by plants through photosynthesis
Energy obtained from tidal currents alone
Heat stored only in the Earth's mantle
67.x: Biomass energy represents solar energy captured and stored by plants through photosynthesis. It may be burned directly or converted into biogas and biofuels.
67.tq: Trace the energy source through the biological conversion chain.

67.s: Which one of the following is an example of biomass energy?
67.x: Gobar gas is a form of biomass energy because it is produced from organic biological material, especially cattle dung.
67.tq: Classify the example according to its biological feedstock.

67.s: In bagasse cogeneration, sugar mills primarily:
o: Use municipal plastic to produce uranium
Store tidal water for drinking purposes
Burn sugarcane residue to produce steam and power together
67.x: Bagasse, the residue of sugarcane processing, is burned in sugar mills to generate steam and electricity together.
67.tq: Connect the industrial residue with its practical energy use.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Bioenergy Programme:

1. Its Phase-I period is from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026.
2. Its Phase-I outlay is ₹858 crore.
3. It is administered by MNRE through State Nodal Agencies.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All three statements are correct: Phase I covers 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026, has an outlay of ₹858 crore and is implemented by MNRE through State Nodal Agencies.
67.tq: Verify the period, financial figure and implementing structure separately.

67.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Bioenergy Programme?
67.x: The listed components are Waste to Energy, Biomass and Biogas. Deep-sea oil exploration is not a component of the National Bioenergy Programme.
67.tq: Find the unrelated sector among the programme components.

67.s:
Under the National Bioenergy Programme, the Waste to Energy component includes:

1. Biogas and BioCNG
2. Power from urban, industrial and farm waste
3. Small and medium rural biogas plants for cooking and lighting

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Waste to Energy covers biogas, BioCNG and power from urban, industrial and farm waste. Small and medium rural plants for cooking and lighting belong to the Biogas component.
67.tq: Separate closely related subcomponents instead of treating all activities as one category.

67.s: The inspection function under the National Bioenergy Programme is associated with:
o: National Institute of Ocean Technology, Chennai
Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy, Kapurthala
67.x: Inspection under the National Bioenergy Programme is associated with the Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy at Kapurthala, Punjab.
67.tq: Match the administrative function with the named institution and location.

67.s:
Which of the following set of models is correctly associated with the stated biogas application?

1. Zakariyapura — household units
2. Varanasi — centralised plant for a dairy
3. Banas — centralised large-scale model

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Zakariyapura represents household units, Varanasi a centralised dairy plant and Banas a centralised large-scale model.
67.tq: Match each place with its scale and application before selecting the code.

67.s: The co-firing of biomass pellets in 71 coal plants had reduced approximately how much carbon dioxide as of 31 July 2025?
67.x: Biomass co-firing had reduced approximately 3.57 million tonnes, or 3.57 MT, of CO2 by 31 July 2025.
67.tq: Convert the abbreviation MT correctly and avoid a misplaced decimal.

67.s: The floating-drum 'Gramalakshmi' gobar gas plant of the 1950s is associated with:
67.x: The floating-drum Gramalakshmi plant was pioneered by Jashbhai Patel in the 1950s and later popularised by KVIC.
67.tq: Match the named innovation with its pioneer rather than its later popularising organisation.

67.s: The Gramalakshmi gobar gas plant was later popularised by:
67.x: The Gramalakshmi floating-drum plant was popularised by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).
67.tq: Distinguish the inventor or pioneer from the organisation that popularised the technology.

67.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:

A. Launch of SATAT
B. Launch of GOBARdhan
C. Notification of National Policy on Geothermal Energy
D. First geothermal power generation at Larderello

Select the correct sequence.
67.x: Larderello recorded the first geothermal power generation in 1904, followed by SATAT and GOBARdhan in 2018, and the National Policy on Geothermal Energy in 2025.
67.tq: Place the century-old event first and then order the 2018 and 2025 initiatives.

67.s: As of August 2026, India's bio-power capacity was approximately:
67.x: India's bio-power capacity was reported as approximately 11.75 GW in August 2026, in addition to CBG/Bio-CNG plants.
67.tq: Read the decimal and unit together to avoid a tenfold capacity error.

67.s: Biodiesel is commercially produced by which of the following processes?
o: Pyrolysis of lignocellulosic residues without a catalyst
Transesterification of vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol
Fermentation of starch by methanogenic bacteria
Electrolysis of water in the presence of vegetable oil
67.x: Biodiesel is produced by transesterifying vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol, producing fatty-acid methyl or ethyl esters.
67.tq: Identify the precise conversion process rather than a nearby biofuel process.

67.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jatropha — Jatropha curcas
2. Pongamia — Pongamia pinnata
3. Palm stearin oil — Feedstock for about 94% of India's biodiesel
4. Used Cooking Oil — RUCO initiative of FSSAI
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
67.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Jatropha and Pongamia are identified by their botanical names, palm stearin oil accounts for about 94% of biodiesel feedstock, and RUCO concerns used cooking oil.
67.tq: Use the matching list to verify botanical names, proportions and institutional associations.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Pongamia, also known as karanja, in the context of biodiesel?
o: A genetically engineered alga used for fourth-generation fuel
A lignocellulosic grass used in the Panipat plant
A non-edible oilseed plant yielding biodiesel feedstock
An edible cereal used for first-generation ethanol
67.x: Pongamia pinnata, commonly called karanja, is a non-edible oilseed plant used as a biodiesel feedstock.
67.tq: Distinguish similar renewable feedstocks by their food status and fuel application.

67.s:
With reference to biodiesel in India, consider the following statements:
1. Its blending in diesel remains below 0.5%.
2. India has set a target of 5% biodiesel blending by 2030.
3. Biodiesel feedstock is entirely domestically sourced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because biodiesel is mostly dependent on imported feedstock.
67.tq: Find the false absolute claim in a policy-status question.

67.s: The biodiesel project launched by the Belgian firm VITO in April 2023 was located at:
67.x: VITO launched a two-year biodiesel project at Ayodhya in April 2023.
67.tq: Match the foreign partner with the correct project location and date.

67.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. VITO launched a two-year biodiesel project at Ayodhya
B. The target year for 5% biodiesel blending
C. The first commercial 2G ethanol plant at Panipat
D. Dedication of the bamboo bioethanol plant at Numaligarh
67.x: The Panipat 2G plant was established in 2022, the VITO project began in April 2023, the biodiesel target is for 2030, and the Numaligarh bamboo plant was dedicated on 14 September 2025.
67.tq: Place dated events first and use the target year as the latest policy milestone.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding Indian biodiesel procurement is correct?
o: Procurement increased from 1.1 lakh litres in FY16 to 36.7 lakh litres in FY25.
Oil marketing company procurement increased from 1.1 crore litres in FY16 to 36.7 crore litres in FY25.
Procurement declined from 36.7 crore litres in FY16 to 1.1 crore litres in FY25.
Procurement remained fixed at 5 crore litres between FY16 and FY25.
67.x: Oil marketing company procurement rose substantially, from 1.1 crore litres in FY16 to 36.7 crore litres in FY25.
67.tq: Check both the direction of change and the units of the reported figures.

67.s: Power alcohol in India is best described as:
o: Fuel-grade ethanol made mainly from molasses
Biodiesel made exclusively from palm stearin oil
Hydrogen produced by electrolysis of water
67.x: Power alcohol refers to fuel-grade ethanol, which in India is made mainly from molasses, a by-product of the sugar industry.
67.tq: Discriminate between closely related fuel terms by their feedstock and composition.

67.s: Which microorganism is associated with the production of bioethanol by fermentation of sugar or starch?
67.x: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a yeast, ferments sugars or starch-derived sugars to produce bioethanol.
67.tq: Use the organism–product association rather than confusing ethanol with biobutanol production.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about biobutanol:
1. It is associated with Clostridium acetobutylicum.
2. It has higher energy density than ethanol.
3. It is produced from genetically engineered algae only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because biobutanol is associated with Clostridium acetobutylicum and is not restricted to genetically engineered algae.
67.tq: Separate the organism and property of biobutanol from those of other biofuel generations.

67.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the generation of biofuel?
o: 2G — food crops such as sugarcane and corn
67.x: Third-generation biofuels use algae or algal biomass. First-generation fuels use food crops, second-generation fuels use non-food lignocellulosic material, and fourth-generation fuels use genetically engineered organisms.
67.tq: Start with the sure generation–feedstock pair and eliminate the reversed classifications.

67.s: Which of the following feedstocks is characteristic of second-generation biofuels?
67.x: Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues such as rice straw, straw, husk, wood chips and bamboo.
67.tq: Classify the feedstock according to whether it is food-based, residual or genetically modified.

67.s: The first commercial 2G ethanol plant at Panipat used which of the following as its principal feedstock?
67.x: The IOCL Panipat plant, described as the first commercial 2G plant in 2022, used rice straw as feedstock.
67.tq: Link the plant with its distinctive residue feedstock rather than with first-generation materials.

67.s: Which one of the following is a major advantage of second-generation biofuels over first-generation biofuels?
o: They avoid the food-versus-fuel conflict by using non-food residues.
They require no biochemical or thermochemical conversion.
They are produced exclusively from edible vegetable oils.
They use only genetically modified algae.
67.x: Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues and therefore avoid the food-fuel conflict, although their conversion is technically complex.
67.tq: Apply the food-versus-fuel distinction to identify the advantage of the technology.

67.s: The Numaligarh Refinery bamboo bioethanol plant is located in:
67.x: The bamboo-based 2G ethanol plant is at Numaligarh Refinery in Golaghat district of Assam.
67.tq: Use the location–feedstock association to distinguish the two major 2G projects.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Numaligarh bamboo bioethanol plant:
1. It was dedicated on 14 September 2025.
2. It is described as India's first commercial-scale bamboo bioethanol plant.
3. It is a first-generation plant based mainly on corn.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because bamboo is a non-food lignocellulosic feedstock associated with second-generation bioethanol.
67.tq: Reject the generation mismatch by checking the plant's non-food feedstock.

67.s:
Assertion (A): Fourth-generation biofuels have the potential to be carbon-negative.
Reason (R): They use genetically engineered algae or microbes designed to capture more carbon dioxide.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
67.x: Both statements are true, and the enhanced carbon-dioxide capture by genetically engineered algae or microbes explains the potential carbon-negative character of fourth-generation fuels.
67.tq: Test whether the biological feature in the Reason directly explains the environmental outcome in the Assertion.

67.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated limitation of algal biofuel production?
o: Dependence on edible cereal crops as the only feedstock
67.x: Dependence on edible cereal crops is not an algal-biofuel limitation. The stated limitations include high cultivation and harvesting costs, contamination, scale-up problems, energy-intensive lipid extraction, and heavy water and nutrient needs.
67.tq: Find the option that belongs to a different generation rather than to the list of algal limitations.

67.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the advantages of algal biofuel?
o: High yield per unit area, ability to use wastewater and use of carbon dioxide
Low cultivation cost, no need for nutrients and exclusive use of seawater
Use of only edible crops and complete absence of contamination risk
No requirement for harvesting or lipid extraction
67.x: Algae can provide high yield per unit area and can use wastewater and carbon dioxide. However, cultivation, harvesting, contamination and nutrient-related constraints remain.
67.tq: Select the option containing only the stated advantages and avoid absolute claims about costs or requirements.

67.s: Which of the following sites has the greatest tidal-energy potential among the listed Indian sites?
67.x: The Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat is identified as India's best tidal-energy site, with an estimated potential of about 7,000 MW.
67.tq: Distinguish the best tidal site from an offshore-wind site and other ocean-energy locations.

67.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Durgaduani Creek — pilot tidal project — Sundarbans
Vizhinjam — first Indian wave-energy plant — Gujarat
Gulf of Mannar — best tidal site — Gujarat
Lakshadweep — first wave-energy plant — West Bengal
67.x: The Durgaduani Creek tidal project is a pilot project in the Sundarbans. Vizhinjam is in Kerala, Gulf of Mannar is associated here with offshore wind, and Lakshadweep is an OTEC location.
67.tq: Use the project–technology–location combination to expose swapped sites.

67.s: India's first wave-energy plant was established at:
67.x: India's first wave-power pilot was established at Vizhinjam, Kerala, in 1991.
67.tq: Combine the distinctive site with the associated year and technology.

67.s: The Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) system requires approximately what temperature difference between surface and deep water?
67.x: OTEC requires an approximately 20°C temperature difference between warm surface water and cold deep water.
67.tq: Recall the threshold figure and reject values representing smaller or excessive differences.

67.s: OTEC is considered viable mainly in which latitudinal belt?
67.x: OTEC is viable in tropical regions, broadly between 30°N and 30°S, where the required surface-to-deep-water temperature difference is available.
67.tq: Use the geographic belt associated with tropical thermal conditions.

67.s: Which of the following is an additional benefit of OTEC apart from electricity generation?
67.x: OTEC can provide electricity as well as desalination, which is particularly useful for islands.
67.tq: Identify the co-benefit directly linked to ocean thermal operation in island regions.

67.s:
Which of the following locations are associated with OTEC potential in India?
1. Lakshadweep
2. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
3. Gulf of Khambhat
4. Gulf of Kutch
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are identified as Indian OTEC locations. The Gulfs of Khambhat and Kutch are discussed as tidal-energy sites.
67.tq: Separate OTEC island locations from tidal-energy gulfs.

67.s: Which institution is India's lead ocean-energy research body?
o: CSIR-NIIST, Golaghat, under the Ministry of Petroleum
IOCL, Panipat, under the Ministry of Agriculture
NIOT, Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences
67.x: The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is India's lead ocean-energy research body.
67.tq: Identify the correct institutional authority by matching body, location and ministry.

67.s:
Assertion (A): The Gulf of Mannar is not the appropriate answer when a question asks for India's tidal-energy site in this context.
Reason (R): It is identified as an offshore-wind zone rather than as one of the listed tidal sites.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
67.x: Both statements are true. The Gulf of Mannar is distinguished from the listed tidal sites because it is identified as an offshore-wind zone.
67.tq: Use the confusable-location trap by distinguishing technologies associated with similar coastal sites.

67.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: Discouraging the production of advanced biofuels
67.x: The National Policy on Biofuels aims to reduce import dependence, promote domestic feedstock, strengthen energy security and generate employment. It does not discourage advanced biofuels.
67.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated policy objectives.

67.s:
With reference to the National Policy on Biofuels, consider the following statements:
1. The 2018 policy widened the ethanol feedstock base beyond molasses.
2. Sugarcane juice, surplus FCI rice, maize and damaged foodgrains were included as ethanol feedstocks.
3. Jatropha, pongamia and algae were identified in relation to biodiesel production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All three statements are correct. The 2018 policy expanded ethanol feedstocks beyond molasses and recognised non-food oilseeds such as jatropha and pongamia, along with algae, for biodiesel.
67.tq: Check the complete feedstock list rather than stopping at the familiar molasses option.

67.s:
The original targets under the National Policy on Biofuels were which of the following?
1. 20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2030
2. 5% biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030
3. 30% ethanol blending in petrol by 2030
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: The original targets were E20 in petrol and B5 in diesel by 2030. The 30% ethanol target is a later target, not the original policy target.
67.tq: Separate the original 2030 targets from the later E30 target.

67.s: The 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels advanced the target for E20 from 2030 to which of the following?
67.x: The 2022 amendment advanced the E20 target to Ethanol Supply Year 2025–26 from 2030.
67.tq: Distinguish the revised target year from the original 2030 deadline.

67.s:
Which of the following changes was introduced through the 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels?
1. More feedstocks were permitted.
2. Biofuel units in SEZs and EOUs were permitted under the Make in India provision.
3. Exports were permitted in specific cases.
4. New members could not be added to the NBCC.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The amendment allowed more feedstocks, covered biofuel units in SEZs and EOUs, and permitted exports in specific cases. It also allowed new members to be added to the NBCC, so statement 4 is false.
67.tq: Identify the single reversed statement in a list of amendment provisions.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes basic biofuels from advanced biofuels under the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: Basic biofuels include 1G bioethanol and biodiesel, whereas advanced biofuels include 2G ethanol, drop-in fuels, 3G biofuels and bio-CNG.
Basic biofuels and advanced biofuels have identical categories and feedstocks.
Basic biofuels include 2G ethanol and bio-CNG, whereas advanced biofuels include only biodiesel.
Basic biofuels are produced only from municipal solid waste, whereas advanced biofuels are produced only from sugarcane.
67.x: Basic biofuels comprise 1G bioethanol and biodiesel. Advanced biofuels include 2G ethanol, drop-in fuels from MSW, 3G biofuels and bio-CNG.
67.tq: Use the category boundary to eliminate options that swap basic and advanced fuels.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM JI-VAN Yojana:
1. Its revised implementation period extends up to 2028–29.
2. The expression ‘2G ethanol’ was replaced by ‘advanced biofuels’ in the revised formulation.
3. It covers bolt-on and brownfield plants.
4. It provides for about 12 commercial projects with an outlay of ₹1,969.50 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All four statements correctly describe the revised PM JI-VAN Yojana, including its extension to 2028–29, wider advanced-biofuel coverage, eligible plant types, projects and outlay.
67.tq: Test the scheme through its date, terminology, coverage and financial figures.

67.s: The Ethanol Interest Subvention Scheme is primarily associated with which of the following?
67.x: The Ethanol Interest Subvention Scheme supports the financing and expansion of distillery capacity.
67.tq: Match the scheme with the sectoral capacity it is designed to finance.

67.s:
Which of the following statements regarding enabling provisions for biofuels is correct?
1. Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act permits engine conversion to biofuels.
2. Automatic-route 100% FDI is permitted for biofuel technology when intended for domestic use.
3. FDI is permitted for plantations connected with biofuel production.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Plantations are barred from FDI, making statement 3 false.
67.tq: Watch for the reversed exception concerning FDI in plantations.

67.s: Which combination of measures is associated with promoting advanced biofuels?
o: Import quotas, export bans and uniform pricing only
Compulsory plantation ownership and customs duties
Free electricity, tidal subsidies and nuclear bonds
Viability Gap Funding, tax credits and differential pricing
67.x: Viability Gap Funding, tax credits and differential pricing are identified as enabling measures for advanced biofuels.
67.tq: Select the option containing the policy instruments specifically linked to advanced biofuels.

67.s: E20 petrol with a minimum Research Octane Number of 95 became mandatory in India from:
67.x: Mandatory E20 petrol with a minimum RON of 95 was scheduled from 1 April 2026.
67.tq: Read the complete milestone as a date-plus-standard combination.

67.s: The next ethanol-blending target after E20 is which of the following?
67.x: The next stated target is 30% ethanol blending, or E30, by 2030.
67.tq: Distinguish the current E20 milestone from the subsequent target.

67.s: BIS standard IS 19850:2026 covers which of the following petrol blends?
67.x: IS 19850:2026 covers E22, E25, E27 and E30 petrol standards.
67.tq: Check every member of the named standards list; one familiar blend is not enough.

67.s: E85 is primarily associated with which of the following?
67.x: E85 is used in flex-fuel vehicles.
67.tq: Discriminate between a high-ethanol blend and the vehicle technology designed for it.

67.s: The Ethanol Blended Petrol programme is implemented by which ministry, while ethanol is procured from distilleries by OMCs?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
67.x: The Ethanol Blended Petrol programme is run by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. Oil Marketing Companies procure ethanol from distilleries.
67.tq: Use the ‘who runs the programme?’ method to distinguish the responsible ministry from related ministries.

67.s: In the feedstock-differentiated pricing of ethanol procured by Oil Marketing Companies, the correct order from highest to lowest price is:
67.x: Ethanol made from maize has the highest price, rice-based ethanol the lowest, and molasses-based ethanol lies between them.
67.tq: Arrange the three feedstocks by price instead of merely recalling one isolated value.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gasohol — anhydrous ethanol used as motor fuel
67.x: Gasohol means a petrol–ethanol blend. Power alcohol refers to anhydrous ethanol used as motor fuel.
67.tq: Separate the two look-alike terms by matching each with its precise definition.

67.s: Power alcohol refers to:
o: Anhydrous ethanol used as motor fuel
Hydrogen blended with compressed natural gas
Ethanol mixed only with aviation turbine fuel
67.x: Power alcohol is anhydrous ethanol used as a motor fuel.
67.tq: Prefer the exact technical term over the broader petrol–ethanol blend definition.

67.s:
Arrange the following ethanol-blending milestones in chronological order:
A. E10 was achieved
B. Pilot programme was initiated
C. E20 became mandatory with minimum RON 95
D. E5 was introduced in nine States and four Union Territories
Select the correct sequence.
67.x: The sequence is pilot in 2001, E5 introduction on 1 January 2003, E10 achievement in June 2022, and mandatory E20 from 1 April 2026.
67.tq: Fix the earliest pilot first and the 2026 milestone last, then arrange the middle events.

67.s: The pilot ethanol-blending programme and the subsequent E5 rollout are associated respectively with:
67.x: The pilot programme began in 2001, and E5 was introduced in nine States and four Union Territories on 1 January 2003.
67.tq: Pair each milestone with its precise year or date.

67.s: E10 blending was achieved in India in:
67.x: E10 was achieved in June 2022, ahead of the November 2022 target.
67.tq: Distinguish the actual achievement date from the later target date.

67.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported gains from ethanol blending?
o: Foreign-exchange savings exceeding ₹1.97 lakh crore and ₹1.66 lakh crore paid to farmers
Foreign-exchange savings of ₹1.66 lakh crore and ₹1.97 lakh crore paid to farmers
Foreign-exchange savings exceeding ₹1.66 lakh crore and ₹1.97 lakh crore paid to farmers
Foreign-exchange savings of ₹1.97 crore and ₹1.66 lakh crore paid to farmers
67.x: The reported gains include foreign-exchange savings exceeding ₹1.97 lakh crore and ₹1.66 lakh crore paid to farmers.
67.tq: Keep the two large figures attached to their correct outcomes.

67.s: Between Ethanol Supply Year 2014–15 and 2024–25, approximately how much ethanol was blended?
67.x: A total of 3,544.21 crore litres was blended during Ethanol Supply Years 2014–15 to 2024–25.
67.tq: Check both the numerical value and its unit before selecting the answer.

67.s: Which one of the following statements about ethanol pricing is correct?
o: Rice-based ethanol has the highest price and maize-based ethanol the lowest.
All feedstocks receive an identical ethanol price.
Maize-based ethanol has the highest price, rice-based ethanol the lowest, and molasses-based ethanol is intermediate.
Molasses-based ethanol is priced above maize-based ethanol.
67.x: The feedstock-differentiated order is maize highest, molasses intermediate and rice lowest. The price of maize ethanol recorded a CAGR of 11.7% during FY22–25.
67.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to identify the correct price order.

67.s: The recorded compound annual growth rate of the price of maize ethanol during FY22–25 was:
67.x: The price of maize ethanol recorded a CAGR of 11.7% during FY22–25.
67.tq: Test the exact percentage rather than relying on the general price trend.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) targets for international flights:
1. The target is 1% by 2027.
2. The target is 2% by 2028.
3. The target is 5% by 2030.
4. The roadmap is linked to ICAO’s net-zero 2050 objective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All four statements are correct. The SAF roadmap specifies 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028 and 5% by 2030, in line with ICAO’s net-zero 2050 objective.
67.tq: Read the targets as a progression and connect them with the stated international objective.

67.s: Which policy specifically supports bio-jet fuel among the following?
67.x: The BioE3 Policy 2024 supports bio-jet fuel.
67.tq: Match the policy name with its stated fuel application.

67.s: Which one of the following statements about global ethanol production is correct?
o: Brazil produces more ethanol than the United States, using mainly maize.
Brazil has prohibited high ethanol blends such as E27.
The United States produces more ethanol than Brazil, with maize or corn as its principal feedstock, while Brazil mainly uses sugarcane.
Both the United States and Brazil use only sugarcane as feedstock.
67.x: The United States produces more ethanol than Brazil and mainly uses maize or corn, whereas Brazil mainly uses sugarcane. Brazil mandates high blends such as E27.
67.tq: Compare both the producer ranking and the principal feedstock before choosing.

67.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Brazil is correct in the context of ethanol blending?
o: Brazil uses only rice-based ethanol and has no blending mandate.
Brazil’s principal feedstock is maize, while the United States relies mainly on sugarcane.
Brazil mandates high ethanol blends, including E27.
Brazil has adopted E85 exclusively for all vehicles.
67.x: Brazil mandates high ethanol blends, including E27. Its principal feedstock is generally sugarcane, whereas the United States mainly uses maize or corn.
67.tq: Reject options that reverse the country-specific blend or feedstock association.

67.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the first Indian biojet-fuelled flight?
o: It was an Air India flight from Delhi to Mumbai in August 2018 using algae-based fuel.
It was an IndiGo flight from Mumbai to Delhi in August 2018 using sugarcane-based fuel.
It was a SpiceJet flight from Dehradun to Delhi in August 2018 using jatropha-based fuel from CSIR-IIP.
It was a SpiceJet flight from Delhi to Dehradun in January 2019 using maize-based fuel.
67.x: India’s first biojet-fuelled flight was SpiceJet’s Dehradun–Delhi flight in August 2018, using jatropha fuel developed from CSIR-IIP sources.
67.tq: Combine the operator, route, date and feedstock details to avoid close distractors.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Power alcohol — water-rich ethanol unsuitable for motor fuel
E85 — blend used in flex-fuel vehicles
67.x: Power alcohol is anhydrous ethanol used as motor fuel, not water-rich ethanol unsuitable for such use. The other pairs are correctly matched.
67.tq: Find the option that changes the defining property of a technical term.

67.s: In India, a hydropower plant is classified as a small hydro plant when its capacity is:
67.x: In India, hydroelectric plants with capacity up to 25 MW are classified as small hydro plants.
67.tq: Use the exact capacity cut-off and distinguish it from neighbouring classifications.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding small hydro classification:
1. Micro hydro refers to plants up to 100 kW.
2. Mini hydro refers to plants from 101 kW to 2 MW.
3. Small hydro refers to plants above 2 MW and up to 25 MW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All three statements correctly describe the micro, mini and small hydro capacity ranges.
67.tq: Check each numerical range separately before selecting the coded combination.

67.s:
Small hydro projects are commonly developed using which of the following site conditions?
1. Hill streams
2. Canal falls
3. Toes of dams
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Run-of-river small hydro projects may use hill streams, canal falls and water released at dam toes.
67.tq: Recognise the application-based list and avoid treating run-of-river projects as dam-only projects.

67.s: Approximately what share of India's estimated small hydro potential had been installed, with installed capacity of about 5.18 GW?
67.x: The installed capacity of about 5.18 GW represented approximately 25 percent of the estimated potential.
67.tq: Relate the installed capacity to the stated percentage of potential.

67.s: Which group of States holds about half of India's small hydro potential?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana
67.x: Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand together hold about half of India's small hydro potential.
67.tq: Identify the geographically clustered high-potential Himalayan States.

67.s: Technical support for the small hydro programme is provided by the Department of Hydro and Renewable Energy, IIT Roorkee. Which statement is correct regarding this department?
o: It provides technical support but is not under MNRE control.
It is an autonomous body of the United Nations.
It functions directly under the control of MNRE.
It functions under the Ministry of Power alone.
67.x: The Department of Hydro and Renewable Energy at IIT Roorkee provides technical support and is not under the control of MNRE.
67.tq: Apply the authority-versus-technical-support distinction.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding waste-to-energy routes:

List-I (Route)
a. Incineration
b. Pyrolysis
c. Gasification
d. Refuse-derived fuel

List-II (Description)
i. Dry combustible part of segregated municipal solid waste
ii. Heating without oxygen
iii. Partial oxidation
iv. Direct burning of municipal solid waste for heat or power

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Incineration directly burns MSW; pyrolysis heats it without oxygen; gasification uses partial oxidation; RDF is the dry combustible fraction of segregated MSW.
67.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that reverse pyrolysis and gasification.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes pyrolysis of waste?
o: Microbial conversion of wet waste into methane only
Heating in the absence of oxygen to produce biochar, bio-oil and syngas
Complete burning in excess oxygen to produce only ash
Capture of methane escaping from a landfill
67.x: Pyrolysis is the heating of waste without oxygen and can produce biochar, bio-oil and syngas.
67.tq: Discriminate pyrolysis from incineration, biomethanation and landfill gas recovery.

67.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence for gasification?
67.x: Gasification uses partial or controlled oxidation and produces syngas.
67.tq: Separate gasification from incineration by focusing on limited oxygen and syngas.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gasification — complete combustion in excess oxygen
Biomethanation — microbial conversion of wet organic waste into biogas
Landfill gas recovery — capture of methane from landfills
Incineration — burning in oxygen with possible steam generation
67.x: Gasification involves controlled or partial oxidation, not complete combustion in excess oxygen. The other pairs are correctly matched.
67.tq: Find the process whose oxygen condition has been deliberately reversed.

67.s:
Source segregation is essential for which of the following processes?
1. Gasification
2. Anaerobic digestion
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Proper source segregation is essential for both gasification and anaerobic digestion because the feedstock must be suitably separated and relatively free from incompatible materials.
67.tq: Apply the waste-management principle to both dry and wet treatment routes.

67.s:
Which of the following locations in Andhra Pradesh are associated with Jindal waste-to-energy plants?
1. Guntur
2. Naidupalem
3. Kapuluppada, Visakhapatnam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Jindal waste-to-energy plants are associated with Guntur, Naidupalem and Kapuluppada in Visakhapatnam.
67.tq: Use location-based recall and include all listed plant sites.

67.s: Which of the following correctly states the waste-to-energy capacity figures?
o: National capacity 0.88 GW; Andhra Pradesh municipal solid waste power 40.96 MW and industrial waste power 36.15 MW
National capacity 8.80 GW; Andhra Pradesh municipal solid waste power 40.96 MW and industrial waste power 36.15 MW
National capacity 0.88 GW; Andhra Pradesh municipal solid waste power 36.15 MW and industrial waste power 40.96 MW
National capacity 5.18 GW; Andhra Pradesh municipal solid waste power 21.13 MW and industrial waste power 7.13 MW
67.x: The national waste-to-energy capacity is 0.88 GW, while Andhra Pradesh has 36.15 MW from municipal solid waste and 40.96 MW from industrial waste.
67.tq: Keep the national figure separate from the two Andhra Pradesh component figures.

67.s: The first Indian biofuel flight in 2018 operated on which route?
67.x: The first Indian biofuel flight operated from Dehradun to Delhi on 27 August 2018 using jatropha-based fuel produced with CSIR-IIP support.
67.tq: Separate the route detail from the airline-name recall commonly used in similar questions.

67.s: The first Indian biofuel flight was conducted on:
67.x: The first Indian biofuel flight took place on 27 August 2018.
67.tq: Use the exact date and reject the close-year distractors.

67.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: CSIR-IIP — authority responsible for RUCO collection
IOCL Panipat — first Indian ISCC CORSIA-certified SAF producer
IOCL Panipat — first Indian commercial nuclear fuel producer
Numaligarh Refinery — first Indian ISCC CORSIA-certified SAF producer
67.x: IOCL Panipat became India's first ISCC CORSIA-certified SAF producer in August 2025. RUCO is an FSSAI initiative, while Numaligarh is associated with a bamboo-based 2G ethanol plant.
67.tq: Check the institution against the precise certification and production claim.

67.s: RUCO, associated with biofuels, is a drive of the:
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
67.x: RUCO is an FSSAI drive to collect used cooking oil for conversion into biodiesel.
67.tq: Identify the implementing body rather than the end-use fuel.

67.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the listed feedstocks for Sustainable Aviation Fuel?
67.x: Agricultural residues, corn grain, wastewater treatment sludge and wood-mill waste are listed SAF feedstocks. Uranium ore is not a biofuel feedstock.
67.tq: Find the option that belongs to nuclear energy rather than biofuel production.

67.s: Sustainable Aviation Fuel differs from direct ethanol blending in that SAF uses:
o: Only hydrogen generated from nuclear power
Directly blended ethanol as the sole fuel component
67.x: SAF uses drop-in synthesised hydrocarbons suitable for aviation fuel systems; it is not simply direct ethanol.
67.tq: Distinguish a compatible drop-in fuel from direct ethanol blending.

67.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the revised PM JI-VAN Yojana?
1. It supports advanced biofuels.
2. Its implementation timeline extends to 2028–29.
3. It covers bolt-on and brownfield projects.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: The revised scheme replaces the narrower expression '2G ethanol' with 'advanced biofuels', extends the timeline to 2028–29 and covers bolt-on and brownfield projects.
67.tq: Track the changes introduced by the revised scheme rather than its original title alone.

67.s: The PM JI-VAN Yojana was launched in:
67.x: PM JI-VAN Yojana was launched in 2019 to support 2G ethanol and subsequently expanded to advanced biofuels.
67.tq: Use the launch year, not the later revision period, as the deciding fact.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly states the scale of the revised PM JI-VAN Yojana?
o: 10 commercial advanced biofuel plants, an outlay of ₹1,296.50 crore and 12 demonstration units
12 commercial advanced biofuel plants, an outlay of ₹1,969.50 crore and about 10 demonstration units
12 commercial advanced biofuel plants, an outlay of ₹969.50 crore and about 20 demonstration units
25 commercial advanced biofuel plants, an outlay of ₹1,969.50 crore and 10 demonstration units
67.x: The revised scheme provides for 12 commercial advanced biofuel plants, an outlay of ₹1,969.50 crore and approximately 10 demonstration units.
67.tq: Match the three numerical components as a single scheme profile.

67.s:
Match the following 2G ethanol plants with their locations or feedstocks:

List-I (Plant)
a. IOCL Panipat
b. Numaligarh Refinery
c. HPCL Bathinda
d. BPCL Bargarh

List-II (Location or feedstock)
i. Odisha
ii. Haryana; rice straw and bagasse
iii. Golaghat, Assam; bamboo
iv. Punjab

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: IOCL Panipat is in Haryana and uses rice straw and bagasse; Numaligarh is in Golaghat, Assam and uses bamboo; HPCL Bathinda is in Punjab; BPCL Bargarh is in Odisha.
67.tq: Begin with the distinctive bamboo–Numaligarh pair and then complete the remaining matches.

67.s: Which one of the following statements about the Numaligarh Refinery 2G plant is correct?
o: It is located in Panipat, Haryana, and uses rice straw and bagasse.
It is located in Bathinda, Punjab, and uses municipal solid waste.
It is located in Golaghat, Assam, uses bamboo and was dedicated on 14 September 2025.
It is located in Bargarh, Odisha, and uses used cooking oil.
67.x: The Numaligarh Refinery plant is located in Golaghat, Assam, uses bamboo and was dedicated on 14 September 2025; it was described as the world's first of its kind.
67.tq: Combine location, feedstock and date to defeat plant-location swaps.

67.s: Under SATAT, compressed biogas is produced from:
o: Agricultural residues and municipal solid waste
67.x: SATAT promotes compressed biogas produced from agricultural residues and municipal solid waste.
67.tq: Identify the eligible feedstocks rather than confusing CBG with conventional natural gas.

67.s: The Compressed Biogas Obligation under SATAT is scheduled as:
o: 5 percent in FY 2026–28, followed by 1 percent from 2028–29
3 percent, 4 percent and 5 percent in FY 2026–28, followed by 1 percent from 2028–29
1 percent, 3 percent and 4 percent in FY 2026–28, followed by 5 percent from 2028–29
1 percent, 2 percent and 3 percent in FY 2026–28, followed by 4 percent from 2028–29
67.x: The CBG obligation is 1 percent, 3 percent and 4 percent during FY 2026–28, rising to 5 percent from FY 2028–29.
67.tq: Read the obligation as a rising sequence and retain the transition year.

67.s: GOBAR-DHAN, launched in 2018, primarily seeks to convert:
o: Cattle dung into biogas or bio-CNG
67.x: GOBAR-DHAN was launched in 2018 to promote conversion of cattle dung into biogas and bio-CNG.
67.tq: Break the acronym conceptually and identify the stated feedstock-output pair.

67.s: In biomass gasification, biomass or waste is heated with limited oxygen to produce syngas consisting mainly of:
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen and carbon dioxide
Sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and ammonia
