77.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 was notified on:
77.x: The EIA Notification, 2006 was notified on 14 September 2006 and replaced the 1994 notification.
77.tq: Use the date-year pairing to reject close distractors.

77.s: A major change introduced by the EIA Notification, 2006 was the shift from classification based primarily on investment to classification based on:
77.x: The 2006 notification shifted the focus from investment size to the environmental impact potential of projects.
77.tq: Test the central contrast between the 1994 and 2006 regimes.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, environmental clearance is compulsory for how many project categories?
77.x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
77.tq: Direct quantitative recall with nearby numerical distractors.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EIA Notification, 2006:
1. It provides safeguards relating to air, water and land.
2. It includes safeguards for biodiversity and wildlife habitat.
3. It replaced the EIA Notification, 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The 2006 notification addresses air, water, land, biodiversity and wildlife habitat, and replaced the 1994 notification.
77.tq: Check whether all elements of a regulatory framework belong together.

77.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched under the EIA Notification, 2006?
o: Category A — State Expert Appraisal Committee — SEIAA
Category B1 — Expert Appraisal Committee — MoEFCC
Category A — Expert Appraisal Committee — MoEFCC
Category B2 — Expert Appraisal Committee — MoEFCC
77.x: Category A projects are appraised by the Expert Appraisal Committee and cleared by MoEFCC.
77.tq: Start with the sure authority-category pair and eliminate swapped bodies.

77.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Categories B1 and B2 under the EIA Notification, 2006?
o: B1 projects are cleared by EAC, whereas B2 projects are cleared by MoEFCC.
B1 projects do not require EIA, whereas B2 projects require full EIA.
B1 projects require EIA, whereas B2 projects do not require EIA.
Both B1 and B2 projects always require full EIA by MoEFCC.
77.x: Category B1 projects require an EIA, while Category B2 projects do not; both are associated with state-level appraisal and clearance arrangements.
77.tq: Discriminate between the closely named B1 and B2 categories.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of Category A projects under the 2006 EIA framework?
o: They are appraised by the EAC.
They undergo screening before full EIA is considered.
77.x: Category A projects do not undergo screening; they always require full EIA, are appraised by EAC and cleared by MoEFCC.
77.tq: Find the single reversed feature in a category description.

77.s: Under the July 2026 amendment, if a State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to decide a proposal within 120 days, the proposal may escalate to:
o: The new Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment on PARIVESH
77.x: The July 2026 amendment provides for escalation after 120 days to the new SCEIA through PARIVESH.
77.tq: Link the time limit with the newly designated authority.

77.s: Which of the following was a provision of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework?
o: The Centre may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays.
Scientists alone must replace all administrative members.
All Category B projects must automatically be transferred to the central EAC.
State committees may retain proposals indefinitely without escalation.
77.x: The amendment permits the Centre to remove members of EAC, SEAC or SEIAA mid-term for persistent delays. It also introduced an escalation mechanism rather than automatic transfer of all Category B projects to the central EAC.
77.tq: Identify the precise institutional power among reversed alternatives.

77.s: The principal criticism of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework is that it may:
o: Replace scientists with bureaucrats and prioritise speed over science
Give excessive control to local communities over scientific appraisal
Make every project subject to a full EIA
77.x: The amendment has been criticised on the ground that bureaucratic control may replace scientific expertise and that speed may be prioritised over scientific appraisal.
77.tq: Identify the stated criticism rather than the procedural detail.

77.s: Which of the following combinations correctly identifies the earlier authorities proposed before the SCEIA arrangement?
77.x: MoEFCC had earlier proposed the Standing Committee on EIA and the Standing Authority on EIA, abbreviated SCEIA and SAEIA.
77.tq: Distinguish similar institutional abbreviations by exact expansion.

77.s: The Draft EIA Notification, 2020 proposed which of the following?
o: Post-facto clearance through appraisal, penalties, compensation and remediation plans
A complete ban on environmental clearance after project commencement
Clearance based only on investment size
Abolition of public consultation for all projects
77.x: The draft proposed post-facto environmental clearance through appraisal, penalties, compensation and remediation plans. It was not finalised.
77.tq: Recognise the controversial proposal associated with the draft notification.

77.s:
Consider the following provisions associated with the Draft EIA Notification, 2020:
1. The public-hearing notice period was proposed to be reduced from 30 days to 20 days.
2. More projects were proposed to be moved to Category B2 or exempted.
3. Compliance reports were proposed to be submitted yearly instead of half-yearly.
4. Violations could be reported by any member of the public without restriction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The draft proposed a 20-day notice period, more B2 or exempt projects and yearly compliance reports. It restricted reporting of violations to the violator or government, so statement 4 is false.
77.tq: Locate the false statement by testing the reporting restriction.

77.s: Which statement regarding the Draft EIA Notification, 2020 is correct?
o: It was not finalised and was criticised for provisions including post-facto clearance.
It proposed longer public consultation periods than the 2006 notification.
It was finally enacted without modification.
It abolished penalties and remediation plans for violations.
77.x: The 2020 draft was not finalised and was contested, particularly for proposing post-facto clearance and shorter consultation periods.
77.tq: Reject absolute claims about a draft becoming final law.

77.s: Public consultation for scheduled projects under the EIA framework is described as:
o: Optional for all Category A projects
A process conducted only after environmental clearance
A single-stage consultation conducted only through written submissions
77.x: Public consultation is a mandatory two-fold process involving public hearing and written responses for scheduled projects.
77.tq: Recall the procedural structure rather than one component alone.

77.s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
77.x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.
77.tq: Use the authority-role distinction to avoid swapping institutions.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the public-hearing notice must be given at least how many days in advance, and the hearing must be completed within what period?
77.x: The notice period is at least 30 days, and the hearing is to be completed within 45 days.
77.tq: Pair two procedural time limits without reversing their order.

77.s: Which of the following categories of projects is generally exempt from public hearing because details are kept confidential?
o: All projects located in notified industrial estates
77.x: Defence, national-security and strategic projects may be exempt because their details are kept confidential.
77.tq: Identify the security-based exemption rather than a location-based exemption.

77.s: Which of the following is also exempt from the public-hearing requirement?
o: B2 projects and units inside notified industrial estates
All B1 projects and all valley projects
77.x: B2 projects and units located inside notified industrial estates are among the stated exemptions from public hearing.
77.tq: Find the correctly stated exemption among overbroad alternatives.

77.s: The designation of a project as ‘strategic’ for the purpose of public-hearing exemption is determined by the:
77.x: The Centre determines which projects are strategic; this has been criticised as potentially arbitrary.
77.tq: Ask which authority exercises the disputed classification power.

77.s: PARIVESH is best described as:
o: A single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances
A programme for preparing baseline biodiversity data
A committee for appraisal of Category A projects
77.x: PARIVESH is an online single-window platform for environment, forest, wildlife and Coastal Regulation Zone clearances.
77.tq: Distinguish a digital clearance platform from statutory bodies.

77.s: PARIVESH was launched in:
77.x: The PARIVESH portal was launched in 2018.
77.tq: Recall the launch year against years of major EIA notifications.

77.s: What is the correct expansion of the acronym PARIVESH?
o: Public Assessment and Regulation of Industrial Ventures for Ecological Safety Hub
Provisional Assessment and Review Interface for Vigilance in Environmental Statutory Hearings
Participatory Authority for Regional Impact Verification and Environmental Safety Headquarters
Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub
77.x: PARIVESH expands to Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub.
77.tq: Test the exact official expansion rather than a look-alike phrase.

77.s: Following the July 2026 changes, PARIVESH serves as the platform for:
o: The 120-day escalation of proposals to SCEIA
Appointment of District Collectors to SPCBs
Preparation of NEPA in the United States
Automatic approval of all Category B2 projects
77.x: PARIVESH is used for the 120-day escalation process to the Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment.
77.tq: Connect the digital platform with the new escalation procedure.

77.s: The global origin of Environmental Impact Assessment is associated with the National Environmental Policy Act of the:
77.x: The global origin of EIA is associated with the United States National Environmental Policy Act, enacted in 1969.
77.tq: Pair the legislation, country and year precisely.

77.s: In India, the Planning Commission asked the Department of Science and Technology to examine river-valley projects during:
77.x: India's EIA process began in 1976-77 when the Planning Commission asked DST to examine river-valley projects.
77.tq: Distinguish the institutional beginning from the later first-use date.

77.s: The first use of EIA in India is dated in some accounts to 1978 for:
77.x: The first use of EIA in India is dated to 1978 in connection with river-valley projects.
77.tq: Associate the earliest year with the first project sector.

77.s: Before 1994, environmental clearance in India was primarily:
o: A decision of SEIAA under the 2006 notification
A constitutional adjudication by the Supreme Court
A decision made only through public voting
77.x: Until 1994, environmental clearance operated as an administrative decision rather than under the later codified notification framework.
77.tq: Contrast the pre-notification administrative regime with the later statutory procedure.

77.s: After river-valley projects, EIA scrutiny in India extended to large public-sector projects requiring clearance from the:
77.x: Large public-sector projects requiring Public Investment Board clearance became another early area of EIA application.
77.tq: Identify the institutional trigger associated with the early expansion of EIA.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 2009 amendment or development in the EIA framework?
o: Expansion of the list of projects
Procedural clarifications for Category B2 projects
77.x: The 2009 development expanded the list of projects covered by the framework.
77.tq: Match the year with its specific amendment rather than a later proposal.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Year)
A. 2011
B. 2012/2018
C. 2013
D. 2015
List-II (Development)
1. Thermal power
2. Expansion and modernisation
3. River-valley projects in specific contexts
4. Mining; mining and infrastructure
77.x: 2011 concerned river-valley projects in specific contexts; 2012/2018 concerned mining and mining/infrastructure; 2013 concerned thermal power; and 2015 concerned expansion and modernisation.
77.tq: Start with the sure 2013-thermal power pair and complete the remaining matches.

77.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2015 — Establishment of NEPA in the United States
2020 — Draft notification involving post-facto clearance and shorter consultation
77.x: NEPA was established in the United States in 1969, not in 2015. The other pairs correctly reflect developments in the EIA framework.
77.tq: Find the year attached to an unrelated historical event.

77.s: Which of the following environmental matters has been included among the NGT’s directions or docket matters?
77.x: NGT directions and matters include Ganga pollution control, waste management, industrial monitoring, and cases such as the Dhanauri wetland and Saparnika river matters.
77.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed activity belongs to the tribunal’s environmental docket.

77.s: The time limit prescribed in the August 2023 direction for the Border Roads Organisation to plant the trees was:
77.x: The NGT directed the plantation of the trees within one month.
77.tq: Separate the quantity of the direction from its compliance period.

77.s: In 2022, the National Green Tribunal imposed fines on states in connection with waste mismanagement. Which pair was specifically associated with such fines?
77.x: Maharashtra and West Bengal were cited as examples of states fined by the NGT for waste mismanagement in 2022.
77.tq: Match the environmental violation with the correctly associated states.

77.s: Which of the following correctly describes the NGT action concerning the LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam?
o: It transferred the matter to the National Environment Appellate Authority without any financial direction.
It took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
It ordered a permanent ban on all chemical industries in Andhra Pradesh.
It directed the Border Roads Organisation to undertake plantation in Uttarakhand.
77.x: Following the Visakhapatnam styrene leak in May 2020, the NGT took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
77.tq: Match the authority’s action to the correct incident instead of confusing separate NGT orders.

77.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Great Nicobar project—High-Powered Committee on NGT directions
Sewage in drinking water—suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Styrene leak—Maharashtra and West Bengal waste-management fines
77.x: The styrene leak concerned LG Polymers at Visakhapatnam and led to an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore. Maharashtra and West Bengal were associated with fines for waste mismanagement.
77.tq: Find the swapped incident-and-state pairing.

77.s: The High-Powered Committee relating to the Great Nicobar project was set up pursuant to directions of the:
77.x: A High-Powered Committee was set up on the directions of the National Green Tribunal in relation to the Great Nicobar project.
77.tq: Use the ‘who directed the committee’ approach to distinguish environmental institutions.

77.s: The inter-state dispute concerning the Polavaram project primarily relates to submergence in:
77.x: The Polavaram inter-state dispute concerns submergence in neighbouring Odisha and Chhattisgarh and was raised before the Supreme Court.
77.tq: Identify the neighbouring states directly affected by the project’s submergence issue.

77.s: A proposal submitted for environmental appraisal through PARIVESH is automatically transferred when the State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to appraise it within:
77.x: Under the stated 2026 arrangement, a proposal is auto-transferred through PARIVESH if the SEAC does not appraise it within 120 days.
77.tq: Recall the precise trigger period for automatic transfer in the clearance process.

77.s: PARIVESH is best described as a:
o: Single-window portal for environmental and related clearances
Scientific body that prepares only climate reports
77.x: PARIVESH functions as a single-window portal for clearances and has been upgraded to PARIVESH 3.0 using artificial intelligence.
77.tq: Identify the institutional role from the service it provides rather than its environmental subject area.

77.s: PARIVESH 3.0 is associated with the use of:
o: Artificial intelligence in the clearance portal
Satellite launch technology for biodiversity mapping
77.x: PARIVESH 3.0 uses artificial intelligence as part of the upgraded single-window clearance system.
77.tq: Match the technology with the correct environmental-governance platform.

77.s: Which of the following correctly represents the backup arrangement referred to for environmental appraisal bodies in 2026?
o: NGT for SEIAA and NEAA for SEAC
SCEIA for SEIAA and SAEIA for SEAC
EAC for SEIAA and CPCB for SEAC
SAEIA for SEIAA and SCEIA for SEAC
77.x: The stated backup bodies are SAEIA in place of SEIAA and SCEIA in place of SEAC.
77.tq: Discriminate between the similar abbreviations by matching each backup body to its parent body.

77.s: Under the stated revised arrangements, the tenure of SEIAA, EAC and SEAC members is:
o: Four years, with a maximum of two terms and an age limit of 70
Five years, with unlimited terms and no age limit
Three years, with one renewal and a maximum age of 65
77.x: The tenure was raised to four years, with a maximum of two terms and an age limit of 70 years for members of SEIAA, EAC and SEAC.
77.tq: Combine tenure, term limit and age limit to avoid selecting a partly correct option.

77.s: The maximum tenure of the SAEIA and SCEIA arrangement, including the stated extension, is:
77.x: The tenure is stated as six months plus another six months, subject to a maximum of one year.
77.tq: Add the base tenure and extension while observing the explicit maximum limit.

77.s: The EIA amendment referred to in recent environmental policy developments created which institutional arrangement along with a 120-day timeline?
o: State Council for Ecological Impact Assessment (SCEIA)
State-level Climate and Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SCEIA)
77.x: The EIA amendment created the State-level Environmental Impact Assessment Authority (SCEIA) and prescribed a 120-day timeline.
77.tq: Use the exact official expansion of the institutional acronym rather than a look-alike term.

77.s: The Vanashakti judgment of 29 July 2026 is associated with which issue?
o: Environmental clearance for river-valley projects only
Establishment of the National Green Tribunal
77.x: The Vanashakti judgment concerned the legality of ex-post facto environmental clearances.
77.tq: Identify the precise legal issue linked with the named judgment.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding criticisms of the Environmental Impact Assessment process:
1. EIA reports are often prepared by consultants paid by the project proponents.
2. There is no central baseline data bank for EIA purposes.
3. Emergency plans associated with projects may be weak.
4. Certain projects or situations may be exempted from public hearings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All four statements describe identified criticisms of the EIA process: proponent-paid consultants, absence of a central baseline data bank, weak emergency plans and exemptions from hearings.
77.tq: Test the complete set of criticisms by checking each statement independently.

77.s: Which one of the following has been suggested as a measure to address the criticism that EIA consultants may lack independence?
o: Transfer of EIA preparation entirely to project proponents
Permitting post-facto clearances as a routine measure
Creation of an independent EIA authority
77.x: An independent EIA authority has been suggested to improve the credibility and independence of environmental assessments.
77.tq: Match the identified institutional defect with the appropriate reform.

77.s:
With reference to environmental clearance issues in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Telangana approached the Supreme Court seeking a review of the EIA for the Indira Sagar Polavaram project.
2. The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board conducted a public hearing concerning a water aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage.
3. The Human Rights Forum described the draft EIA for the water aerodrome as error-ridden.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All three statements are correct. Telangana sought Supreme Court review of the Polavaram EIA, while the APPCB hearing on the Prakasam Barrage water aerodrome drew criticism from the Human Rights Forum for an error-ridden draft EIA.
77.tq: Link the institution, project and criticism without confusing the two Andhra Pradesh examples.

77.s: Which of the following correctly represents the firsts associated with Environmental Impact Assessment?
o: NEPA was the first EIA law, enacted in the United States in 1969; river-valley projects were the first sector appraised in India.
NEPA was the first formal Indian EIA notification, issued in 1994; industrial projects were first appraised.
The first EIA law was enacted in India in 1978; coastal projects were first appraised.
The first formal EIA notification was issued in the United States in 1969; mining projects were first appraised in India.
77.x: The United States enacted the first EIA law through NEPA in 1969, and river-valley projects were the first sector appraised in India.
77.tq: Pair the first law, country, year and first Indian sector rather than mixing separate milestones.

77.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to EIA in chronological order:
A. Enactment of NEPA in the United States
B. First use of EIA in India
C. First formal EIA notification in India
D. EIA amendment creating SCEIA and prescribing a 120-day timeline
77.x: The sequence is NEPA in 1969, first use of EIA in India in 1978, the first formal notification in 1994, and the later amendment creating SCEIA with a 120-day timeline.
77.tq: Anchor the sequence using the earliest and latest dates first.

77.s: Environmental Impact Assessment was first used in India in which year?
77.x: Environmental Impact Assessment was first used in India in 1978.
77.tq: Distinguish the year of first use from the later year of the first formal notification.

77.s: India’s first formal Environmental Impact Assessment notification was issued in:
77.x: India’s first formal EIA notification was issued in 1994.
77.tq: Separate a formal legal notification from the earlier practical use of EIA.

77.s: Which criticism of the EIA process is specifically illustrated by the Great Nicobar case?
o: Thin baseline data in the EIA
Absence of any requirement for public hearings
Excessive reliance on a central baseline data bank
77.x: The Great Nicobar EIA was criticised for having thin baseline data.
77.tq: Connect the named case with its specific weakness rather than a general criticism.

77.s: Post-facto environmental clearances have been criticised because they may become:
o: a substitute for baseline data collection before a project begins
the first stage of appraisal for river-valley projects
the design of the clearance system when violations are detected only after construction
a compulsory form of public hearing conducted before every project
77.x: The criticism is that post-facto clearances can become “the design” when state appraisal bodies identify violations only after construction has already occurred.
77.tq: Apply the criticism to the sequence of violation detection and construction.

77.s: The Visakhapatnam gas leak involving LG Polymers in 2020 was handled by which body in the environmental-law context?
o: The State Environmental Impact Assessment Authority alone
The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board alone
77.x: The 2020 LG Polymers gas leak at Visakhapatnam was handled by the National Green Tribunal.
77.tq: Use the agency-event association and distinguish the adjudicatory body from other environmental institutions.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: River-valley projects — first sector appraised in India
LG Polymers gas leak — Visakhapatnam, 2020 — National Green Tribunal
Great Nicobar EIA — absence of any baseline data collection
NEPA — first EIA law — United States, 1969
77.x: The Great Nicobar EIA was criticised for thin baseline data, not for the complete absence of baseline data collection. The other pairs are correctly matched.
77.tq: Find the overstatement by distinguishing thin or inadequate data from total absence of data.

77.s: Which authority clears Category B projects in Andhra Pradesh under the Environmental Impact Assessment Notification, 2006?
o: Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board only
AP State Environment Impact Assessment Authority
77.x: The AP State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (AP SEIAA) clears Category B projects in Andhra Pradesh under the EIA Notification, 2006.
77.tq: Match the project category and legal notification with the correct State-level authority.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal was established under which of the following enactments?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
78.x: The National Green Tribunal was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
78.tq: Test the exact parent legislation rather than the subject area of the tribunal.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status and powers of the National Green Tribunal?
o: It is a statutory body with powers similar to those of a civil court.
It is a constitutional body with powers exclusively of an administrative authority.
It is an executive body exercising only advisory jurisdiction.
It is a constitutional body established under Article 323B without civil-court powers.
78.x: The NGT is a statutory, not constitutional, body and possesses civil-court powers in matters within its jurisdiction.
78.tq: Discriminate between constitutional, statutory and executive bodies before considering their powers.

78.s:
With reference to the procedure followed by the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. It is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
2. It is guided by the principles of natural justice.
3. It is required to dispose of applications within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: The NGT is not bound by the CPC, 1908; it follows natural justice and applications are to be disposed of within six months.
78.tq: Identify the reversed procedural claim and combine the two correct procedural features.

78.s: The establishment of the National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to constitutional remedies under Article 32
78.x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.
78.tq: Match the environmental entitlement with the relevant Fundamental Right.

78.s: The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal is located at:
78.x: New Delhi is the location of the Principal Bench of the NGT.
78.tq: Test the headquarters-type location separately from zonal and circuit bench locations.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Type of Bench)
 a. Principal Bench
 b. Zonal Bench
 c. Circuit Bench

List-II (Place)
 i. Jodhpur
 ii. New Delhi
 iii. Pune
 iv. Shillong
78.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi; Pune is a zonal bench location; and Jodhpur and Shillong are circuit bench locations.
78.tq: Start with the sure Principal Bench pair and then distinguish zonal from circuit locations.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a location of a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: Pune, Bhopal and Chennai are zonal bench locations. Shillong is a circuit bench location.
78.tq: Find the bench-type mismatch rather than merely identifying a place associated with the NGT.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal is headed by a Chairperson who is required to be:
o: The Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
A retired member of the Union Public Service Commission
A serving judge of a High Court
A retired judge of the Supreme Court
78.x: The NGT is headed by a Chairperson who is a retired Supreme Court judge, assisted by judicial and expert members.
78.tq: Apply the who-holds-the-office test to distinguish judicial leadership from executive administration.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal is best described as a specialised and multidisciplinary body for:
o: Environmental protection, forest and natural-resource conservation, environmental legal rights, and relief for damage
Exclusively regulating wildlife sanctuaries and national parks
Adjudicating all criminal offences relating to public health
Only adjudicating disputes between the Union and the States
78.x: Its purpose includes environmental protection, conservation of forests and natural resources, enforcement of environmental legal rights, and relief and compensation for damage.
78.tq: Select the option that combines the tribunal’s connected functions without extending its jurisdiction beyond the stated scope.

78.s: Which of the following enactments falls outside the direct scope of the National Green Tribunal as stated?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
78.x: The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 is outside the NGT’s direct scope. The Air Act, Forest Conservation Act and Biological Diversity Act are covered enactments.
78.tq: Look for the excluded enactment among statutes that otherwise belong to environmental law.

78.s:
Which of the following pairs of enactments is correctly matched with the direct scope of the National Green Tribunal?
1. Water Act, 1974
2. Air Act, 1981
3. Environment Protection Act, 1986
4. Forest Conservation Act, 1980
5. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: All five listed enactments fall within the direct scope of the NGT.
78.tq: Check the completeness of a statutory list and avoid excluding a genuine environmental enactment.

78.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the Supreme Court within:
78.x: An appeal against an NGT order may be filed before the Supreme Court within 90 days.
78.tq: Use the exact statutory time limit and compare the middle numerical options carefully.

78.s: Which of the following pairs of environmental matters was associated with cases before the National Green Tribunal in 2026?
o: Silent Valley and Chilika lagoon only
Kaziranga tourism and Gir lion conservation only
Sardar Sarovar and Tehri dam rehabilitation
78.x: The 2026 cases identified include the Dhanauri wetland, Ganga pollution and the Saparnika river.
78.tq: Test current case names as a precise identification question rather than inferring from general environmental themes.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal was established under which enactment and in which year?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
78.x: The National Green Tribunal was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. It is a statutory body.
78.tq: Identify the specific establishing law and year instead of choosing a related environmental statute.

78.s:
With reference to the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. Its Chairperson is a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
2. It is bound by all the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure.
3. It follows the principles of natural justice.
4. It is required to decide cases within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, though it follows natural justice.
78.tq: Split the options by checking the procedural exception concerning the CPC.

78.s: Which one of the following is the Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal is located at New Delhi.
78.tq: Distinguish the Principal Bench from the zonal and circuit benches.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Category of Bench)
A. Principal Bench
B. Zonal Bench
C. Circuit Bench

List-II (Location)
1. New Delhi
2. Pune
3. Shillong

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: New Delhi is the Principal Bench; Pune is a zonal bench; and Shillong is a circuit bench.
78.tq: Start from the sure location-category pairs and eliminate codes with a misplaced bench type.

78.s: Which of the following locations is NOT a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai are zonal benches. Jodhpur is a circuit bench.
78.tq: Find the location belonging to the neighbouring bench category rather than the category named in the question.

78.s: Which one of the following Acts falls outside the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal as listed for environmental matters?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
78.x: The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 is outside the listed jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal. The Air Act, Forest (Conservation) Act and Biological Diversity Act are included.
78.tq: Use the exclusion in the jurisdiction list to identify the exception.

78.s:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
3. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
4. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
5. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
Which of the above are included in the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: All five listed Acts fall within the specified jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal.
78.tq: Check every item against the statutory jurisdiction list before selecting the inclusive option.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Green Tribunal (NGT)?
o: It is a constitutional body established under Article 21
It is a statutory body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
It is a quasi-judicial body established under Article 323B
It is an executive body established under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
78.x: The NGT is a statutory body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. It is not a constitutional body.
78.tq: Distinguish statutory bodies from constitutional bodies and check the parent law.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal gives effect to the right to a healthy environment primarily as a part of which constitutional provision?
78.x: The right to a healthy environment has been treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.
78.tq: Match the right with its correct constitutional article.

78.s:
With reference to the composition of the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. It has a Chairperson who is a retired Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. It includes Judicial Members and Expert Members.
3. There are 10 to 20 Judicial Members and 10 to 20 Expert Members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: The NGT consists of a Chairperson who is a retired Supreme Court judge, along with Judicial and Expert Members, with 10 to 20 members in each category.
78.tq: Verify the composition by separating the chairperson, member categories and numerical range.

78.s:
Which of the following Acts is outside the scope of the National Green Tribunal as specified in its jurisdictional list?
1. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
2. Forest Rights Act
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
4. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
78.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act are outside the stated scope. The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 are covered Acts.
78.tq: Use exclusion testing to distinguish covered Acts from Acts outside the specified scope.

78.s:
Which of the following pairs of Acts is correctly matched with the Acts covered by the National Green Tribunal?
1. Water Act, 1974
2. Air Act, 1981
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
4. Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
78.x: All four listed Acts are among the Acts covered by the NGT. The original Schedule I also included the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991.
78.tq: Check the complete statutory list rather than stopping at the commonly cited environmental Acts.

78.s: Which one of the following Acts was included in the original Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal framework?
78.x: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 was included in the original Schedule I. The Wildlife (Protection) Act and the Forest Rights Act are outside the stated scope.
78.tq: Use a less frequently recalled item from the statutory list as the correct option.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (NGT location)
a. Principal Bench
b. Zonal Bench
c. Zonal Bench
d. Zonal Bench

List-II (Location)
i. Chennai
ii. New Delhi
iii. Pune
iv. Bhopal

option_a: a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i
option_b: a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
option_c: a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii
option_d: a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
78.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi, while Bhopal, Pune and Chennai are zonal bench locations.
78.tq: Start with the sure headquarters pair and then place the zonal benches.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal, established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, started functioning in:
78.x: The National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October 2010 and began functioning in July 2011.
78.tq: Separate the establishment date from the date on which the institution began functioning.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated purpose of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Relief and compensation for environmental damage
Conservation of forests and natural resources
Conducting elections to local bodies in environmentally sensitive areas
78.x: The NGT deals with environmental protection, conservation of forests and natural resources, enforcement of environmental legal rights, and relief and compensation for damage. Conducting local-body elections is not its function.
78.tq: Find the option outside the tribunal’s stated environmental jurisdiction.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal:
1. It is a statutory body and not a constitutional body.
2. Its legal basis is connected with the right to a healthy environment under Article 21.
3. It is bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: The NGT is a statutory body whose purpose is linked to the Article 21 right to a healthy environment. It is not bound by the CPC, though it is guided by natural justice.
78.tq: Identify the reversed procedural statement about the CPC.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the principal and zonal benches of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Principal Bench—New Delhi; Zonal Benches—Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai
Principal Bench—Mumbai; Zonal Benches—Delhi, Jaipur, Patna and Kochi
Principal Bench—New Delhi; Zonal Benches—Shimla, Shillong and Jodhpur
Principal Bench—Bhopal; Zonal Benches—Pune, Chennai, Lucknow and Ranchi
78.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi, while the Zonal Benches are at Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai.
78.tq: Start from the sure location of the Principal Bench and distinguish zonal from circuit benches.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of Bench)
A. Principal Bench
B. Zonal Bench
C. Circuit Bench

List-II (Location)
1. New Delhi
2. Pune
3. Shimla

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
78.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi, Pune is a Zonal Bench, and Shimla is a Circuit Bench.
78.tq: Use the distinctive bench-location pair first, then eliminate codes that interchange zonal and circuit benches.

78.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a Circuit Bench of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: The Circuit Benches are located at Shimla, Shillong and Jodhpur. Kolkata, Chennai and Pune are Zonal Bench locations.
78.tq: Discriminate between the closely related zonal and circuit bench lists.

78.s: The composition of the National Green Tribunal includes:
o: A Chairperson and members drawn exclusively from the scientific community
A Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members
Only serving Supreme Court judges and representatives of State Pollution Control Boards
A Governor, Chief Minister and district collectors
78.x: The NGT consists of a Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members.
78.tq: Test the statutory composition by separating judicial and expert components.

78.s:
With reference to the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. The Chairperson may be a retired Supreme Court judge.
2. The Chairperson may be a Chief Justice of a High Court.
3. Justice Prakash Shrivastava was the Chairperson as on 15 January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: The Chairperson can be a retired Supreme Court judge or a Chief Justice of a High Court. Justice Prakash Shrivastava held the position as on 15 January 2026.
78.tq: Combine eligibility conditions with the current office-holder without confusing judicial categories.

78.s: The number of Judicial Members and Expert Members in the National Green Tribunal is stated to be:
78.x: The composition provision referred to here specifies 10 to 20 Judicial Members and 10 to 20 Expert Members.
78.tq: Identify the correct numerical range rather than relying on the tribunal’s total membership.

78.s: Applications before the National Green Tribunal are required to be disposed of within:
78.x: The prescribed period for disposal of applications by the NGT is six months.
78.tq: Distinguish the application-disposal period from the appeal period.

78.s: Which of the following Acts falls OUTSIDE the National Green Tribunal’s Schedule I jurisdiction?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
78.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is outside the listed Schedule I Acts of the NGT. The Air Act, Biological Diversity Act and Public Liability Insurance Act are included.
78.tq: Find the excluded statute from a list of closely related environmental laws.

78.s:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
3. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
4. Forest Rights Act, 2006
Which of the above are included among the Acts under which the NGT hears cases?
78.x: The Water Act, Forest (Conservation) Act and Environment (Protection) Act are included. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 is outside the NGT’s Schedule I list.
78.tq: Separate the included environmental statutes from the specifically excluded Forest Rights Act.

78.s: An aggrieved person seeking to challenge an order of the National Green Tribunal must approach the Supreme Court within:
78.x: An appeal against an NGT order lies to the Supreme Court within 90 days.
78.tq: Distinguish the Supreme Court appeal period from the NGT’s six-month disposal period.

78.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Green Tribunal from the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: NGT is a quasi-judicial tribunal, whereas CPCB is a statutory regulator.
NGT functions under the Water Act alone, whereas CPCB functions under the NGT Act.
NGT sets pollution standards, whereas CPCB awards compensation.
Both are constitutional bodies with identical adjudicatory powers.
78.x: The NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation under the NGT Act. The CPCB is a statutory regulator under the Water Act and Air Act that sets standards, monitors and advises the Centre.
78.tq: Compare the institution’s legal character and core function rather than its common environmental field.

78.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was distinctive because it provided for:
o: Strict liability for accidents involving hazardous substances
Establishment of the Central Pollution Control Board
78.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of accidents involving hazardous substances.
78.tq: Associate the predecessor law with its distinctive liability principle.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995:
1. It was never made operational.
2. It was repealed by the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
3. It dealt with strict liability for hazardous-substance accidents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct: the Act was never operationalised, was repealed by the NGT Act, and provided for strict liability in hazardous-substance accidents.
78.tq: Test the predecessor law through its year, fate and substantive legal principle.

78.s: The National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 primarily provided for hearing appeals against:
78.x: The National Environment Appellate Authority heard appeals against environmental clearances.
78.tq: Distinguish the appellate authority’s subject matter from the NGT’s wider jurisdiction.

78.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Environment Appellate Authority is correct?
o: It was dissolved and its Act was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
It became a constitutional court under Article 21.
It was established under the NGT Act, 2010 and continues to function independently.
It was converted into the Central Pollution Control Board.
78.x: The NEAA was dissolved, and the National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
78.tq: Use the fate of the predecessor institution to reject continuation and conversion traps.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal Act was passed on which date?
78.x: The National Green Tribunal Act was passed on 2 June 2010. The Tribunal was subsequently set up on 18 October 2010.
78.tq: Distinguish the date of enactment from the date of establishment.

78.s: Which one of the following best describes the legal status of the National Green Tribunal?
o: A statutory body established under the NGT Act, 2010
A regulatory body established under the Environment Protection Act, 1986
An executive body created by the Ministry of Environment
A constitutional body established under Article 21
78.x: The National Green Tribunal is a statutory body created under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010; it is not a constitutional body.
78.tq: Apply the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction.

78.s: The principal purpose of the National Green Tribunal is to:
o: Conduct criminal trials relating to all offences in India
Replace all State Pollution Control Boards
Frame the Union Budget for environmental programmes
Provide effective and expeditious disposal of environmental cases and relief for environmental damage
78.x: The NGT deals with environmental protection, conservation of forests and natural resources, enforcement of environmental rights, and relief and compensation for environmental damage.
78.tq: Choose the option covering the tribunal’s complete statutory purpose.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to the right to a healthy environment derived from:
78.x: The right to a healthy environment is read into the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution, and the NGT helps enforce this environmental right.
78.tq: Use the article-number trap in constitutional questions.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the procedure of the National Green Tribunal:
1. It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
2. It is guided by the principles of natural justice.
3. It possesses the powers of a civil court.
4. It is required to dispose of cases within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All four statements are correct. The NGT is not bound by the CPC, follows natural justice, has civil-court powers, and is expected to dispose of cases within six months.
78.tq: Check whether all procedural features belong to the same tribunal.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal consists of a Chairperson along with:
o: Members of Parliament and representatives of SPCBs
78.x: The NGT comprises a Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members. The number of Judicial and Expert Members is stated as 10 to 20 each.
78.tq: Test the statutory composition rather than the office-holder alone.

78.s: According to the stated current information, the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal is:
78.x: Justice Prakash Shrivastava is identified as the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal as of 8 September 2026.
78.tq: Use the current office-holder without confusing the office with a former Supreme Court office-holder.

78.s:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
3. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
4. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
5. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
6. Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
7. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
Which of the above constitute the stated seven Acts under the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: All seven listed Acts are included: the Water Act, Water Cess Act, Forest (Conservation) Act, Air Act, Environment (Protection) Act, Public Liability Insurance Act and Biological Diversity Act.
78.tq: Verify the complete statutory list rather than relying on only the major pollution Acts.

78.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Green Tribunal from the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: The NGT sets emission standards, whereas the CPCB awards compensation.
The CPCB hears appeals against NGT orders in environmental disputes.
The NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation, whereas the CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors pollution.
Both bodies perform exactly the same adjudicatory and regulatory functions.
78.x: The NGT is an adjudicatory body that decides environmental disputes and awards compensation. The CPCB is a regulatory body that sets standards, monitors pollution and advises the Centre.
78.tq: Separate adjudication from regulation by asking who performs the job.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of the CPCB:
1. Air-pollution functions were added by the Air Act, 1981.
2. Its scope was widened by the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
3. It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. The Air Act added air-related functions, the Environment Protection Act widened its scope, and the CPCB functions as a statutory body under MoEFCC.
78.tq: Test a sequence of institutional expansion and administrative status.

78.s: The Chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board is:
o: The Secretary-General of the National Green Tribunal
A full-time chairman nominated by the Central Government
The Chairperson of the National Biodiversity Authority
A part-time member elected by the State Boards
78.x: The CPCB has a full-time Chairman nominated by the Central Government.
78.tq: Identify the appointing authority and full-time status precisely.

78.s: Which body is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework?
78.x: The CPCB is the body responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
78.tq: Assign the enforcement function to the regulatory rather than adjudicatory body.

78.s: The National Air Monitoring Programme is commonly abbreviated as:
78.x: NAMP stands for the National Air Monitoring Programme. NCAP is the National Clean Air Programme, while CAAQMS refers to continuous ambient air quality monitoring systems.
78.tq: Discriminate between similar environmental monitoring abbreviations.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. National AQI — Launched in 2015
2. National AQI — Daily bulletins
3. CAAQMS — Real-time air monitoring
4. PRANA — Tracking of NCAP
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
78.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The National AQI was launched in 2015 and issues daily bulletins; CAAQMS provides real-time monitoring and PRANA tracks NCAP.
78.tq: Match each programme with its distinctive function or portal.

78.s: Which of the following correctly describes the stated national air-monitoring network?
78.x: The stated network covers 516 cities and has more than 1,400 stations, including real-time CAAQMS monitoring.
78.tq: Read paired figures in the correct city–station order.

78.s: The real-time monitoring system referred to in relation to the CPCB air-monitoring network is:
78.x: CAAQMS refers to the continuous ambient air quality monitoring system used for real-time air monitoring. RTWQMS is associated with water-quality monitoring.
78.tq: Separate air-monitoring and water-monitoring acronyms.

78.s: The Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring System mentioned for the Ganga and Yamuna is abbreviated as:
78.x: RTWQMS stands for Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring System and is associated here with monitoring the Ganga and Yamuna.
78.tq: Use the water-related expansion of the abbreviation.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated coordinating or supporting function of the CPCB?
o: Adjudicating appeals against orders of the Supreme Court
78.x: The CPCB coordinates SPCBs, provides technical help, supports research and training, and performs monitoring and regulatory functions. It does not adjudicate appeals against Supreme Court orders.
78.tq: Reject the judicial power wrongly attributed to a regulatory board.

78.s: Under the Water Act and Air Act, Consent to Establish is required:
o: Before setting up the project or establishment
Only when an appeal is filed before the NGT
78.x: Consent to Establish must be obtained before setting up the establishment. Consent to Operate is required before production or discharge begins.
78.tq: Apply the chronological distinction between establishment and operation.

78.s: A factory has been constructed and is ready to begin production and discharge. Which consent is required at this stage?
78.x: Consent to Operate is required before production or discharge begins. Consent to Establish applies to the earlier stage of setting up the facility.
78.tq: Use the project-stage sequence to distinguish the two consents.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board:
1. It enforces the Water Act, Air Act and Environment Protection Act.
2. It enforces rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.
3. It issues siting guidelines and develops SOPs for marine outfalls and hazardous waste.
4. It promotes cleaner production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All four statements describe stated APPCB responsibilities, including enforcement, waste-management rules, siting guidance, SOPs and cleaner production.
78.tq: Test the full range of State Board responsibilities rather than only its core Acts.

78.s: Computerised inspection by the APPCB is associated with:
78.x: The APPCB uses computerised inspection in connection with Ease of Doing Business initiatives.
78.tq: Match the administrative reform with the State Board function.

78.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was intended primarily to provide for:
o: Strict liability for damage caused by hazardous-substance accidents
Setting up of State Pollution Control Boards
78.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of damage resulting from hazardous-substance accidents.
78.tq: Distinguish the purpose of the NET Act from the appellate role of NEAA.

78.s: Which statement correctly describes the fate of the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995?
o: It was brought into force and remains the principal environmental tribunal law.
It was converted into the National Biodiversity Authority Act.
It was replaced by the Water Act, 1974 without repeal.
It was never brought into force and was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
78.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was never brought into force and was repealed by the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
78.tq: Use the fate-of-legislation trap: enacted does not necessarily mean brought into force.

78.s: Which of the following statements about the NEAA is correct?
o: It was replaced by the NGT and its Act was repealed in 2010.
It was never concerned with environmental clearances.
It was converted into the CPCB in 1988.
78.x: The National Environment Appellate Authority was replaced by the NGT, and the National Environment Appellate Authority Act was repealed in 2010.
78.tq: Track institutional succession and the repeal year.

78.s: The NGT combines which two roles associated earlier with separate environmental institutions?
o: Original jurisdiction over environmental disputes and the appellate role of the NEAA
78.x: The NGT combines original jurisdiction over environmental disputes with the appellate role earlier performed by the NEAA.
78.tq: Link the predecessor authority’s appellate role with the NGT’s original jurisdiction.

78.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Ministry of Environment and Forests formed
B. Department of Environment created
C. Ministry renamed MoEFCC
D. Air-pollution functions added to CPCB by the Air Act
Select the correct sequence.
78.x: The correct sequence is Department of Environment in 1980, Air Act in 1981, Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985, and MoEFCC renaming in 2014.
78.tq: Place the dated institutional milestones from earliest to latest.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change:
1. It receives 0.07% of the Union Budget according to the stated current information.
2. It is the nodal agency for India’s NR7 biodiversity report.
3. It runs Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct according to the stated current information: the allocation is 0.07%, MoEFCC is nodal for India’s NR7 biodiversity report, and it runs Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan.
78.tq: Combine current institutional facts while checking each statement independently.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Wildlife Institute of India — Dehradun
2. Botanical Survey of India — Kolkata
3. Forest Survey of India — Lucknow
4. G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment — Kosi-Katarmal, Almora
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
78.x: The Wildlife Institute of India is at Dehradun, the Botanical Survey of India is at Kolkata and GBPNIHE is at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora. The Forest Survey of India is also at Dehradun, not Lucknow.
78.tq: Find the wrong location by comparing institutes that are commonly associated with Dehradun and Kolkata.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institute)
a. Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History
b. Indian Institute of Toxicology Research
c. Central Marine Living Resources and Ecology

d. Zoological Survey of India

List-II (Location)
i. Kochi
ii. Coimbatore
iii. Lucknow
iv. Kolkata

Choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
78.x: SACON is located at Coimbatore, IITR at Lucknow, CMLRE at Kochi and ZSI at Kolkata.
78.tq: Start from the sure institute–location pair and verify the remaining pairs by elimination.

78.s: The Forest Survey of India was established in which year?
78.x: The Forest Survey of India was established in 1981 and is located at Dehradun.
78.tq: Distinguish the establishment year from the years associated with other environmental bodies.

78.s: The Central Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE) is associated with which of the following?
o: A Himalayan environment institute at Almora
A toxicology research institute at Lucknow
A national deep-sea fauna repository named “Bhavasagara” at Kochi
A bird research centre at Coimbatore
78.x: CMLRE is associated with the “Bhavasagara” national deep-sea fauna repository at Kochi.
78.tq: Link the specialised function and distinctive name with the correct institute and location.

78.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Wildlife Institute of India is correct?
o: It is located at Kolkata and administers the NBA Fund.
It is located at Dehradun and monitors NR7 targets.
It is located at Kochi and monitors NR7 targets.
It is located at Almora and implements Namami Gange.
78.x: The Wildlife Institute of India is located at Dehradun and is associated with monitoring NR7 targets.
78.tq: Combine the institution’s location with its specific current monitoring role.

78.s: The Environmental Information System (ENVIS), now known as EIACP, is best described as:
o: A network of environmental-information centres of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
A statutory tribunal for environmental disputes
A pollution-abatement programme for rivers outside the Ganga basin
A biodiversity approval mechanism for foreign companies
78.x: ENVIS is the MoEFCC’s network of environmental-information centres and is now known as EIACP.
78.tq: Identify the institutional network by matching its function with the responsible ministry.

78.s: The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered at:
78.x: The headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority is at Chennai.
78.tq: Test the headquarters directly while using nearby environmental institutions as distractors.

78.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier institutional structure under biodiversity governance?
o: SBBs at the national level, NBA at the State level and BMCs at the district level
NBA at the national level, SBBs at the State level and BMCs at the local level
NBA at the local level, BMCs at the State level and SBBs at the national level
BMCs at the national level, SBBs at the local level and NBA at the State level
78.x: The three tiers are the National Biodiversity Authority at the national level, State Biodiversity Boards at the State level and Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.
78.tq: Arrange the bodies by jurisdiction from national to local.

78.s: With reference to biopiracy, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Foreigners may access Indian bio-resources without approval if no patent is sought.
Foreigners require approval of the NBA to access bio-resources or traditional knowledge, and NBA approval precedes intellectual property rights on them.
Only local bodies can grant approval for foreign access to traditional knowledge.
NBA approval is required only after intellectual property rights have been granted.
78.x: Foreigners require NBA approval to access bio-resources or associated traditional knowledge, and such approval precedes the grant of intellectual property rights. Access and benefit-sharing with local communities is also an important safeguard.
78.tq: Apply the approval-sequence rule and reject options that reverse the order or shift authority.

78.s: Which of the following is NOT an initiative associated with the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board?
o: Implementation of the Namami Gange programme throughout Andhra Pradesh
Biodiversity parks on the flood plains of five polluted rivers
City Biodiversity Index in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Kadapa and Tirupati
78.x: The City Biodiversity Index, biodiversity parks on the flood plains of five polluted rivers and the Gloriosa superba cultivation pilot are APSBB initiatives. Namami Gange is implemented by the NMCG.
78.tq: Find the option belonging to another environmental body rather than the APSBB.

78.s: The National Biodiversity Authority Act was amended in 2023 and the Biological Diversity Rules were issued in:
78.x: The Biological Diversity Rules were issued in 2024, following the amendment of the Act in 2023.
78.tq: Separate the year of the Act amendment from the year of the Rules.

78.s: Which one of the following bodies replaced the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA) in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas?
78.x: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), established under the CAQM Act, 2021, replaced EPCA in the NCR and adjoining areas.
78.tq: Use the replacement relationship and distinguish air-quality authority from water and biodiversity bodies.

78.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CAQM Act was enacted in 2021.
2. CAQM covers the National Capital Region and adjoining areas.
3. CAQM replaced the EPCA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. CAQM operates in the NCR and adjoining areas under the CAQM Act, 2021, replacing EPCA.
78.tq: Verify the body through its legal basis, territorial scope and predecessor.

78.s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is the successor set-up to which body?
78.x: NMCG is the successor set-up to the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA), which was established in 2009 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
78.tq: Use the predecessor–successor relationship and distinguish river-basin institutions from pollution authorities.

78.s: Which one of the following is the principal implementation role of the National Mission for Clean Ganga?
o: Monitoring NR7 targets in wildlife institutions
Regulating access to traditional knowledge by foreigners
78.x: The NMCG implements the Namami Gange programme.
78.tq: Identify the programme directly associated with the body’s mandate.

78.s: The National River Conservation Plan covers pollution abatement in:
o: 16 rivers in 38 districts of the National Capital Region
38 rivers in 16 States outside the Ganga basin
16 rivers in 38 States outside the Ganga basin
38 rivers in all States within the Ganga basin
78.x: The National River Conservation Plan covers pollution abatement in 38 rivers in 16 States outside the Ganga basin.
78.tq: Keep the two figures attached to the correct units—rivers and States—and note the basin exclusion.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under which programme?
78.x: The NGT directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).
78.tq: Distinguish the air-quality programme from river-conservation and biodiversity programmes.

78.s: Under the NCAP action plans referred to in the context of southern States and Puducherry, approximately what share of expenditure went towards road dust?
78.x: Approximately 86% of the expenditure under the referred NCAP action plans went towards road dust.
78.tq: Test the exact expenditure share and reject nearby percentage distractors.

78.s: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 provide for financing of:
78.x: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 provide for financing CPCB and State Pollution Control Boards.
78.tq: Identify the recipient institutions rather than the ministry or tribunal associated with environmental governance.

78.s: In the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026, Guntur was ranked second in which category?
o: Metropolitan cities with more than one million population
78.x: Guntur stood second in the towns category of Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026, which covered 130 cities.
78.tq: Link the rank with the correct category and retain the survey’s city coverage as a numerical clue.

78.s: How many cities were covered by the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026 referred to in relation to Guntur’s ranking?
78.x: The Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026 covered 130 cities.
78.tq: Recall the precise coverage figure instead of confusing it with the rank or category.

78.s: Which of the following best describes the criticism concerning the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
o: It has no statutory or administrative role in environmental information systems.
It is criticised only for transferring all functions to State governments.
It is criticised as overfunded and excessively centralised in implementation.
It is criticised as underfunded and siloed.
78.x: A stated criticism is that MoEFCC is underfunded and operates in silos.
78.tq: Select the precise criticism and avoid reversing the paired descriptors.

78.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the oldest national pollution body and the institution that replaced the NEAA?
o: NGT, established in 1974; CPCB, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1981; CAQM, established in 2010
CGWA, established in 1974; NMCG, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1974; NGT, established in 2010
78.x: CPCB, established in 1974, is the oldest national pollution body. The NGT, established in 2010, replaced the National Environment Appellate Authority (NEAA).
78.tq: Pair the correct institution with its year and distinguish the pollution regulator from the appellate tribunal.

78.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: CGWA — Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act
78.x: NBA is associated with biodiversity governance, not the National Clean Air Programme. CAQM, CGWA and NMCG are correctly matched with their respective legal basis or programme.
78.tq: Find the body–function mismatch by separating biodiversity, air-quality, groundwater and river missions.

78.s: A foreign company seeks to use a traditional medicinal practice of an Indian local community for developing a commercial product. Which institutional requirement is most appropriate?
o: It requires approval only after obtaining intellectual property rights.
It may proceed without approval because traditional knowledge is not a bio-resource.
It requires approval only from the NMCG.
It must obtain NBA approval, with access and benefit-sharing involving local communities.
78.x: Foreign access to bio-resources or associated traditional knowledge requires NBA approval, and benefit-sharing with local communities is part of the framework. NBA approval precedes intellectual property rights on such resources or knowledge.
78.tq: Apply the biopiracy safeguards to a realistic access-and-commercialisation situation.

78.s: The Central Pollution Control Board was originally constituted in 1974 under the Water Act under which name?
o: National Board for Water and Waste Management
Central Board for Air Quality and Climate Control
Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution
78.x: It was constituted in 1974 as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.
78.tq: Recall the original statutory name before its later renaming.

78.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in 1976 under the authority of the:
o: Government of India under the Air Act, 1981
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
National Green Tribunal under the Water Act, 1974
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974
78.x: The APPCB was established in 1976 by the Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974.
78.tq: Combine the correct State authority, year and parent legislation.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal (NGT):
1. It is a statutory body established under the NGT Act, 2010.
2. It is a constitutional body created directly by the Constitution of India.
3. Its headquarters is at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: The NGT is a statutory body under the NGT Act, 2010, and its headquarters is at New Delhi. It is not a constitutional body.
78.tq: Spot the wrong institutional classification by contrasting statutory and constitutional bodies.

78.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Environment (Protection) Act — 1986
2. Biological Diversity Act — 2002
3. Forest Rights Act — 2006
4. Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act — 2022
78.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: the Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986, the Biological Diversity Act in 2002, the Forest Rights Act in 2006, and the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act in 2022.
78.tq: Check each year-law pair independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs of instruments was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit, 1992?
79.x: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Convention on Biological Diversity were opened for signature at Rio in 1992.
79.tq: Start with the sure pair of agreements associated with the Rio Summit itself.

79.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the UNCCD
B. Rio Earth Summit
C. Rio+5 review
D. Rio+20 Conference
79.x: The Rio Earth Summit was held in 1992, Rio+5 in 1997, the UNCCD was adopted in 1994, and Rio+20 took place in 2012. Therefore, strictly by year the correct order is Rio Summit, UNCCD adoption, Rio+5, Rio+20; however, the provided option sequence does not reflect that order. The correct chronological sequence should be B, A, C, D.
79.tq: Place the dated events first and verify the middle two events carefully.

79.s: Rio+5, held in 1997, primarily involved which of the following?
o: A special session of the UN General Assembly reviewing Agenda 21
Establishment of the UNEA at Nairobi
79.x: Rio+5 was a special session of the United Nations General Assembly held in New York in 1997 to review the implementation of Agenda 21.
79.tq: Match the review conference with its specific institutional setting and subject.

79.s: The United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA), established as an outcome of Rio+20, has which of the following characteristics?
o: It has 193 members and meets biennially in Nairobi.
It has universal membership and meets every four years in New York.
It has 27 members and meets annually in Geneva.
It consists only of Rio Convention parties and meets biennially in Montreal.
79.x: UNEA has universal membership of 193 countries and meets every two years in Nairobi.
79.tq: Separate the body’s membership, meeting frequency and venue from those of other environmental institutions.

79.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Sustainable use of the components of biodiversity
Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies to developing countries
Fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources
79.x: The CBD objectives are conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable benefit-sharing. Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies is not one of its objectives.
79.tq: Identify the option that extends the treaty beyond its stated three-objective structure.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about the Convention on Biological Diversity:
1. It was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1993.
3. Its Secretariat is located in Montreal, Canada.
4. India ratified it in 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All four statements are correct. The CBD was opened at Rio in 1992, entered into force in 1993, has its Secretariat in Montreal and was ratified by India in 1994.
79.tq: Check treaty facts in the order of adoption, entry into force, headquarters and national ratification.

79.s: The first Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity was held at:
79.x: The first CBD COP was held at Nassau, Bahamas, in 1994.
79.tq: Use the earliest COP number to identify the earliest venue in the list.

79.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Instrument)
a. Cartagena Protocol
b. Nagoya Protocol
c. Aichi Targets
d. Kunming-Montreal GBF

List-II (Subject or feature)
i. Access and benefit-sharing
 ii. Biosafety and living modified organisms
 iii. Twenty targets for 2011–2020
 iv. Four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030
79.x: Cartagena concerns biosafety, Nagoya concerns access and benefit-sharing, the Aichi Targets numbered 20 for 2011–2020, and the Kunming-Montreal GBF contains four 2050 goals and 23 targets for 2030.
79.tq: Begin with the distinctive subject of Cartagena and eliminate codes that swap the protocols.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kunming-Montreal GBF — adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003
Cartagena Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Nagoya Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Aichi Targets — adopted in 2022 for the period 2030–2050
79.x: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 at COP-10 and entered into force in 2014. Cartagena was adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003, while the Aichi Targets and GBF have different dates.
79.tq: Check each instrument against its adoption and entry-into-force dates rather than relying on the protocol names alone.

79.s: The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety primarily deals with:
o: Protection of wetlands of international importance
Fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources
Safe transfer of living modified organisms
79.x: The Cartagena Protocol deals with biosafety and the safe transfer of living modified organisms.
79.tq: Distinguish Cartagena’s biosafety function from Nagoya’s access-and-benefit-sharing function.

79.s: The Aichi Targets were associated with which of the following?
o: 23 targets for 2030, adopted at COP-15 in 2022
17 targets for 2030, adopted at Rio in 1992
20 targets for 2011–2020, adopted at COP-10 in 2010
Four goals for 2050, adopted at COP-16 in 2024
79.x: The Aichi Targets comprised 20 targets for 2011–2020 and were adopted at CBD COP-10 in 2010.
79.tq: Pair the target count and time period before checking the COP number and year.

79.s:
With reference to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, consider the following statements:
1. It contains four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030.
2. It was adopted at COP-15 in December 2022.
3. It includes the 30x30 objective.
4. It seeks to halve food waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All four statements are correct. The framework has four 2050 goals, 23 targets for 2030, the 30x30 objective and a target to halve food waste.
79.tq: Test the numerical framework together with its major action targets.

79.s: Under the 30x30 objective of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the target is to protect by 2030:
79.x: The 30x30 objective seeks protection of 30 per cent of the world’s land and oceans by 2030.
79.tq: Read the numerical shorthand literally and avoid replacing the combined land-and-ocean target with forests alone.

79.s: Which of the following targets is associated with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework?
o: Increase harmful subsidies by 500 billion dollars per year
Cut harmful subsidies by 500 billion dollars per year
Eliminate all international trade in genetic resources by 2030
Restore only 3 per cent of degraded ecosystems
79.x: The framework seeks to cut harmful subsidies by 500 billion dollars annually and also aims to restore 30 per cent of degraded ecosystems.
79.tq: Use the direction of the policy target—cut rather than increase—as the key distinction.
