4. NABARD is India’s National Implementing Entity for the Adaptation Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The Adaptation Fund was established under the Kyoto Protocol, is financed by a 2% share of CDM CER proceeds, and NABARD is India’s National Implementing Entity.
95.tq: Combine origin, financing percentage and national implementation facts in one coded question.

95.s: Which of the following correctly describes the chronology of the Adaptation Fund?
o: Set up under Kyoto Protocol in 2001 and running from 2007
Set up at COP27 in 2022 and running from COP28
Set up in 1991 and running from 1992
Set up under the Paris Agreement in 2015 and running from 2016
95.x: The Adaptation Fund was set up under the Kyoto Protocol in 2001 and has been running from 2007.
95.tq: Use the first and last dates to distinguish the Kyoto-era fund from later climate-finance institutions.

95.s: NABARD has which of the following roles in international climate finance?
o: It is India’s National Implementing Entity for the Adaptation Fund and a Direct Access Entity of the GCF.
It is the founding body of the Global Shield and the L&D Fund.
It is the headquarters of the GCF and the trustee of the GEF.
95.x: NABARD is India’s National Implementing Entity for the Adaptation Fund and a Direct Access Entity of the Green Climate Fund.
95.tq: Test institutional roles by asking who performs the national implementation function.

95.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was:
o: created at COP27 and made operational at COP28
created at COP21 and made operational at COP22
created in 1991 and made operational in 2001
created under the Montreal Protocol and made operational at COP29
95.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was created at COP27 and became operational at COP28.
95.tq: Arrange the creation and operationalisation conferences rather than confusing them with the Paris Agreement timeline.

95.s: Which one of the following treaties is NOT primarily concerned with reducing greenhouse-gas emissions?
95.x: The Basel Convention concerns the transboundary movement of hazardous waste, not greenhouse-gas reduction. The UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement address greenhouse-gas emissions and climate change.
95.tq: Find the treaty whose environmental objective belongs to hazardous-waste management rather than climate mitigation.

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Treaty)
a. Montreal Protocol
b. Basel Convention
c. CBD
 d. Ramsar Convention

List-II (Environmental goal)
i. Wetlands
ii. Biodiversity
iii. Ozone-depleting substances
iv. Transboundary movement of hazardous waste
95.x: The Montreal Protocol addresses ozone-depleting substances, Basel concerns hazardous-waste movement, CBD concerns biodiversity and Ramsar concerns wetlands.
95.tq: Start with the distinctive ozone and wetlands pairs, then complete the remaining matches.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basel Convention — endangered species trade; Washington
95.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 in Iran and concerns wetlands.
95.tq: Use the place-year pair as the anchor for distinguishing Ramsar from other environmental treaties.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about CITES:
1. It concerns international trade in endangered species.
2. It is associated with Washington.
3. It was signed in 1973.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: CITES regulates trade in endangered species, is associated with Washington and was signed in 1973.
95.tq: Check all three identifying details before selecting the complete coded option.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the European Green Deal?
o: A voluntary forest declaration adopted at the 2014 UN Climate Summit
A UNFCCC mechanism for financing adaptation in least developed countries
A plan of the European Union to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, with Farm to Fork as a component
A scientific assessment programme jointly run by WMO and UNEP
95.x: The European Green Deal is an EU plan for net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Farm to Fork strategy is one of its components.
95.tq: Use the exact objective and institutional identity to distinguish the initiative from nearby climate mechanisms.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding The Climate Group:
1. It is an international non-profit organisation based in London.
2. It was established in 2003.
3. It runs the RE100 and EV100 initiatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The Climate Group is an international non-profit organisation based in London, established in 2003, and it runs RE100 and EV100.
95.tq: Check all three linked identity, year and associated initiatives before selecting the coded combination.

95.s: Climate Action Tracker is best described as an initiative involving which of the following?
o: The IPCC and the World Meteorological Organization
Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute
95.x: Climate Action Tracker is an independent scientific analysis initiative of Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute.
95.tq: Apply the founder-versus-function distinction to avoid confusing it with intergovernmental bodies.

95.s: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at which event and by which countries?
o: The Rio Earth Summit; India and Brazil
95.x: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at COP27 by Spain and Senegal.
95.tq: Match the initiative with its launch forum and founding countries.

95.s: The principal aim of the Early Warnings for All initiative, commonly abbreviated as EW4All, is to provide universal early-warning coverage by:
95.x: EW4All aims to achieve universal early-warning coverage by 2027.
95.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall pattern and compare the closely spaced distractor years.

95.s: Which one of the following statements about Climate Neutral Now is correct?
o: It is an EU programme launched under the Farm to Fork strategy.
It is a voluntary initiative of the UNFCCC secretariat launched in 2015.
It is a scientific assessment body established by WMO and UNEP.
It is a compulsory mechanism created by the Kyoto Protocol in 1997.
95.x: Climate Neutral Now is a voluntary initiative of the UNFCCC secretariat, launched in 2015.
95.tq: Identify the correct body, year and voluntary nature while rejecting swapped institutional descriptions.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC):
1. It was launched in 2012.
2. UNEP and six countries were involved in its launch.
3. It targets short-lived climate pollutants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The CCAC was launched in 2012 by UNEP and six countries, and it targets short-lived climate pollutants.
95.tq: Verify the date, founding participants and target area as three independent statement components.

95.s: The New York Declaration on Forests is associated with which of the following pairs?
o: 2007 Bali Conference and phase-out of ozone-depleting substances
1992 Rio Summit and compulsory finance by OECD countries
2014 UN Climate Summit and voluntary, non-binding action to halt deforestation
95.x: The New York Declaration on Forests was endorsed at the 2014 UN Climate Summit and is voluntary and non-binding, with the objective of halting deforestation. It also formed the basis of the Bonn Challenge target of 350 Mha.
95.tq: Discriminate the declaration by its year, voluntary character and forest objective.

95.s: The Bonn Challenge target associated with the New York Declaration on Forests is restoration of:
95.x: The New York Declaration on Forests provided the basis for the Bonn Challenge target of restoring 350 million hectares.
95.tq: Test the exact quantitative target rather than the broader forest objective.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):
1. It was adopted on 9 May 1992.
2. It was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit.
3. It entered into force on 21 March 1994.
4. Its secretariat is located in Bonn, Germany.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992, opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit, entered into force on 21 March 1994, and has its secretariat in Bonn, Germany.
95.tq: Separate adoption, signature, entry into force and headquarters facts instead of treating them as one date.

95.s: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 at:
o: Kyoto, before being opened for signature at Paris
Bonn, before being opened for signature at New York
Rio de Janeiro, before being opened for signature at Kyoto
New York, before being opened for signature at Rio
95.x: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 in New York and was subsequently opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992.
95.tq: Distinguish the place of adoption from the place where the treaty was opened for signature.

95.s: The UNFCCC seeks primarily to:
o: Stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level preventing dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system
Provide only financial assistance to small island developing States
Regulate international trade in endangered species
Eliminate all industrial production in developed countries
95.x: The objective of the UNFCCC is to stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
95.tq: Select the option stating the treaty’s precise objective rather than one of its related measures.

95.s:
With reference to the UNFCCC, consider the following statements:
1. It has 198 Parties.
2. The Conference of the Parties is its supreme body.
3. The COP ordinarily meets every year.
4. The SBI and SBSTA meet mid-year in Bonn.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The UNFCCC has 198 Parties; the COP is its supreme body and meets annually, while the SBI and SBSTA meet mid-year in Bonn.
95.tq: Combine institutional composition, hierarchy and meeting frequency in a coded statement question.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the UNFCCC group with its principal obligation?
o: Annex I — provide finance and technology only
Annex II — provide finance and technology to developing countries
Non-Annex I — undertake binding emission cuts identical to Annex I countries
Annex I — receive finance from developing countries
95.x: Annex II consists of OECD members of Annex I and is required to provide finance and technology to developing countries. Annex I parties are expected to lead emission cuts, while Non-Annex I parties include developing countries such as India.
95.tq: Start with the sure obligation and reject reversed authority or membership claims.

95.s: India is classified under which UNFCCC grouping?
o: Annex I and Annex II simultaneously
95.x: India is a developing country included among the Non-Annex I Parties. Non-Annex I Parties do not have binding emission cuts under the stated framework and receive special consideration where applicable.
95.tq: Use membership discrimination to separate Annex I, Annex II and Non-Annex I categories.

95.s: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) rests on the idea that:
o: Only developing countries must reduce emissions
All countries have identical historical responsibility and capabilities
Developed countries, having contributed most to historical emissions, should take the lead
Least developed countries must finance mitigation in OECD countries
95.x: CBDR-RC recognises differentiated historical responsibility and capabilities; developed countries that caused most historical emissions are expected to take the lead.
95.tq: Translate the principle into a practical responsibility allocation rather than memorising only its expansion.

95.s: Special consideration under the UNFCCC is specifically associated with which of the following groups?
o: Annex II countries and G7 members only
OECD members and economies in transition only
95.x: The UNFCCC gives special consideration to Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and Small Island Developing States (SIDS).
95.tq: Decode the paired abbreviations and distinguish vulnerable groups from developed-country categories.

95.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Rio Declaration — Principle 7
2. UNFCCC — Article 3.1
3. Paris Agreement — Article 2.2
4. Kyoto Protocol — Article 10.5
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: CBDR-RC is reflected in Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration, Article 3.1 of the UNFCCC and Article 2.2 of the Paris Agreement. The stated Kyoto Protocol reference is not part of the listed correspondence.
95.tq: Use article-number precision to eliminate the swapped or unsupported treaty reference.

95.s: The two instruments adopted under the UNFCCC framework are:
95.x: The Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement are the two instruments associated with the UNFCCC; their governing meetings are referred to as CMP and CMA respectively.
95.tq: Identify the two related instruments while rejecting treaties from other environmental regimes.

95.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in 1988 by:
o: UNESCO and the International Union for Conservation of Nature
UNDP and the International Energy Agency
UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization
95.x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
95.tq: Apply the institution-founder trap by distinguishing the IPCC’s founding bodies from other environmental organisations.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC:
1. It has 195 member countries.
2. It conducts original research independently of published literature.
3. Its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive.
4. It shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The IPCC has 195 member countries, its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive, and it shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore. It does not conduct its own original research; it assesses published literature.
95.tq: Find the single false statement among institutional role and recognition facts.

95.s: The secretariat of the IPCC is located in:
95.x: The IPCC secretariat is located in Geneva.
95.tq: Use location discrimination to distinguish the IPCC secretariat from the UNFCCC secretariat in Bonn.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly matches an IPCC Working Group with its subject?
o: WG III — impacts, adaptation and vulnerability
95.x: WG I covers the physical science basis, WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and WG III covers mitigation.
95.tq: Use the standard three-way subject mapping and reject the reversed working-group labels.

95.s: In addition to its three Working Groups, the IPCC has a Task Force on:
95.x: The IPCC has a Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories.
95.tq: Identify the exact official function rather than selecting a broadly related climate activity.

95.s:
Arrange the following IPCC Assessment Reports in chronological order:
A. AR4
B. AR1
C. AR5
D. AR2
95.x: AR1 was published in 1990, AR2 in 1995, AR4 in 2007 and AR5 in 2014. Therefore, the order is B, D, A, C.
95.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest assessment years, then place the middle reports.

95.s: The first IPCC Assessment Report, published in 1990, contributed to the development of the:
95.x: The IPCC’s First Assessment Report (AR1), published in 1990, fed into the UNFCCC, which was adopted in 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit process.
95.tq: Connect the report to its immediate institutional outcome rather than to later climate agreements.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the release date of an AR6 Working Group report?
95.x: The AR6 WG I report was released on 9 August 2021. WG II was released on 28 February 2022, WG III on 4 April 2022, and the Synthesis Report on 20 March 2023.
95.tq: Discriminate closely spaced dates by matching each date to the correct report component.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report:
1. WG I was released on 9 August 2021.
2. WG II was released on 28 February 2022.
3. WG III was released on 4 April 2022.
4. The Synthesis Report was released on 20 March 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements correctly give the release dates of the AR6 Working Group reports and the Synthesis Report.
95.tq: Check a complete date series systematically rather than relying on the year alone.

95.s: The Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) of the IPCC began in:
95.x: The IPCC’s AR7 cycle began in July 2023.
95.tq: Test the cycle-start year separately from the projected publication years.

95.s:
With reference to AR7 of the IPCC, consider the following statements:
1. The Working Group reports are expected around mid-2028.
2. The Synthesis Report is expected by late 2029.
3. The AR7 cycle began in July 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: AR7 began in July 2023; its Working Group reports are due around mid-2028 and its Synthesis Report by late 2029.
95.tq: Combine a start date with projected milestones and check each temporal statement independently.

95.s: Which one of the following best describes the role of an IPCC Summary for Policymakers (SPM)?
o: It is the annual negotiating text adopted by the UNFCCC COP.
It is a legally binding emission-reduction schedule for Annex I Parties.
It accompanies each assessment report and summarises its findings for policymakers.
It presents the IPCC’s independent original laboratory research only.
95.x: Each IPCC assessment report carries a Summary for Policymakers, which presents the assessment findings in a form relevant to policymakers. It is not a legally binding negotiating instrument.
95.tq: Distinguish an assessment communication product from a treaty, negotiating text or original research report.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and carbon credits?
o: CDM dealt with ozone-depleting substances and generated HFC credits
CDM projects in developing countries earned Certified Emission Reductions (CERs)
CDM applied exclusively to developed countries and generated Assigned Amount Units
CDM projects earned only renewable-energy certificates issued under the Paris Agreement
95.x: CDM projects in developing countries such as India earned Certified Emission Reductions, or CERs. The CDM is now being replaced by the Article 6.4 Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM).
95.tq: Use the exact mechanism-unit association and distinguish Kyoto mechanisms from Paris mechanisms.

95.s: India sought dedicated agenda space at SB64 for discussion of which Paris Agreement provision?
o: Article 9.1 on finance by developed countries
Article 28 on withdrawal from the Agreement
95.x: India requested dedicated agenda space for Article 9.1, which obliges developed countries to provide climate finance to developing countries. Article 13 concerns transparency, while Article 28 concerns withdrawal.
95.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish provisions dealing with finance, transparency and withdrawal.

95.s: Which one of the following treaties addresses greenhouse gases directly through emission-reduction commitments?
95.x: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, addresses greenhouse-gas reductions. The Basel, Stockholm and Rotterdam Conventions deal respectively with hazardous waste, persistent organic pollutants and hazardous chemicals or pesticides.
95.tq: Use treaty-subject matching to eliminate conventions dealing with waste, pollutants or chemicals.

95.s: One carbon credit generally represents:
o: One tonne of methane emitted into the atmosphere
One tonne of carbon dioxide released under an emission cap
One tonne of coal replaced by renewable energy
One tonne of carbon dioxide-equivalent reduced, avoided or removed
95.x: One carbon credit represents one tonne of carbon dioxide-equivalent emissions reduced, avoided or removed. CDM units are called Certified Emission Reductions (CERs).
95.tq: Read the unit precisely and distinguish a reduction or removal from an emission.

95.s: India signed the Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan in August 2025 under which provision of the Paris Agreement?
95.x: India signed the Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan in August 2025 under Article 6.2. India also adopted its Rules of Implementation.
95.tq: Discriminate between the cooperative approaches of Article 6.2 and the central mechanism of Article 6.4.

95.s: The next new nationally determined contributions under the five-year Paris cycle, referred to as ‘NDC 3.0’, were due for:
95.x: New NDCs are submitted every five years. The NDC 3.0 cycle was due for COP30 in 2025.
95.tq: Match the numbered NDC cycle with the specified COP year.

95.s: Which of the following is associated with Article 13 of the Paris Agreement?
o: The Enhanced Transparency Framework and Biennial Transparency Reports
The Global Stocktake every five years
The obligation to provide finance under Article 9.1
Withdrawal from the Agreement after notice
95.x: Article 13 establishes the Enhanced Transparency Framework, including common reporting through Biennial Transparency Reports. The first reports were due by the end of 2024.
95.tq: Use article-number discrimination to separate transparency, stocktake, finance and withdrawal provisions.

95.s: Under Article 28 of the Paris Agreement, a party may withdraw from the Agreement:
o: Three years after entry into force, with withdrawal taking effect one year after notice
Immediately after ratification, with effect on the same day
Only after unanimous consent of all other parties
Five years after entry into force, with effect after six months
95.x: A party may give notice of withdrawal three years after the Agreement entered into force for it, and the withdrawal takes effect one year after the notice. Unanimous consent is not required.
95.tq: Track the two separate time periods instead of merging the eligibility period with the effective period.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the United States’ withdrawal and re-entry timeline under the Paris Agreement?
o: Withdrawal announced in 2017, effective on 4 November 2020, and re-entry on 19 February 2021
Withdrawal announced in 2016, effective on 1 January 2017, and re-entry in 2020
Withdrawal announced in 2018, effective on 4 November 2019, and re-entry in 2022
Withdrawal announced in 2017, effective on 19 February 2021, and re-entry on 4 November 2020
95.x: The United States announced withdrawal in 2017, its withdrawal became effective on 4 November 2020, and it rejoined on 19 February 2021. The dates in the other options are interchanged or incorrect.
95.tq: Use first, effective and re-entry dates in sequence; beware of reversed dates.

95.s: Which of the following was a historic outcome of COP27 held at Sharm el-Sheikh?
o: Adoption of the UAE Consensus calling for transition away from fossil fuels
Establishment of loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund
Creation of the Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan
Conclusion of the first Global Stocktake
95.x: COP27 produced a historic decision to establish loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund. The UAE Consensus and the first Global Stocktake were outcomes of COP28.
95.tq: Distinguish COP27 outcomes from the later COP28 outcomes.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mitigation Work Programme associated with COP27:
1. It extends from COP27 to 2030.
2. It provides for at least two global dialogues every year.
3. Parties were urged to strengthen their 2030 targets by the end of 2023.
4. It called for phasing down unabated coal and phasing out inefficient fossil-fuel subsidies.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements correctly describe elements of the Mitigation Work Programme. It runs to 2030, includes at least two global dialogues annually and urges stronger 2030 action.
95.tq: Test the programme through its duration, frequency, deadline and policy measures.

95.s: COP27 reaffirmed the objective of keeping the increase in global average temperature:
o: Below 1.5°C as a legally binding immediate limit
Well below 2°C while pursuing efforts towards 1.5°C
95.x: COP27 reaffirmed the goal of keeping warming well below 2°C and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. It did not replace these targets with an exact 1°C limit.
95.tq: Discriminate between ‘well below 2°C’ and the pursuit of the 1.5°C goal.

95.s: Which one of the following was associated with the Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda?
o: Thirty-five outcomes for one billion people by 2025
A methane reduction target of 30 per cent from 2020 levels
Thirty outcomes for four billion people by 2030
A target of 11,000 GW renewable capacity by 2030
95.x: The Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda contained 30 outcomes intended to benefit 4 billion people by 2030. The renewable-capacity and methane targets belong to other initiatives.
95.tq: Match the initiative with its distinctive figures and avoid importing targets from other climate initiatives.

95.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: AWARe — water initiative associated with COP27
MARS — global renewable-capacity pledge of COP28
Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda — methane satellite alert system
Mitigation Work Programme — clean-cooking credit project in Myanmar
95.x: AWARe was a water initiative associated with COP27. MARS was UNEP’s methane satellite alert system, while the other pairings combine unrelated initiatives.
95.tq: Start from the sure initiative-purpose pair and reject cross-linked distractors.

95.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Global Methane Pledge is correct?
o: It was launched at COP28 by India and Japan and seeks a 30 per cent cut from 2015 levels by 2030.
It was launched at COP26 by the United States and the European Union and seeks a 30 per cent cut from 2020 levels by 2030.
It was launched at COP27 by G7 and V20 and targets methane neutrality by 2040.
It was launched at COP26 by Spain and Senegal and addresses drought resilience.
95.x: The Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP26 by the United States and the European Union and aims to cut methane emissions by 30 per cent from 2020 levels by 2030. India is not a member.
95.tq: Check the launch COP, founders, baseline year and target together; one swapped detail makes an option wrong.

95.s: The sector goals of the Glasgow Breakthroughs include all of the following EXCEPT:
95.x: The Glasgow Breakthroughs cover power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture. Mercury management is associated with the Minamata Convention, not the Glasgow Breakthroughs.
95.tq: Find the item that belongs to a different environmental treaty or subject.

95.s: Which of the following correctly describes the UAE Consensus adopted at COP28?
o: It replaced nationally determined contributions with legally fixed national quotas.
It was the first decision to establish the Kyoto Protocol’s CDM.
It limited the Global Stocktake to once every ten years.
It was the first COP decision calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems.
95.x: The UAE Consensus was the first COP decision calling for a transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. It also followed the conclusion of the first Global Stocktake at COP28.
95.tq: Identify the distinctive wording of the COP28 decision and reject substitutions from Kyoto or Paris procedures.

95.s: Which of the following energy pledges was associated with COP28?
o: Reducing renewable capacity to 4,000 GW and increasing efficiency gains to 11 per cent annually
Cutting methane by 30 per cent from 2020 levels and phasing out all coal by 2025
Providing 30 adaptation outcomes for four billion people by 2030
Tripling renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and doubling energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent annually by 2030
95.x: COP28 included pledges to triple renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and double energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent per year by 2030. The other options combine targets from different initiatives or alter the figures.
95.tq: Pair the two numerical targets and their deadline; beware of reversed or borrowed figures.

95.s: Which one of the following statements about COP28 is correct?
o: It operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund and concluded the first Global Stocktake.
It first established the COP27 Mitigation Work Programme and the Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda.
It launched the Global Methane Pledge with India as a member.
It created the Article 28 withdrawal procedure of the Paris Agreement.
95.x: COP28 concluded the first Global Stocktake and operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund. The Mitigation Work Programme and Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda are associated with COP27, while Article 28 is a provision of the Paris Agreement.
95.tq: Use the COP-number timeline to separate outcomes belonging to COP27, COP28 and the Paris Agreement itself.

95.s: At COP26, India advocated which formulation regarding unabated coal power?
95.x: India advocated a phase-down, rather than a phase-out, of unabated coal power at COP26.
95.tq: Distinguish the closely related terms ‘phase-down’ and ‘phase-out’.

95.s: India called for a dedicated agenda on developed-country finance obligations at which forum?
95.x: India called for a dedicated agenda on developed-country finance obligations at Bonn SB64.
95.tq: Match the demand with the forum where it was raised.

95.s: India's position regarding the NCQG was that the core target of US$300 billion per year was:
o: More than sufficient for developing countries
95.x: India criticised the US$300 billion annual NCQG target as inadequate.
95.tq: Use the stated evaluation of the finance target rather than its amount alone.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change concerning India's proposed hosting of COP33?
o: India announced the bid at COP26 and confirmed it at COP30.
India announced the bid at COP28 and withdrew it in April 2026 after reviewing its commitments for 2028.
India announced and withdrew the bid at COP29.
India withdrew the bid before COP28 was held.
95.x: The Prime Minister announced India's bid for COP33 at COP28 on 1 December 2023; it was withdrawn in April 2026 after a review of commitments for 2028.
95.tq: Track the announcement and withdrawal as a two-event sequence.

95.s: The national statement of India at COP30 was delivered on 17 November 2025 by the:
95.x: India's COP30 National Statement was delivered on 17 November 2025 by the Union Environment Minister.
95.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the official statement.

95.s: The earlier climate-finance goal that remained a major focus at COP26 was:
95.x: The earlier goal was to mobilise US$100 billion annually, and it was a major focus at COP26.
95.tq: Separate the earlier finance goal from the later NCQG target.

95.s:
With reference to the Loss and Damage Fund, arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Operationalisation of the Fund
B. Agreement to establish the Fund
C. Opening of the Fund to applications
D. End of the World Bank’s interim-host period
95.x: The Fund was agreed at COP27 in 2022, operationalised at COP28 in 2023, opened to applications at COP30, and the World Bank’s interim role extends until COP33 in 2028.
95.tq: Start with the agreement and then place operationalisation, applications and the terminal year.

95.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was agreed at COP27 and operationalised at:
95.x: The Fund was agreed at COP27 in 2022 and operationalised at COP28 in 2023.
95.tq: Distinguish establishment from operationalisation.

95.s: Which institution serves as the interim host and trustee of the Loss and Damage Fund?
95.x: The World Bank is the interim host and trustee of the Fund for four years, until COP33 in 2028.
95.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ institutional trap.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the Board of the Loss and Damage Fund:
1. It has 26 members.
2. It consists of 14 members from developing countries and 12 from developed countries.
3. It takes decisions by majority vote only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The Board has 26 members, including 14 from developing countries and 12 from developed countries. It decides by consensus, so statement 3 is incorrect.
95.tq: Locate the wrong decision-making method after verifying the composition.

95.s: The Loss and Damage Fund covers losses arising from:
o: Both economic and non-economic losses from sudden- and slow-onset events
95.x: The Fund covers economic and non-economic losses resulting from both sudden-onset and slow-onset events.
95.tq: Check both dimensions of the coverage instead of accepting an ‘only’ statement.

95.s: Which statement correctly describes the start-up phase of the Loss and Damage Fund?
o: It is financed exclusively by the World Bank.
It operates under the Barbados Implementation Modalities, and capitalisation remains small.
It has no application process until COP33.
It operates under the Kyoto Implementation Modalities and is fully capitalised.
95.x: The start-up phase is under the Barbados Implementation Modalities. The Fund was opened to applications at COP30, but its capitalisation remains small.
95.tq: Match the fund with its stated implementation framework and current limitation.

95.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two finance figures associated with the NCQG adopted at COP29?
o: US$300 billion per year by 2035 from developed countries, and a wider call for US$1.3 trillion per year from all sources by 2035
US$1.3 trillion per year by 2030 from developed countries, and US$300 billion from all sources by 2035
US$300 billion in total by 2035 from all countries, with no wider finance call
US$100 billion per year by 2035 from developed countries, and US$300 billion from all sources by 2030
95.x: COP29 set a core mobilisation goal of US$300 billion annually by 2035 for developed countries and made a wider call for US$1.3 trillion annually from all sources by 2035.
95.tq: Separate the core target, its contributor group and the wider finance call.

95.s: The NCQG was adopted at COP29 held in:
95.x: COP29 was held in Baku in November 2024, where the NCQG figures were finalised.
95.tq: Use the location-year pairing to distinguish successive COP outcomes.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the outcome on Article 6 at COP29:
1. Rules for Article 6.2 were finalised.
2. Rules for Article 6.4 were finalised.
3. Article 6.4 establishes the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism under UN supervision.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: COP29 finalised rules for Article 6.2 and Article 6.4. Article 6.4 provides for the UN-supervised Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism, or PACM.
95.tq: Use the all-correct combination after checking each Article 6 component.

95.s: The Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism finalised under Article 6.4 is intended to replace the:
95.x: The UN-supervised Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism under Article 6.4 is intended to replace the Clean Development Mechanism.
95.tq: Distinguish the new Paris mechanism from the earlier Kyoto mechanism.

95.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
95.x: COP30 was described as the ‘COP of Implementation’ and also as the ‘COP of Truth’.
95.tq: Start from the distinctive conference title and reject unrelated labels.

95.s: The outcome package of COP30 was known as the:
95.x: The COP30 outcome was called the Belém Political Package and was framed in a ‘mutirão’ spirit.
95.tq: Match the outcome document with the host city.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about COP30 outcomes:
1. The outcome was framed in a ‘mutirão’ spirit.
2. COP30 identified six thematic axes.
3. The Baku-to-Belém Roadmap concerned mobilisation of US$1.3 trillion.
4. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility was associated with US$125 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements correctly describe the COP30 outcome package and its associated thematic and financial initiatives.
95.tq: Verify each independent COP30 outcome before selecting the complete combination.

95.s: At COP30, the agreed adaptation-finance outcome was to:
o: Fix adaptation finance only for developed countries
95.x: COP30 agreed to at least triple adaptation finance.
95.tq: Identify the direction and minimum scale of the finance commitment.

95.s: How many voluntary indicators were associated with the Global Goal on Adaptation at COP30?
95.x: COP30 associated 59 voluntary indicators with the Global Goal on Adaptation.
95.tq: Recall the exact quantitative detail rather than the nearby finance figures.

95.s: The Belem 4x pledge refers to quadrupling sustainable fuels by:
95.x: The Belem 4x pledge aims to quadruple sustainable fuels by 2035.
95.tq: Link the pledge name to its target year and action.

95.s: Which one of the following is a stated feature of NDC 3.0?
o: It is economy-wide, covers all gases and is intended to align with 1.5°C.
It applies only to developed countries.
It is limited to carbon dioxide alone.
95.x: NDC 3.0 calls for economy-wide, all-gas pledges aligned with the 1.5°C objective and due for COP30.
95.tq: Test the scope of the pledge by checking economy-wide and all-gas coverage.

95.s: Global climate finance was estimated at US$1.9 trillion in 2023. Developing countries excluding China received approximately:
95.x: Developing countries excluding China received approximately 15% of global climate finance in 2023.
95.tq: Use the percentage-share comparison rather than the total finance figure.

95.s: The Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C was released in:
95.x: The Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C was released in October 2018.
95.tq: Distinguish the special report’s release date from the AR6 dates.

95.s: Pathways limiting warming to 1.5°C require global net human-caused CO2 emissions by 2030 to be approximately:
95.x: The pathways require approximately a 45% reduction from 2010 levels by 2030.
95.tq: Check both the percentage and the baseline year.

95.s: The Special Report indicated that global net-zero CO2 emissions should be reached around:
95.x: The report’s 1.5°C pathways require global net-zero CO2 emissions around 2050.
95.tq: Distinguish the net-zero date from the 2030 reduction milestone.

95.s: Which approach is inconsistent with the mitigation pathways described for limiting warming to 1.5°C?
95.x: The pathways require cuts that are deep, rapid and sustained; gradual or limited cuts are not sufficient.
95.tq: Find the option that reverses the required characteristics of mitigation.

95.s: The Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report was released on:
95.x: The Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report was released on 20 March 2023 and closed the AR6 cycle.
95.tq: Match the report title with its exact release date.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the findings of the AR6 Synthesis Report:
1. Human influence has unequivocally warmed the climate.
2. Global surface temperature for 2011–2020 was already about 1.1°C above the pre-industrial level.
3. Greenhouse-gas emissions were at their highest level in human history.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are findings associated with the AR6 Synthesis Report.
95.tq: Verify the evidence statements individually before choosing the complete combination.

95.s: Without immediate, deep emission cuts, the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the:
95.x: The AR6 assessment states that the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the early 2030s without immediate, deep cuts.
95.tq: Distinguish the near-term threshold crossing from the longer net-zero horizon.

95.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the mitigation pathway described in the AR6 assessment?
o: Emissions peak before 2025; net zero by mid-century; renewables provide 70–85% of global electricity by 2050
Emissions peak in 2025; net zero by 2030; renewables provide 100% of electricity by 2040
Emissions peak before 2020; net zero by 2040; renewables provide 40–50% by 2050
Emissions peak after 2035; net zero by 2070; renewables below 30% of electricity by 2050
95.x: The stated pathway requires global emissions to peak before 2025, reach net zero by mid-century, and obtain 70–85% of electricity from renewables by 2050.
95.tq: Check all three linked milestones—peak, net zero and renewable electricity share.

95.s: For a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C, the remaining carbon budget from 2020 was assessed at approximately:
95.x: AR6 Working Group I placed the remaining carbon budget for a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C at about 500 GtCO2 from 2020.
95.tq: Recall the quantitative carbon-budget estimate and its probability condition.

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (AR6 contribution)
a. Working Group I
a. Working Group II
c. Working Group III
d. Synthesis Report

List-II (Title)
i. Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change
ii. Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report
iii. Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis
iv. Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: Working Group I corresponds to the Physical Science Basis; Working Group II to Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability; Working Group III to Mitigation; and the final report is the Synthesis Report.
95.tq: Start with the sure title pair and eliminate codes with mismatched report themes.

95.s: Which one of the following is an India-relevant finding of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6)?
o: India's warming is confined to its coastal regions
India has experienced no significant change in heatwave intensity
India is warming more slowly than the global average
India is warming faster than the global average
95.x: The IPCC AR6 indicates that India is warming faster than the global average and is experiencing more frequent and intense heatwaves.
95.tq: Use the precise comparative statement and reject the reversed comparison.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding climate-related changes in India:
1. Erratic monsoons can cause severe floods.
2. Sea-level rise threatens coastal megacities such as Mumbai and Chennai.
3. High mountains in India are warming at twice the global average.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. AR6 associates erratic monsoons with severe floods, identifies risks to Mumbai and Chennai from sea-level rise, and reports that high mountains are warming at twice the global average.
95.tq: Test each statement independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.

95.s: The Gangotri Glacier has retreated by approximately how much since 1935?
95.x: The Gangotri Glacier has retreated approximately 1,700 metres since 1935.
95.tq: Distinguish the exact numerical value from nearby magnitude distractors.

95.s: Black carbon deposited on snow accelerates glacier melting primarily by
o: preventing solar radiation from reaching the snow
95.x: Black carbon lowers the albedo of snow, causing it to absorb more solar energy and thereby accelerating melting.
95.tq: Apply the albedo relationship to identify the correct cause-and-effect link.

95.s: According to the AR6-related finding, what proportion of mountain species may face extinction by 2100?
95.x: AR6 warns that up to 25 percent of mountain species may face extinction by 2100.
95.tq: Focus on the stated upper-limit figure and the associated time horizon.

95.s: Marine heatwave frequency during 1982–2016 was reported to have
95.x: Marine heatwave frequency doubled during the period 1982–2016.
95.tq: Use the period and the exact trend together to avoid a reversed comparison.

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Special report)
A. Climate Change and Land
B. Ocean and Cryosphere

List-II (Release)
1. August 2019
2. September 2019

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: The Special Report on Climate Change and Land was released in August 2019, while the Special Report on Ocean and Cryosphere was released in September 2019.
95.tq: Start from the sure date-report pair and eliminate codes with a swapped month.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ocean and Cryosphere — oceans absorbed more than 90% of excess heat
Climate Change and Land — food security
Climate Change and Land — desertification and land degradation
Ocean and Cryosphere — reduction in the frequency of marine heatwaves
95.x: The Ocean and Cryosphere report highlighted that marine heatwaves became more frequent, along with coral bleaching and fisheries impacts. The other pairs are correctly matched.
95.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the reported trend.

95.s: The oceans' absorption of more than 90 percent of excess heat and sea-level rise through thermal expansion and ice melt are key findings of which report?
o: IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C
Special Report on Ocean and Cryosphere
Special Report on Climate Change and Land
95.x: These findings are associated with the IPCC Special Report on Ocean and Cryosphere, released in September 2019.
95.tq: Match the distinctive subject matter to the correct report title.

95.s: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) are best described as
o: observational datasets used exclusively for sea-level projections
narratives of future society involving population, economy and policy, used with forcing levels in AR6 scenarios
legally binding emission targets for developed countries
financial mechanisms for compensating climate-related loss and damage
95.x: SSPs are narratives concerning future population, economic and policy conditions that are used with forcing levels in AR6 scenarios.
95.tq: Choose the definition that includes the concept's purpose and component dimensions.

95.s: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways in AR6 replaced which set of scenarios used in AR5?
95.x: SSPs replaced the four Representative Concentration Pathways, or RCPs, used in AR5.
95.tq: Discriminate between scenario frameworks and climate-policy principles.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
95.x: SSP3 represents Regional Rivalry. SSP1 represents Sustainability, SSP2 the Middle of the Road, SSP4 Inequality and SSP5 Fossil-fuelled Development.
95.tq: Use elimination across the closely related SSP narrative names.

95.s: Which of the following represents one of the illustrative AR6 scenarios?
95.x: SSP2-4.5 is one of the AR6 illustrative scenarios. The listed AR6 scenarios also include SSP1-1.9, SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5.
95.tq: Identify the correct combination of the SSP prefix and forcing-level format.

95.s: RCP8.5 was introduced in
95.x: RCP8.5 was introduced in 2011 as one of the four RCPs.
95.tq: Test the precise year rather than the associated assessment-report year.

95.s: Why does AR6 remain the current authority during the initial period of the AR7 cycle?
o: AR6 was issued after AR7 began
AR7 was cancelled after its first meeting
AR7 is limited to biodiversity and excludes climate change
AR7 reports are expected only from about 2028, with synthesis by late 2029
95.x: AR7 began in July 2023, but its Working Group reports are expected only from about mid-2028 and its Synthesis Report by late 2029; therefore AR6 remains the current authority in the interim.
95.tq: Link the sequence of dates to the conclusion rather than treating the cycles as overlapping authorities.

95.s: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize equally with
95.x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize equally with former United States Vice President Al Gore.
95.tq: Use the recipient relationship and year as a paired recall fact.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a mitigation constraint for India?
o: India's complete freedom from dependence on coal
Insufficient availability of appropriate alternative technologies
Need for growth and industrialisation for a large population in poverty
Inability to invest huge funds in research and development
95.x: India remains dependent on coal, so complete freedom from coal dependence is not a stated condition. Limited availability of alternatives, restricted R&D capacity and development needs are recognised constraints.
95.tq: Reject the absolute statement that contradicts the stated constraint.

95.s: India argues that developed countries should provide which of the following for its transition to cleaner development?
o: A waiver from all environmental obligations
Only military technology and concessional food aid
Clean and affordable technology and finance
95.x: India argues that developed countries should provide clean, affordable technology and finance to support the transition.
95.tq: Identify the policy demand that directly connects technology with finance.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT a coal-related technology or measure listed in the context of India's mitigation approach?
95.x: India's listed coal-related measures include coal washing, electrostatic precipitators, coal gasification, wet scrubbers, low-NOx burners and CCS/CCUS. Ocean fertilisation is not among them.
95.tq: Find the unrelated technology among measures belonging to the same mitigation cluster.

95.s: Gevra and Rajmahal, included on the LINGO list of carbon bombs, are respectively located in
95.x: Gevra is a coal mine in Chhattisgarh and Rajmahal is a coal mine in Jharkhand; both are on the LINGO list of carbon bombs.
95.tq: Start with the location pair and avoid reversing the two named mines.

95.s: India's target of net-zero emissions by 2070 is later than the 2050 target of most developed countries primarily because of its
o: development needs and continuing dependence on coal
95.x: India links its later net-zero target to development priorities, a large population needing growth and industrialisation, and continuing coal dependence.
95.tq: Connect the stated socioeconomic and energy constraints to the policy timeline.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding climate equity:
1. Developed countries emitted most of the historical stock of greenhouse gases.
2. India's per capita emissions are much lower than those of industrialised nations.
3. Developing countries argue that they need carbon space to grow.
4. Climate justice recognises that those who emitted least may suffer the most.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements express the climate-equity position: historical responsibility lies mainly with developed countries, India's per capita emissions are lower, developing countries seek carbon space, and those least responsible may suffer most.
95.tq: Combine historical, per-capita, developmental and justice dimensions before selecting the code.

95.s: The Loss and Damage Fund established in the context of COP27 in 2022 was viewed primarily as
o: an ethical win for climate justice
a trade tariff on imported steel
a mechanism for increasing coal production
a replacement for the IPCC assessment process
95.x: The Loss and Damage Fund associated with COP27 in 2022 was regarded as an ethical win in the context of climate justice.
95.tq: Match the named fund with its stated equity significance.

95.s: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) applies to imports including
o: iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity
only crude oil and natural gas

96.s: Which one of the following organisations or initiatives is correctly matched with its focus?
o: IRIS — infrastructure resilience of Small Island Developing States
96.x: IRIS, or Infrastructure for Resilient Island States, focuses on Small Island Developing States and was launched at COP26 in 2021.
96.tq: Match an acronym with its sectoral focus and avoid neighbouring climate institutions.

96.s: IRIS, the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States initiative, was launched at:
o: The UN Climate Action Summit in 2019
96.x: IRIS was launched at COP26 in 2021 and focuses on Small Island Developing States.
96.tq: Distinguish the launch year and forum of a related climate initiative.

96.s: The term ‘LiFE’ in the context of India’s environmental initiatives stands for:
96.x: LiFE is the abbreviation for Lifestyle for Environment.
96.tq: Test the exact official expansion of an acronym rather than a plausible substitute.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Mission LiFE:
1. The idea of LiFE was introduced at COP26.
2. Mission LiFE was launched in October 2022 at Kevadia.
3. The mission was launched in the presence of the United Nations Secretary-General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: The LiFE idea was introduced at COP26, while Mission LiFE was launched at Kevadia in October 2022 in the presence of the UN Secretary-General.
96.tq: Separate the introduction of an idea from the later formal launch of a mission.

96.s: The LiFE Global Movement was launched on:
96.x: The LiFE Global Movement was launched on 5 June 2022.
96.tq: Distinguish the date of the global movement from the date of Mission LiFE's formal launch.

96.s: The principal behavioural orientation of Mission LiFE is to shift the focus from:
o: State action to individual behaviour and mindful consumption
96.x: Mission LiFE seeks to move the focus from state action towards individual behaviour, especially mindful consumption.
96.tq: Apply the mission's central concept to identify the direction of the policy shift.

96.s: In Mission LiFE, the expression ‘P3’ refers to:
96.x: P3 stands for ‘Pro-Planet People’, the community that Mission LiFE seeks to build through environmentally responsible behaviour.
96.tq: Discriminate the official expansion of a short policy expression from familiar environmental phrases.

96.s:
Arrange the following phases of behavioural change under Mission LiFE in the correct sequence:
A. Policy
B. Demand
C. Supply
D. Regulation of international trade
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
96.x: The three phases of behavioural change are demand, followed by supply, followed by policy. Regulation of international trade is not one of the stated phases.
96.tq: Start with the first phase and eliminate the item that does not belong to the sequence.

96.s: Mission LiFE includes how many specified actions organised under how many themes?
96.x: Mission LiFE lists 75 actions under seven themes.
96.tq: Pair the count of actions with the count of themes instead of treating the figures independently.

96.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the seven action themes of Mission LiFE?
96.x: The LiFE themes include saving energy and water, rejecting single-use plastic, sustainable food systems, reducing waste and e-waste, and healthy lifestyles. Expansion of coal-based power generation is not a LiFE action theme.
96.tq: Find the one option outside the environmental-behavioural group.

96.s: Which of the following pairs of existing Indian initiatives is aligned with Mission LiFE?
96.x: UJALA, associated with LED bulbs, and PAT, associated with industrial efficiency, are aligned with Mission LiFE.
96.tq: Match the mission with domestic schemes rather than international organisations or climate partnerships.

96.s: UJALA and PAT are associated respectively with:
o: Single-use plastic bans and e-waste recycling
Water conservation and sustainable food systems
96.x: UJALA is associated with LED bulbs, while PAT is an industrial-efficiency initiative aligned with LiFE.
96.tq: Separate two similarly placed schemes by their specific application areas.

96.s: Mission LiFE has been incorporated into which version of India’s Nationally Determined Contributions?
96.x: LiFE is written into NDC 3.0.
96.tq: Test the exact numbered policy version associated with the initiative.

96.s: India announced its target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070 at which international climate conference?
96.x: India announced its 2070 net-zero target at COP26 held in Glasgow in 2021.
96.tq: Use the event-year association to distinguish the announcement from the later strategy submission.

96.s: India defends its comparatively later net-zero target primarily on the grounds of:
o: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and development needs
The absence of forest and tree cover
96.x: India invokes the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) and its development requirements to justify the 2070 target, later than the 2050 targets of most developed countries.
96.tq: Identify the principle and policy rationale rather than merely recalling the target year.

96.s:
With reference to net-zero emissions, consider the following statements:
1. It means that greenhouse gases emitted by a country are balanced by removals.
2. Forests and carbon capture can contribute to such removals.
3. It necessarily means that all gross greenhouse-gas emissions have become zero.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Net zero does not require gross emissions to become zero; residual emissions are balanced by removals.
96.tq: Reject the absolute interpretation that confuses net-zero emissions with zero gross emissions.

96.s: Which one of the following is identified as a key programme for achieving the carbon-sink target in India's LT-LEDS?
96.x: The Green India Mission is identified as a key programme for the carbon-sink target in the LT-LEDS.
96.tq: Match the programme with the specific function assigned to it.

96.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to India's net-zero pathway:
a. National Green Hydrogen Mission — ₹19,744 crore and 5 MMT annual target
b. Nuclear Mission — Supporting mission for the net-zero pathway
c. Green India Mission — Key programme for the carbon-sink target
d. LT-LEDS — Submitted at COP27 in November 2022
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
96.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Green Hydrogen Mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and a 5 MMT annual target; the Nuclear Mission is also a supporting mission, while the Green India Mission and LT-LEDS have the stated roles and date.
96.tq: Check each programme against its amount, role or date before selecting the coded combination.

96.s: The annual production target associated with the National Green Hydrogen Mission in the net-zero pathway is:
96.x: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is associated with an annual production target of 5 MMT and an outlay of ₹19,744 crore.
96.tq: Use the numerical pair of outlay and annual capacity to avoid confusing the mission’s two figures.

96.s: The Net Zero Portal launched in September 2026 is primarily intended for:
o: Mandatory reporting of only Scope 3 emissions by all firms
Assessment of India's rank in the CCPI
Voluntary disclosure of corporate net-zero targets
96.x: The Net Zero Portal provides for voluntary disclosure of corporate net-zero targets.
96.tq: Identify the portal’s stated purpose rather than associating it with a broader climate institution.

96.s: With reference to reporting under the Net Zero Portal, which one of the following is correct?
o: Scope 1 reporting is voluntary, while Scope 2 and Scope 3 reporting are compulsory.
Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting is encouraged, while Scope 3 reporting is voluntary.
All three scopes are excluded from corporate disclosure.
96.x: The portal encourages reporting of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while Scope 3 reporting is voluntary.
96.tq: Discriminate among the three emissions scopes and note the different reporting status attached to them.

96.s: The Net Zero Portal was launched along with a NAPCC Dashboard that:
96.x: The NAPCC Dashboard launched with the Net Zero Portal tracks the national missions.
96.tq: Link the dashboard to its monitoring function rather than to a single technology or index.

96.s: Which technology is specifically used to capture carbon dioxide from industrial processes?
96.x: Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), also referred to as CCS when utilisation is not specified, captures carbon dioxide from industrial processes.
96.tq: Recognise the exact technology term associated with industrial carbon-dioxide capture.

96.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven transitions identified in India's LT-LEDS?
96.x: The seven transitions include low-carbon electricity systems, low-carbon transport, urban adaptation and efficient buildings, decoupling growth from industrial emissions, CO2 removal, forest and vegetation cover, and low-carbon finance. Expansion of fossil-fuel electricity systems is not one of them.
96.tq: Find the option that reverses the low-carbon direction common to the listed transitions.

96.s:
Arrange the following stages associated with India's climate policy in chronological order:
A. Announcement of the 2070 net-zero target
B. Submission of the LT-LEDS to the UNFCCC
C. Launch of the Net Zero Portal
D. Announcement of the Panchamrit commitments at Glasgow
96.x: The Panchamrit commitments were announced on 1 November 2021; the net-zero target was announced at COP26 in 2021; the LT-LEDS was submitted in November 2022; and the Net Zero Portal was launched in September 2026. In the stated sequence, the Glasgow Panchamrit announcement precedes the other listed stages.
96.tq: Use the dated milestones first and place the portal last from its 2026 date.

96.s: The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is published by which group of organisations?
o: Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network International
96.x: The CCPI is published by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network (CAN) International.
96.tq: Use the publisher-organisation combination to distinguish the CCPI from UN and financial institutions.

96.s: The Climate Change Performance Index is released at the:
o: Conference of the Parties on climate change
Convention on Biological Diversity Conference only
96.x: The CCPI is released at the Conference of the Parties (COP) on climate change.
96.tq: Associate the index with the climate-conference setting in which it is released.

96.s: In the Climate Change Performance Index 2019 considered in the APPSC 2018 examination, India's rank was:
96.x: India was ranked 9th in the 2019 CCPI referred to in the APPSC 2018 question.
96.tq: Distinguish the specified index edition from unspecified later editions.

96.s: The five commitments collectively known as 'Panchamrit' were announced by the Prime Minister at Glasgow on:
96.x: The Panchamrit commitments were announced at Glasgow on 1 November 2021 during COP26.
96.tq: Pair the named initiative with its exact announcement date and venue.

96.s: Which of the following correctly represents the quantitative memory sequence of the five Panchamrit commitments?
96.x: The Panchamrit sequence is 500 GW, 50 percent, 1 billion tonnes, 45 percent and net zero by 2070.
96.tq: Retain the five-number memory hook in its stated order.

96.s: The Panchamrit commitment concerning non-fossil capacity is:
96.x: One Panchamrit commitment is to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
96.tq: Separate the capacity figure from the percentage and long-term net-zero pledge.

96.s:
With reference to the Panchamrit renewable-energy commitment, consider the following statements:
1. It concerns 50 percent of energy requirements from renewables.
2. In the NDC formulation, it is expressed as 50 percent of installed capacity.
3. Its target year is 2070.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The target year for this commitment is 2030, not 2070; 2070 applies to the net-zero commitment.
96.tq: Apply the capacity-versus-energy distinction and identify the wrong target year.

96.s: The Panchamrit commitment to reduce projected emissions by 1 billion tonnes is to be achieved by:
96.x: India’s Panchamrit commitment is to cut projected emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030.
96.tq: Match the reduction figure with the common 2030 milestone of the medium-term commitments.

96.s: The commitment to reduce emissions intensity under Panchamrit is:
96.x: The commitment is to reduce emissions intensity by 45 percent from the 2005 level by 2030.
96.tq: Check the baseline year, percentage and target year together.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported progress relating to the Panchamrit commitments?
o: Non-fossil capacity of 500 GW achieved by 2020
Emissions intensity reduction of 36 percent by 2020
96.x: A 36 percent reduction in emissions intensity from the 2005 level had been achieved by 2020, while the 45 percent target is for 2030.
96.tq: Distinguish an achieved interim figure from the ultimate target.

96.s: As recorded for September 2025, the renewable-energy-related Panchamrit indicator was approximately:
96.x: Approximately 51 percent had been achieved by September 2025 for the commitment concerning the share of energy requirements from renewables, expressed in the NDC as installed capacity.
96.tq: Use the progress date and figure together, avoiding confusion with the 45 percent emissions-intensity target.

96.s:
Which of the following pairs of Panchamrit commitments and target years is correctly matched?
1. 500 GW non-fossil capacity — 2030
2. 45 percent reduction in emissions intensity — 2030
3. Net zero — 2070
4. One billion tonnes reduction in projected emissions — 2050
96.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The one-billion-tonne reduction in projected emissions is targeted for 2030, not 2050.
96.tq: Find the single wrong year among otherwise correctly paired commitments.

96.s: Which two Panchamrit commitments entered India's August 2022 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)?
o: 500 GW non-fossil capacity and net zero by 2070
45 percent emissions-intensity reduction and 50 percent renewable-energy commitment
One billion tonnes reduction and 500 GW capacity
Net zero by 2070 and one billion tonnes reduction
96.x: The 45 percent emissions-intensity reduction commitment and the 50 percent renewable-energy commitment entered the August 2022 NDC.
96.tq: Identify the two medium-term percentage pledges rather than the capacity, reduction-volume or long-term pledge.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the renewable-energy pledge from the non-fossil-capacity pledge under Panchamrit?
o: The former concerns 50 percent, while the latter concerns 500 GW, both with a 2030 target.
The former concerns 500 GW, while the latter concerns 50 percent, both with a 2070 target.
Both concern 50 percent of energy generation by 2030.
Both concern 500 GW of installed capacity by 2070.
96.x: The renewable-energy pledge is expressed as 50 percent of energy requirements, or 50 percent of installed capacity in the NDC formulation, while the separate non-fossil pledge is 500 GW; both are targeted for 2030.
96.tq: Split the options by comparing the unit—percentage versus gigawatts—and the common target year.

96.s: The Green Credit Programme was introduced in October 2023 under which of the following legal provisions?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981

96.s: Which of the following is the administrator of the Green Credit Programme?
o: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, New Delhi
Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, Dehradun

96.s: Which one of the following is NOT covered as an activity under the Green Credit Programme?
96.x: The programme covers activities such as tree planting, water management, sustainable agriculture, waste management, air-pollution reduction, mangroves, ecomark and sustainable buildings. Deep-sea mineral extraction is not listed.
96.tq: Find the option outside the programme’s stated activity list.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Green Credit Programme:
1. It is a market-based incentive mechanism.
2. It is intended only for compulsory environmental actions.
3. Afforestation credits under it can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: The programme is a market-based incentive for voluntary environmental actions, so statement 2 is false. Afforestation under the programme can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
96.tq: Identify the false extreme word ‘only’ and retain the two supported statements.

96.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme of India combines which of the following mechanisms?
o: A compliance mechanism and an offset mechanism
A voluntary mechanism and an import mechanism
A taxation mechanism and a subsidy mechanism
A conservation mechanism and a litigation mechanism
96.x: The Indian Carbon Market combines a compliance mechanism for energy-intensive sectors with an offset mechanism for voluntary projects in ten sectors.
96.tq: Distinguish the two complementary designs of the carbon market.

96.s: Under the compliance mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, an obligated entity that performs better than its notified GHG Emission Intensity target:
o: Must purchase additional Carbon Credit Certificates
Receives a Carbon Credit Certificate that can be traded
Receives a direct compensation from the Union Budget
Is exempted from all environmental regulations
96.x: Entities that beat their notified GHG Emission Intensity targets earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates. Entities that miss their targets must buy certificates.
96.tq: Apply the compliance rule to the entity’s performance against its target.

96.s: Which of the following correctly describes the offset mechanism under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
o: It applies only to obligated aluminium and cement units.
It covers voluntary projects in ten sectors using approved methodologies.
It permits offsets without any approved methodology.
It covers compulsory projects in all agricultural districts.
96.x: The offset mechanism covers voluntary projects in ten sectors, including agriculture and waste, and uses approved methodologies.
96.tq: Separate the voluntary offset design from the mandatory compliance design.

96.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was notified in June 2023 under Section 14AA of the:
o: Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022
96.x: The scheme was notified in June 2023 under Section 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022.
96.tq: Check the exact section-and-statute combination.

96.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was designed to contribute to which intensity-reduction target?
96.x: The scheme was designed to meet the 45 percent intensity target.
96.tq: Use the nearby percentage figures as a numerical discrimination test.

96.s: Who administers the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education under the Ministry of Environment
Central Pollution Control Board under the Ministry of Coal
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
96.x: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, under the Ministry of Power, administers the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.
96.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method for institutional responsibility.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Carbon Market:
1. The compliance mechanism assigns GHG Emission Intensity targets to obligated entities.
2. Entities missing their targets are required to buy Carbon Credit Certificates.
3. The offset mechanism is limited to projects in ten sectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: All three statements are correct: compliance entities receive intensity targets, underperforming entities buy certificates, and the offset mechanism covers voluntary projects in ten sectors.
96.tq: Test the complete compliance-versus-offset comparison.

96.s: The GHG Emission Intensity targets notified in October 2025 initially covered which group of sectors?
o: Aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper
96.x: The October 2025 targets covered aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper.
96.tq: Match the notification with its exact sectoral coverage.

96.s: Which of the following correctly represents the current scale of the Indian carbon market as stated?
o: Ten sectors, about 282 industries and about 477 Mt CO2e
Four sectors, about 490 industries and about 282 Mt CO2e
Seven sectors, about 282 industries and about 490 Mt CO2e
Seven sectors, about 490 industries and about 477 Mt CO2e
96.x: The market covers seven sectors, approximately 490 industries and about 477 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent.

o: China, the European Union and South Korea

96.s: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme demonstrated the effectiveness of market-based regulation by reducing emissions of:

96.tq: Link the scheme with the pollutant and the reduction range.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s negotiating stance on climate change:

96.x: Developing countries other than China received only about 15 percent of global climate finance in 2023.

96.s: Which of the following correctly represents the industrial-emissions breakdown reported for 2022?

13 percent from fuel use in manufacturing and construction, and 9 percent from industrial processes
13 percent from industrial processes, and 9 percent from agriculture
9 percent from fuel use in manufacturing and construction, and 13 percent from industrial processes

Forest cover on 10 Mha without any quality-improvement component

o: It was replaced by a 2035 industrial-emissions target.

It was converted into a target exclusively for mangroves.

Community campaign — mangroves over 540 square kilometres
