103.x: Real-time monitoring is carried out on the APCMMS portal. The APEMC portal tracks hazardous waste using GPS-fitted vehicles, while BMW is sent to CBMWTFs.
103.tq: Match each portal or facility with its specific operational function.

103.s: Biomedical waste in Andhra Pradesh is sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities primarily for
o: Production of RDF for cement kilns only
103.x: Biomedical waste is sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities for incineration. It is not intended for open dumping or untreated agricultural composting.
103.tq: Identify the prescribed treatment route for a specialised waste stream.

103.s: Which portal tracks hazardous waste through GPS-fitted vehicles in Andhra Pradesh?
103.x: The APEMC portal tracks hazardous waste using GPS-fitted vehicles. APCMMS is associated with real-time monitoring.
103.tq: Discriminate between similar-looking portals by their exact function.

103.s: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 was issued through
103.x: The AP Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 was issued through G.O. Ms. No. 26.
103.tq: Recall the exact government-order number associated with the policy.

103.s: Which of the following correctly shows the municipal solid-waste collection chain?
o: Door-to-door collection → segregated transport → transfer station → MRF → processing/recycling → residual landfill
Transfer station → door-to-door collection → landfill → MRF → recycling
Door-to-door collection → landfill → segregation → transfer station → MRF
MRF → door-to-door collection → segregated transport → landfill → processing
103.x: The chain begins with door-to-door collection, followed by segregated transport, transfer station, MRF, processing or recycling, and final residual landfill.
103.tq: Arrange a service chain by its operational sequence.

103.s: According to the cited Andhra Pradesh performance figures, what percentage of wards had full door-to-door coverage?
103.x: Full door-to-door coverage was reported for 94.62% of wards in the cited Andhra Pradesh figures. The 49.32% figure relates to wards with 100% source segregation.
103.tq: Distinguish closely related percentages by the service they measure.

103.s: Which of the following correctly matches the Andhra Pradesh waste-management indicators?
o: 100% source segregation in wards — 49.32%; MRFs — 101 ULBs
100% source segregation in wards — 94.62%; MRFs — 30 ULBs
103.x: The cited figures are 49.32% of wards with 100% source segregation and MRFs in 101 ULBs.
103.tq: Start from the sure percentage and verify the associated institutional count.

103.s: What was the stated target for rural door-to-door waste collection in Andhra Pradesh by March 2026?
103.x: The target was 100% rural door-to-door collection by March 2026. The 97% figure refers to door-to-door collection in municipalities.
103.tq: Separate a target from an already reported performance figure.

103.s: Which statement about the national gaps in municipal solid-waste management is correct?
o: All ULBs had notified SWM by-laws and 45% had achieved full segregation.
Fewer than 45% of ULBs had notified SWM by-laws and 68% had achieved full segregation.
Only 68% of ULBs had notified SWM by-laws and fewer than 45% had achieved full segregation.
68% of ULBs had notified SWM by-laws and more than 45% had achieved full segregation.
103.x: The cited national gaps were that only 68% of ULBs had notified solid-waste-management by-laws and fewer than 45% had achieved full segregation.
103.tq: Keep the two percentages attached to their correct indicators.

103.s: Which of the following statements regarding waste-to-energy in India is correct?
o: There are 21 WtE plants producing exactly 133 MW and no biogas facilities.
There are 133 operational WtE plants producing 21 MW, along with 170 biogas facilities.
There are 170 operational WtE plants producing 21 MW, along with 133 biogas facilities.
There are 21 operational WtE plants producing more than 170 MW, along with 133 biogas facilities.
103.x: The cited figures are 21 operational WtE plants producing more than 170 MW and 133 biogas facilities.
103.tq: Match each number with the correct category and unit.

103.s: Waste-to-energy plants are stated to reduce the volume of municipal solid waste by approximately
103.x: WtE is stated to reduce municipal solid-waste volume by approximately 90%.
103.tq: Recall the approximate quantitative effect rather than an exact unsupported value.

103.s: The additional WtE capacity targeted under SBM-U 2.0 is
103.x: SBM-U 2.0 targets an additional WtE capacity of 10,000 tonnes per day.
103.tq: Distinguish the programme target from existing plant capacity.

103.s: Which of the following correctly describes the SATAT–GOBARdhan linkage?
o: It establishes 500 new MRFs exclusively for e-waste.
It provides 500 MW from existing WtE plants only.
It targets 500 new waste-to-wealth CBG plants.
103.x: The SATAT and GOBARdhan linkage targets 500 new waste-to-wealth compressed biogas plants.
103.tq: Link two initiatives with their stated numerical target and output.

103.s: Compressed biogas plants described in the waste-to-energy context convert municipal wet waste into
103.x: CBG plants convert municipal wet waste into green fuel. The Circular Bioenergy Scheme supports scientific processing in this area.
103.tq: Infer the useful product from the waste input and technology named.

103.s: Which scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas supports 100% scientific processing in the cited circular-bioenergy context?
103.x: The Circular Bioenergy Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas supports 100% scientific processing in the cited context.
103.tq: Identify the scheme from its sector and stated purpose.

103.s: Which pair of Andhra Pradesh cities is associated with WtE plants?
103.x: The cited Andhra Pradesh WtE plants are located at Guntur and Visakhapatnam.
103.tq: Recall a location pair without substituting nearby urban centres.

103.s: Legacy waste refers to
o: Agricultural residue stored for use as animal fodder
Old municipal solid waste piled in dumpsites for years
Only hazardous waste stored in laboratories
Freshly segregated waste awaiting transport for one day
103.x: Legacy waste is old municipal solid waste accumulated in dumpsites over several years. It can emit methane and pollute groundwater.
103.tq: Select the definition that captures both age and storage condition.

103.s: Which of the following is a consequence of accumulated legacy waste?
o: Improvement of groundwater quality without treatment
103.x: Legacy waste can emit methane and pollute groundwater. These impacts necessitate remediation and scientific processing.
103.tq: Connect a waste condition with its stated environmental consequences.

103.s: Biomining of legacy waste involves
o: Burning all waste together in an uncontrolled fire
Excavating the waste and separating recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill
Converting only the biodegradable fraction into manure
Covering the dump permanently without excavation or segregation
103.x: Biomining involves excavation and separation of legacy waste into recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill. It is not uncontrolled burning or mere covering.
103.tq: Identify the complete treatment process from its stages and outputs.

103.s: Under the stated SWM Rules 2026 approach, landfills should be used only for
o: Recyclable plastic and paper before sorting
All mixed municipal waste collected from cities
103.x: Landfills are intended only for waste that is non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert. Recoverable and recyclable materials should be diverted for processing.
103.tq: Use the exclusion principle to identify what may finally enter a landfill.

103.s: Which measure is specifically associated with the management of legacy dumpsites under the stated SWM Rules 2026 approach?
o: Mapping all legacy dumpsites and undertaking time-bound biomining or bioremediation with quarterly reporting
Allowing indefinite accumulation until the dumpsite reaches capacity
Sending all legacy waste directly to agricultural fields
Banning all reporting after the first year of remediation
103.x: The approach requires mapping all legacy dumpsites, time-bound biomining or bioremediation and quarterly reporting.
103.tq: Choose the option containing the complete compliance package rather than one isolated action.

103.s: At Guthikondavaripalem in Ongole, how much of the 2.56 lakh tonnes of legacy waste had been processed?
103.x: At Guthikondavaripalem, 1.76 lakh tonnes out of 2.56 lakh tonnes of legacy waste had been processed.
103.tq: Distinguish the processed quantity from the total quantity and the wider state estimate.

103.s: The inherited legacy waste of Andhra Pradesh was placed at approximately
103.x: The inherited legacy waste of Andhra Pradesh was placed at 108 lakh tonnes. This is distinct from the 2.56 lakh tonnes at the Ongole site.
103.tq: Handle Indian-numbering figures carefully and distinguish state totals from site-specific quantities.

103.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen is implemented by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
103.x: SBM-Grameen is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. The ministry was renamed in June 2019.
103.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the programme.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Phase I of SBM-Grameen:
1. It aimed to construct over 10 crore toilets by 2019-20.
2. It aimed at making all villages open-defecation free.
3. Rural sanitation coverage increased from 39% in 2014 to 100% in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements correctly describe the targets and reported sanitation-coverage increase under Phase I of SBM-Grameen.
103.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after checking each numerical and outcome statement.

103.s: The second phase of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen was approved in 2020 and is intended to continue up to:
103.x: Phase II of SBM-Grameen was approved in 2020 for implementation up to 2024-25.
103.tq: Distinguish the end year of Phase II from nearby programme periods.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an ODF Plus village?
o: A village with only piped drinking-water connections
A village where ODF status is sustained along with management of greywater, faecal sludge and plastic waste
A village with only household toilets and no waste-management facilities
A village where all waste is incinerated
103.x: ODF Plus combines sustained ODF status with management of greywater, faecal sludge and plastic waste, along with options such as biogas and composting.
103.tq: Test the exact expanded meaning of a familiar sanitation term.

103.s: Which of the following is the correct progression of ODF Plus levels?
103.x: The three progressive ODF Plus levels are Aspiring, Rising and Model.
103.tq: Arrange staged classifications in their stated progression.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The incentive for an Individual Household Latrine under SBM-Grameen is ₹12,000.
2. Greywater management support is ₹280 per capita for villages up to 5,000 population.
3. Greywater management support is ₹660 per capita for villages above 5,000 population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: The IHHL incentive is ₹12,000; greywater support is ₹280 per capita in villages up to 5,000 population and ₹660 per capita in larger villages.
103.tq: Check each amount and population threshold before selecting the combined code.

103.s: The Rural Sanitation Strategy covering the period 2019–2029 was prepared by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
103.x: The ten-year Rural Sanitation Strategy for 2019–2029 was prepared by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
103.tq: Identify the department associated with a named strategy.

103.s: Clean Andhra Pradesh, popularly known as the CLAP programme, was launched on 2 October 2021 as:
103.x: CLAP was launched on 2 October 2021 under the name Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam. Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra is a later state drive launched in January 2025.
103.tq: Use the exact official name to distinguish related sanitation initiatives.

103.s:
Arrange the following sanitation programmes in chronological order:
A. Total Sanitation Campaign
B. Swachh Bharat Mission
C. Central Rural Sanitation Programme
D. Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan
103.x: The correct order is Central Rural Sanitation Programme (1986), Total Sanitation Campaign (1999), Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (2012), and Swachh Bharat Mission (2014).
103.tq: Fix the earliest and latest schemes first, then place the middle programmes by year.

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. Integrated Low Cost Sanitation
b. Central Rural Sanitation Programme
c. Total Sanitation Campaign
d. Nirmal Gram Puraskar

List-II (Year)
i. 1980–81
ii. 1986
iii. 1999
iv. 2003

Choose the correct answer using the codes given below.
103.x: Integrated Low Cost Sanitation dates to 1980–81, the Central Rural Sanitation Programme to 1986, the Total Sanitation Campaign to 1999 and Nirmal Gram Puraskar to 2003.
103.tq: Start with the earliest sure year and verify the remaining chronological pairs.

103.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its principal focus?
o: Total Sanitation Campaign — only construction of subsidised rural latrines
Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan — introduction of sanitation for the first time in India
Central Rural Sanitation Programme — award for ODF gram panchayats
Integrated Low Cost Sanitation — conversion of dry latrines to pour-flush latrines and liberation of manual scavengers
103.x: The Integrated Low Cost Sanitation programme focused on converting dry latrines into pour-flush latrines and freeing manual scavengers. The other options assign incorrect descriptions.
103.tq: Detect the swapped programme-focus pair.

103.s: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, introduced in 2012, was the renamed form of the:
103.x: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan was the renamed Total Sanitation Campaign and followed a saturation approach.
103.tq: Discriminate between predecessor programmes with similar sanitation objectives.

103.s: Nirmal Gram Puraskar was primarily an award for:
o: Municipal corporations with the highest waste generation
103.x: Nirmal Gram Puraskar, introduced in 2003, recognised open-defecation-free gram panchayats.
103.tq: Link a named award with its specific recipient category.

103.s: GOBARdhan, launched in 2018 under SBM-Grameen, is associated with conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into:
103.x: GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into biogas and bio-slurry, supported by a unified portal.
103.tq: Identify the input-output relationship in a waste-to-resource initiative.

103.s: Which one of the following statements about Swachhata Hi Seva is correct?
o: It is an award given to ODF gram panchayats.
It is a plastic-import restriction introduced in 2018.
It is a ten-year rural sanitation strategy beginning in 2019.
It is a fortnight-long shramdaan campaign conducted every year since 2017.
103.x: Swachhata Hi Seva has been observed as a fortnight shramdaan campaign every year since 2017.
103.tq: Separate a recurring campaign from strategies, awards and regulatory measures.

103.s: Which of the following is NOT among the identified items covered by India's single-use plastic ban?
103.x: Plastic-stemmed earbuds, straws, stirrers and PVC banners below 100 microns are among the identified banned items. Polycarbonate water storage tanks are not listed in this group.
103.tq: Find the item outside the specified banned-item list.

103.s: Which authorities are primarily responsible for enforcing the identified single-use plastic ban?
o: Only the Ministry of Jal Shakti
SPCBs/PCCs and local bodies, supported by national and state task forces
Only the National Disaster Management Authority
Only municipal corporations in metropolitan cities
103.x: Enforcement involves State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control Committees and local bodies, along with a National Level Taskforce and State Special Task Forces.
103.tq: Identify the correct combination of implementing authorities.

103.s: The identified single-use plastic ban covers approximately what proportion of total plastic waste?
103.x: The ban covers only about 11% of total plastic waste.
103.tq: Recall the precise proportion rather than assuming that the ban covers all plastic waste.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bangladesh — first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002
China — first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002
New Zealand — first ban on thin plastic bags in 2002
103.x: Bangladesh was the first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002. China's National Sword Policy began in 2018, while New Zealand's supermarket produce-bag ban was in July 2023.
103.tq: Detect swapped countries and years in closely related international measures.

103.s: China's National Sword Policy of 2018 and Thailand's 2025 measure primarily restrict:
o: Domestic manufacture of all plastic products
103.x: China's National Sword Policy and Thailand's 2025 measure restrict imports of plastic waste.
103.tq: Identify the regulated activity rather than the broad environmental theme.

103.s: Nurdles are best described as:
o: Secondary microplastics formed only by tyre wear
Primary microplastic pellets generally measuring 1–5 mm
Biodegradable plastic fibres used in clothing
103.x: Nurdles are primary microplastic pellets, generally 1–5 mm in size.
103.tq: Distinguish a specific microplastic form from its sources and effects.

103.s: India's first major nurdle landing was reported in:
o: Kerala, from the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck
West Bengal, from a fishing vessel
103.x: The first major nurdle landing in India occurred in Kerala following the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck. The nurdles included LDPE and HDPE.
103.tq: Combine location, event and source-vessel clues.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about microplastics:
1. FSSAI detected microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples.
2. Microbeads in cosmetics are prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules.
3. Microplastics in the Sundarbans can drive plastic-degrading enzymes in microbes carrying antimicrobial-resistance genes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The stated responses include the microbead restriction and the National Action Plan for Marine Litter.
103.tq: Test findings, regulatory action and ecological consequence together.

103.s: Which plastic is commonly used for water and soft-drink bottles and may leach additives when heated?
103.x: PET is widely used for water and soft-drink bottles and may leach additives when heated.
103.tq: Match an everyday product with its material and hazard.

103.s: Polycarbonate containers are associated with the release of which endocrine-disrupting substance?
103.x: Polycarbonate hard bottles and containers can release bisphenol A, or BPA, an endocrine disruptor.
103.tq: Use the product–additive association to resolve a material question.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: LDPE/HDPE — carry bags and milk bottles
103.x: Synthetic rubber is associated with tyres, not drinking-water bottles. LDPE/HDPE, synthetic polymers and cellulose acetate have the associations shown in the other options.
103.tq: Find the product-material mismatch among familiar plastic applications.

103.s: Tyre-wear microplastics are principally associated with:
103.x: Tyres contain synthetic rubber, and their wear is a source of microplastics.
103.tq: Link a pollution source to the material from which it is made.

103.s: Which standard must compostable plastics meet?
103.x: Compostable plastics must meet the IS/ISO 17088 standard.
103.tq: Recall the exact technical standard rather than a general environmental certification.

103.s: Under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2024, which of the following is required for makers of biodegradable plastics?
o: Approval only from local village panchayats
Certification by the Central Pollution Control Board
Certification only by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
Registration with the National Disaster Management Authority
103.x: The 2024 amendment defined biodegradable plastics and required CPCB certification for their makers.
103.tq: Identify the competent certifying authority in a regulatory provision.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about plastic-waste management:
1. Plastic roads are promoted under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.
2. Energy recovery from plastic waste is promoted under the same framework.
3. Plastic waste can serve as a feedstock for advanced biofuel.
4. Waste-to-oil is an allowed end-of-life route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All four statements describe recognised or promoted routes for plastic-waste utilisation and recovery.
103.tq: Check whether each listed recovery route belongs to the same regulatory framework.

103.s: UNEA-5.2, held in Nairobi in March 2022, adopted which resolution that led to the establishment of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)?
103.x: The UNEA-5.2 resolution titled “End Plastic Pollution” established the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee.
103.tq: Use the exact title of the resolution rather than a broad subject description.

103.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the venues of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee on the global plastics treaty, beginning with the earliest?
o: Punta del Este – Paris – Nairobi – Ottawa – Busan – Geneva
Paris – Punta del Este – Nairobi – Busan – Ottawa – Geneva
Nairobi – Punta del Este – Paris – Ottawa – Geneva – Busan
Punta del Este – Nairobi – Paris – Busan – Ottawa – Geneva
103.x: The INC venues were Punta del Este, Paris, Nairobi, Ottawa, Busan and Geneva in that order. Busan hosted INC-5 in 2024 and Geneva hosted INC-5.2 in August 2025.
103.tq: Fix the first and last venues, then arrange the middle venues chronologically.

103.s:
The INC-5.2 meeting held in Geneva in August 2025 ended with no agreement. Which of the following were identified as major sticking points?
1. Production caps
2. Chemicals of concern
3. Finance
4. Establishment of informal e-waste hubs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: Production caps, chemicals of concern and finance were the major sticking points. Informal e-waste hubs were not an issue in the INC negotiations.
103.tq: Eliminate the statement imported from a neighbouring environmental topic.

103.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the ban on single-use plastic and carry bags applies to carry bags having thickness below:
103.x: Andhra Pradesh bans single-use plastic and carry bags below 120 microns, with enforcement involving the Revenue Department, Police and Pollution Control Board.
103.tq: Distinguish the precise statutory threshold from nearby thickness values.

103.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the action reported under Andhra Pradesh plastic curbs during AP SES 2025–26?
o: 3,571.40 tonnes carry bags and 5,505.06 tonnes single-use plastic seized
3,571.40 kg carry bags and 5,505.06 kg single-use plastic seized
5,505.06 tonnes carry bags and 3,571.40 tonnes single-use plastic seized
5,505.06 kg carry bags and 3,571.40 kg single-use plastic seized
103.x: The reported seizures were 5,505.06 kg of carry bags and 3,571.40 kg of single-use plastic.
103.tq: Check both the units and the order of the two figures.

103.s:
With reference to the plastic curbs in Guntur, consider the following statements:
1. A complete ban was scheduled from 15 August 2026.
2. Fines could extend up to ₹5,000.
3. Fines were to be collected through the Swachh App.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct: Guntur’s complete ban was scheduled from 15 August 2026, fines could reach ₹5,000, and the Swachh App was to be used for fines.
103.tq: Verify the date, monetary limit and enforcement mechanism separately.

103.s: Which of the following best defines e-waste in the context of the ITU definition?
o: Only hazardous electronic equipment exported across borders
Only discarded computers sent for recycling
All household waste containing any metal component
Discarded electrical and electronic equipment and parts not meant for reuse
103.x: E-waste consists of discarded electrical and electronic equipment and parts that are not intended for reuse.
103.tq: Prefer the definition covering both equipment and parts, and excluding items meant for reuse.

103.s: Which one of the following is NOT a hazardous constituent released by old computers?
103.x: Old computers can release beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury and lead, besides PCBs and PBBs. Plutonium is not included in this list.
103.tq: Find the outsider among the listed hazardous constituents.

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Constituent)
a. Lead
b. Mercury
c. Cadmium
d. Brominated flame retardants (PBBs)

List-II (Main harm or characteristic)
i. Kidney and bone damage
ii. Persistent nature and endocrine effects
iii. Nervous-system and kidney effects
iv. Brain and kidney damage; bioaccumulation in fish

Codes:
103.x: Lead affects the nervous system and kidneys; mercury damages the brain and kidneys and bioaccumulates in fish; cadmium damages kidneys and bones; PBBs are persistent and have endocrine effects.
103.tq: Start from the sure pair, especially cadmium with kidney and bone damage.

103.s: Improper disposal of biomedical waste and e-waste can contribute to biodiversity loss primarily because it:
o: increases the natural regeneration rate of forests
converts all pollutants into harmless nutrients
prevents the release of toxic substances into groundwater
increases soil and water toxicity and damages ecosystems
103.x: Improper disposal releases toxic substances into soil and water, thereby damaging ecosystems and biodiversity.
103.tq: Trace the cause-and-effect chain from waste disposal to ecosystem damage.

103.s: Which of the following is correctly arranged as the authorised e-waste recycling chain?
o: Producer → consumer → landfill → dismantler → recovered materials
Consumer → collection centre or producer take-back → authorised dismantler → authorised recycler → recovered materials
Consumer → informal hub → landfill → authorised recycler → producer take-back
Consumer → authorised recycler → collection centre → informal hub → recovered materials
103.x: The authorised chain begins with the consumer and collection or producer take-back, followed by dismantling, recycling and recovery of materials.
103.tq: Follow the material flow from generation to recovery and reject informal or disposal stages.

103.s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate action for a citizen disposing of an old electronic device?
o: Burn it to recover copper and aluminium
Mix it with municipal solid waste after removing the battery
Sell or deposit it with an authorised recycler or collection centre after wiping data
Hand it over to any informal dismantler without data removal
103.x: Citizens should use authorised recyclers or collection centres and wipe personal data before handing over old electronics.
103.tq: Apply the recommended citizen action while avoiding unsafe informal handling.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about India’s e-waste recycling system:
1. E-waste should not be mixed with other waste.
2. Seelampur and Moradabad are identified as informal e-waste hubs.
3. India has 468 authorised recyclers with a combined capacity of 1.6 million tonnes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. Separate handling is required; Seelampur and Moradabad are informal hubs; and CPCB data mention 468 authorised recyclers with 1.6 million tonnes of capacity.
103.tq: Check the operational rule, locations and capacity figure independently.

103.s: What does the R2 Code of Practices primarily promote?
o: Environmentally responsible practices in electronics recycling
103.x: R2, or Responsible Recycling, is a code of practices promoting environmentally responsible electronics recycling.
103.tq: Expand the abbreviation and link it to its specific sector.

103.s: India’s first e-waste clinic was established at:
103.x: Bhopal was the location of India’s first e-waste clinic.
103.tq: Use the specific institutional-location association rather than an informal hub location.

103.s: India is presently described as the world’s ______ largest generator of e-waste, after China and the United States.
103.x: India is the third-largest e-waste generator, after China and the United States.
103.tq: Read the ranking together with the named countries to avoid reversing the order.

103.s: The e-waste generation attributed to India for 2025 was approximately:
103.x: India’s e-waste generation was reported as approximately 2.2 million tonnes in 2025. The 3.54 lakh tonnes figure refers to e-waste collected and processed in FY 2021.
103.tq: Separate generation figures from collection-and-processing figures and compare their units.

103.s: Which organisations jointly publish the Global E-waste Monitor?
103.x: The Global E-waste Monitor is published by the International Telecommunication Union and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research.
103.tq: Identify the correct institutional pair instead of substituting neighbouring UN bodies.

103.s: The Global E-waste Monitor groups e-waste into how many categories?
103.x: The Global E-waste Monitor uses six categories, including cooling equipment, screens, lamps, large equipment, small equipment and IT equipment.
103.tq: Count the classification categories rather than the examples within them.

103.s: Which of the following was issued by the CPCB in response to biomedical waste generated during the COVID-19 period?
o: Global E-waste Monitor and Basel Protocol
R2 electronics recycling code and plastic treaty guidelines
COVID19BWM tracking app and COVID-19 waste guidelines
103.x: The CPCB issued COVID-19 biomedical-waste guidelines in 2020 and introduced the COVID19BWM tracking app.
103.tq: Match the emergency, authority and digital tracking instrument.

103.s:
Which of the following statements regarding India’s status under the Basel and Rotterdam Conventions is correct?
1. India ratified the Basel Convention in June 1992.
2. India acceded to the Rotterdam Convention in 2005.
3. India’s designated authorities for Rotterdam-related matters include the Chemicals and Fertilisers and Agriculture Ministries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: India ratified Basel in June 1992, acceded to Rotterdam in 2005, and has designated authorities in the Chemicals and Fertilisers and Agriculture Ministries.
103.tq: Combine treaty dates with India-specific institutional details.

103.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Basel Convention and India?
o: The Convention entered into force in 2004, and India acceded to it in 2005.
The Convention concerns mercury, and India ratified it in June 2005.
The Convention entered into force on 5 May 1992, and India ratified it in June 1992.
The Convention was adopted in 2013, and India ratified it in 2034.
103.x: The Basel Convention was adopted in 1989, entered into force on 5 May 1992, and India ratified it in June 1992.
103.tq: Separate adoption year, entry-into-force date and India’s ratification date.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Stockholm Convention currently includes 34 chemicals, including chlorpyrifos and PFAS.
2. The Minamata Convention concerns mercury.
3. Dental amalgam phase-out under the Minamata framework is associated with the year 2034.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: The current figure given for Stockholm is 34 chemicals, including chlorpyrifos and PFAS. Minamata concerns mercury, and dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by 2034.
103.tq: Test the treaty’s subject together with its current chemical count and target year.

103.s: The global issue involved in the transboundary movement of hazardous waste refers to:
o: exchange of agricultural seeds under biodiversity agreements
movement of only biodegradable waste between rural districts
transport of clean energy equipment to developed countries
physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, often to developing countries
103.x: Transboundary hazardous-waste movement involves the physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, frequently to developing countries.
103.tq: Use the operational meaning of the term rather than an unrelated environmental transfer.

103.s: Which body functions as the nodal division for hazardous substances management in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
103.x: The Hazardous Substances Management Division (HSMD) of MoEFCC is the nodal body for hazardous substances management.
103.tq: Match the function with the specialised administrative division.

103.s: The gas responsible for the Bhopal disaster of 2–3 December 1984 was:
103.x: The Bhopal disaster involving Union Carbide India Ltd was caused by methyl isocyanate. More than 5,400 lives were reported lost.
103.tq: Distinguish the Bhopal chemical from the Visakhapatnam chemical.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
103.x: The Bhopal disaster in December 1984 involved methyl isocyanate. The LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam in May 2020 involved styrene vapour.
103.tq: Use the location–date–chemical triplet to detect swapped disaster details.

103.s:
With reference to the Bhopal waste cleanup reported in early 2025, consider the following statements:
1. About 337 tonnes of waste were incinerated.
2. Approximately 900 tonnes of toxic residual ash resulted.
3. The Supreme Court asked the victims’ NGO to approach the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct: 337 tonnes were incinerated, about 900 tonnes of toxic residual ash remained, and the Supreme Court directed the victims’ NGO to approach the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
103.tq: Check the quantities, procedural direction and court involved as separate facts.

103.s: The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) was enacted after which major chemical disaster?
103.x: The EPA of 1986 was enacted after the Bhopal disaster, which occurred in December 1984.
103.tq: Apply the chronological cause-and-effect relationship between the disaster and legislation.

103.s: Which one of the following best describes PFAS, often referred to as “forever chemicals”?
o: They are biodegradable chemicals used exclusively in cement production
They persist in the environment, occur in products such as food packaging, and may accumulate in animal bodies
They rapidly decompose in soil and water and do not accumulate in organisms
They are radioactive substances used mainly in fluorescent lamps
103.x: PFAS are persistent chemicals found in drinking water, food and food packaging. They do not break down easily and can accumulate in animal bodies.
103.tq: Use the option that combines the defining properties and common exposure pathways.

103.s:
With reference to PFAS, consider the following statements:
1. PFAS are widespread in drinking water, food and food packaging.
2. PFAS do not break down easily in the environment.
3. PFAS have been listed under the Stockholm Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. PFAS are persistent contaminants found in several consumer exposure pathways and are now listed under the Stockholm Convention.
103.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.

103.s: Fluorescent lamps and compact fluorescent lamps are treated as household hazardous waste primarily because they contain:
103.x: Fluorescent lamps and CFLs contain mercury. When broken, they can release mercury vapour into the surroundings.
103.tq: Identify the hazardous constituent associated with the specific consumer product.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the legal control associated with mercury-added products?
o: They are exempt from international environmental agreements
They are being phased out under the Minamata Convention
They are being promoted under the Stockholm Convention
They are regulated exclusively under the Basel Convention
103.x: Mercury-added products are being phased out under the Minamata Convention, which addresses mercury pollution and its risks.
103.tq: Discriminate between international conventions by matching the pollutant with the correct treaty.

103.s: Which of the following is an example of construction and demolition waste that is generally regarded as mostly inert?
o: Mercury vapour and fluorescent lamp powder
Concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris
Used syringes, blood-soaked cotton and pathological waste
103.x: Construction and demolition waste is mostly inert and commonly consists of concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris.
103.tq: Select the option containing the characteristic material group rather than hazardous waste categories.

103.s: Approximately how much construction and demolition waste is generated annually, as indicated for India?
103.x: Construction and demolition waste generation is indicated to be about 12 million tonnes per year.
103.tq: Use scale comparison to distinguish the stated annual quantity from tenfold alternatives.

103.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised reuse of construction and demolition waste?
o: Use as a substitute for all hazardous chemical treatment
103.x: C&D waste can be reused as recycled aggregates and in bricks and tiles. It is not a substitute for hazardous chemical treatment.
103.tq: Find the option outside the stated reuse pathway by separating construction applications from hazardous-waste treatment.

103.s: The Burari facility in Delhi is notable as:
o: India’s first fly-ash-based thermal power plant
India’s first secure landfill for hazardous waste
India’s first construction and demolition waste recycling plant
103.x: Delhi’s Burari plant is recognised as India’s first construction and demolition waste recycling plant.
103.tq: Match the named place with its distinctive facility rather than a neighbouring waste-management activity.

103.s: Under the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016, which of the following activities falls within the scope of construction and demolition waste management?
o: Building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline work
103.x: The 2016 Rules cover waste arising from building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline activities.
103.tq: Prefer the comprehensive scope when the rule covers multiple related activities.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. The Rules provide for collection, transport, storage and re-processing of C&D waste.
2. Bulk generators may be subject to charges.
3. Construction and demolition waste is treated as a resource.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: The 2016 framework covers collection, transport, storage and re-processing, permits charges on bulk generators and treats C&D waste as a resource.
103.tq: Test the rule through its management stages, economic provision and resource-oriented approach.

103.s: Which new framework is associated with the Environment (Construction and Demolition Waste Management) Rules, 2025?
o: Extended Producer Responsibility for C&D waste
A national prohibition on using recycled aggregates
A complete ban on recycling construction waste
103.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified an Extended Producer Responsibility framework for C&D waste under the 2025 rules.
103.tq: Identify the policy instrument directly linked with the newer rules.

103.s: The Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 replaced which earlier rules?
o: The Hazardous Wastes (Management, Handling and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2008
103.x: The 2016 Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules replaced the 2008 Rules.
103.tq: Separate closely related rule years by identifying the earlier framework that was replaced.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly states a feature of the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016?
o: Import of hazardous waste for disposal is prohibited, and prevention is preferred over disposal
The Rules deal only with municipal biodegradable waste
The Rules prohibit all forms of recycling and co-processing
Hazardous waste may be imported freely for disposal without prior approval
103.x: The framework bans import of hazardous waste for disposal and follows a hierarchy in which prevention precedes safe disposal.
103.tq: Apply the waste-management hierarchy and identify the option consistent with both controls.

103.s: In the context of transboundary movement of hazardous waste, PIC refers to:
103.x: PIC means Prior Informed Consent, a control associated with the import and export of hazardous waste.
103.tq: Break the abbreviation into its regulatory meaning before evaluating the options.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MSIHC Rules, 1989 — manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals
CAEPPR Rules, 1996 — insurance compensation without fault
Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 — constitution of crisis groups
Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 — regulation of fluorescent lamp manufacture
103.x: The MSIHC Rules, 1989 address the manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals. CAEPPR concerns crisis groups, while the Public Liability Insurance Act provides no-fault relief.
103.tq: Start with the sure pair and reject options that swap the functions of neighbouring legal instruments.

103.s: The principal purpose of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 is to provide:
o: Compensation only after criminal conviction of the polluter
No-fault insurance cover and immediate relief to victims of hazardous-substance accidents
Insurance exclusively for transport of municipal waste
Long-term subsidies to industries using fly ash
103.x: The Act provides no-fault insurance cover intended to give immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.
103.tq: Identify the legal purpose by focusing on the beneficiary, liability basis and timing of relief.

103.s: Under the Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025, which sequence correctly represents the time limits for assessment by the State Pollution Control Board?
o: Preliminary assessment in 30 days followed by a detailed survey in 60 days
Preliminary assessment in 90 days followed by a detailed survey in the next 90 days
Preliminary assessment in 180 days followed by a detailed survey in 30 days
Both preliminary assessment and detailed survey within 15 days
103.x: The SPCB is required to undertake a preliminary assessment within 90 days and a detailed survey in the subsequent 90 days.
103.tq: Track the sequential time periods and distinguish the first assessment from the follow-up survey.

103.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 is correct?
o: District reports on suspected contaminated sites are prepared half-yearly, and the framework covers 189 hazardous chemicals
The Rules cover only radioactive substances and require monthly reports
District reports on suspected contaminated sites are prepared annually
The Rules apply only to municipal dumping grounds and cover 89 chemicals
103.x: The framework requires district half-yearly reports on suspected contaminated sites and identifies 189 hazardous chemicals.
103.tq: Combine the reporting frequency with the stated chemical count and reject altered figures.

103.s: The Fly Ash Utilisation Notification requires fly ash to be used for bricks, cement and road construction within what distance of thermal power plants?
103.x: The notification requires utilisation of fly ash for specified construction purposes within 300 km of thermal plants, helping prevent dumping on soil.
103.tq: Use the distance-based regulatory limit and distinguish it from nearer or broader alternatives.

103.s: Which of the following is a recognised use of fly ash in construction?
o: Treating hazardous waste without any further processing
Replacing all aggregates in every type of concrete
Making building bricks and partly replacing Portland cement in concrete
103.x: Fly ash can be used to make building bricks and can partly replace Portland cement in concrete.
103.tq: Select the option that states practical uses without introducing an absolute or exclusive claim.

103.s: Which principle best describes the preferred approach to hazardous-waste disposal?
o: Landfilling is the first and preferred option for all hazardous waste
Hazardous waste should always be burned in open areas
Landfill is the last resort, while co-processing in cement plants and waste exchange are preferred where suitable
All hazardous waste must be discharged into surface water after dilution
103.x: Landfill is considered the last resort. APPCB prefers suitable co-processing as fuel in cement plants and exchange of waste between industries.
103.tq: Apply the waste hierarchy and reject options based on absolute or environmentally unsafe practices.

103.s: The two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDFs) in Andhra Pradesh are located at:
103.x: The two CHWTSDFs identified for Andhra Pradesh are located in Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
103.tq: Use location-based recall and distinguish the named facility sites from other Andhra Pradesh cities.

103.s: Which system is used by APEMC for tracking hazardous-waste movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Biometric tracking of every waste container
103.x: APEMC uses GPS tracking for monitoring hazardous-waste movement and management.
103.tq: Match the institution with the specific monitoring technology stated for it.

103.s:
With reference to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. They came into force on 1 April 2026.
2. Household hazardous waste has been recognised as a separate ‘special care’ stream.
3. They deal exclusively with industrial hazardous waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026 and recognise household hazardous waste as a separate ‘special care’ stream. They are not confined exclusively to industrial hazardous waste.
103.tq: Identify the statement that wrongly narrows the scope by using the word ‘exclusively’.

103.s: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025 were scheduled to come into force on:
103.x: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025 were scheduled to come into force on 1 April 2026.
103.tq: Use the date-specific elimination method when several nearby dates are given.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SPSR Nellore — Operation Clean Sweep headquarters
103.x: Biomining of legacy waste is associated with Ongole. Anantapur is associated with a proposed 170 TPD waste-processing plant, while CHWTSDFs are located at Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
103.tq: Start with the sure location-activity pair and eliminate swapped places.

103.s: Operation Clean Sweep in Andhra Pradesh during 2026 was conducted:
o: in 113 Urban Local Bodies from 1 April to 31 May
in all villages from 23 May to 20 June
in 123 Urban Local Bodies from 20 June to 23 July
in 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June
103.x: Operation Clean Sweep was conducted across all 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June 2026 under the Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra initiative.
103.tq: Combine the coverage figure with the correct date range before selecting an option.

103.s: A municipal authority requiring an apartment complex to maintain two separate bins for waste segregation is an example associated with:
103.x: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) threatened to seal an apartment that did not maintain two segregation bins.
103.tq: Identify the implementing local authority from the nature of the municipal enforcement action.

103.s: Which one of the following best reflects the reported compliance position of Urban Local Bodies regarding remediation data?
o: More than 75% submit data on time
Less than 10% submit data on time
103.x: Only 35% of Urban Local Bodies were reported to submit timely remediation data.
103.tq: Watch for percentage-range traps and avoid replacing an exact figure with an approximate extreme.

103.s: The campaign associated with SBM-G in 2026 was:
o: Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel - Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath
103.x: The 2026 campaign of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen was titled “Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata”. “Swachh Gaon, Surakshit Jalvayu” was the theme associated with June 2026.
103.tq: Separate the campaign title from the related monthly theme and state initiative.

103.s: The theme associated with June 2026 under SBM-G was:
103.x: The June 2026 theme was “Swachh Gaon, Surakshit Jalvayu”. It should not be confused with the broader 2026 SBM-G campaign, “Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata”.
103.tq: Discriminate between a campaign name and a time-specific theme.

103.s: The Supreme Court order of 18 August 2026 regarding responsibility for waste at the threshold held that:
o: Only Urban Local Bodies are responsible for such waste
Only sanitary workers are responsible for such waste
Responsibility begins only after waste reaches a landfill
Generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for such waste
103.x: The Supreme Court held that generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for waste at the threshold.
103.tq: Reject the exclusive responsibility claim by focusing on the phrase ‘not only’.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court’s intervention in solid-waste governance:
1. The relevant order was delivered on 18 August 2026.
2. The Bench included Justice S.V.N. Bhatti.
3. On 1 September 2026, the Court pulled up the Union and State governments for not institutionalising the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The order was dated 18 August 2026, involved a Bench including Justice S.V.N. Bhatti, and the Court criticised the Union and States on 1 September 2026.
103.tq: Check each date, institutional actor and judicial action independently before choosing the combination.

103.s: Which one of the following changes has been reported in the composition of rural waste?
o: A shift from municipal waste towards only industrial hazardous waste
A shift from biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste
A complete disappearance of sanitary waste from rural areas
A shift from plastic waste towards exclusively biodegradable waste
103.x: Rural waste is shifting from predominantly biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste.
103.tq: Identify the direction of change by comparing the earlier and emerging waste categories.

103.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported compliance position concerning Extended Producer Responsibility for plastic waste?
o: Fewer than 50% of producers comply with EPR targets
EPR targets have been withdrawn for producers
More than 90% of producers comply with EPR targets
Exactly 70% of producers comply with EPR targets
103.x: Fewer than 50% of producers were reported to comply with Extended Producer Responsibility targets, leading to criticism about enforceability.
103.tq: Distinguish the compliance percentage from the separate figure relating to informal recycling.

103.s:
With reference to plastic recycling and waste-pickers, consider the following statements:
1. More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers.
2. The NAMASTE scheme aims to formalise informal workers.
3. About 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers, NAMASTE seeks to formalise them, and approximately 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
103.tq: Keep distinct percentages, scheme objectives and population estimates separate while evaluating the statements.

103.s: Which of the following is an example of ‘invisible e-waste’ commonly discarded with regular waste?
o: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories
Glass bottles, steel cans and paper cartons
Construction aggregates, fly ash and cement bags
Food scraps, garden leaves and crop residue
103.x: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories are examples of ‘invisible e-waste’ that may be thrown into regular waste streams.
103.tq: Use the category clue and select the cluster of small electronic products.

103.s: Weak source segregation in the reported waste-management context is indicated by segregation levels of:
103.x: Source segregation was reported to be under 25%, indicating weak segregation practices. This figure is distinct from the 35% of Urban Local Bodies submitting timely remediation data.
103.tq: Distinguish closely related percentages referring to different indicators.

103.s: Which of the following correctly describes the criticism surrounding the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2026?
o: They were criticised on the ground that compliance was eased.
They were criticised for abolishing Extended Producer Responsibility.
They were criticised for completely banning all plastic products.
They were criticised for transferring all plastic regulation to local bodies.
103.x: Critics argued that the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2026 eased compliance requirements. The criticism did not amount to a complete ban or abolition of EPR.
103.tq: Reject extreme interpretations such as ‘completely’, ‘all’ and ‘abolishing’.

103.s: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 particularly targets:
103.x: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 targets industrial hazardous waste.
103.tq: Match the policy with its stated target instead of selecting an over-narrow category.

103.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the legal frameworks for which the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella?
o: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 as the only framework
103.x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella for frameworks including the EIA, Hazardous Waste, Coastal Regulation Zone and Contaminated Sites Rules. It is not described as an umbrella exclusively for the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
103.tq: Find the option that improperly uses an exclusive formulation and narrows a broader legal relationship.

103.s: Which of the following best explains the major institutional concern raised in relation to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: Questions concerning federalism and administrative design
A proposal to eliminate all Urban Local Bodies
A proposal to replace all recycling with incineration
A decision to exempt rural areas from waste regulation
103.x: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 have raised questions concerning federalism and administrative design. The other options do not represent the stated criticism.
103.tq: Identify the governance dimension of a policy debate rather than an unrelated operational claim.

103.s: In the Union Budget 2026–27, the allocation for SBM-Urban was reduced from ₹5,000 crore to:
103.x: The SBM-Urban allocation was halved from ₹5,000 crore to ₹2,500 crore in the Union Budget 2026–27.
103.tq: Track the direction and exact amount of a budget change.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding urban local government in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh has 17 municipal corporations.
2. Andhra Pradesh has 113 municipalities.
3. Andhra Pradesh has 7 cantonment boards.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Andhra Pradesh has 17 municipal corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards.
103.tq: Check each numerical component before selecting the combined code.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about waste-to-energy technologies:
1. Incineration burns waste in oxygen and may produce steam for power generation.
2. Incineration can reduce waste volume by approximately 90 percent.
3. Incineration may generate ash and emissions.
4. Biomethanation converts wet organic waste into biogas through microbial action.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All four statements correctly describe incineration or biomethanation. Incineration produces steam, reduces volume substantially and has ash and emission concerns, while microbes convert wet organic waste into biogas.
103.tq: Test the complete technology profile rather than relying on only the principal output.

103.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kyoto Protocol — greenhouse gas cuts by developed countries
2. Basel Convention — transboundary movement of hazardous waste
3. Cartagena Protocol — biosafety relating to living modified organisms under the Convention on Biological Diversity
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
103.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Kyoto addresses greenhouse-gas cuts by developed countries, Basel concerns transboundary hazardous waste movement, and Cartagena concerns biosafety and living modified organisms under the CBD.
103.tq: Match each treaty with its distinctive environmental subject.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Irrigated paddy in India emits about 3.9 million tonnes of methane annually.
2. This quantity is a little more than Germany's total methane emissions.
3. India's waste sector accounted for 25.6% of national emissions in 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: India's irrigated paddy emits about 3.9 million tonnes of methane annually, slightly more than Germany's total methane emissions. The waste sector's share was 2.56%, not 25.6%.
103.tq: Reject the statement containing a misplaced decimal and retain the two linked methane facts.

103.s: The waste sector accounted for approximately what share of India's emissions in 2020?
103.x: The waste sector accounted for 2.56% of India's emissions in 2020 according to the Fourth Biennial Update Report.
103.tq: Pay attention to the decimal placement in percentage-based options.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Montreal Protocol primarily addresses ozone-depleting substances, although some such substances are also greenhouse gases.
2. The Paris Agreement addresses global warming through nationally determined contributions.
3. The Minamata Convention addresses mercury.
4. The Stockholm Convention addresses persistent organic pollutants.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All four statements are correct. The Montreal Protocol has an indirect greenhouse-gas relevance because CFCs are greenhouse gases, while the other statements correctly identify the subjects of the Paris, Minamata and Stockholm instruments.
103.tq: Separate the principal subject of each treaty from its indirect environmental relevance.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the national waste-management figures stated for India?
103.x: About 60–70% of waste is collected, while only 15–20% is processed.
103.tq: Avoid reversing the collection and processing percentages.

103.s: Which State is identified as the highest solid-waste-generating State in India?
103.x: Maharashtra is identified as the highest solid-waste-generating State.
103.tq: Test the precise State association rather than the general urban-waste trend.

103.s: Urban waste processing increased from approximately what level in 2014 to 82% in 2026?
103.x: Urban waste processing increased from 16% in 2014 to 82% in 2026.
103.tq: Recall the baseline figure paired with the stated outcome figure.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly states the urban local-government set-up in Andhra Pradesh mentioned for waste management?
o: 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards
113 Municipal Corporations, 17 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards
7 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 17 cantonment boards
17 Municipal Corporations, 7 municipalities and 113 cantonment boards
103.x: The stated urban set-up consists of 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards.
103.tq: Keep the three administrative counts matched with their correct categories.

103.s:
Arrange the following stages of the hazardous-waste management hierarchy in the correct order from higher to lower priority:
A. Recycling
B. Prevention
C. Recovery
D. Safe disposal
103.x: The hierarchy places prevention above recycling, recovery and safe disposal. The relevant sequence is prevention, recycling, recovery and safe disposal.
103.tq: Arrange the stages by priority rather than by time of occurrence.

103.s: Which of the following correctly represents the complete hazardous-waste hierarchy given in the specified order?
o: Reuse, prevention, recovery, minimisation, recycling, disposal, co-processing
Minimisation, prevention, recycling, reuse, co-processing, recovery, disposal
Prevention, minimisation, reuse, recycling, recovery, co-processing, safe disposal
Prevention, recycling, minimisation, reuse, safe disposal, recovery, co-processing
103.x: The stated hierarchy is prevention, minimisation, reuse, recycling, recovery, co-processing and safe disposal.
103.tq: Recall the exact sequence in a graded management hierarchy.

103.s: Which of the following correctly describes hazardous-waste management infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Two CHWTSDFs, twelve pre-processing facilities and six permitted cement units
Six CHWTSDFs, two pre-processing facilities and twelve permitted cement units
Twelve CHWTSDFs, six pre-processing facilities and two permitted cement units
Two CHWTSDFs, six pre-processing facilities and twelve permitted cement units for co-processing
103.x: Andhra Pradesh has two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities, six pre-processing facilities and twelve cement units permitted for co-processing.
103.tq: Split the numerical options into infrastructure categories and match each figure to its correct category.

104.s:
The National Carbon Project under the ISRO Geosphere Biosphere Programme seeks to assess which of the following?
1. Carbon pools
2. Carbon fluxes
3. Net carbon balance of India’s terrestrial biomes
4. Only atmospheric carbon, excluding vegetation and soil
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: The project assesses carbon pools, carbon fluxes and the net carbon balance of terrestrial biomes. It includes vegetation and soil carbon and is not restricted to atmospheric carbon alone.
104.tq: Reject the extreme exclusion in statement 4 and retain the three components of the project.

104.s:
Which of the following components are specifically covered while assessing carbon under the National Carbon Project?
1. Vegetation carbon
2. Soil carbon
3. Land/ocean-atmosphere fluxes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: The National Carbon Project covers vegetation carbon, soil carbon and land/ocean-atmosphere carbon fluxes.
104.tq: Check whether each carbon component belongs to the project’s accounting framework.

104.s:
According to the sector-wise distribution of India's greenhouse-gas emissions, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Cement — approximately 6%
2. Aluminium — approximately 2.8%
104.x: Cement accounts for approximately 6% and aluminium for approximately 2.8% of India's greenhouse-gas emissions.
104.tq: Use a comparison of sector shares and check both numerical values independently.

104.s: NITI Aayog's decarbonisation roadmaps for the cement, aluminium and MSME sectors rely on which combination of measures?
o: Round-the-clock renewable-energy power, nuclear power and CCUS
Hydropower, biofuels and ocean alkalinity enhancement only
Natural gas, nuclear disarmament and direct air capture only
Coal expansion, diesel generation and afforestation only
104.x: The roadmaps rely on renewable energy available round the clock, nuclear power and carbon capture, utilisation and storage.
104.tq: Identify the complete policy package rather than selecting a single decarbonisation measure.

104.s:
With reference to biomass co-firing in coal-based power plants, consider the following statements:
1. Coal plants are required to co-fire 5% biomass from FY 2024-25.
2. The requirement rises to 7% from FY 2025-26.
3. The SAMARTH mission monitors this requirement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct: the biomass co-firing requirement is 5% in FY 2024-25 and 7% from FY 2025-26, with monitoring by the SAMARTH mission.
104.tq: Check the two successive percentages and then identify the agency associated with monitoring.

104.s: What was the share of India's emissions attributable to the waste sector in 2020, according to BUR-4?
104.x: The waste sector accounted for 2.56% of India's emissions in 2020 according to BUR-4.
104.tq: Distinguish the precise percentage from nearby numerical distractors.

104.s: In the context of climate policy, the term 'carbon bomb' refers to a fossil-fuel project that could emit more than:
o: 1 gigatonne of CO2 over its lifetime
500 million tonnes of CO2 over its lifetime
100 million tonnes of CO2 over its lifetime
104.x: A carbon bomb is a fossil-fuel project capable of emitting more than 1 gigatonne of CO2 during its lifetime.
104.tq: Match the policy term with its defining threshold and time period.

104.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the LINGO-listed carbon bombs is correct?
o: The list contains 225 projects and is led by India, Brazil, Canada and Australia.
The list contains 525 projects and is led by China, India, Russia and Iran.
The list contains 425 projects and is led by Japan, Germany, France and the UK.
The list contains 425 projects and is led by China, the USA, Russia and Saudi Arabia.
104.x: LINGO lists 425 carbon-bomb projects, with China, the USA, Russia and Saudi Arabia as the leading countries associated with them.
104.tq: Combine the list size with its leading countries; both parts must match.

104.s: Gevra and Rajmahal, identified as Indian carbon-bomb projects, are respectively located in:
104.x: The Gevra coal mine is in Chhattisgarh and the Rajmahal coal mine is in Jharkhand.
104.tq: Use the location pair carefully because the two projects are easily interchanged.

104.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: CCS — capture of CO2 at stationary sources and storage in geological or ocean formations
CCUS — removal of CO2 only from ambient air
Direct Air Capture — storage of carbon only in forests and soil
Ocean alkalinity enhancement — spreading basalt on land
104.x: CCS captures CO2 at stationary sources such as power plants and stores it in geological or ocean formations. Direct Air Capture removes CO2 from ambient air, while the other two descriptions are interchanged.
104.tq: Start with the sure definition and reject options that swap neighbouring carbon-removal terms.

104.s:
Consider the following statements about carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS):
1. It captures CO2 and either uses it or stores it permanently.
2. It supports coal gasification and hydrogen.
3. It is restricted to the storage of atmospheric CO2 in forests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: CCUS involves using captured CO2 or storing it permanently and can support coal gasification and hydrogen. It is not restricted to forest storage of atmospheric CO2.
104.tq: Reject the overly restrictive statement and retain the two functional features of CCUS.

104.s:
Which of the following is NOT a type or location of carbon sequestration identified in the context of carbon storage?
1. Geological storage in saline aquifers
2. Storage in depleted oil and gas fields
3. Ocean storage
4. Terrestrial storage in forests and soil
5. Atmospheric storage in the upper atmosphere
104.x: Geological, ocean and terrestrial storage are recognised forms of sequestration. Atmospheric storage in the upper atmosphere is not one of the listed forms.
104.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the recognised storage categories.

104.s: Direct Air Capture is distinguished from capture at a stationary industrial source because it:
o: converts basalt into carbonate without capturing air
captures only CO2 dissolved in seawater
captures CO2 directly from ambient air
104.x: Direct Air Capture pulls CO2 directly from ambient air rather than capturing emissions at a fixed industrial source.
104.tq: Discriminate between the source of CO2 and the place where it is captured.

104.s: Enhanced rock weathering removes carbon dioxide by:
o: adding fossil fuels to seawater to increase alkalinity
spreading crushed silicate rock such as basalt on land, where it binds CO2 as carbonate
injecting pure oxygen into depleted oil fields
104.x: Enhanced rock weathering uses crushed silicate rocks such as basalt, which chemically bind CO2 as carbonate when spread on land.
104.tq: Apply the process to the material used and the chemical form produced.

104.s: Ocean alkalinity enhancement involves:
o: capturing emissions exclusively from cement kilns
removing all dissolved salts from seawater
adding alkaline minerals to seawater so that it absorbs more CO2
spreading silicate rock only on agricultural land
104.x: Ocean alkalinity enhancement adds alkaline minerals to seawater to increase its capacity to absorb CO2.
104.tq: Use the operation and its intended effect to distinguish it from enhanced rock weathering.

104.s: The DST's cement-sector initiative concerning carbon capture and utilisation consists of:
o: three CCU testbeds forming a regional demonstration network
seven DAC testbeds for urban transport
five CCU testbeds forming a first-of-its-kind research cluster
five CCS testbeds located only in coal mines
104.x: DST has established five Carbon Capture and Utilisation testbeds in the cement sector as a first-of-its-kind research cluster.
104.tq: Check both the number of testbeds and the technology abbreviation.

104.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the footprint it measures?
o: Water footprint — only land required to absorb solid waste
Ecological footprint — only the volume of freshwater used in manufacturing
Carbon footprint — only direct emissions from owned sources
Carbon footprint — total greenhouse gases emitted by human activities, expressed in tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year
104.x: The carbon footprint measures total greenhouse-gas emissions from human activities in tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year. The other options describe ecological, water or Scope 1 concepts incorrectly.
104.tq: Match each footprint with its measured resource or emission category, not with a related sub-concept.

104.s: The ecological footprint represents the:
o: land and water needed to produce what people consume and absorb their waste
greenhouse gases emitted from purchased electricity alone
total freshwater used only for drinking purposes
104.x: The ecological footprint measures the land and water needed to produce consumed goods and absorb associated waste.
104.tq: Identify the broader resource-demand concept rather than a single emission category.

104.s: Which of the following correctly describes blue, green and grey water in the context of the water footprint?
o: They are three categories of carbon emissions from power plants.
They refer respectively to geological, ocean and terrestrial carbon storage.
They are three scopes of greenhouse-gas accounting.
They are categories included in the total freshwater used to produce goods and services.
104.x: The water footprint measures total freshwater used to produce goods and services and includes blue, green and grey water.
104.tq: Separate the water-footprint classification from carbon-storage and emissions classifications.

104.s: A company's diesel generator emits greenhouse gases, its purchased electricity causes indirect emissions, and emissions occur in the manufacture and transport of its purchased inputs. These are respectively classified as:
104.x: Direct emissions from owned sources are Scope 1, emissions from purchased electricity or heat are Scope 2, and the remaining value-chain emissions are Scope 3.
104.tq: Classify the emissions by asking whether they are owned, purchased-energy or value-chain emissions.

104.s: Which pair correctly identifies the first country to propose and the first country to actually levy a livestock carbon tax?
104.x: New Zealand was the first country to propose a tax on agricultural emissions, while Denmark is to become the first to actually levy a livestock carbon tax from 2030.
104.tq: Distinguish a proposal from actual implementation and keep the countries in the correct order.

104.s: The definitive phase of the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) began on:
104.x: The CBAM transitional phase began in 2023, while its definitive phase started on 1 January 2026.
104.tq: Separate the transitional start date from the definitive phase date.

104.s: Which of the following sectors is covered by the EU CBAM?
104.x: The CBAM covers iron and steel, aluminium and cement, among other sectors such as fertilisers, hydrogen, electricity and certain downstream goods.
104.tq: Use the inclusive option when every listed sector belongs to the covered group.

104.s: Under the EU CBAM, importers meet their carbon obligation primarily by purchasing:
o: voluntary offsets priced by the IPCC
agricultural emissions permits priced by the WTO
CBAM certificates priced on the EU Emissions Trading System
carbon-neutrality bonds priced by the World Bank
104.x: Importers purchase CBAM certificates whose price is linked to the EU Emissions Trading System.
104.tq: Match the instrument with the market mechanism used to price it.

104.s: What is the principal concern for Indian exporters arising from the EU CBAM?
o: CBAM applies only to India's domestic electricity consumption.
Decarbonisation costs may shift to exporters while the revenue remains in Europe.
CBAM removes the need for Indian industries to decarbonise.
Indian exporters receive all CBAM revenue directly from the EU.
104.x: CBAM can place decarbonisation costs on exporters, while the resulting revenue is retained in Europe.
104.tq: Apply the policy mechanism to the exporter–importer relationship rather than confusing it with a domestic tax.

104.s: Under Article 9 of the CBAM Regulation, which of the following may be deducted from the CBAM liability?
o: Voluntary forest plantation undertaken anywhere in the world
Only the importer's income tax paid in the EU
The entire value of the exported goods
A carbon price already paid in the exporting country, such as under the CCTS
104.x: Article 9 permits deduction of a carbon price already paid, including a price paid under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, from the CBAM liability.
104.tq: Identify the legally recognised deduction and reject unrelated economic payments.

104.s: The United Kingdom's CBAM is scheduled to start on:
104.x: The UK CBAM is scheduled to commence on 1 January 2027.
104.tq: Distinguish the UK's start date from the EU CBAM's definitive-phase date.

104.s: Recognition of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme by the United Kingdom in September 2026 has the effect of:
o: abolishing all carbon reporting by Indian exporters
increasing the CBAM liability on Indian exports
making the EU ETS applicable to India's domestic market
lowering the CBAM liability on Indian exports
104.x: Recognition of the CCTS as a qualifying carbon price lowers the CBAM liability on Indian exports to the UK.
104.tq: Trace the direction of effect of recognising a qualifying carbon price.

104.s: According to the World Bank's State and Trends of Carbon Pricing 2026, carbon pricing instruments covered approximately what share of global greenhouse-gas emissions?
104.x: Carbon pricing covered approximately 29% of global greenhouse-gas emissions.
104.tq: Retain the exact coverage percentage rather than rounding it to a nearby figure.

104.s:
Which one of the following combinations is correct regarding global carbon pricing in 2025–26?
1. Revenue exceeded $107 billion in 2025.
2. ETS coverage had tripled since 2016.
3. Carbon pricing covered 29% of global greenhouse-gas emissions.
104.x: All three figures are stated: revenue exceeded $107 billion in 2025, ETS coverage tripled since 2016, and carbon pricing covered 29% of global greenhouse-gas emissions.
104.tq: Check the monetary, growth and coverage figures together before choosing the complete combination.

104.s: The National Carbon Project is implemented under which programme?
o: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change only
104.x: The National Carbon Project is implemented under the ISRO Geosphere-Biosphere Programme.
104.tq: Identify the parent programme rather than a related climate or air-pollution initiative.

104.s:
Which set of activities is associated with the National Carbon Project?
1. Assessment of carbon pools and carbon fluxes
2. Assessment of the net carbon balance of India's terrestrial biomes
3. Study of vegetation carbon, soil carbon and vegetation/soil–atmosphere fluxes
4. Measurement of only carbon emissions from coastal shipping
Select the correct answer using the code below.
104.x: The project assesses carbon pools, fluxes and the net carbon balance of terrestrial biomes, with sub-projects on vegetation carbon, soil carbon and related fluxes. Coastal shipping alone is not its stated scope.
104.tq: Select the three related project objectives and reject the unrelated narrow activity.

104.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five IPCC carbon pools?
104.x: The five pools are above-ground biomass, below-ground biomass, dead wood, litter and soil organic carbon. Atmospheric oxygen is not one of them.
104.tq: Recall the five-member list and identify the item outside the classification.

104.s:
Arrange the following IPCC carbon pools in the order in which they are listed:
A. Soil organic carbon
B. Dead wood
C. Above-ground biomass
D. Litter
E. Below-ground biomass
104.x: The listed order is above-ground biomass, below-ground biomass, dead wood, litter and soil organic carbon.
104.tq: Use the first and last members of the recognised five-part list, then place the middle pools.

104.s: Which pair of satellites is correctly associated with CO2 observation?
104.x: NASA's OCO-2 and Japan's GOSAT are CO2-observing satellites.
104.tq: Match each satellite with its country or agency and avoid swapping the pair.

104.s: The Allam-Fetvedt cycle power plant of NET Power is associated with which of the following locations?
104.x: NET Power’s Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant is located at La Porte, Texas.
104.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the named demonstration plant from unrelated carbon initiatives.

104.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Allam-Fetvedt cycle:
