1. It burns natural gas in oxygen.
2. It uses supercritical carbon dioxide in the cycle.
3. It captures nearly all the carbon dioxide released.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: The Allam-Fetvedt cycle burns gas in oxygen, uses supercritical CO2 and captures nearly all the released CO2.
104.tq: Check each process component separately before selecting the combined statement.

104.s: Which one of the following technologies is designed to produce net-negative emissions by combining bioenergy with carbon capture and storage?
104.x: BECCS means bioenergy with carbon capture and storage; it can generate net-negative emissions.
104.tq: Break the acronym into its component terms and identify the mitigation pathway.

104.s: Approximately what proportion of the world’s low-carbon electricity is supplied by nuclear power?
104.x: Nuclear power supplies close to one-third of the world’s low-carbon electricity.
104.tq: Distinguish the approximate fraction from the larger and smaller distractor shares.

104.s: The Clean Development Mechanism under the Kyoto Protocol issues which of the following units?
104.x: The Clean Development Mechanism issues CERs, or Certified Emission Reductions.
104.tq: Match the Kyoto mechanism with its specific tradable unit rather than with a voluntary standard.

104.s: Carbon credits began in the international policy framework associated with which instrument and year?
104.x: The carbon-credit framework described here began with the Kyoto Protocol adopted in 1997.
104.tq: Pair the policy instrument with its associated year instead of choosing a related climate agreement.

104.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Gold Standard — Indian Carbon Credit administrator
CDM — voluntary standard founded by WWF
104.x: Verra runs the Verified Carbon Standard. BEE administers India’s CCTS, while CERs are issued under the CDM.
104.tq: Use the institution-function pairing to eliminate swapped authorities and standards.

104.s: Gold Standard, a voluntary carbon standard, was founded by which organisation?
104.x: Gold Standard was founded by WWF, the World Wide Fund for Nature.
104.tq: Identify the founding organisation rather than the administrator of a different carbon market.

104.s: Maruti Suzuki’s Gujarat in-plant railway siding has been described as the world’s first project of which type registered with Verra’s VCS?
104.x: The railway siding is the world’s first modal-shift project registered with Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard.
104.tq: Focus on the project’s defining activity—shifting freight movement to rail.

104.s:
Consider the following statements about Maruti Suzuki’s Gujarat railway siding project:
1. It is registered with Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard.
2. It is expected to generate about 1.7 lakh credits during FY24–FY33.
3. It follows CDM methodology AM0090.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements describe the Gujarat in-plant railway siding project: its Verra registration, expected credits and AM0090 methodology.
104.tq: Verify the organisation, quantity and methodology as separate factual elements.

104.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)?
o: It is a voluntary farmer-only market trading CERs issued by the Kyoto Protocol.
It is India’s first mandatory compliance carbon market and trades Indian Carbon Credits.
It is an international market operated exclusively by Verra.
It is a forest conservation programme administered by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
104.x: The CCTS is India’s first mandatory compliance carbon market and trades Indian Carbon Credits. It is not a farmer-only or exclusively international voluntary market.
104.tq: Find the option that combines the correct nature of the scheme with its correct traded unit.

104.s:
Under the CCTS, emission-intensity targets notified in October 2025 covered which sectors?
1. Aluminium
2. Cement
3. Chlor-alkali
4. Pulp and paper
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: The notified sectors were aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper.
104.tq: Treat each listed sector as an independent inclusion test before selecting the complete set.

104.s: How many obligated entities were covered by the CCTS emission-intensity targets notified in October 2025?
104.x: The October 2025 targets covered 282 obligated entities.
104.tq: Separate the number of obligated entities from the larger number of industries covered in the wider scheme.

104.s: The offset mechanism under the CCTS comprises how many methodologies?
104.x: The CCTS offset mechanism has nine methodologies.
104.tq: Use the exact count and reject nearby numerical distractors.

104.s: According to the stated 2026 coverage, the CCTS extends to approximately how many sectors, industries and million tonnes of CO2 equivalent, respectively?
104.x: The stated coverage is seven sectors, about 490 industries and about 477 Mt CO2e.
104.tq: Keep the three quantities in their original order and avoid swapping similarly sized figures.

104.s: Which of the following correctly characterises the Budget 2026–27 carbon credit programme?
o: It follows the DST roadmap and is industrial in orientation, rather than being a farmer-only scheme.
It is a panchayat-level programme focused only on blue carbon.
It follows the Kyoto Protocol and is administered exclusively by WWF.
It is a voluntary scheme restricted to 282 agricultural entities.
104.x: The programme follows the DST roadmap and concerns industrial carbon credits; it is not a farmer-only scheme.
104.tq: Distinguish the policy’s target and institutional roadmap from attractive but incorrect sectoral labels.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with India’s voluntary carbon-credit potential and registered agri-food projects?
104.x: India could earn 20–40 billion dollars from voluntary credits by 2030, and 242 agri-food projects are registered.
104.tq: Match the monetary range with the project count instead of mixing figures from the compliance market.

104.s: Which of the following is NOT a natural carbon sink identified in the context of carbon sequestration?
104.x: Forests, soil and oceans are natural carbon sinks. Chlor-alkali plants are industrial entities covered by emission-intensity targets, not natural sinks.
104.tq: Find the odd category by separating natural systems from an industrial sector.

104.s: Blue carbon is primarily stored by which combination of ecosystems?
o: Tropical peatlands, deserts and alpine meadows
104.x: Blue carbon is stored in coastal ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrass beds and salt marshes.
104.tq: Associate blue carbon with the listed coastal and marine ecosystems.

104.s: REDD+ primarily concerns which of the following?
o: Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation
Regulating carbon credits from aviation alone
Replacing all forests with commercial plantations
104.x: REDD+ stands for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation, with conservation and sustainable forest management dimensions.
104.tq: Expand the acronym to identify the exact forest-related objective.

104.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India participates in REDD+.
2. Forest conservation under REDD+ can earn tradable credits.
3. The Green India Mission and National Afforestation Programme can raise carbon stock.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: India participates in REDD+, forest conservation can generate tradable credits, and the two named programmes raise forest carbon stock.
104.tq: Test participation, economic outcome and linked programmes as separate propositions.

104.s: Which terrestrial ecosystem stores more carbon per hectare than any other terrestrial ecosystem?
104.x: Tropical peatlands store more carbon per hectare than any other terrestrial ecosystem.
104.tq: Identify the superlative comparison and avoid substituting a generally forested ecosystem.

104.s: CO2 fertilisation is estimated to account for what proportion of the Earth’s recent greening?
104.x: CO2 fertilisation accounts for approximately 70% of the Earth’s recent greening.
104.tq: Distinguish the stated dominant contribution from rounded lower and higher estimates.

104.s: Palli village in Samba district was declared India’s first carbon-neutral panchayat in which year?
104.x: Palli in Samba, Jammu and Kashmir, was declared India’s first carbon-neutral panchayat in 2022.
104.tq: Combine the first-in-India claim with its exact year and location.

104.s:
Which of the following measures is associated with Ladakh’s effort to become a carbon-neutral Union Territory?
1. Solar water lifting
2. Passive solar buildings
3. Geothermal heating
4. Electric vehicles
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: Ladakh’s carbon-neutral effort includes solar water lifting, passive solar buildings, geothermal heating and electric vehicles.
104.tq: Check whether all listed mitigation measures belong to the same regional strategy.

104.s: The criticism that the CBAM may make India a “rule-taker” is primarily framed as an issue of what kind?
104.x: The criticism of CBAM as potentially placing India in a rule-taker position is framed as a climate-justice issue.
104.tq: Connect the quoted policy concern with its broader analytical category.

104.s: Agricultural carbon credits face which principal concern identified in the carbon-market debate?
o: Inability to use any voluntary standard
104.x: Agricultural credits face measurement and credibility gaps, which affect the reliability of claimed reductions or removals.
104.tq: Select the specific implementation concern rather than an absolute claim about the market.

105.s: Which one of the following is an example of green technology in the cement industry?
o: Use of efficient kilns with precalciners and dry-process technology
Disposal of untreated effluents into water bodies
105.x: Green technology includes cleaner processes and products, such as efficient kilns with precalciners and dry-process technology.
105.tq: Identify the option describing a cleaner production process rather than an end-of-pipe measure.

105.s: Which of the following is associated with green cement technology?
105.x: Portland limestone cement is identified as an example of green cement technology.
105.tq: Use the exact product example associated with the concept.

105.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Green technology may use biomass and waste-derived fuels as alternative fuels.
2. Carbon capture and storage captures carbon dioxide from point sources such as cement plants.
3. Carbon capture and storage is already universally deployed as a mature pollution-control technology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. CCS remains largely at the research stage, so statement 3 is incorrect.
105.tq: Reject the extreme maturity claim and retain the statements describing actual functions.

105.s: Bioremediation primarily involves:
o: Burning all contaminated material at high temperature
Capturing carbon dioxide only from power plants
Using microbes or plants to clean polluted water and soil
Replacing all biological treatment with chemical treatment
105.x: Bioremediation uses microbes or plants to clean polluted water and soil. It is eco-friendly and cost-effective, but generally slower and condition-dependent.
105.tq: Match the environmental method with its defining biological agency and target.

105.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bioremediation is correct?
o: Its results are independent of local environmental conditions.
It is invariably faster than all conventional methods.
It is eco-friendly and cost-effective, but its results may vary with conditions.
It can be used only for air pollution.
105.x: Bioremediation is eco-friendly and cost-effective, but it is slower and its effectiveness varies with environmental conditions.
105.tq: Choose the balanced statement containing both the benefit and the limitation.

105.s: Incineration of waste is best classified as:
o: A conventional method of waste treatment
105.x: Incineration is a conventional waste-treatment method and is not classified as an alternative pollution-control approach in this context.
105.tq: Discriminate between a conventional pollution-control method and alternatives to it.

105.s: Which of the following is NOT a conventional end-of-pipe pollution-control tool?
105.x: Electrostatic precipitators, scrubbers and selective catalytic reduction are conventional end-of-pipe tools. Bioremediation is an alternative biological approach.
105.tq: Find the item belonging to an alternative category rather than the listed end-of-pipe group.

105.s: Which of the following functions is associated with the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board?
o: Issuing siting guidelines for industries near habitations, water bodies and fragile areas
Administering the Green Credit Programme nationally
Auditing the accounts of the Environmental Protection Fund
Awarding the Blue Flag eco-label to beaches
105.x: APPCB issues siting guidelines for industries near habitations, water bodies and fragile areas. The other functions belong to different institutions or bodies.
105.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the state pollution regulator’s function.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about APPCB’s regulatory arrangements:
1. It has standard operating procedures for effluents, marine outfalls and hazardous waste.
2. It uses computerised inspection allocation based on risk.
3. It permits industrial siting without considering fragile areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. APPCB’s siting guidelines specifically consider fragile areas, making statement 3 incorrect.
105.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the stated regulatory safeguard.

105.s: Under the Business Reform Action Plan, Andhra Pradesh streamlined environmental clearances mainly through:
o: Transfer of all clearances to local self-government bodies
Compulsory physical inspection for every application
105.x: Andhra Pradesh streamlined clearances through digitisation and single-window systems under BRAP.
105.tq: Link the administrative reform objective with its practical implementation mechanism.

105.s: Ecomark was originally launched in 1991 by the:
105.x: Ecomark was launched in 1991 by the environment ministry for environment-friendly consumer products.
105.tq: Match the eco-label with its launching authority and year.

105.s: Which one of the following product groups was NOT covered under the original Ecomark categories?
105.x: The notified Ecomark categories included soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics and aerosols. Drugs and antibiotics were not covered.
105.tq: Find the excluded category from a list containing closely related consumer products.

105.s: The Ecomark Rules notified on 26 September 2024 primarily sought to:
o: Remove consumer information from product labels
Replace all environmental standards with voluntary advertising
Improve accurate labelling and prevent misleading green claims
105.x: The 2024 Ecomark Rules replaced the 1991 scheme and aim to ensure accurate labelling, prevent misleading green claims and support informed purchases.
105.tq: Combine the date with the principal regulatory purpose instead of confusing it with the original launch.

105.s: PRAMAAN is associated with:
o: Certification of electric vehicle charging stations
Voluntary third-party certification for sustainable forestry and agroforestry
Certification of indoor air quality in hospitals
105.x: PRAMAAN is a voluntary third-party forest and wood certification initiative for sustainable forestry and agroforestry.
105.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed environmental labels by their certified subject.

105.s: How many Indian beaches were recommended for Blue Flag certification in 2020?
105.x: Eight Indian beaches were recommended for Blue Flag certification in 2020.
105.tq: Recall the specific count and year rather than substituting a later status figure.

105.s: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 decriminalised minor offences under the:
o: Wildlife Protection Act and Biological Diversity Act
105.x: The 2023 Jan Vishwas amendment decriminalised minor offences under the Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act by replacing imprisonment with monetary penalties.
105.tq: Match the amendment with the specific laws covered in the stated year.

105.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the 2024 amendment from the 2023 Jan Vishwas changes?
o: The Water Act was amended in 2024 in a similar manner.
The Water Act was excluded from all Jan Vishwas-related changes.
The 2024 amendment restored imprisonment for all minor offences.
The Air Act was first amended in 2024, while the Water Act was amended in 2023.
105.x: The Water Act was amended in 2024 in a similar manner, following the 2023 changes concerning minor offences under the Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act.
105.tq: Separate closely dated legal amendments by identifying the statute attached to each year.

105.s: The regulatory approach associated with the Jan Vishwas reforms is described as a shift from:
o: Trust-based regulation to manual command-and-control regulation
Technology-enabled regulation to prohibition of digital systems
Command-and-control regulation to trust-based, technology-enabled regulation
Judicial regulation to complete self-regulation without technology
105.x: The reforms are described as moving regulation from a command-and-control model to trust-based, technology-enabled regulation.
105.tq: Identify the correctly oriented before-and-after comparison.

105.s: Under the Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026, penalties are credited to the Environmental Protection Fund under:
105.x: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 place penalties in the Fund under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act, in the Public Account.
105.tq: Match the fund mechanism with the correct statutory provision.

105.s: What is the prescribed distribution of money in the Environmental Protection Fund between States/Union Territories and the Centre?
105.x: The prescribed distribution is 75% to States and Union Territories and 25% to the Centre.
105.tq: Recall the percentage split and maintain the stated order of recipients.

105.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated use of the Environmental Protection Fund?
o: Providing universal subsidies for fossil-fuel consumption
Monitoring and remediation of contaminated sites
Laboratories and clean-technology research and development
105.x: The Fund may support monitoring, remediation of contaminated sites, laboratories and clean-technology R&D. Universal fossil-fuel subsidies are not a stated use.
105.tq: Eliminate the unrelated expenditure and retain the listed environmental purposes.

105.s: The accounts of the Environmental Protection Fund are to be audited by the:
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
105.x: The Environmental Protection Fund is subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
105.tq: Identify the constitutional audit authority rather than a policy or adjudicatory body.

105.s: In August 2025, the Supreme Court upheld the power of Pollution Control Boards to impose environmental compensation under:
o: Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act
Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act alone
Section 33A of the Air Act and Section 31A of the Water Act
105.x: The Supreme Court upheld PCB power under Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act.
105.tq: Match each statutory section with the correct Act instead of swapping the pair.

105.s: Which statement correctly describes the revised industrial categories?
o: The mandatory 33% green belt was retained without any change.
All industries were placed in one category based only on location.
A new Blue category was introduced, and the mandatory 33% green belt was replaced by pollution-potential norms.
The Blue category was abolished, and a mandatory 50% green belt was introduced.
105.x: The revised categories introduced a new Blue category, illustrated by compressed biogas, and replaced the mandatory 33% green belt requirement with pollution-potential norms.
105.tq: Test both halves of a regulatory change and reject reversed percentages or categories.

105.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PM Ujjwala Yojana — 2016 — clean cooking and reduced indoor smoke
PM-KUSUM — 2016 — free LPG connections to poor households
PM E-DRIVE — 2019 — rooftop solar for households
PM Surya Ghar — 2024 — solar pumps exclusively for farmers
105.x: PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016 to provide free LPG connections to poor households, promoting clean cooking and reducing indoor smoke.
105.tq: Start with the sure scheme-year-objective combination and reject swapped objectives.

105.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019.
2. It promotes solar pumps and farm solar plants for farmers.
3. It primarily provides free LPG connections to poor households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 and concerns solar pumps and farm solar plants for farmers. Statement 3 describes PM Ujjwala Yojana, not PM-KUSUM.
105.tq: Separate similar clean-energy schemes by their beneficiaries and technology.

105.s: PM E-DRIVE, launched in 2024, is intended to provide incentives for:
o: Solar pumps and agricultural land restoration
105.x: PM E-DRIVE was launched in 2024 to incentivise electric vehicles and charging infrastructure. It is the successor to FAME.
105.tq: Identify the scheme from its transport technology and stated successor relationship.

105.s:
Arrange the following schemes in chronological order of their launch:
A. PM E-DRIVE
B. PM Ujjwala Yojana
C. PM-KUSUM
D. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
105.x: PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016, PM-KUSUM in 2019, and both PM E-DRIVE and PM Surya Ghar in 2024; the stated sequence is B, C, A, D.
105.tq: Place the earliest two schemes first, then distinguish the two 2024 initiatives.

105.s: The UNEP-CCAC ‘Hidden Assets’ assessment identifies PMUY as a model programme for:
105.x: The assessment cites PMUY as a model clean-cooking programme and identifies clean cooking and heating as South Asia’s leading solution towards 2035.
105.tq: Match the programme with the environmental problem it directly addresses.

105.s: According to the integrated clean-cooking and heating assessment, every one dollar invested in integrated action yields approximately:
105.x: The assessment states that every 1 dollar in integrated action yields approximately 15 dollars.
105.tq: Recall the specific quantified benefit rather than selecting a rounded distractor.

105.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between CCS and CCUS initiatives in India?
o: CCS research has been completed for all industries, and the CCUS report was issued in 2016.
CCS research is ongoing for cement plants, while NITI Aayog issued a CCUS policy-framework report in 2022.
CCUS applies only to household cooking, while CCS applies only to beaches.
Neither CCS research nor policy work has been undertaken in India.
105.x: Research on CCS is ongoing for cement plants, and NITI Aayog published a report on a CCUS policy framework in 2022.
105.tq: Keep the technical research activity distinct from the policy-framework milestone.

105.s: Which of the following pollutants is NOT tracked by the Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring System (CAAQMS)?
105.x: CAAQMS tracks PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NOx, CO, O3 and NH3. Methane is not included in the listed CAAQMS parameters.
105.tq: Find the one item that does not belong to the stated monitoring list.

105.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. CAAQMS tracks PM2.5 and PM10.
2. CAAQMS monitors sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide.
3. Ozone and ammonia are also among the pollutants tracked by CAAQMS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: All three statements are correct. The listed CAAQMS parameters are PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NOx, CO, O3 and NH3.
105.tq: Verify each statement against the complete list before selecting the inclusive option.

105.s: Which application provides public access to air-quality data generated through the monitoring system?
105.x: Public access to the relevant air-quality data is provided through the SAMEER app.
105.tq: Distinguish the public-data application from portals, programmes and grants.

105.s: PARIVESH 3.0 is primarily designed as a:
o: single-window portal for clearances and compliance monitoring
grant scheme for strengthening Pollution Control Boards
programme for replacing BS-IV vehicles with BS-VI vehicles
mobile application for publishing air-quality readings
105.x: PARIVESH 3.0 functions as a single-window portal for environmental clearances and compliance monitoring.
105.tq: Identify the precise institutional function rather than the associated environmental programme.

105.s: Which one of the following is the appropriate application of Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs)?
o: Issuing environmental clearances through a single window
Treatment of emissions from all thermal power stations
Monitoring of ambient air quality in major cities
Treatment of effluents generated by clusters of small industries
105.x: CETPs are intended for clusters of small industries, enabling common treatment of their effluents.
105.tq: Apply the facility to the industrial setting for which it is specifically intended.

105.s: The State Assistance for Abatement of Pollution (SAAP), introduced in 1992, provides grants primarily to:
o: finance Blue Flag certification of beaches
105.x: SAAP, dating from 1992, provides grants to strengthen Pollution Control Boards.
105.tq: Link the scheme with its year and the institution it supports.

105.s: With regard to online continuous emission and effluent monitoring, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It is administered by the State Assistance for Abatement of Pollution without CPCB involvement.
It is voluntary for all industries but compulsory only for municipal bodies.
It applies exclusively to industries producing household solid waste.
It is compulsory for highly polluting industries belonging to the 17-category classification.
105.x: The CPCB made online continuous emission and effluent monitoring compulsory for highly polluting industries in the 17-category classification.
105.tq: Use the authority, target group and compulsory nature together to identify the correct statement.

105.s: India implemented BS-VI emission standards from:
105.x: BS-VI emission standards came into force in India from 1 April 2020.
105.tq: Select the exact date from closely spaced chronological distractors.

105.s: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules referred to in the recent environmental initiatives are associated with the year:
105.x: The relevant Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules are the 2026 Rules.
105.tq: Use the exact year attached to the named legal instrument.

105.s: Which of the following concerns has been raised in debates relating to recent environmental regulatory changes?
o: The prohibition of clean fuels and eco-labelling.
The replacement of all Pollution Control Boards by local bodies.
Decriminalisation and relaxed green-belt norms may weaken deterrence.
The complete abolition of all environmental clearances for industries.
105.x: The debates include concerns that decriminalisation and relaxed green-belt norms could reduce deterrence. The other alternatives do not represent the stated concerns.
105.tq: Identify the genuine criticism rather than an extreme or absolute claim.

105.s: The expression 'ex-post facto environmental clearances' refers to clearances that are:
o: obtained before a project is proposed
issued only for projects outside green-belt areas
given automatically through the BRAP portal
granted after the project or activity has already commenced
105.x: Ex-post facto clearances are granted after the relevant project or activity has already begun, making them a subject of environmental debate.
105.tq: Distinguish a clearance granted after commencement from prior approval.

105.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of Andhra Pradesh's environmental initiatives?
o: APPCB — siting guidelines; BRAP — single-window system
APPCB — NAAQS formulation; BRAP — CETP construction
APPCB — Blue Flag certification; BRAP — ozone monitoring
APPCB — Environmental Protection Fund Rules; BRAP — SAAP grants
105.x: APPCB is associated with siting guidelines, while BRAP is associated with a single-window system. The other pairings assign unrelated functions to these bodies or initiatives.
105.tq: Start with the sure institutional-function pair and eliminate swapped responsibilities.

105.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the emerging approach to industrial pollution control?
o: A shift from end-of-pipe control towards prevention through clean fuels, eco-labels and market credits
A policy of replacing compliance monitoring with voluntary disclosure alone
A restriction of pollution control measures to large industries only
A shift from prevention towards exclusive dependence on end-of-pipe treatment
105.x: The emerging approach moves beyond end-of-pipe control towards prevention, including clean fuels, eco-labels and market credits.
105.tq: Identify the correct direction of policy change and its associated instruments.

105.s: Under the Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026, the Fund is constituted under which provision, and how is it divided between the States/Union Territories and the Centre?
o: Section 33A of the Water Act; 75% and 25%
Section 31A of the Air Act; 25% and 75%
105.x: The Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026 place the Fund under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act. Seventy-five per cent goes to States/UTs and 25 per cent to the Centre.
105.tq: Combine the enabling provision with the percentage split instead of treating them as separate figures.

105.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the revised approach to green belts in industrial regulation?
o: Green-belt norms have been abolished without replacement
A mandatory 33% green belt requirement has been replaced by norms based on pollution potential
Green belts are required only for White-category industries
The mandatory green belt has been increased from 33% to 50% for every industry
105.x: The mandatory 33% green-belt requirement was replaced by norms based on the pollution potential of industries.
105.tq: Recognise the policy shift from a uniform percentage requirement to pollution-potential-based norms.

106.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a biological disaster?
106.x: Epidemics, pandemics and pest attacks are biological disasters. Earthquakes are geophysical, cyclones are hydro-meteorological, and nuclear incidents are man-made or technological.
106.tq: Classify the example rather than the general term.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Class)
 a. Geological or geophysical
 b. Hydro-meteorological
 c. Climatological
 d. Man-made or technological

List-II (Example)
 i. Extreme temperatures
 ii. Chemical and industrial accidents
 iii. Earthquakes
 iv. Floods

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: Earthquakes are geological or geophysical; floods are hydro-meteorological; extreme temperatures are climatological; and chemical and industrial accidents are man-made or technological.
106.tq: Start with the distinctive technological and geological examples.

106.s: Which of the following is an emerging hazard identified in addition to conventional natural and technological hazards?
106.x: Cyber attacks, space weather and AI failures are identified as emerging hazards.
106.tq: Pick the item belonging to the emerging-hazard category.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about notified disasters eligible for SDRF or NDRF assistance:
1. The number of notified disasters became 14 after August 2026.
2. Heatwave and lightning were added on the advice of the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
3. Man-made calamities are included among the notified disasters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The number rose to 14 after heatwave and lightning were added; no man-made calamity is notified for this purpose.
106.tq: Find the single false statement by checking the eligibility exception.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding international disaster-risk-reduction frameworks:

List-I (Framework)
a. IDNDR
b. Hyogo Framework for Action
c. Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
d. CDRI

List-II (Period or launch year)
i. 2015–2030
ii. 1990–1999
iii. Launched in 2019
iv. 2005–2015

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
106.x: IDNDR covered 1990–1999, Hyogo covered 2005–2015, Sendai covers 2015–2030, and CDRI was launched in 2019.
106.tq: Start with the distinctive CDRI launch year and verify the remaining periods.

106.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the major international disaster-risk-reduction frameworks or initiatives?
106.x: The chronological order is IDNDR (1990–1999), Hyogo (2005–2015), Sendai (2015–2030), and CDRI, launched in 2019.
106.tq: Fix the first and last items before arranging the middle frameworks.

106.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Hyogo Framework for Action and the Sendai Framework?
o: Hyogo was the predecessor of Sendai.
Sendai was the predecessor of Hyogo.
Hyogo was the successor to Sendai.
Both were launched in the same year and cover the same period.
106.x: The Hyogo Framework for Action for 2005–2015 preceded and was succeeded by the Sendai Framework for 2015–2030.
106.tq: Test predecessor–successor direction in a paired framework question.

106.s:
With reference to the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, consider the following statements:
1. It covers the period 2015–2030.
2. It contains four priorities for action.
3. It contains seven global targets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: The Sendai Framework covers 2015–2030 and contains four priorities and seven global targets.
106.tq: Combine the framework’s period with its two key numerical features.

106.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework?
o: Investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience
Replacing all community-based systems with centralised response agencies
106.x: The four priorities include understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in risk reduction, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and Build Back Better. Replacing community systems is not a Sendai priority.
106.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the recognised priority set.

106.s: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) is best described as:
o: A predecessor framework to the Hyogo Framework for Action
A UN treaty body headquartered in Geneva
An India-led infrastructure-resilience coalition with its secretariat in New Delhi
A State-level fund administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs
106.x: CDRI is an India-led coalition focused on infrastructure resilience, and its secretariat is located in New Delhi.
106.tq: Combine the organisation’s identity, leadership and headquarters.

106.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a hydro-meteorological disaster?
106.x: Cyclones are hydro-meteorological disasters. Earthquakes are geological, epidemics are biological and nuclear incidents are man-made or industrial disasters.
106.tq: Use the classification table to distinguish disasters by their governing natural or human process.

106.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Geological disasters — Earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
2. Biological disasters — Epidemics and pest attacks
3. Emerging disasters — Cyber attacks and space weather
4. Man-made disasters — Chemical accidents and nuclear incidents
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
106.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Geological, biological, emerging and man-made disasters include the examples stated respectively.
106.tq: Match each example with its disaster category before selecting the coded combination.

106.s: A widespread outbreak of a communicable disease such as COVID-19 is classified under which category of disaster?
106.x: Epidemics and pandemics, including COVID-19, are biological disasters.
106.tq: Test the category directly by identifying the underlying biological agent.

106.s: Which one of the following is an example of an emerging disaster rather than a conventional natural disaster?
106.x: Cyber attacks, space weather and artificial intelligence failures are listed as emerging disasters.
106.tq: Discriminate emerging technological risks from geological, climatic and biological hazards.

106.s: Chemical accidents are regulated, among other provisions, under which pair of rules?
o: EIA Rules, 2006 and Bio-medical Waste Rules, 2016
Environment Protection Rules, 1986 and Forest Rules, 1992
106.x: Chemical accidents fall under the Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules, 1989 and the Chemical Accidents (Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Response) Rules, 1996.
106.tq: Recall the paired legal instruments and their years without confusing them with environmental pollution rules.

106.s: Under the arrangements for chemical accidents, Crisis Groups may be constituted at which levels?
o: Central, State, District and Local levels
106.x: The institutional arrangement for chemical accidents includes Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups.
106.tq: Use the complete administrative-level sequence to avoid dropping the local or district tier.

106.s: The National Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the:
106.x: The Prime Minister chairs the National Disaster Management Authority.
106.tq: Use the constitutional-political head associated with the apex disaster-management authority.

106.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function associated with the NDMA?
o: Serving as the State Emergency Operations Centre of Andhra Pradesh
106.x: The State Emergency Operations Centre is run by APSDMA. NDMA lays down policies, approves the National Plan and provides policy for NIDM, among other functions.
106.tq: Distinguish national-level NDMA functions from the state-level operational role of APSDMA.

106.s: The overall coordination of disaster management at the Union level is undertaken through the disaster management division of the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
106.x: The disaster management division of the Ministry of Home Affairs undertakes overall coordination.
106.tq: Identify the responsible ministry rather than the operational force or technical ministry.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about fire services in India:
1. Fire services are a State subject.
2. The Directorate General of Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. Fire services have no advisory role in disaster management.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Fire services are a State subject, and the DG Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards under MHA has an advisory role. Statement 3 is false.
106.tq: Spot the false absolute statement and retain the two compatible administrative facts.

106.s: The southern campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
106.x: The southern campus of NIDM was set up at Kondapavuluru in Krishna district, pursuant to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
106.tq: Combine the institution, location and district to avoid nearby-place substitutions.

106.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority?
o: It is chaired by the Governor and manages only post-disaster compensation.
It is chaired by the Chief Minister and functions as the chief nodal agency for disaster management in the State.
It is chaired by the District Collector and controls the National Disaster Response Force.
It is headed by the Municipal Commissioner and operates only in municipal corporations.
106.x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister, serves as the State’s chief nodal agency, runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and supports early warning.
106.tq: Match the authority with its chairperson and operational responsibilities in a state-level scenario.

106.s: The AP Disaster Management Rules associated with APSDMA were issued in:
106.x: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules are of 2007.
106.tq: Separate the year of the State rules from the years of the central Act, policy and Reorganisation Act.

106.s:
Arrange the following global disaster-risk-reduction milestones in chronological order:
A. Yokohama Strategy
B. Sendai Framework
C. International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction
D. Hyogo Framework for Action
Select the correct answer.
106.x: The sequence is IDNDR (1990–99), Yokohama Strategy (1994), Hyogo Framework (2005–2015), and Sendai Framework (2015–2030).
106.tq: Fix the broad decade markers first, then place the 1994 Yokohama milestone within them.

106.s: The International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction was the first concerted effort of the United Nations during which period?
106.x: The IDNDR covered the 1990s, specifically 1990–1999, and represented the first concerted UN effort in this field.
106.tq: Use the decade range rather than confusing IDNDR with the later Hyogo or Sendai periods.

106.s: The Yokohama Strategy is best described as the:
o: blueprint that emerged from the IDNDR process
106.x: The Yokohama Strategy, adopted in 1994, was the blueprint developed from the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
106.tq: Identify the framework’s relationship with IDNDR rather than its date alone.

106.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a framework with its period and principal emphasis?
o: Yokohama Strategy — 2005–2015 — resilience of nations and communities
Sendai Framework — 2015–2030 — succeeds the Hyogo Framework
106.x: The Sendai Framework covers 2015–2030 and succeeds the Hyogo Framework for Action. Hyogo covered 2005–2015 and focused on the resilience of nations and communities.
106.tq: Check both the date and the relationship or emphasis in each paired option.

106.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework?
o: Replacing national planning with international relief operations
Investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience
106.x: The four priorities are understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and to Build Back Better.
106.tq: Recall the four-priority structure and reject the option that changes preparedness into an unrelated policy.

106.s: Which of the following is included among the seven global targets of the Sendai Framework?
o: Reduction of international cooperation in disaster management
106.x: The Sendai global targets include increasing the availability of and access to multi-hazard early-warning systems, along with reducing mortality, affected people, economic loss and infrastructure damage.
106.tq: Identify the positive disaster-risk-reduction target among reversed or unrelated policy statements.

106.s: Which set contains the three post-2015 frameworks identified as shaping India’s disaster-risk reduction approach?
o: Sendai Framework, Sustainable Development Goals and Paris Agreement
Hyogo Framework, Kyoto Protocol and Montreal Protocol
Yokohama Strategy, SDGs and Convention on Biological Diversity
IDNDR, Paris Agreement and Ramsar Convention
106.x: The three post-2015 frameworks are the Sendai Framework, the Sustainable Development Goals for 2015–2030 and the Paris Agreement.
106.tq: Use the post-2015 time filter to eliminate the earlier IDNDR, Yokohama and Hyogo instruments.

106.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes a hazard from a disaster?
o: A hazard and a disaster are identical terms used in disaster management
A hazard refers only to economic loss, whereas a disaster refers only to physical damage
A hazard is always caused by human activity, whereas a disaster is always natural
A hazard is a potentially damaging event, whereas a disaster results when hazard interacts with vulnerability and causes serious harm
106.x: A hazard is a potentially damaging event. It becomes a disaster when it interacts with vulnerability and produces serious adverse consequences.
106.tq: Discriminate between closely related technical terms instead of treating them as synonyms.

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding vulnerability:
1. Vulnerability denotes susceptibility to harm.
2. It may have physical, social, economic and environmental dimensions.
3. It is determined exclusively by the intensity of a hazard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Vulnerability is susceptibility to harm and may be physical, social, economic or environmental. It is not determined exclusively by hazard intensity.
106.tq: Find the statement that wrongly narrows a multidimensional concept through the word 'exclusively'.

106.s: Which one of the following correctly describes capacity in disaster management?
o: The strengths and resources available to cope with hazards
The process of restoring infrastructure after a disaster
The susceptibility of a community to damage
The probability that a hazard will occur
106.x: Capacity comprises the strengths and resources available to individuals, communities and institutions to cope with hazards.
106.tq: Match the exact definition with the appropriate disaster-management term.

106.s: The ability of a community to resist, absorb and recover quickly from the effects of a hazard is called
106.x: Resilience is the ability to resist, absorb and recover quickly from the effects of a hazard.
106.tq: Use the defining action words to identify the technical term.

106.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
106.x: Cyclone shelters and shelter belts are mitigation measures for cyclones. Drought is administered by the Ministry of Agriculture, along with hailstorm, frost and pest attack.
106.tq: Find the mismatched mitigation measure by relating it to the hazard it addresses.

106.s:
The mitigation of cyclones and storm surges may include which of the following?
1. IMD warnings
2. Cyclone shelters and evacuation
3. Shelter belts and mangroves
4. Seismic zoning as the primary measure
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves are cyclone-related measures. Seismic zoning is primarily an earthquake mitigation measure.
106.tq: Separate hazard-specific measures from a plausible but unrelated technical measure.

106.s: Coringa and Krishna are mentioned in the context of
o: mangroves used in cyclone and storm-surge mitigation
106.x: Coringa and Krishna are associated with mangroves that help mitigate cyclones and storm surges.
106.tq: Use location-based recall for a specific mitigation example.

106.s: Which Ministry administers drought-related disaster management along with hailstorm, frost and pest attack?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
106.x: The Ministry of Agriculture administers drought-related matters along with hailstorm, frost and pest attack.
106.tq: Apply the 'who administers this subject?' authority-identification method.

106.s: Which one of the following is the appropriate mitigation approach for earthquakes?
o: Cyclone shelters and coastal evacuation only
106.x: Earthquake mitigation includes seismic zoning and safe construction practices.
106.tq: Match the hazard with its distinctive structural mitigation measure.

106.s: Tsunami mitigation and preparedness in India are associated with
o: IMD warnings and shelter belts only
INCOI warnings and Tsunami Ready villages
106.x: Tsunami warning information is associated with INCOI, while Tsunami Ready villages support local preparedness.
106.tq: Distinguish tsunami-specific institutions and preparedness measures from those for other hazards.

106.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
1. Flood — embankments and flood forecasting
2. Landslide — hazard zonation mapping and early warning
3. Heat wave — maximum temperature of at least 40°C in plains with a departure of at least 4.5°C
4. Cold wave — minimum temperature of at most 10°C in plains with a departure of at most −4.5°C
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: All four statements are correct. Floods are mitigated through embankments and forecasting; landslides through zonation and warnings; and the stated thresholds define heat-wave and cold-wave conditions in plains.
106.tq: Check each hazard against its specific mitigation measure or quantitative criterion.

106.s: For a heat wave in the plains, the stated criterion is
o: minimum temperature of at most 10°C with a departure of −4.5°C
maximum temperature of at least 40°C with a departure of at least 4.5°C
maximum temperature of at least 45°C without reference to departure
maximum temperature of at least 35°C with a departure of 2.5°C
106.x: The stated heat-wave criterion for plains is a maximum temperature of at least 40°C along with a departure of at least 4.5°C.
106.tq: Separate the heat-wave threshold from the similar-looking cold-wave threshold.

106.s: Which of the following correctly states the criterion for a cold wave in the plains?
o: Minimum temperature at or below 10°C with a departure at or below −4.5°C
Minimum temperature at or below 5°C without a departure criterion
Maximum temperature at or below 10°C with a departure at or below −4.5°C
Maximum temperature at or above 40°C with a departure at or above 4.5°C
106.x: The cold-wave criterion in the plains is a minimum temperature of 10°C or below with a departure of −4.5°C or below.
106.tq: Compare the minimum-temperature and maximum-temperature criteria without reversing their signs.

106.s: The Tsunami Ready recognition programme associated with UNESCO-IOC has recognised how many villages in Odisha?
106.x: Twenty-four Odisha villages have been recognised under the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready programme. The target is 100 villages.
106.tq: Distinguish the achieved number from the larger target number.

106.s: The National Tsunami Ready Board (NTRB) was set up by the
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
106.x: The NTRB was set up by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and is chaired by the Director of INCOI.
106.tq: Identify the responsible ministry rather than the operational warning institution.

106.s: Who chairs the National Tsunami Ready Board?
106.x: The National Tsunami Ready Board is chaired by the Director of INCOI.
106.tq: Use the chairperson detail as a direct institutional discriminator.

106.s: Which of the following supports the management of all hazards through a GIS database and satellite-based disaster management capabilities?
106.x: ISRO's Disaster Management Support programme and the National Database for Emergency Management support all hazards, with NDEM functioning as a GIS database.
106.tq: Match the technological system with its stated cross-hazard function.

106.s: The National Project for Strengthening Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction in PRIs provides for how many Model Gram Panchayats on six hazard themes?
106.x: The project provides for 20 Model Gram Panchayats based on six hazard themes.
106.tq: Distinguish the number of model units from the project’s wider coverage figures.

106.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies under the disaster-management framework?
o: They are responsible only for international humanitarian assistance
They have a legal role involving local plans, relief and capacity building
They have no legal role and may act only after approval from NDRF
They replace State Disaster Management Authorities in every function
106.x: The Disaster Management Act gives PRIs and ULBs a legal role in local plans, relief and capacity building.
106.tq: Reject extreme institutional claims and identify the defined local-government functions.

106.s: Aapda Mitra is primarily associated with
o: maintaining a national GIS database of hazards
training community volunteers as first responders
106.x: Aapda Mitra is an NDMA scheme for training community volunteers to act as first responders.
106.tq: Match a named scheme with its distinctive operational purpose.

106.s: Which statement regarding the use of social media in disaster risk reduction is correct?
o: Social media has no role in community-based disaster management
Social media is a complete replacement for official warning systems
Social media can be used only after the recovery phase
Social media is a complementary tool and not a replacement for established systems
106.x: Social media can support communication and community engagement, but it is a complementary tool rather than a replacement for official disaster-management systems.
106.tq: Avoid absolute claims and identify the limited but useful complementary role.

106.s: Operation Vanilla was associated with humanitarian assistance to
o: Turkey and Syria after the 2023 earthquake
106.x: Operation Vanilla assisted Madagascar following Cyclone Diane in 2020.
106.tq: Link the operation name to the assisted country and disaster event.

106.s:
Match the following HADR operations with the countries assisted:

A. Maitri
B. Dost
C. Karuna
D. Sadbhav

1. Turkey and Syria
2. Nepal
3. Myanmar
4. Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: Maitri assisted Nepal, Dost assisted Turkey and Syria, Karuna assisted Myanmar, and Sadbhav assisted Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar.
106.tq: Start with the distinctive multi-country pair and eliminate codes that swap neighbouring operations.

106.s: Which operation was associated with assistance to Myanmar following Cyclone Mocha in 2023?
106.x: Operation Karuna was associated with assistance to Myanmar after Cyclone Mocha in 2023. Operation Brahma was associated with Myanmar after the 2025 earthquake.
106.tq: Separate similar country associations by comparing the operation and event year.

106.s: Operation Brahma, as listed in the humanitarian assistance context, was associated with
o: the 2024 Typhoon Yagi in Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar
the 2023 earthquake in Turkey and Syria
106.x: Operation Brahma assisted Myanmar following the 2025 earthquake.
106.tq: Use the event-year combination to distinguish operations with the same assisted country.

106.s: The National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR) is chaired by the
106.x: NPDRR is a multi-stakeholder body chaired by the Union Home Minister.
106.tq: Identify the chairperson of the coordinating body rather than its implementing agencies.

106.s: SACHET is best described as
o: an ISRO GIS database for all hazards
an NDMA alert system based on the Common Alerting Protocol and developed by C-DOT
a volunteer-training scheme run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj
106.x: SACHET is NDMA's Common Alerting Protocol-based alert system, developed by C-DOT.
106.tq: Match the system with its authority, technical protocol and developer.

106.s: The 'Resilient India 2047' push is associated with
o: the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready recognition process
only the Ministry of Agriculture's drought programme
106.x: The 'Resilient India 2047' push is associated with NDMA and Ministry disaster-management plans.
106.tq: Identify the institutional setting of a named policy initiative.

106.s: The amount released by Andhra Pradesh under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26, as compared with Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27, was
106.x: Andhra Pradesh released Rs 277.63 crore under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26, compared with Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27.
106.tq: Distinguish successive-year figures from the separate SDMF/NDMF allocation.

106.s: Which statement correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's coastline in the stated geographical context?
o: It is the longest coastline in India and lies on the west coast
It is the second-longest coastline in India and the shortest on the east coast
It has no significant exposure to coastal hazards
It is the third-longest coastline in India and the longest on the east coast
106.x: The stated current AP position is that Andhra Pradesh has the third-longest coastline in India and the longest coastline on the east coast.
106.tq: Handle comparative rankings carefully and avoid substituting an older figure for the stated current one.

106.s: The July 2026 Godavari floods primarily tested the effectiveness of
o: NDRF/SDRF operations and early warning systems
106.x: The Godavari floods in July 2026 tested NDRF and SDRF operations along with early-warning mechanisms.
106.tq: Identify the disaster-management capabilities directly engaged by a flood event.

106.s: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 is considered significant because it shifted India's disaster-management approach from
106.x: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 marked a shift from a primarily relief-oriented approach towards risk reduction and more comprehensive disaster management.
106.tq: Test the policy significance through the direction of institutional change.

106.s: Which programme is specifically associated with the recognition of tsunami-ready communities?
o: Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme of UNESCO-IOC
Aapda Mitra Response Programme of NDRF
106.x: The Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme is implemented under UNESCO-IOC for recognising tsunami-ready communities.
106.tq: Discriminate between programmes for general safety education and the specialised tsunami-recognition programme.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme:
1. It is associated with UNESCO-IOC.
2. Recognition is based on 12 indicators.
3. Recognition is renewable every four years.
4. India has targeted 100 tsunami-ready villages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: The programme is associated with UNESCO-IOC, uses 12 indicators, has recognition renewable every four years, and India has targeted 100 tsunami-ready villages.
106.tq: Combine the institutional, numerical and renewal-period details before choosing the coded option.

106.s: How many Odisha villages had been recognised under the Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme?
106.x: Twenty-four villages in Odisha had been recognised under the Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme.
106.tq: Distinguish the number already recognised from India's larger target of 100 villages.

106.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Geological — Earthquakes and landslides
2. Hydro-meteorological — Cyclones and droughts
3. Biological — Epidemics and pest attacks
4. Man-made — Chemical accidents and nuclear incidents
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
106.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the stated disaster classifications.
106.tq: Check each classification category before selecting the comprehensive code.

106.s:
Which of the following statements about the coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. Twelve districts touch the coast after the 2022 reorganisation.
2. Srikakulam has the longest district coastline, measuring 193 km.
3. West Godavari has the shortest district coastline, measuring 23 km.
106.x: All three statements are correct. After the 2022 reorganisation, 12 districts touch the coast; Srikakulam has 193 km and West Godavari has 23 km.
106.tq: Check the district count together with the longest–shortest comparison.

106.s: The State Emergency Operations Centre and early-warning functions in Andhra Pradesh are operated under the authority of
o: The National Disaster Management Authority alone
106.x: APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and the early-warning system in Andhra Pradesh.
106.tq: Match an operational function with the responsible state body.

106.s: The CAEPPR Rules, 1996 provide for the establishment of:
o: Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups
106.x: The CAEPPR Rules, 1996 provide for Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups for preparedness and response to chemical emergencies.
106.tq: Read the composition literally and avoid dropping the lower administrative levels.

107.s: Which geospatial application is specifically useful for identifying persons who may have been exposed to an infectious disease?
107.x: Geospatial technology can support contact tracing by identifying people who may have been exposed to an infectious disease.
107.tq: Use the direct function-to-tool association.

107.s:
Geospatial technology is useful in epidemic management for which of the following purposes?
1. Contact tracing
2. Mapping hotspots or containment zones
3. Real-time spatial planning of vaccine distribution
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Geospatial technology supports contact tracing, hotspot and containment-zone mapping, and GIS-based real-time vaccine distribution planning.
107.tq: Check whether all three statements describe related applications of GIS.

107.s: The COVID war room supported by GIS was set up by which organisation?
107.x: The GIS-supported COVID war room was set up by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).
107.tq: Identify the local authority associated with the operational measure.

107.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IHIP portal — real-time pooling of grassroots surveillance data
U-WIN — genome sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 variants
107.x: The IHIP portal pools grassroots data in real time. U-WIN tracks immunisation, while INSACOG tracks variants through genome sequencing.
107.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate swapped functions.

107.s: U-WIN is primarily associated with which activity?
107.x: U-WIN is a current surveillance and tracking tool for immunisation.
107.tq: Use the exact purpose of the named digital platform.

107.s: Distributing vaccines before the occurrence of an epidemic is classified under which phase of the disaster management cycle?
107.x: Pre-outbreak vaccine distribution reduces the potential impact of an epidemic and is therefore a mitigation measure.
107.tq: Classify the measure by asking whether it reduces impact before the event.

107.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mitigation — sanitation and vector control
2. Preparedness — hospital readiness and mock drills
3. Response — isolation, quarantine and contact tracing
4. Recovery — rehabilitation and economic relief
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
107.x: All four pairs correctly associate epidemic measures with the mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery phases respectively.
107.tq: Match each measure to the phase in which it is normally undertaken.

107.s:
Arrange the following epidemic-management measures in the correct order of the disaster management cycle:
A. Rehabilitation and economic relief
B. Surveillance and hospital readiness
C. Isolation and contact tracing
D. Sanitation and vector control
107.x: The sequence is mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery: sanitation and vector control, surveillance and readiness, isolation and contact tracing, and finally rehabilitation and relief.
107.tq: Use the first and last phases, then place preparedness before response.

107.s: Which of the following statements regarding the National Disaster Management Plan is correct?
o: It deals exclusively with post-disaster rehabilitation.
It was issued in 2005 under the Epidemic Diseases Act.
It was India's first National Disaster Management Plan, issued in 2016.
It excludes biological disasters from its scope.
107.x: The National Disaster Management Plan issued in 2016 was India's first such plan and covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery.
107.tq: Reject statements that narrow the scope or substitute the wrong legal basis.

107.s:
The National Disaster Management Plan is aligned with which of the following?
1. Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, 2015–2030
2. Sustainable Development Goals
3. Paris Agreement
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: The plan aligns with the Sendai Framework, the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Agreement.
107.tq: Recognise the complete set of international frameworks linked with the plan.

107.s: For disaster-management purposes, epidemics are classified as which type of disasters?
107.x: Epidemics are treated as biological disasters in disaster-management planning.
107.tq: Identify the disaster category from the nature of the hazard.

107.s: Which of the following is the technical arm of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare?
107.x: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) functions as the technical arm of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
107.tq: Distinguish the technical arm from coordinating and surveillance bodies.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC):
1. It was formerly known as the National Institute of Communicable Diseases.
2. It is the apex surveillance and outbreak-response agency.
3. It runs the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: NCDC, formerly NICD, is the apex surveillance and outbreak-response agency and runs IDSP.
107.tq: Use the organisation’s former name and functions together.

107.s: Which organisation sends Outbreak Investigation Teams and runs the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre?
107.x: The NCDC sends Outbreak Investigation Teams and runs the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre.
107.tq: Link the operational outbreak-response functions to the correct agency.

107.s:
With reference to the institutional framework for health emergencies, consider the following statements:
1. NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. State Disaster Management Authorities are chaired by Chief Ministers.
3. NDMA lays down guidelines and coordinates health emergencies under the Disaster Management Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three statements correctly describe the leadership and coordinating role of NDMA and SDMAs.
107.tq: Verify both the chairpersons and the statutory function before selecting the code.

107.s: The Biological Disaster Management guidelines were issued by the National Disaster Management Authority in which year?
107.x: NDMA issued the Biological Disaster Management guidelines in 2008.
107.tq: Separate the guideline year from the years of the DM Act and National Plan.

107.s: Which of the following was designated as the nodal unit for pandemic planning in December 2020?
o: National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre
107.x: The Disaster Management Cell of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare became the nodal unit for pandemic planning in December 2020.
107.tq: Identify the exact institutional unit rather than the parent ministry alone.

107.s: HRDEMS is intended to establish how many NELS skill centres?
107.x: HRDEMS is intended to set up 120 NELS skill centres.
107.tq: Focus on the distinctive programme target rather than other health-emergency figures.

107.s: Under PM-ABHIM, which combination is correctly associated with the health-emergency infrastructure deployed during Operation Sindoor?
o: 15 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 50 BHISHM Cubes
50 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 15 BHISHM Cubes
120 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 10 BHISHM Cubes
2 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 15 BHISHM Cubes
107.x: PM-ABHIM includes 15 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 50 BHISHM Cubes, which were deployed during Operation Sindoor.
107.tq: Match each infrastructure item with its precise numerical count.

107.s: The Covid Pharma application launched in Andhra Pradesh on 25 April 2020 was used to track persons purchasing which medicines over the counter?
o: Medicines for cough, cold and fever
107.x: The AP Medical and Health Department launched Covid Pharma on 25 April 2020 to track people buying over-the-counter medicines for cough, cold and fever.
107.tq: Combine the app’s launch date, authority and precise purpose.

107.s: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 primarily provides the legal framework for which of the following?
107.x: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 provides the legal framework for dealing with biological disasters and epidemics and was used during COVID-19.
107.tq: Choose the legal instrument according to its subject matter and historical use.

107.s: Under the Epidemic Diseases Act framework, which of the following is correctly matched?
107.x: Urgent cases must be reported within 24 hours, while routine cases must be reported within three days.
107.tq: Separate the shorter urgent-reporting period from the routine period.

107.s: Which one of the following statements about the 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act is correct?
o: It removed all criminal penalties for violence against health workers.
It made violence against health workers cognizable and non-bailable.
It was enacted for the first time in March 2020 without an ordinance.
It transferred port-inspection powers exclusively to State Governments.
107.x: The 2020 amendment made violence against health workers cognizable and non-bailable and also gave the Centre powers over inspection at ports of entry.
107.tq: Reject options that reverse the legal effect or substitute the wrong authority.

107.s: Which sequence correctly represents the 2020 legislative action concerning the Epidemic Diseases Act?
o: Act in April, ordinance in September
Ordinance in April, Act in September
Ordinance in March, Act in April
Act in January, ordinance in December
107.x: The amendment was introduced through an ordinance in April 2020 and became an Act in September 2020.
107.tq: Arrange the temporary ordinance and subsequent Act in sequence.

107.s: For violence against health workers causing grievous hurt, the 2020 amendment provided which punishment range?
o: Six months to seven years and a fine of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh
Seven years to ten years and a fine of Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh
One year to three years and a fine of Rs 10,000 to Rs 50,000
Three months to five years and a fine of Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh
107.x: For grievous hurt, the amendment provided imprisonment from six months to seven years and a fine of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh.
107.tq: Distinguish the enhanced grievous-hurt penalty from the ordinary offence penalty.

107.s: The nationwide COVID-19 lockdown in March 2020 was ordered under which legal framework?
o: The Disaster Management Act, 2005, by NDMA and MHA
107.x: The national COVID lockdown was ordered by NDMA and the Ministry of Home Affairs under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
107.tq: Identify the statute and authorities actually associated with the lockdown.

107.s: Which body ran the pandemic response through empowered groups?
107.x: Empowered Groups constituted under the Ministry of Home Affairs ran the pandemic response.
107.tq: Distinguish the coordinating ministry from the health-surveillance agency.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Draft Public Health Bill, 2017:
1. It was intended to replace the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.
2. It concerned prevention, control and management of epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters.
3. It has been enacted as a law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: The draft Bill was intended to replace the 1897 Act and covered epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters, but it has not been enacted.
107.tq: Find the false statement by checking the legal status of the draft Bill.

107.s: The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme was launched in which year under the National Health Mission?
107.x: IDSP was launched in 2004 under the National Health Mission and is implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
107.tq: Separate the launch year of IDSP from the later IHIP years.

107.s: Which organisational structure is associated with the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme?
o: One District Surveillance Unit for each international port
One Central Surveillance Unit in Delhi and State and District Surveillance Units
Only a Central Surveillance Unit without State units
107.x: IDSP consists of a Central Surveillance Unit in Delhi along with State and District Surveillance Units.
107.tq: Identify the complete administrative structure rather than a single level.

107.s: The Integrated Health Information Platform was launched nationwide from which month and year?
107.x: IHIP was launched in a few states in 2018 and became nationwide from September 2021.
107.tq: Distinguish the initial limited launch from nationwide implementation.

107.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three categories of reporting used in disease surveillance?
107.x: Surveillance data are reported through syndromic (S), presumptive (P) and laboratory-confirmed (L) categories.
107.tq: Expand the surveillance abbreviations and distinguish them from site categories.

107.s: Which sites can feed data into the disease-surveillance system?
107.x: Data are fed into the surveillance system by sentinel sites as well as private sites.
107.tq: Avoid the extreme-word trap in the word ‘only’.

107.s: Approximately what proportions of infectious diseases and emerging infectious diseases, respectively, are zoonotic?
107.x: About 60% of infectious diseases and 75% of emerging infectious diseases are zoonotic.
107.tq: Preserve the order of the two percentages while comparing disease categories.

107.s: Which organisation asked States to strengthen IDSP surveillance for Ebola?
o: The State Disaster Management Authorities alone
107.x: The Centre asked States to step up IDSP surveillance for Ebola.
107.tq: Identify the coordinating level of government from the surveillance action.

107.s:
Andhra Pradesh’s zoonotic disease action plan is being prepared under which approach and with which institutions?
1. One Health approach
2. NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego
3. INSACOG, UNEP and WHO only
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: AP is preparing the plan under the One Health approach with NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego. The third statement names institutions not given for this action plan.
107.tq: Spot the substituted institutional partners in the false statement.

107.s: Which laboratory is regarded as the apex virology laboratory in India and has BSL-4 containment?
107.x: ICMR-NIV Pune is the apex virology laboratory and has BSL-4 containment facilities.
107.tq: Match the apex laboratory with its location and containment level.

107.s: BSL-3 laboratories are being added mainly through which channels?
107.x: Additional BSL-3 laboratories are being established through Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories and PM-ABHIM.
107.tq: Distinguish laboratory-expansion programmes from surveillance platforms.

107.s: INSACOG was set up in which month and year?
107.x: The Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium was established in December 2020.
107.tq: Separate the consortium’s formation date from the dates of COVID legislation and testing expansion.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about INSACOG:
1. Its full form is Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium.
2. It is a network of genome-sequencing laboratories.
3. It tracks SARS-CoV-2 variants.
4. It functions under the combined institutional framework of DBT, ICMR, CSIR and MoHFW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All four statements correctly describe INSACOG, its composition and its role in tracking variants.
107.tq: Confirm the full form, network function, purpose and sponsoring institutions together.

107.s: By January 2022, COVID-19 testing in India had reached which approximate laboratory count?
107.x: By January 2022, COVID testing had expanded to 1,364 government and 1,753 private laboratories.
107.tq: Read the government-private categories in the stated order and reject the reversal.

107.s: Under PM-ABHIM, what is the prescribed scale of Integrated Public Health Laboratories (IPHLs)?
107.x: PM-ABHIM provides for 744 Integrated Public Health Laboratories, with one IPHL in every district.
107.tq: Directly recall the programme component and its numerical scale.

107.s:
With reference to the Critical Care Hospital Blocks under PM-ABHIM, consider the following statements:
1. Their prescribed number is 631.
2. They are to be established in districts having more than five lakh people.
3. They are the same as Block Public Health Units established in 11 high-focus states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: There are 631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks, intended for districts with more than five lakh people. Statement 3 is false because Block Public Health Units are a separate component with a scale of 3,389 in 11 high-focus states.
107.tq: Separate closely related programme components before selecting the coded combination.

107.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the scale of Block Public Health Units under PM-ABHIM?
o: 631 units in districts with over five lakh people
107.x: PM-ABHIM provides 3,389 Block Public Health Units in 11 high-focus states.
107.tq: Match the exact institutional component with its number and coverage area.

107.s: Which of the following pairs regarding Rural and Urban Health and Wellness Centres under PM-ABHIM is correctly matched?
107.x: The prescribed scale is 23,224 Rural Health and Wellness Centres and 13,736 Urban Health and Wellness Centres.
107.tq: Use the comparison row and watch for reversal of rural and urban figures.

107.s: Under the PM-ABHIM component relating to points of entry, preparedness is specified at:
107.x: Preparedness at 50 points of entry is included among the PM-ABHIM scales.
107.tq: Recall the small but distinct numerical figure rather than the larger programme totals.

107.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which combination correctly describes the PM-ABHIM facilities opened at Vijayawada?
o: 12 Critical Care Blocks and 10 IPHLs at a cost of Rs 744 crore
10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Block Public Health Units at a cost of Rs 631 crore
10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs at a cost of Rs 250 crore
12 Critical Care Blocks and 10 IPHLs at a cost of Rs 250 crore
107.x: At Vijayawada, 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories were opened at a cost of Rs 250 crore.
107.tq: Combine the location, facility numbers and expenditure figure without reversing paired numbers.

107.s: The International Health Regulations (2005) are best described as:
o: A domestic law enacted under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897
A voluntary agreement administered by the World Bank
A legally binding instrument of the World Health Organization
A non-binding declaration adopted by BRICS
107.x: The IHR (2005) are a legally binding instrument of the World Health Organization.
107.tq: Distinguish a legally binding international health instrument from voluntary declarations and domestic laws.

107.s: The International Health Regulations (2005) came into force in:
107.x: Although adopted as the IHR (2005), the Regulations came into force in 2007.
107.tq: Distinguish the year in the title from the year of entry into force.

107.s:
Under the IHR (2005), Member States are required to:
1. Build core capacities for surveillance and response.
