2. Report possible Public Health Emergencies of International Concern to WHO within 24 hours.
3. Designate a National IHR Focal Point.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three are obligations under the IHR (2005): building surveillance and response capacities, reporting possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours, and naming a National IHR Focal Point.
107.tq: Select the comprehensive option when all listed international obligations are supported.

107.s: A country detects an event that may constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Under the IHR (2005), the possible PHEIC should be reported to WHO within:
107.x: The IHR (2005) require Member States to report possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours.
107.tq: Apply the reporting deadline to an operational surveillance scenario.

107.s: Which of the following was added by the 2024 amendments to the IHR (2005)?
o: A higher tier called a pandemic emergency
A requirement to establish PM-ABHIM in every district
A replacement of WHO by the World Bank as the reporting authority
107.x: The 2024 amendments added a higher emergency tier termed a pandemic emergency. They did not abolish the PHEIC category or replace WHO as the relevant international health body.
107.tq: Identify the newly added tier while rejecting institutional and legal substitutions.

107.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ebola outbreak of May 2026:
1. It was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
2. It met the criteria for the higher pandemic-emergency tier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: The May 2026 Ebola outbreak was a PHEIC, but it did not meet the criteria for the higher pandemic-emergency tier.
107.tq: Separate the existing PHEIC category from the newly created higher pandemic-emergency tier.

107.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on:
107.x: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025.
107.tq: Distinguish the adoption date from dates associated with later reporting and outbreaks.

107.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the BRICS New Delhi Declaration?
o: Adoption of the WHO Pandemic Agreement
Declaration of the May 2026 Ebola outbreak as a pandemic emergency
Creation of a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases
107.x: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration set up a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases.
107.tq: Match the international forum with its specific institutional outcome.

107.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 is correct?
o: It was replaced by the 2017 draft Bill, which is already in force.
It has been criticised as colonial and for lacking a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and rights safeguards.
It applies only to non-infectious diseases.
It provides a detailed statutory definition of dangerous epidemic disease and comprehensive rights safeguards.
107.x: The 1897 Act is criticised as colonial and for lacking both a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and adequate rights safeguards.
107.tq: Find the option that accurately reflects the criticism rather than an exaggerated legal claim.

107.s:
With reference to the proposed legal framework for epidemic management, consider the following statements:
1. The 2017 draft Bill is still pending.
2. The 2017 draft Bill has already replaced the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: The 2017 draft Bill remains pending; it has not replaced the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897. Therefore, Statement 1 is correct and Statement 2 is false.
107.tq: Use the legal-status distinction between a pending draft and an enacted replacement.

107.s: Which of the following is associated with the Andhra Pradesh-specific preparedness and response measures?
o: Covid Pharma app and a zoonoses action plan in July 2026
The WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in May 2025
A new pandemic-emergency tier under the IHR amendments
The BRICS New Delhi Declaration’s infectious-disease sub-working group
107.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific measures include the Covid Pharma app and a zoonoses action plan launched in July 2026.
107.tq: Separate the State-specific initiatives from international legal and diplomatic developments.

107.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the preparedness development mentioned for Andhra Pradesh in September 2026?
107.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific current-affairs angle includes PM-ABHIM units opened in Vijayawada.
107.tq: Match the State location with the programme physically established there.

107.s: An advisory issued to States in May 2026 in the context of current infectious-disease preparedness was related to:
107.x: An Ebola advisory was issued to States in May 2026.
107.tq: Use the disease-specific cue to distinguish the advisory from other vector-borne diseases.

108.s: Which of the following most appropriately describes bioremediation?
o: Thermal destruction of contaminated soil by incineration
Removal or degradation of pollutants by organisms or their enzymes
Physical excavation and permanent burial of contaminated material
Chemical conversion of all pollutants into radioactive substances
108.x: Bioremediation uses organisms such as bacteria, fungi, algae and plants, or their enzymes, to degrade or remove pollutants and restore a contaminated environment.
108.tq: Use the exact definition and distinguish biological treatment from thermal or physical treatment.

108.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bioventing — injection of air below the water table
Biosparging — supply of air or nutrients through wells
Landfarming — treatment in a slurry bioreactor
108.x: Bioaugmentation involves adding microorganisms to enhance contaminant degradation. Bioventing supplies air or nutrients through wells, whereas biosparging injects air below the water table.
108.tq: Match each technique with its defining operation before eliminating swapped descriptions.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bioremediation techniques:
1. Bioventing supplies air or nutrients through wells.
2. Biosparging involves injection of air below the water table.
3. Landfarming is an ex-situ technique.
4. Slurry and aqueous reactors are generally the fastest and costliest bioremediation systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All four statements are correct. Bioventing and biosparging are in-situ methods, landfarming is ex-situ, and bioreactors are described as the fastest but costliest systems.
108.tq: Split the statements by category and verify the location, operation and performance of each technique.

108.s: Which of the following sets contains only ex-situ bioremediation techniques?
108.x: Landfarming, composting and biopiles require contaminated material to be treated outside its original location and are ex-situ techniques.
108.tq: Classify the techniques by whether the contaminated material remains at the site.

108.s: A contaminated site is treated without excavating the polluted material, using a passive and relatively cheaper method. This approach is known as:
108.x: In-situ bioremediation treats contamination at its original site and is generally cheaper and more passive than ex-situ treatment.
108.tq: Apply the site-treatment condition first: treatment at the original location indicates in-situ remediation.

108.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Approach)
A. Phytoremediation
B. Mycoremediation
C. Rhizoremediation
D. Bioaugmentation

List-II (Agent or basis)
1. Fungi
2. Added microorganisms
3. Plants
4. Microorganisms associated with plant roots

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: Phytoremediation uses plants, mycoremediation uses fungi, rhizoremediation uses root-zone microbes, and bioaugmentation adds microorganisms.
108.tq: Start with the sure pairs based on the prefixes phyto-, myco- and rhizo-.

108.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Water hyacinth — phytoextraction of heavy metals
Eucalyptus along sewage ponds — arsenite degradation by bacteria
Ideonella sakaiensis — removal of arsenate from groundwater
Bacillus flexus — degradation of PET plastic
108.x: Water hyacinth can be used in phytoextraction of heavy metals, while eucalyptus has been associated with sewage ponds. Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic and Bacillus flexus is associated with arsenate removal.
108.tq: Use the pollutant-agent association and reject the options that swap biological agents.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bacillus flexus is associated with the removal of arsenate.
2. Acinetobacter junii is associated with the removal of arsenite.
3. Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Bacillus flexus is associated with arsenate removal, Acinetobacter junii with arsenite removal, and Ideonella sakaiensis with PET degradation.
108.tq: Check each named microbe against its specific pollutant rather than treating all microbial remediation as interchangeable.

108.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an application of bioremediation?
o: Oil spills — bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria
Heavy metals — exclusive use of algal blooms
Sewage drains — burning of contaminated soil
108.x: Oil spills and oily sludge may be treated through bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria. The other options describe harmful processes or unsuitable treatments.
108.tq: Match the pollutant with its biological treatment route and reject reversed ecological processes.

108.s:
With reference to Indian applications of bioremediation, consider the following statements:
1. TERI has used a consortium for oil-spill treatment at Chennai port.
2. CPCB has undertaken bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils.
3. CSIR-NEERI has developed technology for heavy-metal removal from industrial effluents.
4. Legacy municipal waste can be addressed through biomining along with bioremediation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All four statements are correct. The examples include TERI's Chennai port work, CPCB treatment of oil-contaminated soils, CSIR-NEERI heavy-metal technology and biomining of legacy waste.
108.tq: Treat each institutional example as a separate statement and check the agency, pollutant and application.

108.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Arsenic contamination — exclusive treatment through PET-degrading bacteria
Legacy municipal waste — biomining plus bioremediation
Mine waste and tailings — long-term effluent-treatment monitoring
Sewage and lakes — biostimulation, aquatic plants and constructed wetlands
108.x: Arsenic contamination is associated with resistant bacteria such as Bacillus flexus and Acinetobacter junii, not PET-degrading bacteria. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
108.tq: Find the pollutant-treatment mismatch by identifying the option that uses an unrelated microbial function.

108.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes biomagnification from bioremediation?
o: Biomagnification is the rise of persistent toxins up a food chain, whereas bioremediation degrades or removes pollutants.
Bioremediation increases DDT concentration at successive trophic levels.
Biomagnification is a method of treating oil spills with bacteria.
Both terms refer to the biological removal of pollutants from soil.
108.x: Biomagnification is the increasing concentration of persistent toxins such as DDT or mercury along a food chain. Bioremediation is the biological degradation or removal of pollutants.
108.tq: Separate similar-looking biological terms by their direction of effect: pollutant increase versus pollutant removal.

108.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bioremediation is correct?
o: It can address oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and organic pollutants.
It is restricted to soil and cannot be applied to water or air.
It always requires excavation of contaminated material.
108.x: Bioremediation can be applied to soil, water and air and may address oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and other organic pollutants. It may be in-situ or ex-situ, and engineered microbes can be used.
108.tq: Test the scope of the process across media, pollutants and treatment conditions.

108.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of relative speed and cost for bioreactors as described in environmental biotechnology?
108.x: Slurry and aqueous bioreactors are described as the fastest bioremediation systems, but they are also the costliest.
108.tq: Read the paired comparison carefully; both descriptors must be retained rather than selecting only speed or cost.

108.s: Which of the following statements about genetically modified microbes and plants is correct?
o: They can be designed to reduce pollution and conserve resources.
They are restricted to medical applications.
They are used only for increasing biomagnification.
They cannot degrade oil or plastic.
108.x: Biotechnology uses genetically modified microbes and plants for pollution reduction and resource conservation, including oil degradation and plastic breakdown.
108.tq: Apply the stated role of genetic engineering to environmental problems rather than limiting it to medicine.

108.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Engineered Pseudomonas and algae — oil-spill treatment
2. PETase-producing bacteria — plastic degradation
3. PLA and PHA — bioplastics from engineered microbes
4. Biofilters — microbe-laden beds for pollutants in air and gas streams
108.x: All four pairs are correct. Engineered Pseudomonas and algae can target oil spills, PETase-producing bacteria break down plastic, engineered microbes can produce PLA and PHA, and biofilters use microbe-laden beds to treat air or gas streams.
108.tq: Verify each tool by its product or environmental application; the comprehensive option is justified when all pairs align.

108.s: Pilot plants for producing bioplastics such as PLA and PHA from engineered microbes are mentioned in:
108.x: Pilot plants for microbial production of the bioplastics PLA and PHA are mentioned in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.
108.tq: Use the location-product association and distinguish bioplastics sites from waste-to-energy locations.

108.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: 2G ethanol from crop residue — IOCL Panipat
Municipal waste to CNG — Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu pilot plants only
E20 blending target — Hyderabad and Pune waste-to-CNG plants
108.x: IOCL Panipat is associated with 2G ethanol production from crop residue. Gobar-Dhan concerns biogas, municipal waste-to-CNG is associated with Hyderabad and Pune, and Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu are linked with bioplastics pilot plants.
108.tq: Match each technology with its feedstock or location, watching for swapped examples.

108.s: The E20 blending target referred to in the context of biofuels is associated with which period?
108.x: The E20 blending target is associated with the period 2025–26.
108.tq: Check the year range precisely; nearby-year options are designed to test date retention.

108.s:
Arrange the following applications in the order in which they are associated with the relevant technologies listed:
A. Gobar-Dhan — biogas
B. PETase-producing bacteria — plastic degradation
C. IOCL Panipat — 2G ethanol from crop residue
D. Biofilters — treatment of pollutants in air and gas streams
Which of the following is the correct order from bioenergy to pollution-treatment applications?
108.x: The sequence follows the listed progression from Gobar-Dhan biogas, to 2G ethanol at IOCL Panipat, to PET degradation, and finally biofilters for air and gas streams.
108.tq: Use the functional sequence from bioenergy production to plastic and air-pollutant treatment.

108.s: The BioE3 policy was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
108.x: The BioE3 policy, meaning Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment, was approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024.
108.tq: Retain the exact approval month and year instead of relying only on the policy acronym.

108.s: Which of the following is identified as a key thematic area of the BioE3 policy?
o: Restriction of biotechnology to pharmaceutical imports
Replacement of all biological treatment by incineration
108.x: Climate-resilient agriculture is identified as a key thematic area of the BioE3 policy, whose full form is Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment.
108.tq: Link the policy acronym with its stated thematic priority rather than an unrelated sector.

108.s: India accounts for approximately what share of global vaccine demand and is described as the world's largest vaccine manufacturer?
108.x: India is identified as the largest vaccine manufacturer and meets approximately 60% of global vaccine demand.
108.tq: Use the numerical figure as the deciding clue.

108.s: Which one of the following vaccines is correctly matched with its developer and target?
o: Cervavac — Serum Institute of India — HPV/cervical cancer
108.x: Cervavac is developed by the Serum Institute of India against HPV and cervical cancer. The other pairs interchange developers or targets.
108.tq: Start from the sure developer–target pair and eliminate swapped combinations.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about vaccine platforms:
1. mRNA is an indigenous vaccine platform used in India.
2. Viral-vector vaccines are among the vaccine platforms used in India.
3. Protein-subunit vaccines are included among the indigenous platforms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: mRNA, viral-vector and protein-subunit platforms are all identified as indigenous vaccine platforms in India.
108.tq: Test each platform independently before selecting the coded combination.

108.s: ZyCoV-D, associated with Zydus Cadila, is notable as India’s first indigenous:
108.x: ZyCoV-D was developed by Zydus Cadila and is identified as the first DNA vaccine, targeting COVID-19.
108.tq: Discriminate between vaccine platform and disease target.

108.s: R21/Matrix-M is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Serum Institute of India and cervical cancer
108.x: R21/Matrix-M was developed by Oxford University and made by the Serum Institute of India for malaria.
108.tq: Separate the original developer from the manufacturing institution.

108.s: NexCAR19 was developed through the collaboration of:
o: IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial, through ImmunoACT
CMC Vellore and DBT, through Serum Institute of India
Roslin Institute and NDRI, through BIRAC
ICMR and Oxford University, through Bharat Biotech
108.x: NexCAR19 was developed by IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial through ImmunoACT.
108.tq: Use the institutional collaboration rather than the broad therapy category.

108.s: India’s first indigenous trial of gene therapy for haemophilia A was conducted at:
108.x: The first indigenous haemophilia A gene-therapy trial was conducted at CMC Vellore with support from the Department of Biotechnology.
108.tq: Identify the institution and supporting agency without swapping authorities.

108.s: The hybridoma technique used for producing monoclonal antibodies involves fusion between:
108.x: Hybridoma technology fuses antibody-producing B-cells with myeloma cells to create continuously multiplying antibody-producing cells.
108.tq: Break the technique into its two cellular components.

108.s: Kohler and Milstein are associated with the development of the hybridoma technique in:
108.x: Kohler and Milstein developed the hybridoma technique in 1975.
108.tq: Use the year–discoverer association to reject nearby dates.

108.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research — 2017
2. ART (Regulation) Act — 2021
3. Hybridoma technique — 1975
4. NexCAR19 — 1996
108.x: The Guidelines date to 2017, the ART (Regulation) Act to 2021 and the hybridoma technique to 1975. NexCAR19 dates to 2023, not 1996.
108.tq: Find the incorrect year in an otherwise familiar list.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic area of white biotechnology?
108.x: White biotechnology includes enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics, precision fermentation and green chemicals. Marine ecosystems relate to blue biotechnology rather than white biotechnology.
108.tq: Find the item belonging to a neighbouring biotechnology branch.

108.s: Which recombinant enzyme is used in cheese production?
108.x: Recombinant chymosin is used in cheese production; amylase is associated with bread and pectinase with juice processing.
108.tq: Match each enzyme with its specific industrial application.

108.s: Which one of the following enzyme–application pairs is correctly matched?
108.x: Amylase is used in bread production. Chymosin is used for cheese and pectinase for juice processing.
108.tq: Reject the swapped enzyme–application pairs.

108.s: Which of the following is included among the DBT biofuel targets?
o: Fuel from agricultural residue and municipal waste
108.x: The targets include fuels from agricultural residue and municipal waste, algal fuels, sustainable aviation fuel and integrated biorefineries.
108.tq: Prefer the option stated as a positive biotechnology application.

108.s: BioE3 Policy, approved in August 2024, primarily promotes:
108.x: BioE3 stands for Economy, Environment and Employment and promotes high-performance biomanufacturing.
108.tq: Use the policy objective rather than a neighbouring economic sector.

108.s: The three dimensions represented by ‘E3’ in BioE3 are:
108.x: The three E’s in BioE3 are Economy, Environment and Employment.
108.tq: Expand the acronym precisely; do not substitute related policy terms.

108.s: The Indian bioeconomy increased from approximately $10 billion in 2014 to what amount in 2024, with a target of $300 billion by 2030?
108.x: The bioeconomy is stated to have risen from $10 billion in 2014 to $165.7 billion in 2024, with a target of $300 billion by 2030.
108.tq: Read the middle value in a three-stage growth sequence carefully.

108.s: India is ranked at which positions in biotechnology globally and in the Asia-Pacific region, respectively?
108.x: India is ranked 12th globally and 3rd in the Asia-Pacific region in biotechnology.
108.tq: Preserve the order of the two geographical comparisons.

108.s: The Department of Biotechnology was established in 1986 after emerging from:
108.x: The DBT was established in 1986 and emerged from the National Biotechnology Board, established in 1982.
108.tq: Arrange the predecessor and successor institutions by their years.

108.s: Which of the following correctly describes Bio-RIDE?
o: A wildlife conservation programme of the Ministry of Environment
An umbrella scheme formed by merging two DBT schemes
A DNA fingerprinting repository at CCMB
A single vaccine manufacturing unit of the Serum Institute
108.x: Bio-RIDE is formed by merging two DBT umbrella schemes.
108.tq: Distinguish an umbrella scheme from an institution or facility.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of Bio-RIDE?
o: National wildlife census and habitat mapping
108.x: Bio-RIDE has three components: R&D; industrial and entrepreneurship development; and bio-manufacturing and bio-foundry. Wildlife census is not one of them.
108.tq: Identify the unrelated component among a policy’s stated pillars.

108.s: AMTZ refers to the:
o: Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone located at Visakhapatnam
Agricultural Microbial Technology Zone located at Vijayawada
Advanced Medical Training Zone located at Amaravati
Andhra Pradesh Marine Technology Zone located at Kakinada
108.x: AMTZ is the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone located at Visakhapatnam.
108.tq: Discriminate between similar expansions and locations.

108.s: Which biofertiliser is a free-living nitrogen fixer?
108.x: Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen fixer. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in legume nodules.
108.tq: Separate symbiotic and free-living nitrogen fixation.

108.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Rhizobium — Symbiotic nitrogen fixation in legume nodules
2. Azolla — Fern associated with Anabaena and used in paddy
3. Blue-green algae — Anabaena and Nostoc, associated with paddy
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
108.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Rhizobium functions in legume nodules, while Azolla and blue-green algae are associated with nitrogen enrichment in paddy systems.
108.tq: Verify each organism–role pair before choosing the combined code.

108.s: Which of the following is NOT a biopesticide listed among the agricultural biotechnology applications?
108.x: Bacillus thuringiensis, Trichoderma and NPV are listed as biopesticides. Azotobacter is a biofertiliser and nitrogen fixer.
108.tq: Distinguish biopesticides from biofertilisers.

108.s: Tissue-culture applications involving banana and pineapple are associated with:
108.x: BARC is associated with tissue-culture applications for banana and pineapple.
108.tq: Match the institution with the crop application.

108.s: Marker-assisted selection is exemplified by the development of:
108.x: Sub1 flood-tolerant rice is given as an example of marker-assisted selection.
108.tq: Link the breeding method to its crop example.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of cloned-animal facts?
108.x: Dolly was the first cloned mammal, a sheep produced at Roslin Institute in 1996; Garima was a buffalo cloned at NDRI in 2009; and Noori was a Pashmina goat cloned in 2012.
108.tq: Use both the animal identity and the chronological order to eliminate swaps.

108.s: Ganga, the first cloned Gir calf, was born in:
108.x: Ganga is identified as the first cloned Gir calf and was born in 2023.
108.tq: Distinguish the recent cloning milestone from earlier animal-cloning dates.

108.s: Noori, cloned at SKUAST-Kashmir, is a:
108.x: Noori is a Pashmina goat cloned at SKUAST-Kashmir in 2012.
108.tq: Match the animal name with the species and institution.

108.s: The Genome India Project aims to sequence approximately:
108.x: The Genome India Project aims to cover 10,000 genomes.
108.tq: Select the exact scale of the national genomics project.

108.s: The Indian Biological Data Centre is a national repository for:
108.x: IBDC serves as the national repository for publicly funded life-science data.
108.tq: Identify the repository’s data scope, not merely its location.

108.s: The Indian Biological Data Centre is located at:
108.x: IBDC is located at the Regional Centre for Biotechnology, Faridabad.
108.tq: Match the data centre with its host institution and location.

108.s: DNA fingerprinting primarily uses which type of DNA variation?
108.x: DNA fingerprinting uses variations in repetitive DNA, particularly variable number tandem repeats (VNTRs).
108.tq: Distinguish the genetic marker from the laboratory enzyme used in DNA work.

108.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kohler and Milstein — DNA fingerprinting in 1984
108.x: Alec Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting in 1984. In India, Lalji Singh is associated with DNA fingerprinting research at CCMB.
108.tq: Use the discoverer–year pair and reject swapped achievements.

108.s: India’s first zoo bio-bank was established at:
o: Nehru Zoological Park, Hyderabad, with BARC
Indira Gandhi Zoological Park, Visakhapatnam, with RCB
Padmaja Naidu Zoo, Darjeeling, with CSIR-CCMB
Central Zoo, New Delhi, with NDRI
108.x: India’s first zoo bio-bank is at Padmaja Naidu Zoo, Darjeeling, in collaboration with CSIR-CCMB.
108.tq: Match the facility with its location and collaborating institution.

108.s: The storage temperature specified for India’s first zoo bio-bank is:
108.x: The zoo bio-bank at Padmaja Naidu Zoo stores material at −196°C.
108.tq: Distinguish cryogenic storage from ordinary freezing temperatures.

108.s: According to the CBD definition cited for biotechnology, biotechnology involves the use of biological systems to:
o: Classify organisms only by external appearance
Replace every chemical process with a mechanical process
108.x: The CBD 1992 definition describes biotechnology as using biological systems to make or modify products.
108.tq: Select the precise wording of the definition rather than an extreme interpretation.

108.s: Which one of the following branches is correctly matched with its broad field?
108.x: Red biotechnology concerns medicine, green agriculture, white industry and blue marine applications.
108.tq: Match colour coding with the sector it represents.

108.s:
Arrange the major stages of PCR in the correct order: 
A. Extension
B. Denaturation
C. Annealing
D. Polymerase-mediated synthesis of the complementary strand
108.x: PCR proceeds through denaturation, annealing and extension; extension involves polymerase-mediated synthesis of the complementary strand.
108.tq: Remember the standard first–second–third PCR cycle sequence.

108.s: Which enzyme is essential for amplification of DNA during PCR?
108.x: DNA polymerase synthesises new DNA strands during PCR. Ligase joins DNA fragments but is not the principal amplification enzyme.
108.tq: Separate the enzyme that amplifies DNA from the enzyme that joins fragments.

108.s: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments primarily on the basis of their:
108.x: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to size.
108.tq: Identify the physical property used in the separation method.

108.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly describes tools used in recombinant DNA technology?
o: Restriction enzymes cut DNA, ligase joins DNA, and plasmids can act as vectors
Restriction enzymes join DNA, ligase replicates cells, and plasmids destroy vectors
Restriction enzymes produce antibodies, ligase ferments sugar, and plasmids are enzymes
Restriction enzymes separate proteins, ligase fixes nitrogen, and plasmids are vaccines
108.x: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites, ligase joins DNA fragments, and plasmids can function as vectors.
108.tq: Assign each tool its core function and reject reversed roles.

108.s: Which of the following is an IN-SITU technique for treating contaminated material?
108.x: Bioventing is an in-situ technique. Landfarming, composting after removal and slurry bioreactors are ex-situ approaches.
108.tq: Use the treatment location as the first filter.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding in-situ and ex-situ treatment:
1. In-situ treatment is carried out at the contaminated site.
2. Ex-situ treatment involves excavation or removal for treatment in beds or reactors.
3. Bioventing and biosparging are in-situ techniques.
4. Landfarming, composting and biopiles are ex-situ techniques.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All four statements correctly describe the site and techniques of in-situ and ex-situ treatment.
108.tq: Classify each technique by whether material remains at the site or is removed.

108.s: Which statement best describes the cost comparison between in-situ and ex-situ bioremediation?
o: In-situ treatment is generally the most cost-efficient; ex-situ bioreactors have high capital and operating costs.
Ex-situ bioreactors require no operating expenditure.
In-situ treatment always has higher capital costs than all ex-situ methods.
All ex-situ techniques are more expensive than every in-situ technique.
108.x: In-situ treatment is generally the most cost-efficient. Landfarming and biopiles may be low-cost ex-situ methods, while bioreactors involve high capital and operating costs.
108.tq: Watch for the trap created by the word ‘all’ in cost comparisons.

108.s: Which one of the following is a limitation of in-situ bioremediation?
o: High capital cost of every treatment operation
Environmental constraints and long treatment time
108.x: In-situ treatment may face environmental constraints, require a long treatment time and be complicated by metals or inorganic contaminants.
108.tq: Identify the limitation that belongs to the treatment method rather than its alternative.

108.s: Which of the following is associated with ex-situ treatment limitations?
o: No need to handle contaminated material
Treatment always being slower than in-situ treatment
Need for space, excavation and possible mass-transfer problems
108.x: Ex-situ treatment can require excavation and space and may face abiotic losses, mass-transfer limitations and poor bioavailability.
108.tq: Match the operational limitation with the method requiring removal of material.

108.s: Under optimised conditions, which ex-situ method can provide the fastest treatment because of rapid kinetics?
108.x: Ex-situ bioreactors can be the fastest option under optimised conditions because they permit rapid kinetics.
108.tq: Compare speed only after identifying the controlled treatment environment.

108.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Technique)
a. Mycoremediation
b. Rhizofiltration
c. Biosparging
d. Rhizoremediation

List-II (Typical application)
i. Absorption or precipitation of contaminants from water by plant roots
ii. Injection of air under pressure below the water table
 iii. Use of fungi for treating organic pollutants
iv. Stimulation of microbes in the rhizosphere by plant roots

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: Mycoremediation uses fungi, rhizofiltration uses plant roots to remove contaminants from water, biosparging injects air below the water table, and rhizoremediation involves root–microbe interactions in the rhizosphere.
108.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing an incorrect technique–application match.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bioaugmentation and biostimulation:
1. Bioaugmentation introduces specific pollutant-degrading microbes into a contaminated site.
2. Biostimulation enhances the activity of existing microbes by supplying nutrients and oxygen.
3. Oilzapper is an example associated with bioaugmentation, whereas addition of nitrogen and phosphorus to polluted lakes is associated with biostimulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All three statements are correct. Bioaugmentation adds pollutant-degrading microbial consortia, while biostimulation supports native microbes through nutrient and oxygen addition.
108.tq: Use the meaning–example distinction to separate bioaugmentation from biostimulation.

108.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Technique — Typical target
o: Biosparging — Contaminated soil through nutrient-supplying wells
Bioventing — Groundwater below the water table
Biostimulation — Polluted water bodies and soil
Rhizofiltration — Volatilisation of contaminants into the atmosphere
108.x: Biostimulation is used in polluted water bodies and soil by adding nutrients and oxygen. Bioventing supplies nutrients through wells to contaminated soil, whereas biosparging injects air below the water table.
108.tq: Check whether the medium named in each option matches the defining operation of the technique.

108.s:
With reference to Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S, consider the following statements:
1. They are bacterial consortia developed by TERI.
2. Their development involved collaboration with Indian Oil.
3. They are used for degrading oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites.
4. They leave no harmful residue after degradation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S are bacterial consortia developed by TERI with Indian Oil. They degrade oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites without leaving harmful residue.
108.tq: Test the complete profile of a named technology rather than relying only on its headline application.

108.s: Oilzapper has also been used at which of the following places?
108.x: Oilzapper has been used at Chennai Port for remediation of oil-contaminated material.
108.tq: Use the location-specific application as the distinguishing clue.

108.s: The first genetically engineered oil-eating bacterium, popularly described as a ‘superbug’, was based on:
o: Bacillus subtilis engineered by Norman Borlaug
Escherichia coli engineered by Ian Wilmut
Pseudomonas putida engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty
Rhizobium leguminosarum engineered by Hargobind Khorana
108.x: The first genetically engineered oil-eating bacterium was Pseudomonas putida engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty.
108.tq: Match the organism with the scientist responsible for its engineering.

108.s: The legal significance associated with Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty’s genetically engineered bacterium is that it was involved in:
o: The first patent for a human gene, affirmed by the International Court of Justice in 1990
The first patent granted for a living organism, affirmed in Diamond v. Chakrabarty in 1980
The first international treaty on genetically modified crops, adopted in 1980
The first patent for a cloned mammal, granted in 1980 by the World Health Organization
108.x: The case Diamond v. Chakrabarty, decided by the US Supreme Court in 1980, is associated with the first patenting of a living organism.
108.tq: Identify the legal event by linking the case name, year and subject matter.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of bioremediation?
o: It is usually cheaper than conventional clean-up methods
It invariably produces rapid results irrespective of pollutant and site conditions
In-situ treatment can cause little disruption at the contaminated site
It generally uses fewer chemicals and may avoid secondary pollution
108.x: Bioremediation is often slow, and its results vary with the pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants. The other three are recognised advantages.
108.tq: Identify the absolute claim that conflicts with the variable performance of biological treatment.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about the limitations of bioremediation:
1. Its effectiveness may vary with the pollutant, organism and site conditions.
2. Metals and other inorganic contaminants can complicate treatment.
3. Ex-situ methods may require excavation and additional space.
4. Regulation and monitoring may be unnecessary once microbes are introduced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Bioremediation may require regulation and monitoring; introducing microbes does not make oversight unnecessary.
108.tq: Find the single overgeneralised statement among otherwise precise limitations.

108.s:
Match the phytoremediation sub-type with its principal process:

List-I (Sub-type)
a. Phytoextraction
b. Phytostabilisation
c. Phytodegradation
d. Phytovolatilisation

List-II (Process)
i. Plant enzymes break down organic pollutants
ii. Contaminants are taken up and released into the air in volatile form
iii. Contaminants are stored in roots and shoots and the plant is harvested
iv. Roots immobilise contaminants and reduce leaching and erosion

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: Phytoextraction involves uptake and harvesting, phytostabilisation immobilises contaminants, phytodegradation uses plant enzymes, and phytovolatilisation releases contaminants in volatile form.
108.tq: Break each technical term into its process meaning and then verify the full code.

108.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Phytovolatilisation — Uptake and release of mercury or selenium in volatile form
Phytostabilisation — Plant enzymes degrade organic contaminants
Phytodegradation — Roots immobilise metals in mine spoils
Phytoextraction — Injection of air below the water table
108.x: Phytovolatilisation involves plant uptake followed by release into the air in volatile form; mercury and selenium are examples associated with this process.
108.tq: Distinguish the phytoremediation sub-types by the fate of the contaminant after plant uptake.

108.s: Which of the following statements regarding natural phytoremediators is correct?
o: Eucalyptus removes surplus wastewater mainly by injecting oxygen into groundwater.
Mangroves are used exclusively for thermal treatment of contaminated soil.
Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation can act as natural phytoremediators, while Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater.
Only desert shrubs can act as natural phytoremediators because wetland plants cannot absorb contaminants.
108.x: Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation are natural phytoremediators. Eucalyptus planted along sewage ponds can transpire surplus wastewater.
108.tq: Combine the habitat clue with the plant process instead of confusing phytoremediation with air injection or thermal treatment.

108.s:
Match the plant with the principal metal or contaminant associated with its hyperaccumulation:

List-I (Plant)
a. Pteris vittata
b. Brassica juncea
c. Thlaspi (Noccaea) caerulescens
d. Alyssum species

List-II (Metal)
i. Nickel
ii. Arsenic
iii. Zinc and cadmium
iv. Lead, cadmium and selenium

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: Pteris vittata accumulates arsenic; Brassica juncea accumulates lead, cadmium and selenium; Thlaspi caerulescens accumulates zinc and cadmium; and Alyssum species accumulate nickel.
108.tq: Begin with the distinctive arsenic–fern pair and use elimination for the remaining metals.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about plants used in phytoremediation:
1. Sunflower can accumulate heavy metals, uranium and other radionuclides.
2. Water hyacinth can take up heavy metals and toxic materials from water.
3. Indian mustard is associated with the accumulation of lead, cadmium and selenium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All three statements are correct. Sunflower, water hyacinth and Indian mustard are associated with the listed contaminant-accumulation roles.
108.tq: Check each plant–contaminant association independently before selecting the coded combination.

108.s: Which one of the following sets contains only biological clean-up methods?
o: Microbial degradation, composting organic waste and constructed wetlands
Thermal treatment, phytoremediation and chemical treatment
Chemical dust suppression, desalination and burning contaminated soil
108.x: Microbial degradation, composting and constructed wetlands are biological methods. Incineration, burning, chemical treatment, desalination and excavation are non-biological methods.
108.tq: Classify every item by method type before choosing the all-biological set.

108.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?

Method — Classification
o: Chemical dust suppressants such as calcium chloride — Chemical
108.x: Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride used as chemical dust suppressants represent chemical treatment. Burning is thermal, while desalination and excavation with landfilling are physical methods.
108.tq: Use the method of operation to reject the swapped biological, thermal, chemical and physical classifications.

108.s: A municipal authority uses bacteria to break down organic waste. This activity is best classified as:
108.x: The biological breakdown of organic waste by bacteria is microbial degradation and therefore constitutes bioremediation.
108.tq: Identify the biological agent and process before distinguishing it from physical or thermal treatment.

108.s:
Match the Indian institution with the associated bioremediation product or role:

List-I (Institution)
a. TERI
b. CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur
c. CPCB
d. DBT-BIRAC

List-II (Product or role)
i. Funding biotechnology start-ups developing microbial kits for sewage plants and landfills
ii. Bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils
iii. Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S
aiv. Nodal bioremediation research and development, including heavy-metal removal from effluents

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: TERI is associated with Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S; CSIR-NEERI undertakes nodal bioremediation R&D; CPCB is associated with oil-contaminated soils; and DBT-BIRAC funds relevant biotechnology start-ups.
108.tq: Start with the distinctive TERI–Oilzapper pair and then match the institutional roles.

108.s: A contaminated lake contains native microbes capable of degradation, but their activity is limited by nutrient deficiency. Which intervention is most appropriate?
o: Add nitrogen and phosphorus to stimulate the native microbes
Harvest plant shoots without addressing microbial activity
Burn the contaminated soil surrounding the lake
Inject air below the water table without adding nutrients
108.x: Biostimulation adds nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, and may also supply oxygen, to enhance the activity of existing microbes in polluted water bodies.
108.tq: Ask whether the intervention adds new microbes or improves the performance of microbes already present.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly describes rhizofiltration?
o: Fungi degrade organic pollutants in soil
Plant roots absorb or precipitate contaminants from water
Air is injected under pressure below the water table
Plant enzymes convert all metals into volatile gases
108.x: Rhizofiltration uses plant roots to absorb or precipitate contaminants from water, particularly metals and radionuclides.
108.tq: Use the root-based prefix to distinguish filtration by roots from microbial, air-injection and enzyme-based processes.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly describes rhizoremediation?
o: Contaminated soil is excavated and sent to a landfill
Plant roots stimulate microbes in the rhizosphere to address organic pollutants or nutrient imbalance in soil
Contaminants are released into the atmosphere in volatile form by air injection
Plant shoots are harvested after storing contaminants in their tissues
108.x: Rhizoremediation depends on plant roots stimulating microbial activity in the rhizosphere and is associated with organic pollutants and nutrient imbalance in soil.
108.tq: Distinguish root-zone microbial stimulation from plant harvesting, volatilisation and physical disposal.

108.s: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is associated with which of the following?
o: Ministry of Jal Shakti under Namami Gange
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under AMRUT 2.0
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under SBM-U 2.0
108.x: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is an initiative of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.
108.tq: Use the ministry-and-scheme association to eliminate swapped-authority options.

108.s: What is the stated target of the Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator?
108.x: The target of the accelerator is described as “Lakshya Zero Dumpsites”, focusing on clearing legacy dumpsites through accelerated bioremediation.
108.tq: Test the exact official slogan rather than a broad descriptive substitute.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SWM Rules 2026:
1. Annual auditing of landfills is mandatory.
2. All legacy dumpsites are to be mapped with biomining and bioremediation.
3. Landfills are intended for recyclable waste and energy-recoverable waste.
4. Environmental Compensation follows the ‘polluter pays’ principle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because landfills are intended only for non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste.
108.tq: Find the reversed classification in the statement about what belongs in landfills.

108.s: Landfills under the SWM Rules 2026 are meant for which category of waste?
108.x: The specified landfill category consists of non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste.
108.tq: Use precise category boundaries to distinguish disposal waste from recoverable waste.

108.s: Approximately what proportion of waste is collected and processed, respectively, in the context of the legacy dumpsite problem?
108.x: The reported figures are approximately 60–70% collection and 15–20% processing.
108.tq: Keep paired percentages in their stated order and reject the reversed pair.

108.s: What proportion of the waste is described as biodegradable?
108.x: Approximately 55–60% of the waste is biodegradable.
108.tq: Match the numerical range to the waste characteristic rather than to collection or processing.

108.s: Constructed wetlands are best described as systems in which:
o: Excavation removes contaminated soil for off-site disposal
Thermal treatment incinerates all sewage solids
Only chemical agents remove pollutants from groundwater
Plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants
108.x: Constructed wetlands may be natural or engineered systems where plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants, especially in sewage treatment.
108.tq: Identify the biological mechanism from the functions performed by plants and microbes.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Phytorid technology?
o: A chemical oxidation process developed by the US EPA
A constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI
A thermal sewage-treatment system developed under SBM-U
An excavation-based technology developed by AMTZ
108.x: Phytorid is a constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI.
108.tq: Link the technology with its developer and treatment category, avoiding swapped institutions.

108.s: In Phytorid technology, wastewater passes through:
108.x: Phytorid treats wastewater as it passes through a planted gravel bed.
108.tq: Test the distinctive operational feature of the technology.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Visakhapatnam sewage-discharge issue:
1. The matter involved a Public Interest Litigation before the Andhra Pradesh High Court.
2. The stormwater drain passes through MVP Colony and Lawson’s Bay Colony.
3. The drain enters the sea at Pedda Jalaripeta.
4. The proposal favoured only large-scale pumping schemes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because immediate bioremediation and decentralised STPs were proposed as a lower-cost alternative to pumping schemes.
108.tq: Locate the single reversed policy claim among otherwise factual statements.

108.s: Who proposed immediate bioremediation along with decentralised sewage-treatment plants in the Visakhapatnam matter?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board
108.x: Petitioner Bollisetty Satyanarayana proposed immediate bioremediation together with decentralised STPs.
108.tq: Use the person-and-action association rather than confusing the petitioner with an implementing agency.

108.s: Which pair of aquatic plants is used for phytoremediation of ponds?
108.x: Water hyacinth and duckweed are used for phytoremediation of ponds.
108.tq: Start from the sure plant pair and reject substitutions from other ecological contexts.

108.s: Which one of the following comparisons between bioremediation and conventional remediation is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bioremediation — large infrastructure as its defining scale
108.x: Bioremediation is described as scalable and community-applied, whereas conventional remediation is associated with large infrastructure.
108.tq: Find the comparison row that has been reversed rather than choosing the generally familiar feature.

108.s:
With reference to bioremediation and conventional remediation, consider the following statements:
1. Bioremediation is generally slower than conventional remediation.
2. Bioremediation can be scalable and community-applied.
3. Conventional remediation is generally less dependent on site biology.
4. Bioremediation always has uniform reliability irrespective of pollutant, organism and site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the reliability of bioremediation varies with the pollutant, organism, site and co-contaminants.
108.tq: Treat the absolute word ‘always’ as a warning and verify the stated limitations.

108.s: Which of the following is an advantage of bioremediation over conventional thermal, chemical or excavation-based remediation?
o: It necessarily works faster at every site
It uses minimal chemicals and avoids secondary pollution
It is independent of the pollutant and site conditions
108.x: Bioremediation uses minimal chemicals and is associated with no secondary pollution in the comparison. Its speed and reliability are not uniform at every site.
108.tq: Select the carefully worded benefit while rejecting absolute claims about speed and reliability.

108.s: Which factor can cause the reliability of bioremediation to vary?
o: Only the size of the municipality
The colour of the treatment plant
Only the availability of excavation machinery
108.x: Bioremediation reliability varies with the pollutant, the organism used, site conditions and co-contaminants.
108.tq: Apply the limitation list to a practical site-assessment scenario.

108.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Synthetic biology — current relevance in bioremediation discussions
2. Precision biotherapeutics — BioE3
3. Marine biomaterials research facility — Visakhapatnam
4. AMTZ — Vizag
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: All four associations are correct: synthetic biology is a current relevance area, precision biotherapeutics are linked with BioE3, Visakhapatnam was chosen for a marine biomaterials research facility, and AMTZ is associated with Vizag.
108.tq: Verify each association separately before selecting the all-inclusive code.

108.s: Which of the following is proposed as part of the national approach to bioremediation in India?
o: Replacement of all biological methods by excavation
Exclusive funding through the US EPA
A ban on all community-based treatment
108.x: The proposed approach includes national microbe-approval protocols under MoEFCC, State bioremediation hubs and DBT-BIRAC startup funding.
108.tq: Identify the responsible domestic authority in a policy proposal.

108.s: State bioremediation hubs and startup funding by DBT-BIRAC are proposed primarily to:
o: Support a scalable national bioremediation approach
Promote only thermal treatment of waste
108.x: State bioremediation hubs and DBT-BIRAC startup funding are proposed to strengthen and scale bioremediation in India.
108.tq: Connect institutional measures with their stated policy objective.

108.s: The US EPA Superfund bioremediation guidelines are cited as a model in relation to:
108.x: The US EPA Superfund bioremediation guidelines are cited as a comparative model for India’s bioremediation approach.
108.tq: Use the programme-name association to distinguish an environmental model from biotechnology initiatives.

108.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
108.x: Lakshya Zero Dumpsites is associated with India’s SBM-U 2.0 context, not the United States. China, the European Union and Kenya are matched with soil-remediation clusters, the Horizon fund and community phytoremediation respectively.
108.tq: Detect the country-and-initiative swap in a comparative international list.

108.s: Which organisation is identified as the nodal research and development body for bioremediation in India?
108.x: CSIR-NEERI is identified as the nodal R&D body for bioremediation in India. TERI and CPCB are associated with particular applications, while IOCL is linked with biofuel initiatives.
108.tq: Use the institutional-role distinction: nodal R&D body is different from an implementing or industrial organisation.

109.s: The primary goal of sustainable agriculture is to:
o: Replace all farm labour with mechanisation
Maximise yields through continuous use of chemical inputs
Produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations
109.x: Sustainable agriculture seeks to produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations.
109.tq: Identify the definition that combines production, environmental protection and intergenerational resource conservation.

109.s:
Consider the following practices:
1. Crop rotation
2. Organic farming
3. Mixed or inter-cropping
4. Green manuring
5. Cover crops
6. Reduced tillage
7. Drip irrigation
8. Integrated pest management
Which of the above are sustainable agricultural practices?
109.x: All eight listed practices are identified as sustainable agricultural practices.
109.tq: Use the inclusive option after verifying each practice against the sustainable-practice list.

109.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally regarded as a harmful agricultural practice?
109.x: Integrated pest management is a sustainable practice. Excessive chemical fertiliser use, pesticide overuse and monoculture are listed as harmful practices.
109.tq: Find the one sustainable practice hidden among harmful practices.

109.s:
With reference to sustainable agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. It may use synthetic inputs judiciously.
2. Integrated pest management and precision farming can be part of sustainable agriculture.
3. Sustainable agriculture is identical to organic farming because neither permits synthetic inputs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously, unlike the stricter approach generally associated with organic farming; statement 3 is false.
109.tq: Separate the broader concept of sustainable agriculture from the more restrictive organic-farming approach.

109.s: The shift from the Green Revolution towards the ‘evergreen revolution’ is associated with which combination?
o: ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management
Only genetically modified crops and mechanised harvesting
Monoculture, over-irrigation, pesticide intensification and soil mining
Expansion of chemical fertilisers without resource conservation
109.x: The evergreen revolution approach is associated with ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management.
109.tq: Match the newer sustainability-oriented approach with its defining practices.

109.s: Which organic amendment consists of organic waste digested by earthworms and is associated with restoration of soil microbes and organic carbon?
109.x: Vermicompost is produced by the digestion of organic waste by earthworms and helps restore soil microbes and organic carbon.
109.tq: Distinguish amendments by their production process and principal soil benefit.

109.s: Farmyard manure is primarily composed of:
o: Leguminous crops ploughed into the soil while green
Dung, urine and litter of farm animals
109.x: Farmyard manure consists of the dung, urine and litter of farm animals.
109.tq: Use composition-based discrimination among similar organic amendments.

109.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Farmyard manure — slow-release nutrients and better soil structure
Biochar — immediate nitrogen fixation in legume nodules
Green manure — long-term carbon sequestration through pyrolysis
Compost — association of fungi with plant roots
109.x: Farmyard manure supplies slow-release nutrients and improves soil structure. Biochar, green manure and compost have different compositions and functions.
109.tq: Start with the sure composition-benefit pair and reject swapped functions.

109.s: Green manure is best described as:
o: Charcoal obtained by pyrolysis of biomass
Leguminous crops ploughed into the soil while green, adding nitrogen and organic matter
Animal dung and urine stored after complete drying
Organic waste digested only by aquatic ferns
109.x: Green manure consists of leguminous crops such as sunn hemp and dhaincha that are ploughed into the soil while green, adding nitrogen and organic matter.
109.tq: Identify the practice from its defining action and nutrient contribution.

109.s: Which of the following correctly describes biochar?
o: It is a charcoal-like material produced by pyrolysis of biomass and can aid long-term carbon sequestration, water retention and nutrient retention.
It is decomposed animal litter used only as a pesticide.
It is a bacterial culture that fixes nitrogen in cereal root nodules.
It is a legume ploughed into the field before flowering.
109.x: Biochar is charcoal produced through pyrolysis of biomass. Its stated benefits include long-term carbon sequestration and improved water and nutrient retention.
109.tq: Break the term into its production process and environmental functions.

109.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh plan mentioned for waste-processing centres, the planned manure production is:
o: 1,500 MT per day from 107 waste-processing centres
109.x: The plan provides for 1,500 MT of manure per day from 107 waste-processing centres.
109.tq: Read the unit and the associated number together; the daily figure is the key discriminator.

109.s: Under the AP Kharif 2026 green-manure programme, which combination is correct?
o: Subsidy of Rs 26.20 crore and 91,918 quintals of seed
Subsidy of Rs 92.20 crore and 61,918 quintals of seed
Subsidy of Rs 62.20 crore and 91,918 quintals of seed
Subsidy of Rs 62.20 crore and 19,918 quintals of seed
109.x: The programme provides a subsidy of Rs 62.20 crore and 91,918 quintals of green-manure seed.
109.tq: Pair the two numerical figures rather than treating the subsidy and seed quantity independently.

109.s: In the AP Kharif 2026 green-manure seed distribution, which crop-wise allocation is correctly stated?
o: Sunn hemp 20,316 quintals, dhaincha 21,291 quintals and green gram 50,311 quintals
Sunn hemp 21,291 quintals, dhaincha 50,311 quintals and green gram 20,316 quintals
Sunn hemp 50,311 quintals, dhaincha 20,316 quintals and green gram 21,291 quintals
Sunn hemp 50,311 quintals, dhaincha 21,291 quintals and green gram 20,316 quintals
109.x: The allocation is sunn hemp (Jilledu) 50,311 quintals, dhaincha (Janumu) 21,291 quintals and green gram 20,316 quintals.
109.tq: Check each crop-number pairing, since the distractors reverse otherwise familiar figures.

109.s:
Indiscriminate use of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides may result in:
1. Secondary pest outbreaks
2. Pesticide resistance
3. Ecosystem contamination
4. Soil and water contamination
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Indiscriminate agrochemical use can cause secondary pest outbreaks, pesticide resistance, ecosystem contamination and contamination of soil and water.
109.tq: Select the comprehensive environmental-impact option after checking each consequence.

109.s: Broadcasting granular fertiliser can result in the loss of approximately what proportion of applied nitrogen as ammonia or nitrate leaching into aquifers?
109.x: Broadcasting granular fertiliser may lose 50–70 percent of the applied nitrogen through ammonia loss or nitrate leaching into aquifers.
109.tq: Distinguish the stated range from lower and exaggerated percentage traps.

109.s: The phenomenon in which pesticide residues become concentrated through successive levels of a food chain is called:
109.x: Pesticide residues can bioaccumulate in the food chain, leading to increasing concentration across feeding levels.
109.tq: Discriminate between environmental fate terms by focusing on concentration through the food chain.

109.s: Carbosulfan was proposed for banning because it:
o: Fixes nitrogen but causes nitrate leaching
Improves soil microbial activity but reduces crop yield
Breaks down to highly toxic carbofuran and harms birds and aquatic life
Is a natural pesticide that attracts secondary pests
109.x: Carbosulfan breaks down into highly toxic carbofuran and is harmful to birds and aquatic life. The proposed ban was recommended by the Registration Committee under the Insecticides Act, 1968.
109.tq: Link the pesticide with its breakdown product and ecological harm.

109.s: Which State banned the sale of glyphosate in 2018?
109.x: Punjab banned the sale of glyphosate in 2018.
109.tq: Use the location-year pair and avoid substituting another agricultural State.

109.s: Under PM-PRANAM, States may retain what share of the fertiliser subsidy saved by reducing fertiliser use, in the form of grants?
109.x: PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50 percent of the saved fertiliser subsidy as grants.
109.tq: Recall the exact percentage associated with the incentive mechanism.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF):
1. It was formerly known as Zero Budget Natural Farming.
2. Jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham are associated bio-inputs.
3. It covers more than seven lakh farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct: APCNF was formerly ZBNF, uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham, and covers over seven lakh farmers.
109.tq: Use the all-inclusive code only after verifying the programme’s name, inputs and coverage.

109.s: AP Community-managed Natural Farming received global recognition through the:
o: UNEP Champions of the Earth Award, 2024
109.x: APCNF received the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024.
109.tq: Discriminate among similarly prestigious awards using the exact award-name and year pair.

109.s: A Kenyan delegation praised APCNF as a climate-resilient model after visiting farms in which district?
109.x: The Kenyan delegation visited farms in Guntur district and praised APCNF as a climate-resilient model.
109.tq: Match the international delegation’s observation with the correct district.

109.s: The crop-diversified plots visited by the Kenyan delegation included which of the following as trap crops?
109.x: The visited farms included crop-diversified plots using marigold and castor as trap crops.
109.tq: Identify the specific trap-crop pair rather than the general crop-diversification idea.

109.s: Which statement correctly describes the State-level initiatives associated with natural farming in Andhra Pradesh?
o: NTR district was declared a monoculture model without produce traceability.
Guntur district was made a chemical-intensive model with QR-based pesticide tracking.
NTR district was promoted as a natural-farming model with QR-based traceability for organic produce.
Natural farming was restricted to farms using only synthetic fertilisers.
109.x: NTR district was promoted as a natural-farming model with QR-based traceability for organic produce.
109.tq: Apply the policy feature to the correct district and distinguish traceability from chemical-input monitoring.

109.s: Which one of the following biopesticides is correctly matched with its principal target?
109.x: NPV is a baculovirus-based biopesticide effective against Helicoverpa and Spodoptera caterpillars. Trichoderma targets soil-borne fungal diseases, neem has a wide insect range, and Beauveria bassiana attacks several insects.
109.tq: Use the source–target association and reject reversed biological targets.

109.s: Trichoderma is primarily used in biological pest management against which of the following?
o: Soil-borne fungal diseases such as wilt and root rot
109.x: Trichoderma is an antagonistic fungus used against soil-borne fungal diseases, particularly wilt and root rot.
109.tq: Identify the organism by its characteristic target rather than by its general category.

109.s: Azadirachtin, used as a biopesticide, is obtained from which source?
109.x: Azadirachtin is derived from neem and acts against a wide range of insects, chiefly as an antifeedant.
109.tq: Test the exact source–compound pairing.

109.s: Beauveria bassiana is best described as a:
o: Entomopathogenic fungus used against borers and whitefly
Plant extract used as an antifeedant
109.x: Beauveria bassiana is an entomopathogenic fungus effective against borers, whitefly and other insects.
109.tq: Distinguish closely related biopesticides by source and target.

109.s:
Which of the following characteristics make biopesticides an important component of Integrated Pest Management?
1. Biodegradability
2. Low toxicity
3. Short persistence
4. Permanent elimination of all pests
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Biopesticides are biodegradable, comparatively low in toxicity and short-lived in the environment. They are not intended to permanently eliminate all pests.
109.tq: Find the extreme and absolute statement among otherwise valid environmental characteristics.

109.s: The primary objective of Integrated Pest Management, as defined by the FAO, is to:
o: Replace all biological methods with resistant varieties
Maximise pest mortality through continuous chemical spraying
Keep pests below economic injury levels by optimising the use of suitable methods
Eliminate every pest from the agricultural ecosystem
109.x: IPM uses all suitable methods to keep pest populations below economic injury levels. Its aim is to optimise control, not maximise it.
109.tq: Distinguish the stated management objective from the extreme goal of total eradication.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding components of Integrated Pest Management:
1. Resistant varieties form one component of IPM.
2. Crop rotation and changes in irrigation are cultural methods.
3. Traps and mulches are mechanical or physical methods.
4. Chemical control is used only when needed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All four statements describe recognised IPM components: resistant varieties, cultural practices, mechanical or physical methods, and need-based chemical control.
109.tq: Check whether all listed methods fit the integrated, need-based character of IPM.

109.s: Which one of the following is an example of a biological component of Integrated Pest Management?
o: Use of a resistant seed variety only
Use of green lacewings against aphids
109.x: Green lacewings act as natural enemies of aphids and therefore represent a biological IPM method. Pheromone traps are also included among the listed IPM tools.
109.tq: Separate biological control from cultural and physical control methods.

109.s: Which State was recognised as India’s first fully organic State in 2016?
109.x: Sikkim became India’s first fully organic State in 2016.
109.tq: Recall the first-in-category fact together with its associated year.

109.s: The Prime Minister cited the model of which State during its 50th Statehood celebrations in the context of organic farming?
109.x: The model of Sikkim was cited during its 50th Statehood celebrations because of its status as India’s first fully organic State.
109.tq: Link the milestone State with the associated public-policy reference.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY):
1. It was launched in 2015–16.
2. It was the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming.
3. It follows a cluster-based approach.
4. A standard cluster consists of 50 farmers covering 50 acres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: PKVY was launched in 2015–16 as the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming. Its cluster approach specifies 50 farmers and 50 acres per cluster.
109.tq: Test the scheme through launch year, institutional character and cluster design.

109.s: Which one of the following schemes is specifically associated with the development of organic value chains in the North-Eastern States?
109.x: MOVCDNER promotes organic value chains in the North-Eastern Region, whereas PKVY covers the rest of the country.
109.tq: Distinguish schemes by geographical scope and objective.

109.s:
With reference to organic-farming certification in India, consider the following statements:
1. PGS-India uses participatory, farmer-group certification.
2. PGS-India is intended for the domestic market.
3. NPOP is based mainly on third-party certification.
4. NPOP is mainly associated with exports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: PGS-India uses participatory farmer-group certification for the domestic market. NPOP relies mainly on third-party certification and is chiefly associated with exports.
109.tq: Compare the two certification systems across method and market.

109.s: The National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) was launched in:
109.x: NPOP was launched in 2001 and is mainly associated with third-party certification for exports.
109.tq: Use the year-based distinction between certification milestones.

109.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with PKVY?
o: PKVY — launched in 2024 for nano-fertiliser distribution
PKVY — launched in 2015–16 exclusively for the North-Eastern Region
PKVY — launched in 2015–16 with the jaivikkheti.in portal
PKVY — launched in 2001 for export certification
109.x: PKVY was launched in 2015–16 and is associated with the jaivikkheti.in portal. NPOP concerns export-oriented certification, while MOVCDNER focuses on the North-East.
109.tq: Catch the scheme, year and scope swaps in a long matching statement.

109.s: Up to 31 July 2025, which of the following combinations was associated with PKVY implementation?
o: 8.80 lakh hectares, 18.19 lakh farmers and Rs 1,584 crore released
25.79 lakh hectares, 15.08 lakh farmers and Rs 2,481 crore released
15.08 lakh hectares, 25.38 lakh farmers and Rs 2,524.68 crore released
7.78 lakh hectares, 17,632 farmers and Rs 897 crore released
109.x: The reported PKVY figures up to 31 July 2025 were 15.08 lakh hectares, 25.38 lakh farmers and Rs 2,524.68 crore released.
109.tq: Match a multi-part numerical profile without confusing it with NMNF or Soil Health Card figures.

109.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: MOVCDNER — organic value chains in the North-East
PGS-India — participatory certification for the domestic market
PKVY — third-party certification mainly for exports
NPOP — third-party certification mainly for exports
109.x: PKVY is a cluster-based organic-farming scheme, not a third-party export-certification programme. NPOP is mainly associated with third-party certification for exports.
109.tq: Find the one scheme–function mismatch among three precise pairings.

109.s: In February 2026, how many new certified PKVY organic clusters were reported in tribal Visakhapatnam of Andhra Pradesh?
109.x: Andhra Pradesh reported 200 new certified PKVY organic clusters in tribal Visakhapatnam in February 2026.
109.tq: Test a small, location-specific current-affairs number.

109.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF) was developed by:
109.x: ZBNF was developed by Subhash Palekar. Bill Mollison and David Holmgren are associated with permaculture.
109.tq: Separate the originator of ZBNF from the originators of permaculture.

109.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a natural-farming input or practice?
o: Jeevamrutha — cow dung and urine-based microbial culture
Beejamrutha — soil aeration through moisture regulation
109.x: Jeevamrutha is a microbial culture prepared from cow dung and urine. Beejamrutha is used for seed treatment, Achhadana denotes mulching, and Whapasa relates to soil aeration and moisture.
109.tq: Discriminate among similar-sounding natural-farming inputs by their functions.

109.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Beejamrutha — seed treatment
2. Achhadana — mulching
3. Whapasa — soil aeration and moisture
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
109.x: Beejamrutha is used for seed treatment, Achhadana refers to mulching, and Whapasa concerns soil aeration and moisture balance.
109.tq: Confirm each term–function pair instead of relying on familiar-sounding names.

109.s: Which statement best distinguishes organic farming from natural farming?
o: Organic farming excludes certification, whereas natural farming requires third-party export certification.
Natural farming permits only synthetic fertilisers, whereas organic farming uses only pesticides.
Organic farming is certified and permits approved organic inputs, whereas natural farming relies on on-farm cow-based inputs.
Both systems require exactly the same external inputs and certification procedure.
109.x: Organic farming involves certification and approved organic inputs. Natural farming emphasises on-farm, cow-based inputs and does not follow the same certification framework.
109.tq: Test the exact distinction between two commonly confused agricultural systems.

109.s: Permaculture is best described as the:
o: Design of ecological habitats and food systems suited to a particular site
Certification system for export-oriented organic produce
Chemical treatment of soil to maximise short-term yields
Large-scale replacement of all crops by one perennial crop
109.x: Permaculture involves designing ecological habitats and food systems in a site-specific manner.
109.tq: Choose the definition that captures both the ecological and site-specific dimensions.

109.s: The term ‘permaculture’ was coined by:
o: The founders of NPOP in India
Bill Mollison and David Holmgren in Australia
109.x: The term permaculture was coined by Bill Mollison and David Holmgren in Australia.
109.tq: Distinguish the originators and country associated with a named concept.

109.s: The National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved on:
109.x: NMNF was approved on 25 November 2024.
109.tq: Use the exact approval date rather than the implementation-period figures.

109.s: The total outlay of NMNF up to March 2026, including the Centre and States’ shares, was:
109.x: NMNF had an outlay of Rs 2,481 crore, comprising Rs 1,584 crore from the Centre and Rs 897 crore from the States, up to March 2026.
109.tq: Add or recognise the total while distinguishing component shares from the total.

109.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported NMNF position by March 2026?
o: 15.08 lakh hectares covered and 25.38 lakh farmers reached
7.78 lakh hectares covered and 17,632 farmers reached
8.80 lakh hectares covered and 18.19 lakh farmers reached
25.79 lakh hectares covered and 18.19 crore farmers reached
109.x: By March 2026, NMNF coverage was reported as 8.80 lakh hectares involving 18.19 lakh farmers. The figure of 7.78 lakh hectares was an earlier target.
109.tq: Distinguish achieved coverage from an earlier target and from PKVY figures.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NMNF:
1. It had trained 70,021 Krishi Sakhis by March 2026.
2. It involved 17,632 clusters.
3. Its reported coverage by March 2026 was 8.80 lakh hectares.
4. It had an outlay of Rs 897 crore in total.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Rs 897 crore was the States’ share, not the total NMNF outlay; the total was Rs 2,481 crore.
109.tq: Catch the component-share substitution in an otherwise accurate scheme profile.

109.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the reported economic and implementation aspects of natural farming?
o: It guarantees a market premium immediately after adoption.
It can reduce cultivation cost by 20–40%, while transition may involve knowledge-intensive practices.
It increases cultivation cost by 20–40% and requires no specialised knowledge.
It eliminates the possibility of yield decline during transition.
109.x: Natural farming was reported to reduce cultivation costs by 20–40%, but it is knowledge-intensive. Yield dips during the first two or three years and weak market premiums remain concerns.
109.tq: Balance a stated benefit against the documented transition constraints.

109.s: Which one of the following is a criticism or concern associated with the transition to natural farming?
o: Permanent dependence on imported chemical inputs
A possible yield dip for two to three years
Guaranteed high market premium for all produce
