117.x: The converted network comprised 10,032 Sub Centres, 1,144 PHCs and 560 UPHCs.
117.tq: Match each facility category with its corresponding converted count.

117.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh's emergency and mobile health services, which statement is correct?
o: 104 is the emergency ambulance service and 108 is the advisory service.
104 is a specialty hospital network and 108 is a telemedicine platform.
108 is the emergency ambulance service, while 104 is the mobile medical unit and health advisory service.
Both 104 and 108 are emergency ambulance services.
117.x: The 108 service provides emergency ambulances, whereas 104 provides mobile medical units and health advisory services.
117.tq: Discriminate between two easily reversed service numbers.

117.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh is located at:
117.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam.
117.tq: Use the location-specific hospital association.

117.s: Which institution functions as the telemedicine anchor in Andhra Pradesh and has over 2,500 out-patients a day?
117.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the telemedicine anchor and has over 2,500 OPD patients a day.
117.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive service role and patient figure.

117.s: Greyfield super-specialty blocks were being completed at which set of places?
117.x: The Greyfield super-specialty blocks were being finished at Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru.
117.tq: Identify the complete location set rather than a partially correct pair.

117.s: The Bhore Committee was appointed primarily to:
o: Survey the state of public health
117.x: The Bhore Committee was appointed to survey the state of public health.
117.tq: Match a committee with its stated mandate, not merely its broad sector.

117.s: Which of the following recommendations is associated with the Bhore Committee?
o: Integrated preventive and curative care with a three-tier PHC-based system
Referral Services Complex through village health guides
Consolidation of existing PHCs before expansion only
117.x: The Bhore Committee recommended integrated preventive and curative care and a three-tier PHC-based system.
117.tq: Avoid swapping recommendations among committees with similar health-sector mandates.

117.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their reporting or recommendation period:
A. Shrivastava Committee
B. Bhore Committee
C. Kartar Singh Committee
D. Mudaliar Committee
117.x: The correct sequence is Bhore (1943–46), Mudaliar (1959–62), Kartar Singh (1973), and Shrivastava (1975).
117.tq: Fix the earliest and latest committees first, then arrange the middle two.

117.s: Which committee recommended consolidation of existing PHCs before expansion and strengthening of district hospitals?
117.x: The Mudaliar Committee, working during 1959–62, recommended consolidating existing PHCs before expansion and strengthening district hospitals.
117.tq: Match the distinctive reform recommendation with the committee.

117.s: The recommendation of one PHC for every 50,000 people and the introduction of multipurpose health workers are associated with:
117.x: The Kartar Singh Committee (1973) recommended multipurpose health workers and one PHC per 50,000 people.
117.tq: Link the numerical norm to the committee that proposed it.

117.s: The Shrivastava Committee recommended:
o: Community health volunteers or village health guides and a Referral Services Complex
Only the expansion of medical colleges
One PHC per 50,000 people and multipurpose workers
Consolidation of PHCs before any district hospital strengthening
117.x: The Shrivastava Committee (1975) recommended community health volunteers or village health guides and a Referral Services Complex.
117.tq: Distinguish the community-volunteer recommendation from other committee proposals.

117.s: According to NFHS-3, the private sector was the main source of care for what proportion of urban households?
117.x: NFHS-3 reported that the private sector was the main source of care for 70% of urban households.
117.tq: Recall the survey-linked percentage without confusing it with other health-sector shares.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current private-sector care shares given for India?
o: 43.4% of inpatient care and 1.43% of outpatient care
Over 60% of inpatient care and about 70% of outpatient care
30% of inpatient care and 70% of outpatient care
About 70% of inpatient care and over 60% of outpatient care
117.x: The private sector handles over 60% of inpatient care and about 70% of outpatient care.
117.tq: Keep inpatient and outpatient percentages in their correct order.

117.s: Out-of-pocket expenditure constituted what percentage of total health spending in 2022–23, according to the stated figure?
117.x: Out-of-pocket expenditure was 43.4% of total health spending in 2022–23.
117.tq: Distinguish the expenditure share from GDP-based government spending figures.

117.s: The average hospitalisation cost in a private facility was approximately how much, compared with Rs 6,631 in a government facility?
117.x: The average hospitalisation cost was Rs 50,508 in a private facility, compared with Rs 6,631 in a government facility.
117.tq: Use the paired cost comparison and reject the nearby percentage figures.

117.s: Which of the following was included among the recommendations of the committee concerning hospitalisation costs?
o: Uniform tariffs based only on rural PHC costs
Standard package rates and tariffs capped near nearby three-star hotel rates
A ban on private inpatient care
117.x: The committee made 368 recommendations, including standard package rates and tariffs capped near nearby three-star hotel rates.
117.tq: Identify the specific regulatory recommendation among plausible policy alternatives.

117.s: Approximately what proportion of health infrastructure is located in urban areas, which contain what proportion of the population?
117.x: About 70% of health infrastructure is in urban areas, which contain only 30% of the population.
117.tq: Identify the reversed infrastructure-population distribution trap.

117.s: The latest revision of the Indian Public Health Standards is:
117.x: IPHS 2022 is the latest revision stated for Indian Public Health Standards.
117.tq: Recall the latest revision year and avoid substituting a policy year.

117.s: IPHS 2022 sets norms for which of the following groups of facilities?
o: Only district hospitals and medical colleges
SHC and HWC, PHC, CHC, sub-district hospitals and district hospitals
Only private hospitals and nursing homes
117.x: IPHS 2022 covers SHC and HWC, PHC, CHC, sub-district hospitals and district hospitals.
117.tq: Select the complete scope instead of an artificially restricted list.

117.s: Which statement regarding Andhra Pradesh's Urban Primary Health Centres is correct?
o: They have not been brought under IPHS norms.
They have been upgraded to IPHS norms; 92 are NQAS-certified and 267 scored above 70% for Kayakalp.
117.x: AP's UPHCs have been upgraded to IPHS norms; 92 are NQAS-certified and 267 scored above 70% for Kayakalp.
117.tq: Combine the norm, certification and performance figures without dropping one part.

117.s: The stated doctor-population ratio for NMC-registered allopathic doctors is approximately:
117.x: The stated doctor-population ratio is approximately 1:834 for NMC-registered allopathic doctors.
117.tq: Distinguish the observed ratio from the WHO benchmark.

117.s: The WHO norm against which India's doctor-population ratio is compared is:
117.x: The WHO norm stated for the doctor-population ratio is 1:1,000.
117.tq: Separate the benchmark from the country-specific ratio.

117.s: Why may the real availability of doctors be lower than the registered doctor-population ratio suggests?
o: Doctors are distributed uniformly only in rural areas.
All doctors work exclusively in district hospitals.
The ratio includes only nurses and ASHAs.
117.x: The real availability is lower because doctors are concentrated in cities rather than being evenly distributed.
117.tq: Apply the distributional qualification to an apparently favourable ratio.

117.s: Which of the following correctly describes human-resource challenges in rural healthcare?
o: The nurse ratio exceeds global norms and rural CHCs have no vacancies.
The nurse ratio is below global norms and specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
Only urban CHCs face specialist vacancies.
Rural CHCs have surplus specialists and no nursing shortage.
117.x: The nurse ratio is below global norms, while specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
117.tq: Identify the option that preserves both linked shortages.

117.s: Each Andhra Pradesh Urban Primary Health Centre has how many staff, according to the stated APSES figure?
117.x: Each AP UPHC has seven staff members.
117.tq: Recall the facility-level staffing number directly.

117.s: In Andhra Pradesh's UPHC system, field work is handled primarily by:
o: Medical college professors and district collectors
117.x: ANMs and ASHAs handle field work in the AP UPHC system.
117.tq: Match the operational role with the correct frontline workers.

117.s: Which category of health personnel is stated to carry the heaviest workload?
117.x: Community workers are stated to carry the heaviest workload.
117.tq: Identify the workload-related observation without confusing it with staffing numbers.

117.s: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were launched in:
117.x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were launched in 2018.
117.tq: Recall the launch year, distinct from the later renaming and count milestones.

117.s: By December 2022, how many Health and Wellness Centres had been built by upgrading Sub Health Centres and PHCs?
117.x: By December 2022, 1,50,000 HWCs had been built by upgrading SHCs and PHCs; they were later renamed Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.
117.tq: Distinguish the December 2022 milestone from the later functioning count.

117.s: The number of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs functioning at present in the stated figure is more than:
117.x: More than 1.79 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are stated to be functioning.
117.tq: Separate the current count from the earlier construction milestone.

117.s: Which of the following is included in the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs?
o: NCD screening including hypertension, diabetes and oral, breast and cervical cancer
117.x: The CPHC package includes NCD screening for hypertension, diabetes, and oral, breast and cervical cancers, along with several other services.
117.tq: Recognise the broad primary-care package from its specific screening components.

117.s:
Consider the following services:
1. Mental health
2. ENT and eye care
3. Geriatric and palliative care
4. Yoga and wellness
Which of the services given above form part of the CPHC package at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs?
117.x: Mental health, ENT, eye care, geriatric and palliative care, and Yoga and wellness are all included in the stated CPHC package.
117.tq: Check each service against the complete package before choosing the all-inclusive option.

117.s: Which pair correctly states the medicines and diagnostics available at AAM-PHCs?
117.x: AAM-PHCs provide 172 drugs and 63 diagnostics.
117.tq: Keep the drug count and diagnostic count paired with the correct facility level.

117.s: At AAM-SHCs, the stated availability is:
117.x: AAM-SHCs provide 106 drugs and 14 diagnostics.
117.tq: Compare the SHC package with the larger PHC package without reversing the figures.

117.s: The Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), intended to establish AIIMS-like institutions and upgrade government medical colleges, was launched in which year?
117.x: PMSSY was launched in 2003. Its two major objectives are the establishment of AIIMS-like institutions and the upgradation of government medical colleges.
117.tq: Use the year-based numerical distinction among closely spaced options.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the AIIMS serving Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the AIIMS institution associated with Andhra Pradesh.
117.tq: Discriminate among nearby place-based institutional names.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PMSSY:
1. It seeks to establish institutions modelled on AIIMS.
2. It includes the upgradation of government medical colleges.
3. It is exclusively concerned with private medical colleges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because PMSSY concerns AIIMS-like institutions and government medical colleges, not exclusively private medical colleges.
117.tq: Find the statement that reverses the public-sector scope of the scheme.

117.s: Under PM-JAY, the annual health cover provided per family is:
117.x: PM-JAY provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
117.tq: Recall the scheme amount by separating it from other plausible insurance figures.

117.s: The PM-JAY coverage figure mentioned for families is approximately:
117.x: The stated PM-JAY coverage is Rs 5 lakh per family per year for 12 crore families.
117.tq: Match the scheme with its stated beneficiary count.

117.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to dental education in 2024–25:
1. BDS colleges — 319
2. MDS colleges — 281
Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
117.x: The figures stated for 2024–25 are 319 BDS colleges and 281 MDS colleges; both pairs are correct.
117.tq: Check each numerical pair independently before selecting the combined option.

117.s: eSanjeevani was developed by which organisation?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi
117.x: eSanjeevani was built by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Mohali.
117.tq: Identify the correct technology agency rather than the health-sector organisation.

117.s: Which of the following correctly describes eSanjeevani AAM?
o: Teleconsultation exclusively for armed forces personnel
Patient-to-provider consultation from the patient's home
Mental-health counselling through a national helpline
Provider-to-provider consultation through a hub-and-spoke model
117.x: eSanjeevani AAM provides provider-to-provider teleconsultation through a hub-and-spoke model.
117.tq: Separate the two eSanjeevani variants by user relationship and service setting.

117.s: A patient seeks medical advice from home through a digital platform. Which eSanjeevani variant is intended for this patient-to-provider interaction?
117.x: eSanjeevani OPD provides patient-to-provider consultation from home. eSanjeevani AAM is the provider-to-provider hub-and-spoke variant.
117.tq: Apply the patient-to-provider versus provider-to-provider distinction.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about eSanjeevani infrastructure:
1. It has 1,35,915 AAM spokes.
2. It has 17,893 hubs.
3. More than 1.75 lakh AAMs are linked to it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All three statements correspond to the stated eSanjeevani infrastructure figures: 1,35,915 AAM spokes, 17,893 hubs and more than 1.75 lakh linked AAMs.
117.tq: Verify each quantitative statement before accepting the all-inclusive option.

117.s: ONCONET connects which of the following network of institutions?
117.x: ONCONET comprises a network of 108 peripheral cancer centres and 27 regional cancer centres.
117.tq: Distinguish the two categories as well as their associated numbers.

117.s: The 176th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee referred to in the context of healthcare was tabled on:
117.x: The 176th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee was tabled on 7 August 2026.
117.tq: Separate the tabling date from the date of later reporting.

117.s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani digital health programme, rolled out from August 2026?
o: It provides only cancer treatment through ONCONET.
It replaces all village health clinics with AIIMS institutions.
It is restricted to armed forces personnel through SeHAT.
It issues ABHA IDs and integrates 104, 108, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine.
117.x: The programme issues ABHA IDs and integrates the 104 and 108 services, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine. The other options wrongly assign functions of separate platforms or make unsupported claims.
117.tq: Identify the option that combines the programme's stated functions without importing another platform's role.

117.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of healthcare initiatives or institutions specifically associated with the Andhra Pradesh angle?
o: Village health clinics, 104 and 108 services, Palasa, AIIMS Mangalagiri, CCBs and IPHLs
Tele-MANAS, ONCONET, SeHAT, AIIMS Delhi, PM-JAY and PMSSY
eSanjeevani OPD, MDS colleges, regional cancer centres, SeHAT and Tele-MANAS
AIIMS-like institutions, 17,893 hubs, 319 BDS colleges, ONCONET and PM-JAY
117.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific references include village health clinics, the 104 and 108 services, Palasa, AIIMS Mangalagiri, and the new CCBs and IPHLs.
117.tq: Choose the option in which every item belongs to the same regional set.

117.s: Which of the following is identified as a major criticism or concern in India's healthcare system?
o: Excessive coverage of the missing middle and equal distribution of doctors
Low out-of-pocket expenditure and rural concentration of doctors
Absence of any public healthcare infrastructure and universal insurance coverage
High out-of-pocket expenditure, a missing middle of over 40 crore people without cover, and urban concentration of doctors
117.x: The stated concerns are high out-of-pocket expenditure, more than 40 crore people forming a 'missing middle' without cover, and the urban concentration of doctors.
117.tq: Reject options that reverse the direction of the stated healthcare problems.

117.s: The term 'missing middle' in the healthcare debate refers to:
o: Doctors located between rural and urban areas
Medical colleges between BDS and MDS levels
More than 40 crore people without healthcare cover
117.x: The 'missing middle' refers to over 40 crore people who lack healthcare coverage.
117.tq: Match the policy term with its precise population-based meaning.

117.s:
Assertion (A): Urban concentration of doctors is identified as a concern in India's healthcare system.
Reason (R): Unequal geographical distribution of healthcare human resources can limit access in underserved areas.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
117.x: Both statements are true. Concentration of doctors in urban areas creates unequal access and therefore explains why it is identified as a healthcare concern.
117.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the stated healthcare disparity.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding current technology-oriented governance initiatives in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The year 2026 was declared the Technology-Driven Decision Making Year.
2. Artificial Intelligence is proposed for grievance redress.
3. Mana Mitra is described as WhatsApp Governance.
4. Sanjeevani is a digital health programme associated with ABHA IDs from August 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All four statements are correct. The initiatives cover technology-driven decision-making, AI-based grievance redress, Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance and the Sanjeevani digital health programme with ABHA IDs.
117.tq: Check several current-affairs facts by separating the year, technology, platform and health initiative.

117.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital associated with the Uddanam kidney disease issue is located at:
117.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam district.
117.tq: Use the place-specific association instead of confusing the hospital with the screening institution.

117.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMUY — ₹5 lakh health cover per family per year
PM-JAY — ₹5 lakh per poor family per year
PM-KISAN — ₹300 daily wage for rural workers
PM SVANidhi — free property cards for street vendors
117.x: PM-JAY provides health cover of ₹5 lakh per poor family per year. PMUY concerns LPG connections, PM-KISAN provides farmer income support, and PM SVANidhi provides loans to street vendors.
117.tq: Separate similar welfare benefits by beneficiary group and benefit type.

118.s: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is defined as the number of deaths of infants below one year of age per how many live births in a year?
118.x: IMR denotes deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live births in a year.
118.tq: Distinguish the population base used for IMR from that used for MMR.

118.s: The Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR) refers to deaths occurring during which period per 1,000 live births?
o: The first seven days of life
The first six months of life
118.x: NMR measures deaths during the first 28 days after birth per 1,000 live births.
118.tq: Discriminate between neonatal, infant and under-five age limits.

118.s: Under-Five Mortality Rate (U5MR) is expressed as the number of deaths of children below five years per
118.x: U5MR is the number of deaths under five years per 1,000 live births.
118.tq: Use the exact denominator to separate related mortality indicators.

118.s: Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is measured as maternal deaths per
118.x: MMR is expressed as maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births, unlike IMR, NMR and U5MR, which use a base of 1,000 live births.
118.tq: Split the options by the denominator and identify the distinctive MMR base.

118.s: According to the SRS 2023 figure cited for the latest estimates, India’s IMR was
118.x: The IMR was 25 according to SRS 2023, as cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26. The figures 28 and 35.2 refer to older or different sources.
118.tq: Match the latest year with the correct numerical value rather than using a stale estimate.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s IMR trend:
1. IMR was 40 in 2013.
2. IMR was 39 in 2014.
3. IMR was 37 in 2015.
4. IMR was 34 in 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: The reported IMR values were 40, 39, 37 and 34 for 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016 respectively.
118.tq: Check each year-value pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

118.s: The IMR declined from 40 in 2013 to 25 in 2023. This represents a decline of
118.x: The decline was 15 points from a base of 40, which is 37.5%; hence it was more than 37%.
118.tq: Calculate the percentage change from the original base, not from the final value.

118.s: Which State is credited with having the lowest IMR owing to adequate basic health and education facilities?
118.x: Kerala has the lowest IMR, attributed to adequate basic health and education facilities.
118.tq: Use the state-specific association rather than confusing it with AP or Telangana figures.

118.s: During 1990–2023, the NMR and U5MR declined by approximately
118.x: The NMR fell by 70%, while the U5MR fell by 78% during 1990–2023.
118.tq: Match each indicator with its distinct trend percentage.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
118.x: NFHS-5 reported U5MR as 41.9. The other figures refer to different indicators or sources.
118.tq: Start from the sure indicator-source-value pair and reject swapped measures.

118.s: The IMR, TFR, MMR and institutional delivery percentage reported for Telangana were respectively
118.x: The cited figures for Telangana were IMR 18, TFR 1.5, MMR 43 and 99.9% institutional deliveries.
118.tq: Retain the order of multiple numerical indicators while matching a state profile.

118.s: Which indicator is defined as low height-for-age, more than two standard deviations below the WHO median?
118.x: Stunting is low height-for-age, defined here as more than two standard deviations below the WHO median.
118.tq: Distinguish anthropometric indicators by the body measurement they use.

118.s: Low weight-for-height is the characteristic measure of
118.x: Wasting is measured by low weight-for-height. Underweight uses weight-for-age, while stunting uses height-for-age.
118.tq: Swap-test the height, weight and age components carefully.

118.s: Underweight is measured by
118.x: Underweight refers to low weight-for-age.
118.tq: Identify the exact anthropometric denominator in a confusable group.

118.s: Which of the following correctly presents the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children?
118.x: Underweight declined from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6. The 35.8% figure belongs to NFHS-4.
118.tq: Track both survey round and indicator before choosing the pair.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about nutrition indicators:
1. Stunting was 35.5% in NFHS-5 and 29.3% in NFHS-6.
2. Severe wasting was 7.7% in NFHS-5 and 5.2% in NFHS-6.
3. Wasting was 19.3% in NFHS-5.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All three statements reproduce the cited NFHS values for stunting, severe wasting and wasting.
118.tq: Check whether the survey round and severity level have been swapped.

118.s: The decline between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 was approximately what percentage for stunting and severe wasting respectively?
118.x: Stunting fell by approximately 17%, while severe wasting fell by approximately 32%. Underweight showed little change.
118.tq: Match each percentage decline to the correct nutrition indicator.

118.s: Which statement best describes the change in underweight between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6?
o: It declined by approximately 32%, from 35.8% to 19.3%.
It declined only marginally from 32.1% to 31.8%.
118.x: Underweight moved only from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6 and therefore barely changed.
118.tq: Use the trend wording to distinguish a marginal change from a substantial decline.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, anaemia affected approximately what proportions of children aged 6–59 months and women aged 15–49 years respectively?
118.x: NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 67.1% of children aged 6–59 months and 57.0% of women aged 15–49 years.
118.tq: Keep the age group and percentage in the same order as asked.

118.s: Underweight prevalence was highest among which of the following social groups according to NFHS-5?
o: Other Backward Classes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Scheduled Tribes, followed by Scheduled Castes
Scheduled Castes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Urban households, followed by rural households
118.x: Underweight was highest among Scheduled Tribes at 44.1%, followed by Scheduled Castes at 39.1%. It was also higher in rural areas.
118.tq: Rank the groups using the reported percentages rather than merely identifying both groups.

118.s: The State reported to have high child wasting and underweight in NFHS-6 was
118.x: Madhya Pradesh recorded high child wasting and underweight in NFHS-6, while Meghalaya showed a decline in stunting.
118.tq: Distinguish the state associated with high wasting and underweight from the state associated with declining stunting.

118.s: The State associated with a decline in stunting in NFHS-6 was
118.x: Meghalaya showed a decline in stunting in NFHS-6.
118.tq: Use the state-outcome association rather than assuming the state with poor outcomes is the answer.

118.s: SOFI 2025 reported India’s wasting rate among children as approximately
118.x: SOFI 2025 reported India’s wasting rate as 18.7%, involving approximately 21 million children.
118.tq: Match the global report with its specific indicator and percentage.

118.s: According to SOFI 2025, the approximate number of stunted under-five children in India was
118.x: SOFI 2025 reported approximately 37.4 million stunted under-five children in India; 21 million was associated with wasting.
118.tq: Separate the two large figures by linking each to its specific nutrition outcome.

118.s:
According to the WHO classification, malnutrition in all its forms includes:
1. Undernutrition, including wasting, stunting and underweight.
2. Inadequate vitamins and minerals.
3. Overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: WHO’s broad definition includes undernutrition, micronutrient inadequacy, and overnutrition with diet-related non-communicable diseases.
118.tq: Recognise the comprehensive definition instead of treating malnutrition as undernutrition alone.

118.s: The term ‘double burden of malnutrition’ refers to the coexistence of
o: Micronutrient deficiency and sanitation deficiency only
118.x: The double burden refers to the simultaneous presence of undernutrition and overnutrition.
118.tq: Distinguish the two-burden concept from the broader triple-burden description.

118.s: SOFI 2025 described India’s malnutrition situation as a triple burden comprising
o: Undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency or anaemia, and overweight
Food insecurity, poverty and poor sanitation
118.x: The triple burden consists of undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency or anaemia, and overweight.
118.tq: Separate the named forms of malnutrition from their social and health drivers.

118.s: Food insecurity and poverty may contribute to both undernutrition and overnutrition because they can lead to consumption of
o: Only locally produced fruits and vegetables
118.x: Food insecurity and poverty can produce undernutrition while also encouraging consumption of inexpensive energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods that contribute to overnutrition.
118.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to a realistic dietary situation.

118.s:
Which of the following were identified as linked to child nutrition through NFHS tracking?
1. Sanitation and drinking water
2. Women’s schooling
3. Child marriage
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: NFHS tracks sanitation, drinking water, women’s schooling and child marriage, all of which are linked to child nutrition.
118.tq: Treat the listed social determinants as a combined set rather than isolating dietary factors.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, women with 10 or more years of schooling constituted approximately
118.x: NFHS-5 reported that approximately 41% of women had 10 or more years of schooling.
118.tq: Distinguish the schooling percentage from the child-marriage percentage and anaemia figures.

118.s: The proportion of women married before the age of 18, as cited from NFHS-5, was
118.x: The cited NFHS-5 figure for women married before age 18 was 23.3%.
118.tq: Match the social indicator with its exact percentage.

118.s: At the time of Independence, life expectancy in India was approximately
118.x: Life expectancy at Independence was approximately 32 years.
118.tq: Identify the historical baseline rather than a later SRS life-table value.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SRS abridged life tables for 2016–20:
1. India’s male life expectancy was 68.6 years.
2. India’s female life expectancy was 71.4 years.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s male life expectancy was 69.1 years.
4. Andhra Pradesh’s female life expectancy was 72.2 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements correctly state the SRS abridged life-table values for India and Andhra Pradesh during 2016–20.
118.tq: Verify each sex-state-value combination before selecting the complete code.

118.s: Which of the following correctly describes the gender gap in life expectancy in the cited SRS 2016–20 figures?
o: Men live about three years longer than women in both India and AP.
There is no gender difference in either India or AP.
Women live exactly one year longer than men in both India and AP.
Women live about three years longer than men in both India and AP.
118.x: Women’s life expectancy exceeded men’s by about 2.8 years in India and 3.1 years in Andhra Pradesh, or approximately three years in both.
118.tq: Compare the paired male and female values before interpreting the direction of the gap.

118.s: The older SRS life-table figure of 68.3 years referred to India’s life expectancy during
118.x: The older figure of 68.3 years was reported for the SRS period 2011–15.
118.tq: Distinguish the older reference period from the later 2016–20 life-table period.

118.s: Which Andhra Pradesh scheme provides a nutritious meal along with iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis?
118.x: Anna Amrutha Hastam provides a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis.
118.tq: Match the scheme name with its specific beneficiary and service.

118.s: The primary intended outcomes of Anna Amrutha Hastam include reduction of
o: Crude birth rate and crude death rate
118.x: The scheme aims to reduce infant and maternal mortality through nutrition support and iron-folic acid supplementation.
118.tq: Link the intervention to its stated health outcomes rather than to unrelated demographic indicators.

118.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the other maternal services in Andhra Pradesh?
118.x: JSY, PMSMA and LaQshya are listed among the maternal services in Andhra Pradesh. SOFI is an international food-security report, not an AP maternal service.
118.tq: Find the item belonging to a different category or institution.

118.s: Which of the following is a correct list of maternal services mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
o: JSY, JSSK, PMSMA, PMMVY, SUMAN, LaQshya and MCP cards
SOFI, NFHS, SRS, WHO and WFP
IMR, NMR, U5MR, MMR and TFR
Stunting, wasting, underweight, overweight and anaemia
118.x: The listed AP maternal services are JSY, JSSK, PMSMA, PMMVY, SUMAN, LaQshya and MCP cards.
118.tq: Separate programme names from indicators, surveys and nutrition conditions.

118.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched in 2018 under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
118.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan, also called the National Nutrition Mission, was launched in 2018 under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
118.tq: Apply the ‘who launched or administers the programme?’ authority test.

118.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated objectives of POSHAN Abhiyaan?
o: Reducing anaemia and low birth weight
Increasing the legal retirement age of public employees
118.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan aims to reduce stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight. The legal retirement age of public employees is unrelated to the programme.
118.tq: Find the option outside the programme’s nutrition-related objectives.

118.s:
POSHAN Abhiyaan is based, among other things, on convergence of which of the following programmes or initiatives?
1. ICDS
2. National Health Mission
3. Swachh Bharat
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan promotes convergence among ICDS, the National Health Mission and Swachh Bharat.
118.tq: Recognise convergence questions by checking whether all listed programmes support the stated mission.

118.s: The eighth Poshan Pakhwada was held in:
118.x: The eighth Poshan Pakhwada was held in 2026.
118.tq: Use the event-number and year combination as a direct current-affairs recall point.

118.s: Which of the following correctly describes the beneficiaries of Anganwadi Services under ICDS?
o: Only children below six months of age
Only elderly persons and persons with disabilities
Children aged six months to six years, and pregnant and lactating women
Only school-going children aged six to fourteen years
118.x: Anganwadi Services cover children from six months to six years and pregnant and lactating women.
118.tq: Distinguish the programme’s target groups from beneficiaries of school or social-security schemes.

118.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six services provided through Anganwadi Services?
118.x: The six services include supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral services. Old-age pension distribution is not one of them.
118.tq: Locate the option that does not belong to the programme’s fixed list of six services.

118.s: The school meal programme formerly known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme was renamed as PM POSHAN in:
118.x: The Mid-Day Meal programme was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021.
118.tq: Separate the launch year of one nutrition programme from the renaming year of another.

118.s: The 6x6x6 strategy is associated with which programme?
o: Rice fortification under the Public Distribution System
118.x: Anemia Mukt Bharat uses a 6x6x6 strategy consisting of six interventions, six target groups and six institutional mechanisms.
118.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed nutrition programmes by their signature strategy.

118.s: Fortified rice supplied through the Public Distribution System, ICDS and PM POSHAN is fortified with:
o: Calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
Iodine, zinc and vitamin A only
118.x: The specified fortified rice contains iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 and is supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.
118.tq: Match the intervention with its exact micronutrient combination and delivery channels.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (NFHS Round)
a. NFHS-1
b. NFHS-2
c. NFHS-3
d. NFHS-4

List-II (Year)
i. 2005-06
ii. 1992-93
iii. 2015-16
iv. 1998-99
118.x: NFHS-1 was conducted in 1992-93, NFHS-2 in 1998-99, NFHS-3 in 2005-06 and NFHS-4 in 2015-16.
118.tq: Start with the sure earliest and latest pairs, then complete the middle matches.

118.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the NFHS round with its period?
118.x: NFHS-5 corresponds to 2019-21. NFHS-2 was 1998-99, NFHS-3 was 2005-06 and NFHS-6 was scheduled for 2023-24 with results released in 2026.
118.tq: Use round-to-year matching while rejecting shifted or reversed chronological pairs.

118.s: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with which institution serving as the nodal agency?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, Hyderabad
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
118.x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, is the nodal agency.
118.tq: Apply the institutional-authority trap by distinguishing the conducting ministry from the nodal agency.

118.s: Which of the following is NOT ordinarily covered as an indicator in the National Family Health Survey?
o: India’s annual gross domestic product growth rate
118.x: NFHS covers health, mortality, nutrition, immunisation, fertility, family planning and related social indicators. It does not report India’s annual GDP growth rate as a survey indicator.
118.tq: Find the unrelated macroeconomic indicator among the health and demographic indicators.

118.s:
Which of the following was an addition in NFHS-5?
1. Death registration
2. Menstrual hygiene
3. Alcohol and tobacco use
4. NCD screening for all persons aged 15 years and above
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: NFHS-5 added death registration, pre-school education, menstrual hygiene, alcohol and tobacco use, and NCD screening for all aged 15 years and above. Thus all four listed additions are correct.
118.tq: Treat the additions as a cumulative list and check each item before choosing the complete combination.

118.s: Which statement best describes the reporting of malnutrition in the National Family Health Survey?
o: NFHS reports one single overall malnutrition percentage for the country.
NFHS reports only wasting and excludes stunting and underweight.
NFHS reports malnutrition only for urban children.
NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight separately rather than providing one single overall malnutrition percentage.
118.x: NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight as separate indicators; it does not provide one single overall ‘malnutrition percentage’.
118.tq: Distinguish separate indicators from an aggregated figure that the survey does not provide.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, which statement regarding sex ratio is correct?
o: The overall sex ratio was 1020; the rural ratio was 1,037 and the urban ratio was 985.
The overall sex ratio was 920, with the rural ratio lower than the urban ratio.
The overall sex ratio was 985; the rural ratio was 1,020 and the urban ratio was 1,037.
The overall sex ratio was 1,037, while both rural and urban ratios were below 1,000.
118.x: NFHS-5 reported an overall sex ratio of 1020, with 1,037 in rural areas and 985 in urban areas. The figure 920 refers to the child sex ratio mentioned separately.
118.tq: Avoid the confusable-pair trap between overall sex ratio and child sex ratio, and compare rural with urban values correctly.

118.s: The Child Sex Ratio associated with the NFHS-5 figures was:
118.x: The Child Sex Ratio cited with NFHS-5 was 920. The overall NFHS-5 sex ratio was 1020.
118.tq: Separate closely placed demographic indicators instead of treating sex ratio and child sex ratio as identical.

118.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent nutrition findings attributed to NFHS-6?
o: Stunting increased to 31.8%, while underweight declined to 29.3%.
Stunting declined to 29.3%, while underweight remained at 31.8%.
Both stunting and underweight declined to 29.3%.
Both stunting and underweight increased to 31.8%.
118.x: NFHS-6 findings showed stunting declining to 29.3%, while underweight remained at 31.8%, indicating a continuing double burden of malnutrition.
118.tq: Compare the direction and value of two indicators without swapping their figures.

118.s: The term ‘double burden’ in the context of the recent nutrition findings refers to:
o: The simultaneous presence of declining stunting and persistent underweight
The coexistence of rural and urban sanitation programmes
The replacement of all nutrition programmes by one scheme
The simultaneous rise of life expectancy and fertility
118.x: The reported double burden is reflected in declining stunting alongside underweight remaining high, at 31.8%.
118.tq: Apply the concept to the indicator trend rather than treating ‘double burden’ as two separate programmes.

118.s: Which of the following correctly compares Andhra Pradesh with the national averages mentioned for key health outcomes?
o: Andhra Pradesh performs better than the national averages on IMR, MMR, TFR and life expectancy.
Andhra Pradesh has the same IMR, MMR, TFR and life expectancy as India.
Andhra Pradesh has higher IMR, MMR and TFR than India but lower life expectancy.
Andhra Pradesh performs better only on TFR and worse on all the other listed indicators.
118.x: Andhra Pradesh was reported to outperform the national averages on IMR, MMR, TFR and life expectancy, with IMR 24, MMR 45 and TFR 1.5.
118.tq: Use the direction of comparison across all listed indicators and reject the partially reversed options.

118.s: The Infant Mortality Rate declined from 40 in 2013 to what figure in 2023?
118.x: The Infant Mortality Rate declined from 40 in 2013 to 25 in 2023.
118.tq: Track the exact beginning and ending values in a trend question.

118.s: Crude Birth Rate (CBR) and Crude Death Rate (CDR) are expressed as the number of births and deaths respectively per:
118.x: CBR and CDR are measured per 1,000 of the mid-year population. IMR uses live births as its denominator, while MMR uses live births and a different scale.
118.tq: Distinguish similar vital-rate denominators.

118.s: Maternal Mortality Ratio is expressed as the number of maternal deaths per:
118.x: MMR is measured as maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births.
118.tq: Use denominator discrimination to separate MMR from IMR and CBR.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Andhra Pradesh health indicators is correctly matched?
118.x: Andhra Pradesh has an MMR of 45 and an IMR of 24, both better than the corresponding national averages.
118.tq: Keep the two similarly abbreviated mortality indicators in their correct order.

118.s: According to the NFHS comparison, which indicator declined from 35.5 per cent in NFHS-5 to 29.3 per cent in NFHS-6 among children under five?
118.x: The prevalence of stunting declined from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6 among children under five.
118.tq: Match the pair of percentages to the correct nutrition indicator.

118.s: Which of the following NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 pairs relating to children under five is correctly matched?
118.x: Severe wasting declined from 7.7% in NFHS-5 to 5.2% in NFHS-6. The other options interchange the values of stunting, underweight and severe wasting or use an unsupported anaemia comparison.
118.tq: Use paired numerical values to detect indicator swapping.

118.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children below five years?
118.x: Underweight prevalence declined marginally from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6.
118.tq: Check the direction of change before comparing the two survey rounds.

118.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the NFHS-6 change?
o: Anaemia in children aged 6–59 months — 67.1% to 59.5%
118.x: The NFHS-5 anaemia figure for children aged 6–59 months was 67.1%; no NFHS-6 change to 59.5% is specified. The other three pairs are correctly stated, with the stunting pair referring to NFHS-5 and NFHS-6.
118.tq: Find the option that falsely converts a single reported figure into a two-round comparison.

118.s: NFHS-6, in comparison with NFHS-5, recorded the lowest percentage among the following indicators for children under five years?
o: Breastfeeding within one hour of birth in NFHS-6
118.x: NFHS-6 recorded severe wasting at 5.2%, compared with 29.3% stunting, 31.8% underweight and 50.1% breastfeeding within one hour of birth.
118.tq: Compare the numerical rows rather than assuming that every nutrition indicator moves in the same direction.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 findings for children under five years?
118.x: Stunting declined from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6. The other options reverse the NFHS sequence.
118.tq: Check the direction of change and reject reversed pairs.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. NIDDCP
b. MAA
c. POSHAN Abhiyaan
d. PM POSHAN

List-II (Year of launch)
i. 1992
ii. 2016
iii. 2018
iv. 2021

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: NIDDCP was launched in 1992, MAA in 2016, POSHAN Abhiyaan in 2018 and PM POSHAN in 2021.
118.tq: Start with the sure year pair and eliminate codes that disturb the sequence.

118.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched in 2018.
2. Anaemia Mukt Bharat was launched in 2018.
3. PM POSHAN was renamed from the Mid-Day Meal Scheme in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All three statements are correct. POSHAN Abhiyaan and Anaemia Mukt Bharat were launched in 2018, while PM POSHAN was renamed from the Mid-Day Meal Scheme in 2021.
118.tq: Verify each programme against its launch or renaming year.

119.s: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly known as YSR Aarogyasri, is primarily intended to provide which of the following?
o: Subsidised insurance exclusively for private-sector employees
Free crop insurance to small farmers
Pension support to retired government employees
Cashless health assurance to economically vulnerable families in Andhra Pradesh
119.x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, earlier YSR Aarogyasri, is Andhra Pradesh’s flagship cashless health assurance scheme for economically vulnerable families.
119.tq: Directly identify the purpose of the flagship state scheme.

119.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva and PM-JAY in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is restricted to government hospitals under PM-JAY.
PM-JAY replaced Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva completely in Andhra Pradesh.
The two schemes operate without any institutional relationship.
Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, enabling portability and wider empanelment.
119.x: The Andhra Pradesh scheme is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, particularly providing portability and wider hospital empanelment.
119.tq: Test the functional relationship between two similar health-assurance schemes.

119.s: In March 2026, how many additional critical cardiovascular procedures were added under Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva?
119.x: Five more critical cardiovascular procedures were added in March 2026 to widen access to advanced cardiac care.
119.tq: Use the exact numerical addition rather than the broader policy objective.

119.s: The Budget Estimate for 2024–25 allocated how much to the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust?
119.x: Of the ₹18,732 crore allocated to Health and Family Welfare in the Andhra Pradesh Budget Estimate for 2024–25, ₹4,000 crore was earmarked for the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
119.tq: Separate the scheme allocation from the larger departmental allocation.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding health coverage in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The state scheme, Employee Health Scheme, RSBY, ESIS and CGHS together covered 70% of AP households.
2. About 2,700 private hospitals were registered under the relevant health-assurance network.
3. Of the registered private hospitals, 540 were speciality hospitals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct: the combined schemes covered 70% of AP households, with 2,700 private hospitals registered, including 540 speciality hospitals.
119.tq: Check the combined coverage figure and both hospital-network counts together.

119.s: According to the National Health Accounts data, Government Health Expenditure as a percentage of GDP increased from 2013–14 to 2022–23 by approximately:
119.x: Government Health Expenditure increased from 1.15% of GDP in 2013–14 to 1.43% in 2022–23, a rise of 0.28 percentage points.
119.tq: Subtract the two percentage values instead of confusing percentage points with percentage growth.

119.s: The National Health Accounts are prepared by which organisation under the NHSRC?
o: National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat under NHSRC
National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Home Affairs
National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority under the Ministry of Finance
National Health Authority under NITI Aayog
119.x: The National Health Accounts are prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat under the National Health Systems Resource Centre.
119.tq: Identify the precise institutional authority rather than a neighbouring health body.

119.s: The National Health Accounts use which of the following frameworks and guidelines?
o: System of National Accounts 2008 and NITI Guidelines 2020
System of Health Accounts 2011 and NHA Guidelines 2016
National Health Policy Framework 2017 and SHA Guidelines 2022
Health Management Information System 2016 and Finance Commission Guidelines 2015
119.x: The accounts use the System of Health Accounts (SHA) 2011 and the NHA Guidelines 2016.
119.tq: Test the exact pairing of a framework and its guidelines.

119.s: The first National Health Accounts publication covered which financial year?
119.x: The first National Health Accounts publication covered 2013–14.
119.tq: Recall the first reference year, a commonly tested chronological detail.

119.s: Government Health Expenditure reached what percentage of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22?
119.x: GHE reached 1.84% of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22.
119.tq: Distinguish the exceptional COVID-year peak from the regular annual figures.

119.s: Which of the following statements regarding the National Health Policy, 2017 target is correct?
o: It targeted GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2022, with the Centre contributing 60%.
It targeted GHE of 1.5% of GDP by 2025, with the States contributing 40%.
It targeted GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre contributing 40% of public spending.
It targeted GHE of 3% of GDP by 2030, with no specified Centre share.
119.x: NHP 2017 targeted Government Health Expenditure of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre’s share intended to be 40% of public spending. The target was missed.
119.tq: Match the target year, percentage and Centre-share provision precisely.

119.s: According to the Economic Survey 2021–22 context, Centre and States together spent approximately what percentage of GDP on health in 2019–20?
119.x: Centre and States together spent about 1.3% of GDP on health in 2019–20.
119.tq: Recall the approximate combined public-spending figure rather than the NHP target.

119.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Free Drugs Service Initiative under the National Health Mission?
o: It reimburses outpatient expenses exclusively to government employees.
It provides free generic medicines at public health facilities.
It fixes the prices of all private hospital services.
It provides only imported medicines through private pharmacies.
119.x: The Free Drugs Service Initiative under NHM provides free generic medicines at public facilities.
119.tq: Identify the service and its delivery setting without confusing it with price regulation.

119.s: DVDMS is associated with which function in the public medicine-supply system?
o: Setting the list of essential surgical procedures
119.x: DVDMS manages drug procurement and inventory under the Free Drugs Service Initiative.
119.tq: Match the digital system with its operational function.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority:
1. NPPA was established in 1997.
2. It fixes ceiling prices of scheduled drugs.
3. The scheduled drugs are those included in the National List of Essential Medicines.
4. Its price-control function operates under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All four statements are correct. NPPA, established in 1997, fixes ceiling prices for scheduled NLEM drugs under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013.
119.tq: Verify the institution, year, regulated category and legal instrument separately.

119.s: A survey found that outpatient medicine bills through private pharmacies were approximately how many times higher than through Jan Aushadhi outlets?
119.x: The survey reported that outpatient medicine bills in private pharmacies were about six times higher than those through Jan Aushadhi.
119.tq: Recall the comparative multiplier rather than merely the direction of difference.

119.s: Which of the following correctly represents the trend in OOPE as a share of Total Health Expenditure between 2013–14 and 2022–23?
119.x: OOPE declined from 64.2% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013–14 to 43.4% in 2022–23, although it remained about half of current health expenditure.
119.tq: Reject the reversed trend and distinguish total health expenditure from current health expenditure.

119.s: According to the NSS 80th round health findings, insurance covered what proportion of rural and urban households, respectively?
119.x: Insurance covered 47.4% of rural households and 44.3% of urban households according to the cited NSS 80th round findings.
119.tq: Preserve the rural–urban order in paired percentage questions.

119.s: Which of the following correctly compares childbirth-related OOPE in private and public facilities?
o: ₹18,815 in private and ₹2,299 in public facilities
₹2,299 in private and ₹37,630 in public facilities
₹37,630 in private and ₹2,299 in public facilities
₹37,630 in both private and public facilities
119.x: Childbirth-related OOPE was ₹37,630 in private facilities compared with ₹2,299 in public facilities—more than sixteen times higher in the private sector.
119.tq: Check both the facility category and the direction of the cost comparison.

119.s: Which of the following components account for over 50% of OOPE because they are generally not covered by insurance?
o: Only inpatient surgery and intensive care
Ambulance services and health education alone
119.x: Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines account for over half of OOPE because insurance commonly does not cover them.
119.tq: Apply the coverage gap to identify the major sources of household spending.

119.s: Which pair correctly represents the proportions of adults affected by diabetes and hypertension, respectively?
119.x: Diabetes affected 11.4% of adults and hypertension affected 35.5% of adults in the cited figures.
119.tq: Keep the disease–percentage pairing in the stated order.

119.s: The term “missing middle” in the context of health financing refers to:
o: More than 40 crore Indians lacking financial protection
People covered simultaneously by both public and private insurance
The middle-income group receiving free medicines at public facilities
Households whose insurance claims are pending for less than one month
119.x: The “missing middle” refers to more than 40 crore Indians who lack adequate financial protection; NITI Aayog first flagged the term.
119.tq: Match the distinctive policy term with its precise population description.

119.s: Government-financed health insurance through PM-JAY, state schemes, ESIS and CGHS increased by approximately how much between 2017–18 and 2025?
119.x: Government-financed health insurance rose 2.5-fold between 2017–18 and 2025.
119.tq: Recall the scale of change and do not confuse a fold increase with percentage points.

119.s: Which of the following correctly states the change in the proportion of households having at least one health-insurance member according to NFHS-6?
119.x: NFHS-6 recorded an increase from 41.0% of households to 60.2% having a health-insurance member.
119.tq: Identify the correct baseline and endpoint from a household-coverage trend.

119.s: Which of the following is NOT a commonly cited burden associated with private health insurance?
119.x: Private insurance may involve premiums, exclusions, waiting periods and co-payments. Automatic nationwide portability without conditions is not listed as such a burden.
119.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated list of private-insurance burdens.

119.s: The Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 had been adopted in approximately:
119.x: The Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 had been adopted in only about 11 States and 6 Union Territories.
119.tq: Test the exact State–Union Territory composition and the limiting word “only”.

119.s: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants of approximately what amount through local governments for the period 2021–2026?
119.x: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants amounting to ₹70,051 crore through local governments for 2021–2026.
119.tq: Use the exact figure and period to eliminate nearby numerical distractors.

119.s: Which of the following is NOT a component supported through the 15th Finance Commission health grants to local governments?
o: Diagnostic infrastructure for sub-centres and PHCs
Construction of exclusively private tertiary-care hospitals
119.x: The grants support diagnostic infrastructure for sub-centres and PHCs, block public health units, urban health and wellness centres, and buildings for building-less SCs, PHCs and CHCs. Exclusively private tertiary-care hospitals are not listed as a component.
119.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated public-health infrastructure components.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the health grants recommended by the 15th Finance Commission:
1. They are routed through local governments.
2. They include provision for buildings for building-less SCs, PHCs and CHCs.
3. They are intended only for urban health and wellness centres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the grants cover several components, including rural and block-level infrastructure as well as urban health and wellness centres.
119.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ by checking the complete list of components.

119.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trend in the government share of Total Health Expenditure (THE) in India?
o: It remained unchanged at 43.7% during both periods.
119.x: The government share of THE rose to 43.7%, compared with 28.6% in 2013–14.
119.tq: Read the direction of change before comparing the two percentages.

119.s:
With reference to India’s National Health Accounts estimates, consider the following statements:
1. The government share of Total Health Expenditure was 43.7% in the latest estimate mentioned.
2. The government share was 28.6% in 2013–14.
3. Household out-of-pocket expenditure constituted 43.4% of Total Health Expenditure in the latest estimate mentioned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct: the government share was 43.7%, compared with 28.6% in 2013–14, while household out-of-pocket expenditure was 43.4% of THE in the cited estimate.
119.tq: Verify each percentage independently before selecting the combined code.

119.s: The principal source of the remaining share of health expenditure, after accounting for the government share in the cited National Health Accounts estimate, is identified as:
119.x: The remaining share is described as being mostly household out-of-pocket expenditure, which accounted for 43.4% of THE in the cited estimate.
119.tq: Distinguish the major financing source from unrelated public-revenue sources.

119.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to health expenditure indicators?

 a. SHA 2011 — Base used for National Health Accounts estimates
 b. Government health expenditure — Highest during the COVID-19 period
 c. Household out-of-pocket expenditure — Fell during COVID-19 to 39.4% of THE
 d. Government share in 2013–14 — 43.7%
119.x: Pairs a, b and c are correctly matched. Pair d is incorrect: the government share in 2013–14 was 28.6%, whereas 43.7% refers to the later estimate.
119.tq: Check each pair against the associated base year, period and percentage.

119.s:
Assertion (A): Household out-of-pocket expenditure as a share of Total Health Expenditure fell during the COVID-19 period.
Reason (R): It accounted for 39.4% of Total Health Expenditure during that period.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
119.x: Both statements are true. The figure of 39.4% describes the level of OOPE during COVID-19, but it does not by itself explain why the share fell; therefore, R is not the correct explanation of A.
119.tq: Separate evidence of a level from a causal explanation of a trend.

119.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. National Health Accounts reference base of SHA 2011
B. Government share of 28.6% in 2013–14
C. Period during which government health expenditure was highest during COVID-19
D. National Health Accounts estimate reporting a government share of 43.7%
119.x: The sequence proceeds from the SHA 2011 reference base to the 2013–14 comparison year, then to the COVID-19 period, followed by the later estimate reporting a 43.7% government share.
119.tq: Fix the definite year 2013–14 and the COVID-19 period before placing the later estimate.

119.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the current discussion on universal health coverage in India?
o: The target was withdrawn after the COVID-19 period.
The 2.5% public-health-spending target has been achieved according to recent assessments.
The target applies exclusively to private health insurance expenditure.
Recent assessments indicate that the 2.5% target remains unmet.
119.x: The NHA 2022–23 assessment and the parliamentary panel discussion on the ‘missing middle’ both indicate that the 2.5% target remains unmet.
119.tq: Identify the precise status of the target rather than assuming that a stated target was achieved.

119.s: The parliamentary discussion on the ‘missing middle’ in health coverage primarily reinforces which conclusion?
o: Household out-of-pocket expenditure has been eliminated.
Insurance is the sole necessary solution for universal health coverage.
Universal health coverage has already been fully achieved.
119.x: The parliamentary panel’s discussion on the ‘missing middle’, along with the NHA 2022–23 assessment, confirms that the 2.5% target remains unmet.
119.tq: Link the policy discussion to the specific unresolved financing target.

119.s:
In August 2026, Praja Arogya Vedika sought which combination of measures from the Andhra Pradesh Health Minister?

1. Enactment of a Right to Health Act
2. Withdrawal of public-private partnerships in government medical colleges
3. Reduction of public spending on primary care
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Praja Arogya Vedika sought a Right to Health Act and withdrawal of PPPs in government medical colleges. It did not seek reduction of public spending on primary care.
119.tq: Separate the two stated demands from the reversed policy position in statement 3.

119.s: Which of the following is regarded as a criticism of insurance-led health financing models?
o: They provide universal outpatient coverage in all circumstances.
They increase coverage without necessarily increasing the availability of care.
They reduce coverage while automatically increasing the quality of care.
They eliminate the need for primary healthcare expenditure.
119.x: A stated criticism is that insurance-led models may expand coverage without a corresponding increase in actual care. Greater spending on primary care and outpatient care is suggested as part of the corrective approach.
119.tq: Distinguish nominal financial coverage from actual access to healthcare.

119.s:
According to the debated reform approach to universal healthcare, which combination is considered necessary to address the limitations of insurance-led models?

1. Greater spending on primary care
2. Improved outpatient department coverage
3. Exclusive dependence on insurance expansion
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because exclusive dependence on insurance expansion is precisely the limitation criticised in the insurance-led approach.
119.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusive’ and identify the complementary primary-care measures.

119.s: In March 2026, which addition was made to Dr NTR Vaidya Seva?
119.x: Five cardiac procedures were added to Dr NTR Vaidya Seva in March 2026.
119.tq: Test the specific service addition rather than the broader scheme coverage.

120.s: Which platform provides a 14-digit identification number linking an individual’s health records?
120.x: ABHA provides a 14-digit Health ID that links an individual’s health records.
120.tq: Match the health IT platform with its identifier function.

120.s: The Healthcare Professionals Registry under ABDM is a registry of:
o: Pregnant women and children receiving immunisation
Doctors, nurses and other healthcare providers
Only TB patients notified by States
120.x: The Healthcare Professionals Registry contains doctors, nurses and other healthcare providers. ABDM also includes a Health Facility Registry and a Sandbox.
120.tq: Distinguish a professional registry from patient, facility and disease registries.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: ABHA — registry of only healthcare professionals
120.x: CoWIN is the digital platform for COVID-19 vaccination. U-WIN concerns routine immunisation, eSanjeevani telemedicine and ABHA health records.
120.tq: Use elimination among similar-sounding digital health platforms.

120.s: U-WIN is a digital registry for routine immunisation of:
120.x: U-WIN is the digital registry for routine immunisation of pregnant women and children.
120.tq: Identify the beneficiary group rather than confusing U-WIN with CoWIN.

120.s: eSanjeevani is primarily associated with:
120.x: eSanjeevani is the national telemedicine platform, with a Clinical Decision Support System integrated into it.
120.tq: Match the platform with its service domain and reject cross-sector distractors.

120.s: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission was launched in 2021 and is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
120.x: ABDM was launched in 2021 and is implemented by the National Health Authority.
120.tq: Separate the implementing authority from the ministries associated with nutrition and education.

120.s: Arogya Mitra, in the context of government health programmes, is best described as:
o: A component of the ABDM Health Facility Registry
120.x: Arogya Mitra functions as a PM-JAY hospital facilitator; it is not an ABDM component.
120.tq: Discriminate between a PM-JAY facilitation role and ABDM digital components.

120.s: The National Health Mission (NHM) presently consists of which of the following two sub-missions?
120.x: NHM has two sub-missions: the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM).
120.tq: Identify the exact composition of the mission rather than confusing its schemes with its sub-missions.

120.s:
With reference to ASHA workers, consider the following statements:
1. ASHA stands for Accredited Social Health Activist.
2. ASHA functions as a link between households and the health system.
3. ASHA is a village-level community health worker.
4. ASHA and ANM are regarded as important components of rural healthcare delivery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements are correct. ASHA means Accredited Social Health Activist, and ASHAs and ANMs play a crucial role in linking rural communities with healthcare services.
120.tq: Use the expansion, function, level of operation and institutional role as separate statement checks.

120.s: According to the India Year Book 2026, the number of ASHAs in Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
120.x: Andhra Pradesh has 42,060 ASHAs according to the cited India Year Book 2026 figure.
120.tq: Distinguish the exact numerical value from nearby figures.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)?
o: It provides adolescent counselling through peer educators only.
It provides cash assistance to pregnant women for institutional delivery.
It provides weekly audio messages to mothers and children.
It provides free generic medicines through public facilities.
120.x: JSY provides cash assistance to pregnant women to promote institutional delivery. It is a 100 per cent centrally sponsored scheme.
120.tq: Match the scheme with its principal intervention and avoid swapping it with neighbouring NHM programmes.

120.s:
Which of the following statements regarding JSY is correct?
1. It is 100 per cent centrally sponsored.
2. Andhra Pradesh recorded 1,76,966 beneficiaries during April–December 2024.
3. Its principal focus is cash assistance for institutional delivery.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: All three statements are correct. JSY is fully centrally sponsored, promotes institutional delivery through cash assistance, and recorded 1,76,966 beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh during the stated period.
120.tq: Check the funding pattern, state-specific figure and core objective independently.

120.s: The Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) primarily covers which age group?
120.x: RKSK is directed towards adolescents in the 10–19 years age group.
120.tq: Use the age-range distinction to separate RKSK from child and adult health programmes.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram?
o: Integrated Public Health Laboratories in every district
120.x: Integrated Public Health Laboratories in every district are associated with PM-ABHIM, not RKSK. RKSK includes adolescent clinics, peer educators, menstrual hygiene and weekly iron-folic acid supplementation.
120.tq: Find the item belonging to a different health mission rather than selecting a related adolescent intervention.

120.s: Anaemia Mukt Bharat was launched in which year?
120.x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat was launched in 2018.
120.tq: Test the programme year directly using close neighbouring years as distractors.

120.s: The ‘6x6x6’ strategy is associated with which of the following programmes?
120.x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat follows the 6x6x6 strategy, including IFA supplementation, deworming, testing and treatment, fortified foods and behaviour change.
120.tq: Recognise the distinctive numerical branding of a programme.

120.s:
Which of the following correctly describes Kilkari and Mobile Academy?
1. Kilkari provides 72 free weekly audio messages from the second trimester until the child turns one.
2. Kilkari operates in 27 States/Union Territories.
3. Mobile Academy is an audio course intended for ASHAs.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: All three statements are correct. Kilkari delivers 72 weekly audio messages over the stated period, while Mobile Academy provides an audio course for ASHAs.
120.tq: Separate the beneficiary, duration and function of two similarly named digital health initiatives.

120.s: Which one of the following is the correct description of the Free Drugs Service Initiative?
o: Free generic medicines at public facilities, with DVDMS managing drug supply
Free vaccination records through U-WIN, managed by NHA
Free teleconsultations through Mobile Academy, managed by NIC
Free cash transfers for institutional deliveries, managed by ASHA workers
120.x: The Free Drugs Service Initiative provides generic medicines free of cost at public facilities, and DVDMS manages the drug supply chain.
120.tq: Match the service, delivery point and management system precisely.

120.s: The usual Centre–State funding pattern under the National Health Mission is:
o: 60:40, with 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
120.x: The normal funding pattern is 60:40 between the Centre and States, while North-Eastern and Himalayan States receive a 90:10 pattern.
120.tq: Compare the general funding ratio with the special ratio for specified regions.

120.s: Mission Indradhanush is best described as a catch-up drive under the Universal Immunisation Programme intended primarily to reach:
o: Only pregnant women in urban areas
120.x: Mission Indradhanush is a catch-up immunisation drive for zero-dose and partly immunised children under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
120.tq: Identify the target group from the programme’s operational purpose.

120.s: Mission Indradhanush, launched in December 2014, set a target of achieving approximately what level of full immunisation?
120.x: Mission Indradhanush targeted 90 per cent full immunisation coverage.
120.tq: Distinguish the stated coverage target from absolute or lower percentage claims.

120.s: Which one of the following sets of vaccines is administered at birth under the Universal Immunisation Programme?
o: BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose
MR-2, DPT booster-1 and OPV booster
Td, DPT booster-2 and Rotavirus vaccine
120.x: The birth schedule includes BCG, OPV-0 and the birth dose of Hepatitis B.
120.tq: Start with the age column and eliminate vaccines belonging to later schedules.

120.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. 9–12 months — MR-1
2. 9–12 months — JE-1 in endemic districts
3. 16–24 months — MR-2
4. 5–6 years — DPT booster-2
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
120.x: All four pairs are correct. MR-1, JE-1, MR-2 and the second DPT booster occur in the stated age ranges.
120.tq: Verify each age–vaccine pair independently rather than relying on the sequence alone.

120.s: Which one of the following vaccine–age pairs is NOT correctly matched?
120.x: DPT booster-2 is administered at 5–6 years, not at 6 weeks. The other pairs are correctly matched.
120.tq: Find the deliberately shifted age in a vaccine schedule by checking the chronological sequence.

120.s: The U-WIN platform is intended to digitise which of the following records?
o: Only the list of generic medicines
120.x: U-WIN digitises maternal and child vaccination records and supports immunisation tracking.
120.tq: Distinguish the vaccination-record platform from broader digital health registries.

120.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) is correct?
1. It was launched in September 2021.
2. It is implemented by the National Health Authority.
3. It seeks to create a consent-based and interoperable digital health ecosystem.
4. It is built on Digital Public Infrastructure.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: All four statements are correct. ABDM was launched in September 2021, is run by NHA, and builds a consent-based interoperable ecosystem on Digital Public Infrastructure.
120.tq: Combine date, implementing authority, design principle and technological foundation.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four principal registries of ABDM?
120.x: The four registries are ABHA, Healthcare Professionals Registry, Health Facility Registry and Drug Registry. Arogya Mitra is not an ABDM component.
120.tq: Use the ‘not part of the architecture’ trap to distinguish a familiar health term from an official registry.

120.s:
Which of the following combinations contains only gateways or enabling components associated with ABDM?
1. Health Information Consent Manager
2. Unified Health Interface
3. National Health Claim Exchange
4. Sandbox
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: The Health Information Consent Manager, UHI, NHCX and the ABDM Sandbox are all associated with the ABDM digital architecture.
120.tq: Test the complete list by separating registries from gateways and development environments.

120.s: As reported in June 2026, the number of ABHA accounts had crossed:
120.x: The reported figure was more than 90 crore ABHA accounts in June 2026.
120.tq: Use the scale of the reported figure and distinguish crore-level alternatives.

120.s: The March 2026 direction of the National Medical Commission required medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for:
o: All OPD, IPD and emergency patients
120.x: The NMC directed medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for all OPD, IPD and emergency patients, partly to detect fake patients during inspections.
120.tq: Identify the complete beneficiary category rather than narrowing the order to one department or scheme.

120.s:
Which of the following statements is correct?
1. eSanjeevani has a Clinical Decision Support System.
2. NIC’s NextGen eHospital HMIS is ABDM-aligned.
3. AYUSH HMIS was linked to ABHA in 2024.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: All three statements are correct. eSanjeevani incorporates a Clinical Decision Support System, NextGen eHospital is ABDM-aligned, and AYUSH HMIS was linked to ABHA in 2024.
120.tq: Check the platform, alignment and linkage facts separately within the digital-health cluster.

120.s: Which of the following correctly matches an Ayushman Bharat pillar with its principal role?
o: Ayushman Arogya Mandir — comprehensive primary care
ABDM — construction of BSL-3 laboratories only
PM-ABHIM — cash assistance for institutional delivery
120.x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide comprehensive primary care. PM-JAY is the hospitalisation assurance pillar, ABDM is the digital backbone, and PM-ABHIM strengthens health infrastructure.
120.tq: Match each pillar with its central role and reject cross-swapped functions.

120.s: The target under Ayushman Arogya Mandirs was to convert approximately how many centres?
120.x: The target was to convert 1,50,000 centres into Ayushman Arogya Mandirs; more than 1.73 lakh had been converted according to the cited update.
